# Changelog

All notable public changes to PiG will be recorded in this file.

## [Unreleased]

## [0.8.0] - 2026-11-24

### Upgrading

- If your code supplies or calls `extension.NativeProvider.ResolveAuth` (a host that registers a native provider through `subprocess.Host.SetNativeProviderCallback`, or code that calls the field on a provider it received), change its signature from `func(ctx, *ai.Credential, ai.AuthResolutionOverrides) (*ai.AuthResult, *ai.Credential, error)` to `func(ctx, ai.CredentialStore, ai.AuthResolutionOverrides) (*ai.AuthResult, error)`. The function now receives the registry's credential store and persists a refresh through it (`ai.ResolveProviderAuth` is the implementation to call), so it no longer returns the refreshed credential for the caller to save.
- Node extensions: as in Pi (b7bb7ca905b8), a component's `render()` returns `readonly string[]`, and `Container` returns the same cached array while its children are unchanged. Extensions that modify render output in place, including `super.render()` in a `Container` subclass or an embedded component's output, must copy it first. Applies once the vendored Pi carries the change.
- Go components in the program: a `Container` or `Box` treats a child's lines as unchanged while the child returns the same slice (same first element and length) or equal rows, so a component must return a new slice when its content changes; an in-place edit of a returned slice is not seen. The slice `Container.Render` and `Box.Render` return is borrowed and read-only: copy it with `slices.Clone` before changing a line, also in a type that embeds a `Container` and edits its own `Render` result. Its capacity equals its length, so `append` is safe. A component that changes state without requesting a render stays stale while scrolling, as in Pi (it was already stale without scrolling). The extension SDKs that push lines (Python, Rust, Lisp, subprocess) pass lines by value and are unaffected.
- The experimental `pig-aot` Piglet is now `pig-bolt`, a name that says what it builds on (the Pi-Bolt compiler; it is not an official Pi-Bolt project). `piglets/aot` is now `piglets/pig-bolt`, its Go module is `github.com/MichaelKinsy/PiG/piglets/pig-bolt`, its extension is `boltruntime` and its command is `/bolt-runtime` (was `/aot-runtime`). The TypeScript runtime slot is still `aot`: `extensionsTypescriptRuntime: "aot"`, `PIG_TS_RUNTIME=aot`, the slot directory `aot` and the `PIG_AOT_*` variables work as before. `piglets/pig-bolt/pig-aot.yaml` is a one-file Piglet named `pig-aot` that extends `pig-bolt` (a compatibility alias for the old name): `pig --piglet piglets/pig-bolt/pig-aot.yaml` and `pig piglet build` of that path select and build what `pig-bolt` does under the old name. It does not make the bare name `pig --piglet pig-aot` resolve, the 0.7.0 path `piglets/aot` is gone, and `pig piglet pull` and `update` have nothing to alias because no pig-aot Piglet Binary release exists (remove the alias once no 0.5 or 0.7 setup names it).
- `pig-bolt` pins the Pi-Bolt 1.1.2 compiler (was 0.7.4; Pi-Bolt's `SHA256SUMS` still verifies with the Ed25519 key pinned in the Piglet). The first start after the update installs the new compiler, removes the 0.7.4 one and drops the images the old compiler built; their extension sets run on Bun once and are compiled again in the background.
- Extensions: write `replacement: null` in a `context_edit` draft that omits an entry. A draft without the member is now refused.
- Go extension SDK: `MessageRenderOptions` and `EntryRenderOptions` are no longer comparable, because each gains a `State` map, the renderer state Pi keeps per message or entry in a WeakMap. Compare the fields you need (`Expanded`, `OutputPad`), or use `reflect.DeepEqual`; do not use either type as a map key or compare with `==`. `pig extension upgrade` names the change.
- Rebuild extensions that were built with an SDK before 0.8.0. The extension wire has one shape and no negotiation: a `setModel` that sends the old `provider/id` string is refused with `setModel: model must be a model object`.
- Go: `ctx.SetModel("provider/id")` becomes `ctx.SetModelNamed("provider/id")`. `pig extension upgrade` rewrites every `Context.SetModel` call whose argument is a string and lists, with its line, a call whose argument has another type. `ctx.SetModel(model)` takes a model object, for example one from `ctx.ModelRegistry().Find(provider, id)`.
- Python, Rust, Lisp: no change is needed. A `provider/id` string still works, and the call also takes a model object.
- Node: the call is unchanged, but the object is now used as passed. An extension that selected a registry model with an object carrying only `provider` and `id` must pass the registry's model: `pi.setModel(ctx.modelRegistry.find(provider, id))`.
- If you set an update command (`PIG_SELF_UPDATE_COMMAND`, `PI_SELF_UPDATE_COMMAND` or the `selfUpdateCommand` setting), updating from 0.7.0 to 0.8.0 prints one harmless warning, "Ran <command>, but `pig --version` reports 1.5.1, not 0.8.0". The running 0.7.0 still reads the version from `pig --version`; the update itself succeeded. From 0.8.0 on, `pig update` reads the release from `pig version`, and the warning does not recur.
- extensions (Go embedders): a program that embeds the extension host must call `subprocess.EnableViewWidgets()` (and `subprocess.EnableEditorViews()` for the editor) before it builds a view, or a view that holds one of those kinds is rejected with a message that names the call. The `pig` command is unchanged: it makes both calls before it runs a command.
- One call that worked before is refused now: an event handler that called `waitForIdle` while the session was idle (for example in a `session_start` handler) used to return at once. Call it from a command handler instead, or react to the end of the run in an `agent_settled` handler; the refused call raises (Node: `TypeError`; Go, Python, Rust, Lisp: an error with code `not_a_command_context`).

### Added

- `terminal.framePacing: "adaptive"` in the global settings file, or `PIG_FRAME_PACING=adaptive` for one run (off unless set), lets fullscreen mode begin the next frame of a streaming reply 10 to 16 ms after the last one began: PiG waits four times what the last frame took to draw and write, at least 10 ms and at most Pi's 16 ms. What a frame shows is unchanged, and a key press and the last frame of a reply are never held back. It applies only with the screen writer selected (`terminal.screenWriter: "writer"`, D624, opt-in as well) and on terminals known to show a frame at once at its end (synchronized updates): kitty, Ghostty, WezTerm, Warp, iTerm2, Alacritty, and the VS Code terminal from 1.108 on, never inside tmux, GNU screen, Zellij or herdr, and never while an extension draws on the screen. By default, and with `"pi"`, frames begin 16 ms apart, as Pi's do. Measured with the screen writer on and the terminal declared as Alacritty, the median time between visible changes falls from 15.6 to 9.7 ms on a streamed answer and to 13.4 ms while a file is written, the 95th percentile is under Pi's, the 99th percentile is half a millisecond to 2 ms over it while a file is written, and PiG uses 4 to 7 % more CPU time (D625).
- Interactive mode shows one warning at start when adaptive frame pacing is selected (`terminal.framePacing: "adaptive"` or `PIG_FRAME_PACING=adaptive`) without the screen writer, because the pacing then has no effect: `Adaptive frame pacing (terminal.framePacing, PIG_FRAME_PACING) has no effect without the screen writer (terminal.screenWriter "writer"): frames keep Pi's 16 ms interval.` Print, JSON and RPC mode print nothing new (D625).
- Added Claude Fable 5.2 (`claude-fable-5-2`) to the `anthropic` provider ($8/$40 per million input/output tokens, 1M context, 128K output). Like Fable 5.1 it uses per-message effort and mid-conversation system messages; requests its safety classifiers refuse before any output are answered by Claude Opus 5 through server-side fallback and billed at Opus 5's price. Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 on other providers, such as OpenRouter's `anthropic/claude-fable-5.2`, get the same per-message effort support.
- Added `ModelsProvider.RefreshModelsAuth`. Set it to `RefreshModelsAuthConfigured` for providers whose `RefreshModels` reads a catalog that needs no provider credential, such as pi.dev: `Models.Refresh` then still skips unconfigured providers, but no longer refreshes an expired OAuth token first, so a stale login (`invalid_grant`) no longer fails that provider's catalog refresh. `RefreshModelsContext.Credential` is nil in that network phase.
- `PIG_TELEMETRY` overrides the `enableInstallTelemetry` setting, beside Pi's `PI_TELEMETRY`, which still works alone. When both are set, `PIG_TELEMETRY` decides. `pig` passes the decision on as `PI_TELEMETRY` to the Node extension runtime and to every process it starts.
- An extension can give a child session a member fused into the Piglet Binary by listing `builtin:<member>` in the child's additional extension paths (`AdditionalExtensionPaths`), the form of Pi's `-e builtin:<name>`. A child session never had the Binary's fused members, because they have no path to discover. The path is opt-in: a child that does not list it gets none, so a member that creates children is not loaded in each of them, and a child's child has it only when it lists the path again. `resources.extensionNames` selects the member by its name. A Binary that fuses no member of that name, stock PiG included, reports `Unknown built-in extension` as before.
- Go API `chord/nextnode/plugins`: Chord v2's plugin model (Pi `9823079ad`, slice 12). `PluginsOptions.Api` (`AppApi{Name, Versions}`) checks every import of the app's versioned API (`@acme/app/v3`, per-kind modules such as `@acme/app/v3/web`): an unlisted version, another kind's module, two versions in one facet and a direct import of Chord are build errors naming the file and line, and a computed `require` is refused the same at evaluation. Roots are `PluginRoot{Path, Required}`: a required root's plugin failing, or a problem discovery reports in it, makes `Plugins.Load` return a `*PluginError` after the host's load settled. Files named `<name>.<kind>.<ext>` are of that kind and refused in facets of another kind with the chain of imports named; single-file plugins (`hello.server.ts` at a root's top, host packages only); a package's `chord.plugins` lists its plugins (paths, globs, `!` exclusions); `DiscoverPackage`, `SameFiles`; `InstallPlugin` and `Plugins.InstallPlugin` install plugins from git (`{Git, Ref}`) or npm (`{Npm, Version}`) with a claimed directory, staging and checks. The vendored Node subprocess (evaluate.ts, runtime.ts, host.ts, object.ts, unbound.ts, record.ts) is Pi `9823079ad` as a named catch-up.
- Go API `chord/next/host`, `chord/next/registries`: `Host.UnservedNames`, `ActivationsUnderWay`, `UndeclaredRegistries` (the reads Pi's `testPlugin` uses), `UnboundIndex.Names`, `RegistryRecord.NewestContribution`.
- Chord: `data.Forbidden(message, details...)` (Pi's `forbidden`), `Host.PrincipalAttributes` on the host interface (Pi's `principalAttributes`), and the `surfaces.BaseRole` and `surfaces.ColorDepth` types (`TerminalColor` takes a `ColorDepth`). <!-- fix: d184ab85f1 -->
- `docs/chord/tutorial.md` and `examples/chord-todo`: the Chord tutorial in PiG's API, starting with its first chapter ("One Server": the principals, the API module, the start program, the owner's sign-in). `examples/chord-todo/tutorial_test.go` does Pi's three checks: every quoted block matches its file, the example's steps run, and the output the book shows is what they print.
- Chord plugins (internal): the control channel between a Go host and its Node plugin host carries a link's `event` and `ack` messages in both directions, one message per flush, each acknowledged by count; the Go side writes them from a sender that never blocks a host's flush or the channel's reader and has ended when the process has. Nothing uses them yet: a type with an event member still fails at the bridge with the error that says events do not cross it.
- Chord plugins: the Go side listens to the events of an object that a Node host's plugins serve: `NodeReference.Events(name).On(listener, ctx)` calls the listener with the value and the stamp of each emit, in order with the results of the reference's calls, until `Stop`, the context's abort, the reference's release or the process's exit. The Node host bounds what the Go side has not acknowledged with its event window (`RuntimeLoad.EventWindow`, 32 messages by default) and drops what it emits beyond it, counted `chord.events.dropped{reason=window}`. With this, a type with event members crosses the bridge between a Go host and its Node plugin host in both directions, and the error that said events do not cross it is gone.
- Chord plugins: a plugin on the Node host that holds a type one of the app's Go facets serves gets the events of the type's event members. Its listener (`reference.member.on`) is called with the value and the stamp of the Go object's emit, in order with the results of the plugin's own calls. The Go host bounds what the Node host has not acknowledged with its event window (32 messages by default) and drops what it emits beyond it, counted `chord.events.dropped{reason=window}`. A hold by the Go side of a plugin's type with event members still fails with the error that says events do not cross the bridge.
- Chord host (internal): a consumer that is not a link can take a Go host's event flushes as a link's provider side sends them: one message per flush with the entries in order, under the host's event window (32 unacknowledged messages by default, the next flush's events dropped and counted `chord.events.dropped{reason=window}`), acknowledged by count. It is the Go host's part of carrying events across the plugins bridge; nothing is added to the public API of `chord/next/host`, and no type with an event member crosses the bridge yet.
- Chord: the client runtimes of the page and the terminal (the vendored TypeScript client) have event members: a contract declares `event(schema)` members, an object emits with `self.events()`, a reference subscribes with `member.on`, and React components subscribe with `useEvents(member, listener)`. Ports the client side of Pi 8d30e6306; the wire goldens of the link now cover the event message, the event ack and a hello without a call window.
- Chord: plugins on a Node host can declare event members (`event(schema)` in a local contract, `events` in a remote variant), emit with `self.events()` and subscribe with a reference's `on`: the vendored Node tree of the plugins component carries Pi's chord events (Pi 8d30e6306). The events are delivered inside the Node host; they do not cross to the Go host yet.
- Chord: event members (fire-and-forget) on the host: an object declares `self.Events()` sources, references subscribe with `ref.Events(name).On`, older consumers get their version's mapped values, and a reference can re-expose another's event member. One flush per turn after the published state, listeners in entry then subscription order; `event_mapping_failed` reports a failing mapping once per failure episode. Ports Pi 8d30e6306's host layer; the link and remote layers follow.
- Chord: event messages over links and relays (one `event` message per flush per link and origin, a per-origin event window of 32 by default with dropped events counted as `chord.events.dropped{window}`, event acks apart from state acks), `TuiScope.On`, and call windows only for untrusted links: a trusted link announces no call window and its peer sends every call at once. Ports the link and remote layers of Pi 8d30e6306.
- Go API `chord/nextnode/plugins`: `TestPlugin`, the port of Pi's `testPlugin` (`packages/chord/src/node/plugins/testing.ts`): a plugin built as production builds it, evaluated in a Node host with the app's API modules (files) and an in-memory store beside stub facets (Go facets bridged to the plugin's host, `TestStub`, or JavaScript modules, `CoreFacet`), the registries it contributes to that nobody serves collected by a collecting facet (`TestedPlugin.Contributions`), the contracts its requests wait for unserved listed (`Unserved`), and `RootPrincipal`. `NodeHost.Hold` is `host.hold` for a local type of the plugin's host (the reference at once, whatever its object's state). Divergences D502 and D503 record the live-JavaScript forms that cannot cross the process boundary.
- Chord: `Host.Delegate` lets a host with an address take the remote types it does not serve itself over a route to another host (the Go app kit's server serves its Node plugins' objects through it), and `Host.Serves` tells a delegate's host what that host serves, so a server plugin's object can hold the app's own remote types (the locale and theme choices, telemetry) as Pi's one server host lets it: the server serves the union of its own types and the plugins' both ways; a host without a delegate is unchanged.
- Go API `chord/next/host`: `host.Resume(ctx, work)` runs `work` as one synchronous section of the host's loop on the goroutine of a method handler that suspended (the awaits of Pi's handler resume inside the loop, so code that reads the host's state after a transaction or a blocking call reads it there); a ctx that is no handler's is refused.
- Chord: documents and table rows can belong to a host, as in Pi 1.5.2. `defineState` takes a host kind as `keyed` (its handles take and list addresses of the kind), `keyed(schema, kind)` declares such a contract member, and `host(kind)` is a table column holding an address. The store keeps the host as an indexed column (store schema 3), `Host.ExportHostData`, `ImportHostData` (refuse, replace or copy under another address, older table versions migrated through their owner's history) and `DeleteHostData` work on one address's data in one commit coordinated with the live owners, and the app kit's `ExportData`, `ImportData` (with `existing: "replace"`) and `DeleteData` carry the server's part (archive format 2, `server.archive`, and the Go host's `kit-server.archive`, D462).
- Chord (Go): the terminal kit has `OptimisticBegin`: an optimistic action shows in its caller's turn and goes when the caller settles it, for a key handler that cannot wait for the action's call. `Optimistic` behaves as before.
- Go API `chord/nextnode/plugins` (Pi `c23b9ec1`): `*.module.css` files of a browser build are scoped to their plugin and file (`ScopeCSSModule`; classes `chord_<hash>_<file>_<class>`, `composes` and `@import` kept, `url()` of any stylesheet an asset), and the base marks: `Plugins.WatchBase(BaseInputs)` with `Recorder` (the hash of each file as a base build read it) sets `base` exactly while a recorded file differs, is gone, or a source file is new in a base directory (the server's own code is hashed at start). Starting the watcher over a base directory now reads each of its source files once (5.2 ms for 300 files).
- Chord plugins (internal): `Plugins.WatchTree` and `Plugins.Watches` let Go code that holds the plugins component have its file watcher watch one more tree and ask whether a directory is watched. The tests of the component and of the app use them through one shared barrier (`chord/nextnode/plugins/pluginstest`) to wait until the watcher handled every file event of an edit before they apply the changes: the reload suite's `edit` helper returned at the first event, so a later event of the same edit could leave a plugin dirty after the rollout and fail a test about once in 36 runs. The watcher's behaviour does not change.
- Chord's host traces its work when it has a telemetry adapter (`HostOptions.Telemetry`; Pi main `c23b9ec1`): `chord.load`, `chord.reload` and `chord.revoke` spans and a root's `trace` option, a consumer's `chord.hold` and `chord.call`, a provider's `chord.method` (a type served untraced starts none), `chord.activate` with its `chord.park` and `chord.retry` events, `chord.resolve`, `chord.routine`, a job's `chord.job` intent, run and finish, native open and close, `ctx.trace`, the relay's `chord.relay` for relayed holds, re-holds and calls, and `chord.http` for each routed request (`HttpOptions.Telemetry`, its method and route pattern, never its path; a `traceparent` continues only when a contributed relay verified the request). A hold and a call carry their trace on the link (`HoldMessage.Trace`, `CallMessage.Trace`: at most 8 keys, each name and value at most 256 printable ASCII characters, kept in the order sent), so a provider's spans continue its consumer's trace and a re-hold links to the trace it continues. `HostOptions.PrincipalAttributes` says who a span was for (`chord.principal`, capped). New metrics: `chord.link.bytes`, `chord.links.open`, `chord.holds.active`, `chord.calls.in_flight`, `chord.link.state_messages`, `chord.backpressure.wait` and `chord.park.duration`. A host with telemetry off, or an untraced adapter, starts no span and records nothing; a document's commit allocates nothing more for it.
- The Chord tutorial in PiG's API is complete: `docs/chord/tutorial.md` has Pi's chapters (one server, a list on its own worker, routes, a page, a terminal, a theme, a second user, languages, changing code, moving a list, telemetry with a trace viewer, testing one plugin) with eight screenshots, and `examples/chord-todo` is the Go app and TypeScript plugins they quote. `tutorial_test.go` does Pi's three checks for every chapter, `screens_test.go` takes the screenshots in headless Chromium and checks what the book shows of them, and `lists_test.go` is the lists plugin's own test.
- Chord's app kit: device pairing (`/_chord/pair`) and data archives (`PackData`, `PackStore`, `UnpackData`) in `chord/nextnode/app`, and `HttpRequest.RemoteAddress` in `chord/nextnode/http`.
- Chord: the portable part of Pi main's `surfaces` (messages in code, the `Translations` registry, languages and locale matching, number formatting, page state) in `chord/next/surfaces`, and `TuiScope` for terminal components in `chord/next/tui`.
- `workers.WorkersOptions.Forgotten`: called once an address has no worker, no operation and no failure left (Pi has no such hook; nothing observable changes).
- `chord/context` gains `WithAbortSignalCancel(parent, signal)`: `withCancel(withAbortSignal(parent, signal))` as one context, whose `cancel` also takes it out of the signal's links, for a caller that derives one context per operation and ends the operation before either source aborts.
- Chord's app kit files (Pi main `bb5eafa8a`, `f617ed317`): `chord/nextnode/app` carries Files v2, the file storage of a host: spaces, paths and folders, versions that share blobs, keys that make a retried write store nothing, metadata queries, chunked uploads that resume, caps, a summary per space, `FilesFolder` listing one folder live, and `CopyFiles`, with the secrets and data directory layout they use. <!-- feat: files-v2 -->
- `chord/next/host`: `Reference.Start` and `PendingCall.Wait` start a call and await it apart, and `AwaitingCtx` runs the blocking remainder of an `onLive` routine from another package. <!-- feat: D430 -->
- Chord: the store writes the commits queued behind a running commit step in one backend transaction (group commit, Pi main `8889e623d`, decision S18): each keeps its own seq, outbox commit and adoption in queue order and the metadata is written once; a refusal in a group rolls it back and runs its commits one by one, so only the refusing commit is refused. A backend failure while the store closes is latched and refuses the commits admitted after it. <!-- feat: 8889e623d -->
- Chord: live queries over an object's own tables (Pi main `2439933cf`): `self.Query(table, q, limit)` is a watchable of up to `limit` rows, run before the object goes live and again in the commit step of every commit of the object that writes the table, publishing only the diff in that commit's batch. A failing run makes the query a failed member and is reported once as `query_failed`. <!-- feat: 2439933cf -->
- Chord: the Node SQLite adapter opens a file read-only (`NodeSqliteDatabaseOptions.Mode = ReadOnly`, Pi main `ff33ef42c`): no directory is made, nothing is configured or checkpointed, and its transactions are deferred (`BEGIN`) and read one snapshot. A document's commit records a `chord.commit` event (documents, ops, table rows, duration) on its context's span and a `chord.commit.duration` histogram (ms) on the host's metrics, and a transaction that does not commit while its context is cancelled is reported to its owner (`CancelReporter`).
- Chord: plugins can declare named live queries (a `queries` member with `self.queries`, `self.liveQuery` and `self.count`) over the column sets that a table exposes, and another object's named query can be read through a reference with a query reader. Queries can use `exists` and joins. Port of Pi's Chord slice 14 (Pi 7cc21c24f6b5).
- Chord: a list (`self.list`) loads its rows a page at a time and keeps the pages as one gapless value while rows move, are written in bulk, or the publisher reloads. A commit no longer runs a live query it cannot change, and the counters `chord.query.probes`, `chord.query.skips` and `chord.query.rows` report the probes, the skipped runs and the rows read.
- Chord: a served type whose contract declares an `admission` is served with `admit`, which decides for each caller and hands the factory a typed value. A caller that is refused sees its reference fail with the new `denied` failure kind, a running call is answered `forbidden/revoked`, and a changed decision seals the running attempt and admits a new one. The `denied` kind is byte 3 in the binary codec and letter `d` in the text codec; the refused byte moves from 3 to 4, so a client that decodes failure causes must know `denied` (the Go consumer does).
- Chord: a route takes `admit` too. It is asked once for each principal and address, after `authorize` and before anything is resolved or forwarded. Until its first allow a hold is `loading`, a denial fails the principal's holds `failed { denied }` and releases them at the address's host, and a later allow forwards them again. `createWorkers` passes the option to its route.
- Chord: `DeleteHostData` takes options that limit the delete to the records and tables of one plugin; a plugin that is not loaded is refused as invalid arguments.
- Chord: `chord/sync`, session sync over a store's outbox (Pi main `e5f3b4150`, experimental): `UploadSession` uploads the commits after the last sequence a copy shares with a remote into a slot the remote creates once, `PullSession` pulls a copy forward through `ApplyBatch` (or restores it from an archive into an empty backend), `FoldSession` folds history into snapshots, `FlushScheduler` decides when to upload, and `FileSystemSyncRemote` and `FileSyncStateStore` keep both in a directory. Bodies are gzip-compressed JSON lines read as streams, so a batch, a snapshot and a store are never held whole; a batch body line is bounded as in Pi, at V8's string length (536,870,888 UTF-16 units), on upload and on pull, with `RangeError: Invalid string length`. <!-- feat: e5f3b4150 -->
- Chord: a worker's state carries its `incarnation` (the run of the worker's host) from its link's handshake on, before its first call is handled. A route's `resolve` is told the peer's incarnation through its `opened` callback at the handshake, and the store gains `Settled`, which is ready once the commits queued before the call were adopted or rejected. Port of Pi f57cd9484.
- Chord: `LiveIn` returns a reference narrowed to the variant it is live in, and `TuiScope.Variant` reads one in a scope and follows a change of its variant (the React client's `useVariant` is vendored). Port of Pi f57cd9484.
- A Piglet Binary's fused Go member can own the command line (`extensions/sdk/clihook`): its hook runs before PiG parses its arguments and may serve the invocation (help, version, subcommands) and exit with its own status, rewrite the arguments, set the default retry policy (3 retries, 2000 ms first delay, 60000 ms cap unless it names another; settings.json still overrides each field), and own a print run: PiG then writes nothing to stdout, leaves the stderr line of a failed run to the member, and exits with the status the member recorded when the run succeeded. Stock PiG registers no hook and behaves as before.
- A Go program that embeds Code Mode in a macOS app signed with the Hardened Runtime can run it without a code-signing entitlement: `Interpreter: true` on `codemode.SandboxOptions` (and `InlineSandboxOptions`), `codemode.ServeOptions`, or the built-in extension's `Options` runs the QuickJS sandbox on wazero's interpreter instead of its compiler. The compiler stays the default. Without the option, such an app is killed (SIGKILL) the first time a script runs unless it carries `com.apple.security.cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory`; `com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit` alone does not help. The interpreter was about 50 times slower on two measured scripts (26 ms against 1.2 s, 152 ms against 8.4 s), so the entitlement is the better fix where the app can carry it. The `pig` command is not affected (D263, issue #410).
- The read tool's operations take Pi's `createReadStream` in every SDK: `ReadOperations.CreateReadStream` in Go (`sdk` and `internal/codingagent/tools`), `create_read_stream` in Python, `create_read_stream` and `ReadStream` in Rust and `:create-read-stream` in Lisp. A tool that supplies it reads a text file through the stream and keeps only the lines it shows in memory, where `readFile` loads the whole file. The host reads the stream in chunks of at most 64 KB and closes it when the read ends or is aborted.
- `pig update` lists each updated package with its npm version or git commit change, prints `Packages are already up to date` only when it checked the packages and nothing warned, and says so when offline. <!-- fix: c001170ca5 -->
- A fused Go Piglet member can decide which failed model requests PiG retries and how long it waits (`clihook.RetryPolicy.Decide`), with the status, the response headers and whether the stream had started; the same decision covers the summarization request of a compaction. `Silent` removes PiG's own interactive retry status line and its final "Retry failed after ..." line, and Escape still cancels the retry delay. `HTTPIdleTimeoutMs` sets the default HTTP idle time-out when `settings.json` names none. A `message_end` replacement from an extension keeps the failure response of the message it replaces. Nothing changes without a member that uses it: a failed request builds no failure response and allocates what it did before, and the response is never written to a session file, to RPC or to JSON mode (D654).
- GitHub Copilot Claude models now also send `strict: true` for tools requesting JSON-schema constrained sampling, as direct Anthropic does.
- `ai.GetPromptCacheTtlMs`, `ai.GetCacheWarmingDelayMs`, `ai.IsCacheWarmingReplayable`, `ai.GetCacheWarmingRequestOptions`, `ai.EvaluateCacheWarming`, `ai.CacheWarmingDecision` and the `ai.CacheWarming*` constants: the prompt cache warming policy shared by every host, moved out of the coding agent's cache warmer (Pi c9552c7d, #11857). The coding agent's `GetPromptCacheTtlMs`, `GetCacheWarmingDelayMs` and `IsReplayable` are gone from `internal/codingagent`; `CacheWarmingAction` and `CacheWarmingDecision` there and in `coding/extension` are the `ai` types.
- The docs have a Models Configuration page that lists every field of `models.json` with its type, default and description, generated from the same schema trees as `schemas/models.schema.json` (`make generate-schemas`).
- The built-in documentation has two new pages. `event-bus` (`pig docs show event-bus`) shows how one extension calls another through `pi.events`, across languages: a Go extension asks and a Node or Python extension answers, with the calls of the Node, Go, Python, Rust and Lisp SDKs and the rules of delivery (payload by value, order, no listener, a failing listener, an async listener, reload; D83), and a second example in which the asking extension waits with a time limit for an answer that comes later. `go-hot-reload` (`pig docs show go-hot-reload`) gives the steps to edit a Go extension and run the change with `/reload` in the running session, what the screen shows, what a reload keeps and what a failed build shows (D70). The complete extensions of both pages run in the real binary under `TestDocsEventBusPage` and `TestDocsGoHotReloadPage`. `extensions.md` now states what `/reload` keeps: an extension whose source did not change keeps its process, and an edited Go extension runs in a new process.
- The built-in documentation has a page for extension views, `ui-views` (`pig docs show ui-views`). It describes how an extension mounts one view that the terminal and a web page draw (D614): the mount calls, the node kinds, intents, alternatives chosen by a client's claims, accessibility and focus records, drawings, slots, errors, the calls of each SDK and what each client draws. Its two complete Node extensions run in a test.
- Durable JSONL storage opens read-only with `JsonlStorageOptions{ReadOnly: true}` (`jsonl.Open`, `OpenNodeJsonlStorage`), for a viewer of a directory another process writes, as Pi's `{ readOnly: true }` does. A writable open repairs files on recovery: it truncates torn lines and unconfirmed sidecar records and reclaims sidecars, which can cut records a running writer just appended. The read-only open creates and writes nothing, skips those records in memory, holds the state committed at open, and `Commit` rejects with `*JsonlStorageReadOnlyError`. A recovery that fails because it raced a writer's commit is retried (up to five opens). `HarnessOptions.ReadOnly` does not reach the storage open, so a read-only viewer opens JSONL storage this way too; `NodeFileSystem` gains `FileInfo`, which the retry check reads, and the exported `jsonl.FileSystem` interface now requires `FileInfo(ctx, path) (env.FileInfo, error)`: an implementer outside this repository must add it (any `env.FileSystem` already has it).
- Durable's `SqliteStorage` commits a call of many batches in a few statements, as Pi main now does (`storage/sqlite/commit.ts`): the check state of all batches is read up front, each batch is checked in memory, and the accepted batches are written per table in multi-row statements. A batch with a document copy writes the batches before it first, so a call of many forks costs a few statements per fork. The Durable core's tick model (`hopcost`) counts the new awaits, and the contract corpus and tick tables are regenerated at Pi main c23b9ec1. <!-- fix: fabf916f -->
- A Durable conversation can carry its own compaction settings, including `modelOverrides`, that win over the Harness's for that conversation (`AgentChange.Compaction`, Pi `922c3ff2b`). The overrides keep the order they were set in, in the stored `pi.agent` state and when read back, as the JavaScript object Pi stores does; `durable.CompactionSettings.ModelOverrides` is now a `durable.CompactionOverrides` (`NewCompactionOverrides`, `Get`, `Set`, `All`) instead of a Go map. <!-- fix: 922c3ff2b -->
- Durable `Tx.Submission` reads a submission inside a change, and stream options reach the model call. <!-- fix: 9ca15920 -->
- `durable.SubmissionDraft.OnAbort`, as Pi's `onAbort` (Pi e67aa1a4e): an input submitted with `durable.OnAbortKeep` stays queued through `Conversation.Abort` and abort cascades, as a failed run keeps its queue under `AfterFailedRun` keep: the next input places it and that run answers it. For input its sender cannot take back, such as another agent's message; `Submission.Abort` still withdraws it. The default, `durable.OnAbortWithdraw`, settles the input unanswered with reason `aborted` as before. The inbox item records the flag as `onAbort: "keep"` after its entry, and only for `keep`; an item stored without the field withdraws. The durable core takes the same field in the `submit` event and the transaction op, and the Cloudflare host passes the draft's field through. `harness.WithdrawQueuedInputs` is now `harness.WithdrawAbortedInputs`, and `inbox.WithdrawQueued` of the core is `inbox.WithdrawAborted`; `WithdrawQueuedInputsFor` still withdraws every input.
- Go: the Durable runtime's suspendable work (Pi `473515f9c`). Signals: `durable.DefineSignal` defines a typed JSON value delivered to a live task from outside with `harness.Signal(ctx, harness, taskId, token, key, value)` or `durable.Signal(tx, ...)`, which answer `SignalDelivered`, `SignalDuplicate`, `SignalInvalid`, `SignalClosed`, or `SignalNotFound`; a value is kept in the task, also one that arrives before the sleep on its key, which then wakes at once; `durable.ReadSignal` on `TaskRuntime`, `HookApi`, and `ToolExecutionApi` reads it, migrated to the token's version, until the task ends. A sleep may wait for signals (`TaskState.Signals`, `Until` optional) and ends at whichever comes first, and a wait may use `JoinAny`; a woken task reads why in `TaskState.Wake` (`WakeTime`, `WakeExpired`, `WakeSignal`, `WakeTasks`). `Harness.Wake()` reports parked work inactive.
- Go: tools that park. `Execute` may return a `ToolExecutionResult` whose `Park` holds a `ToolPark` (`Sleep` or `Wait`) and runs again, once woken, with `api.Wake()` and `api.Checkpoint()` set; `ToolRegistration.Cancel` cleans up the external work of a parked call that is aborted; an invalid park ends the call with an `invalid_park` result, and wrappers never park. `ExecuteToolNoWait` starts or finds a nested call and returns a `NestedToolCall`, `CreateTaskErased` takes a `ToolTaskOptions.Key`, explicit keys are required after a wake, and a restart keeps the `AbandonOnRestart` children of a call that was parked or not started. `SubmissionDraft.Notify` delivers `durable.SubmissionSettledSignal` (Pi's `SubmissionSettled`) to a task when the submission settles.
- Go: `BeforeToolResult.Sleep` parks a call at its gates; every wake, registry change, and open runs the whole `call` phase again. `HookApi.Now()` reads the Harness clock. `afterTools` and `onYield` hooks may ask for tasks (`HookTasks`, `YieldTasks`) that run as the generation's children: an `afterTools` task ends the run with `AfterToolsDecision{Terminate: true}`, and `onYield` tasks decide with `YieldDecision` whether the answer stands while the run's inputs stay open (`LiveRun.Yield`). Kept contexts expire while a conversation's live work is all parked.
- The pi-env daemon's `process` operation runs a program with plain pipes for stdin, stdout and stderr, for programs that speak a protocol on stdin and stdout such as MCP servers: `processWrite` and `processCloseStdin` feed its stdin in arrival order, output arrives as raw bytes per stream, and cancelling, a lost connection or the program's own exit kills its process group (on Windows, its job object), so a wrapper such as `npx` that exits leaves nothing running. `hello` reports it in `features`. `env.OpenProcess` returns a `RemoteProcess`; daemons released before it fail the open with `not_supported`. Unlike terminals, it works on Windows too.
- `durable/images/fit`, as Pi's `@earendil-works/pi-durable/images/fit`, fits the images entering a conversation to its model's limits with any `tools.ImageProcessor`, before they are stored, as the coding agent does: `fit.CreateFitImagesExtension(processor)` is an `afterTool` hook for the results of every tool the model calls (MCP tools, code mode's `image()`), and `fit.FitImage(ctx, bytes, mimeType, limits, processor)` and `fit.FitImages(ctx, content, limits, processor)` fit a host's input before it is submitted. An image that cannot be prepared is left out with a note. `tools.ImageLimitsOf(model)` (Pi's `imageLimits`) resolves a model's limits as `read` does, and `tools.PreparedNotes`, `tools.FromBase64` and `tools.DetectSupportedImageMimeType` are exported.
- `deepseek-v4.1-flash` and `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` on the Qwen Token Plan Individual providers (`qwen-token-plan-individual`, `qwen-token-plan-individual-cn`), and a key variable per plan: `QWEN_TOKEN_PLAN_TEAM_API_KEY`, `QWEN_TOKEN_PLAN_TEAM_CN_API_KEY`, `QWEN_TOKEN_PLAN_INDIVIDUAL_API_KEY` and `QWEN_TOKEN_PLAN_INDIVIDUAL_CN_API_KEY`. A plan's variable configures only that plan's provider; the shared `QWEN_TOKEN_PLAN_API_KEY` and `QWEN_TOKEN_PLAN_CN_API_KEY` still work for both plans of their region. <!-- feat: 1397070024 -->
- `qwen4-max-preview` is now available in the `qwen-token-plan-individual` and `qwen-token-plan-individual-cn` providers (Pi #12259).
- Qwen Token Plan Individual (China) provider `qwen-token-plan-individual-cn`, using `QWEN_TOKEN_PLAN_CN_API_KEY`, with the Individual model list on the China endpoint, and `glm-5.3` on `qwen-token-plan-individual`. <!-- feat: c3a48aa340 -->
- GitHub Copilot lists the `microsoft-decision-1` classifier model, which classifies through the account's `/v1/systemone` endpoint. <!-- feat: c3a48aa340 -->
- `compat.requiresNonNullAssistantContent` sends `""` instead of `null` content for replayed assistant messages that carry no text. <!-- feat: 73e1cef071 -->
- `compat.promptCacheKeyMode` (`auto`, `enabled`, `disabled`) controls the `prompt_cache_key` request field on `openai-completions` and `openai-responses`; `enabled` sends it through compatible proxies whenever caching is active. <!-- feat: 7dd0dc1be1 -->
- `compat.requiresToolsWithToolHistory` restores `"tools": []` on `openai-completions` for proxies that need it. <!-- feat: 7dd0dc1be1 -->
- `pig auth login [provider]` and `pig auth logout [provider]` sign in to and out of a provider from the command line, as Pi's `pi auth login` and `pi auth logout` do, including the provider matching and the terminal question the login asks. The MCP sign-in hint now names `pig auth login <provider>`.
- `registerMarkdownTransformer(transformer, { messageTypes })` chooses the surfaces a Markdown transformer runs on, as in Pi: `user`, `assistant` and `assistant-thinking` (the default), `custom` (custom messages without a renderer and expanded skill blocks), `summary` (expanded branch and compaction summaries) and `changelog` (What's New, `/changelog`, Extension Updates and the Update Available note). Skill blocks and summaries hand the transformer their content without the header, and custom, skill and summary messages drawn from a session entry carry its `messageId` and `timestamp`. The Go, Python, Rust and Lisp SDKs and Node extensions take the same option, and the built-in Mermaid transformer also renders diagrams in summaries.
- chord: `Store.OnCommitted(listener, onError)` announces the new `LastSeq` after commits are durable and adopted (a commit, a group, a series, an applied batch), on a goroutine of its own, once for however many commits it covers, one call at a time and in order; a listener that panics is removed and its panic handed to `onError` (Pi 6268cc5cd).
- chord: a web surface for an app with its own HTTP stack: `WebSurfaceOptions.Routes` false contributes no `Http` routes, and the surface gives `File(path, ctx)` (the file forever, 404, 503 when the build failed), `PageAssets(ctx)` and `Base(ctx)` for the app to serve with its own access rules and CSP; `PageBootstrap(hash, set)` is exported. `ClientOptions.Follow` false makes a static client (a page built offline and served elsewhere): it neither follows the scripts object, applies a set, nor asks the server's base, so it is never outdated. `startPage({ themes: false })` runs no kit themes and writes nothing on `:root`; `startPage({ follow: false })` is the static page (Pi 22fe46c7b).
- chord: `BuildBase` takes a `BaseResolution` (`Conditions`, `Tsconfig`), and `WebSurfaceOptions`, `TuiSurfaceOptions`, `AppWeb` and `AppTui` take `Tsconfig`: a base bundle resolves packages through that tsconfig's `paths`, so a source checkout without `dist/` builds its bases; without it no tsconfig.json is read (Pi 53af02378). <!-- feat: f32c342b54 -->
- chord: `LinksOptions.Opened` of `chord/nextnode/http` gets a third parameter, `closeLink`, that terminates that link at once, as a revocation does: no close handshake (the peer sees close code 1006), the link's other links stay open, a later call or a call after the link is gone does nothing, and any goroutine may call it; an app uses it to close the links of a credential it revoked. The function `Opened` returns runs once when the link closes, also when the hook ended the link before it returned (Pi 5f89cc0a7df6).
- chord: `contracts.MemberNamesOf(contract, variant)` returns the names of the state members, methods and event members of one variant of a contract's current version in the order declared (`MemberNameLists`; a local contract's variant is `contracts.LocalVariant`, and its keyed and queries members are not listed), for a helper that fills an implementation from another object's members. An unknown variant is the error `<contract>: no variant "<variant>"`. The vendored TypeScript chord of the page and plugin clients carries Pi's `memberNames` and the exported types `Method`, `LiteralsSchema` and `HostKeyed` (Pi 5f89cc0a7df6).
- Follows Pi e56d35ce5ece: GPT-6.2 Astra (`gpt-6.2-astra`) and GPT-6.2 Sol (`gpt-6.2-sol`) join the `openai`, `azure` and `openai-codex` providers, with Pi's official pricing (Astra: $8 input, $0.40 cached input, $10 cache writes, $40 output; Sol: $2, $0.10, $2.50, $10; long-context tier above 272k), tool search, additional tools and mid-conversation effort changes. Both reject reasoning effort `none` and `minimal`, so `off` is unavailable for them. Azure serves them with a 1.05M context window; Codex uses its 272k default.
- A frontend member can now turn the mouse wheel over an extension's overlay or dock view with `Env.Wheel(frontend.Wheel{Node, Row, Column, ViewPath, Delta})`, the wheel counterpart of `Env.Click`. PiG hands the extension's component one wheel event at that cell with `Delta` as its `wheelDelta` (negative up), as Pi's fullscreen renderer offers a terminal wheel report to the component under the pointer first. It does nothing for a node that is not an extension view, a cell outside it, a `Delta` of 0, or outside fullscreen mode.
- Go extensions can now use the `AgentSession` members of Pi that a child session from `ctx.CreateAgentSession` lacked: the reads (`IsIdle`, `IsStreaming`, `IsCompacting`, `CurrentSessionID`, `CurrentSessionFile`, `SessionName`, `CurrentModel`, `CurrentThinkingLevel`, `CurrentSystemPrompt`, `SteeringMode`, `GetAllTools`, `GetContextUsage`, `GetSessionStats`, `GetLastAssistantText` and the rest), the changes (`SetThinkingLevel`, `SetScopedModels`, `SetActiveToolsByName`, `SetSteeringMode`, `SetAutoCompactionEnabled`, `SetSessionName`, `ClearQueue`, `ExportToJsonl` and the aborts) and the awaited members, the ones Pi declares `async` (`WaitForIdle`, `SetModel`, `CycleModel`, `Reload`, `Compact`, `NavigateTree`, `ExecuteBash`, `SendUserMessage`, `SendCustomMessage`, `SummarizeForBugReport`, `ExportToHTML`). Each one runs on the host's session over two new calls, `childSession.op` and `childSession.opAsync`, so a value is what the session holds at the call. `pi-agent-core`'s `Agent`, `AgentSession.agent` and the session graph handles of a child (`extensionRunner`, `settingsManager`, `resourceLoader`, `modelRuntime`) stay open and are listed in `test/parity/sdk-exports.toml`.
- RPC mode carries plugin views to a client outside the process (D614 wire carrier). A client attaches with `ui_view_attach`, is sent every mount as numbered `ui_view` snapshots, raises intents with `ui_view_intent` and cancels them by request id, reports what it could not draw with `ui_view_report`, and resyncs after a `ui_view_gap`. It works on stdin and stdout and on a `--listen` connection, and a failed carrier command carries a closed `code` beside the error text. A client that sends none of the seven `ui_view_*` commands sees no change. `docs/ui-view-carrier.md` is the page for client authors, with one transcript per message under `internal/viewcarrier/testdata/transcripts`.
- `examples/ui-view-web` is a reference web client for plugin views: a static page that draws mounts, applies their a11y and focus records and raises intents, and a bridge program (Node, standard library only) that relays RPC mode's lines to the page. Pig itself has no web server.
- Plugin UI mounts carry more, in the Go, Node, Python, Rust and Lisp SDKs alike (D614 amendment). A client states `claims`, and a mount offers up to 8 `alternatives`, each with a predicate over the claims; the host sends every client the first alternative that holds for it. A view can carry a `drawing` (a scene of vector shapes, or a pixel grid over an image) whose regions raise declared intents, and `a11y` and `focus` records that name view nodes by id. `finishView` takes a result, which the reply and `viewState` return. The new `viewDiagnostics` returns the notices of a mount: what the host rejected or ended and what a client could not draw. Every member is optional, closed and bounded, and none carries a version. One conformance row, `TestConformance_UIViewExtras`, runs the same probe against every SDK.
- A host can attach more than one client to the plugin UI registry. Each client holds an attachment with numbered full-snapshot deliveries, a gap and resync rule, and its own choice of alternative; `state.uiAbilities` is then the merge of the clients. Every delivery carries an RFC 8785 canonical SHA-256 digest of its content. `docs/extension-api-parity.md` states the ordering, cancellation and error rules.
- Extensions mount views in the client (D614): `ui.view.mount`, `update`, `hide`, `show`, `finish`, `remove` and `state`, answered by one `ui.view.intent` handler, in the Go, Node, Python, Rust and Lisp SDKs. A mount names a slot, a kit view, the intents its nodes may raise (a closed argument and answer shape, an optional timeout and cancel) and bounded images. The host replicates what the client draws as `state.uiAbilities`; an update that carries a stale epoch or revision is refused. One conformance row, `TestConformance_UIViewMounts`, runs the same seven cases against every SDK. <!-- fix: 633aaa054b -->
- Two CI guards protect the plugin UI work. `check-public-hygiene.py` rejects another organization's name, an event label, employer names outside copyright headers and listed person names in the UI paths. `make gui-import-guard` fails when chord imports a plugin UI package, so the dependency stays one-way. The same guard rejects any Wails import or module requirement: the plugin UI contract is host-agnostic, and hosts (TUI, web, MyGo, ACP, third-party) connect through adapters.
- `examples/ui-view-web`: `node bridge.mjs --connect <socket, or the directory it is in>` makes every page a client of the view endpoint of a running interactive session (Piglet keys `viewClient: terminal` and `viewEndpoint: socket`) instead of starting a pig for the page. The page and the terminal then draw the same mounts, and an intent raised in one is redrawn in both. The page has no prompt in this mode, keeps its connection across `/reload`, and attaches to the session that follows a new, resumed, forked or switched one.
- The bridge of the reference web client of plugin views (`examples/ui-view-web/bridge.mjs`) takes `--theme <directory>`: the directory's `theme.css` is linked from the page and its `.css`, `.svg`, `.png`, `.woff2` and `.json` files are served under `/theme/`. A theme sets the colours the page draws a view's theme tokens with, and the page's type and frame. Without `--theme` the page is unchanged.
- Piglet Binaries: `build.fusedReload: source` lets you develop a fused Go member against its Binary. The build records a digest of each fused member's source; when you start the Binary with that source under the member's name (`-e ./member`) and the source has changed, the start and `/reload` run the member as an ordinary subprocess extension built from the source, so an edit is picked up as it is for any source extension. The fused copy is stopped, the member keeps its name and its place in handler order, and it stays a subprocess until `pig piglet build` fuses the edited source. The first start or reload after an edit pays the member's Go build (about a third of a second for a small extension); later ones use the build cache. Without a Go toolchain the fused copy runs and one warning says so. Without the key a Binary behaves as before: it runs the compiled copy and ignores the edit. See "Editing a fused member's source" in the Piglet Binaries guide.
- A Go program that embeds PiG can read part of a long session branch. `SessionManager.BranchRefs` returns the entries `GetBranch` returns, in the same order, as small values with no entry body read, and `SessionManager.ReadEntries(ctx, ids)` reads only the entries it is given, in one batch, and returns an error and no entries for an unknown id, a record that cannot be read back (`coding.RecordChangedError`) or a done context. (issue #451, D655)
- Lisp extensions can now use the `AgentSession` members of Pi that a child session from `ctx-create-agent-session` lacked: the reads (`agent-session-idle-p`, `-streaming-p`, `-compacting-p`, `-current-session-id`, `-current-session-file`, `-current-model`, `-current-thinking-level`, `-current-system-prompt`, `-session-name`, `-steering-mode`, `-get-all-tools`, `-get-context-usage`, `-get-session-stats`, `-get-last-assistant-text` and the rest), the changes (`-set-thinking-level`, `-set-scoped-models`, `-set-active-tools-by-name`, `-set-steering-mode`, `-set-auto-compaction-enabled`, `-set-session-name`, `-clear-queue`, `-export-to-jsonl` and the aborts) and the awaited members, the ones Pi declares `async` (`-wait-for-idle`, `-set-model`, `-cycle-model`, `-reload`, `-compact`, `-navigate-tree`, `-execute-bash`, `-send-user-message`, `-send-custom-message`, `-export-to-html`, `-summarize-for-bug-report`). Each reads or changes the session the host owns; a blocked awaited member never holds a later call, and a cancelled `:ctx` runs Pi's abort for `-compact`, `-navigate-tree` and `-execute-bash`.
- `mcp.PipeTransport`, the MCP stdio transport over a program the caller started (`env.RemoteProcess` is one as it is); `mcp/oauth` sign-in in two halves (`StartMcpSignIn`, `CompleteMcpSignIn`, `ListenForLoopbackSignIn`, `WaitForLoopbackSignIn`, `CreateMcpAuthProvider`) with a refresh that uses the application's redirect URI and a sign-in that can be cancelled while it waits for another process's refresh lock; and the shared `mcp.CreateMcpToolName`, `McpNamespace`, `NormalizeMcpInputSchema`, `LimitMcpContent` and `ValidateMcpServerConfig`. <!-- feat: 5cd76cc454 c407e0ca23 22934263b9 -->
- The Node extension runtime's bundled `@earendil-works/pi-mcp` has `mcpServerSummary`, as Pi's, and the bundled coding agent's `mcp_servers` section reads it: a server whose instructions start with a blank line shows its first line with text. An extension cannot import `pi-mcp`, so no extension API changes.
- `mcp.McpServerSummary(description, instructions)` is a server's one-line summary for the system prompt, as Pi's `mcpServerSummary` of `@earendil-works/pi-mcp`: the first line of the configured description, else of the instructions the server sent in `initialize`. The `mcp_servers` section of the system prompt uses it, so a server whose instructions start with a blank line now shows the first line with text instead of no summary.
- Mermaid diagrams render through a port of lovely-mermaid 0.3.3 (Pi aceb1bd1): pie, mindmap, timeline and gitGraph diagrams, frontmatter titles, `@{}` node shapes, `classDef`/`:::class` styles applied over the theme, composite states, sequence activations, ER and class cardinalities, and `click`/`link` hyperlinks that open only on node text when the terminal supports hyperlinks. <!-- feat: 082b6fd9c9 -->
- Mermaid diagrams stay source in custom messages and changelogs (Pi eebd5d90, #11756).
- Interactive mode now shows a transcript notice when OpenAI drops replayed reasoning items from a request (such as `prefix_mismatch` after compaction on GPT-6.2) when `showCacheMissNotices` is enabled and more items are dropped than in the previous response; both Anthropic and OpenAI drop notices now list the reasons, and the OpenAI Responses, Azure OpenAI Responses, and OpenAI Codex providers record non-`turn_boundary` removals as `openai_input_transformations` assistant message diagnostics.
- `pig-bolt` compiles extensions that find files next to their own module: a file that names its own location (`import.meta.url`, `import.meta.dirname`, `__dirname`, `__filename`, `require.resolve`, `import.meta.resolve`, a computed `require()` or `import()`) is compiled from a copy in which those expressions give the installed file's location, as Pi-Bolt's own `pi-bolt compile` does, so the extension reads its skills, locales and data from where it is installed. `@juicesharp/rpiv-todo` and `pi-mcp-adapter` compile in and register identically on Node, Bun and the compiled host. Only `import.meta` used as a value (`const m = import.meta`) in a file that also reads files or starts processes stays refused, and the set runs on Bun.
- Python extensions can now use the `AgentSession` members of Pi that a child session from `ctx.create_agent_session` lacked: the reads (`is_idle`, `is_streaming`, `is_compacting`, `current_session_id`, `current_session_file`, `session_name`, `current_model`, `current_thinking_level`, `current_system_prompt`, `steering_mode`, `get_all_tools()`, `get_context_usage()`, `get_session_stats()`, `get_last_assistant_text()` and the rest, Pi's getters as properties), the changes (`set_thinking_level`, `set_scoped_models`, `set_active_tools_by_name`, `set_steering_mode`, `set_auto_compaction_enabled`, `set_session_name`, `clear_queue`, `export_to_jsonl` and the aborts) and the awaited members, the ones Pi declares `async` (`wait_for_idle`, `set_model`, `cycle_model`, `reload`, `compact`, `navigate_tree`, `execute_bash`, `send_user_message`, `send_custom_message`, `summarize_for_bug_report`, `export_to_html`). Each one runs on the session the host owns, so it returns what the session holds now; a blocked `compact`, `navigate_tree` or `execute_bash` is aborted by `abort_compaction`, `abort_branch_summary` or `abort_bash` from another thread.
- The Go, Rust, Python and Lisp SDKs serve TypeBox's `Value.Check` and `Value.Errors` (Go `sdk.Value.Check` and `Errors`, Rust `pig_sdk::value::Value::check` and `errors`, Python `pig_sdk.Value.check` and `errors`, Lisp `value-check` and `value-errors`), so an extension tool can check the constraints of its `Type.Refine` refinements in `execute()`, where Pi 1.5.2 asks authors to check them, as a Node extension does with `Value` from `typebox/value`. The refinements run in the extension, in TypeBox's order (a node's refinements after its other keywords; `Check` stops at the first failure, `Errors` words each failure with the refinement's message), checked against typebox 1.3.27 itself. Tool arguments are still not refined, as in Pi. Only `Check` and `Errors` are served, not the other members of `Value` (D226).
- Each release now publishes `pig-acp-<version>-<os>-<arch>` archives (`.tar.gz`, `.zip` on Windows) for linux, darwin and windows on amd64 and arm64, with the `pig` of the same release beside `pig-acp`. They carry the same SBOMs, scan, checksums (in the release `SHA256SUMS`), build-provenance attestation and Sigstore bundle as the pig archives, and are smoke-tested through ACP on linux/amd64, darwin/arm64 and windows/amd64 before the draft release is created. `pig-acp` is built from the `@pi-in-go/pigpen-acp` version pinned in `automation/release/pig-acp.lock` (size and sha512 checked).
- `pig --mode rpc --listen <path>` serves one Pi RPC session per connection on a Unix socket, in one process, so an additional session costs a few MB instead of a process of its own. Every session has its own extension processes, so no extension process, and none of its module-level state, is shared between sessions (extensions compiled into the host program run in the server process in both modes). `--listen-share-extensions` makes the sessions share the extension processes, which cuts the cost of a session that loads extensions further; module-level state (Node module variables, `process.env`, `globalThis`, timers; Go, Rust, Python and Lisp package variables) is then shared between the sessions that share a process, and the flag's help line says so (D232). The socket is private to you: mode 0600 on Unix, and on Windows PiG refuses to serve a socket whose directory lets other users reach it. Nobody is authenticated beyond that, so keep the socket in a directory only you can write. Contributed by @balcsida (#404).
- Rust extensions can now use the `AgentSession` members of Pi that a child session from `ctx.create_agent_session` lacked: the reads (`is_idle`, `is_streaming`, `is_compacting`, `current_session_id`, `current_session_file`, `session_name`, `current_model`, `current_thinking_level`, `current_system_prompt`, `steering_mode`, `get_all_tools`, `get_context_usage`, `get_session_stats`, `get_last_assistant_text` and the rest), the changes (`set_thinking_level`, `set_scoped_models`, `set_active_tools_by_name`, `set_steering_mode`, `set_auto_compaction_enabled`, `set_session_name`, `clear_queue`, `export_to_jsonl` and the aborts) and the awaited members, the ones Pi declares `async` (`wait_for_idle`, `set_model`, `cycle_model`, `reload`, `compact`, `navigate_tree`, `execute_bash`, `send_user_message`, `send_custom_message`, `summarize_for_bug_report`, `export_to_html`). Each one runs on the host's session over `childSession.op` and `childSession.opAsync`, so it returns what the session holds now. A member Pi awaits blocks until it settles; call an abort from another thread to cancel it.
- `schema.BigInt(options...)` builds `{"type":"bigint"}`; a bigint is a `*big.Int` and `schema.Undefined` is `undefined`, for the `bigint` and `undefined` types and the number keywords of either kind. Follows Pi main af79b0c3d.
- `schema.Validate` returns the value or its errors without coercing, on every validator; `schema.Recursive(id, build)` builds a schema that contains itself; `schema.Equal(a, b)` is the JSON equality `const`, `enum` and `uniqueItems` use; `schema.Unsafe(schema...)` returns the schema it is given, or `{}`, as Pi's `unsafe()` does. Follows Pi main af79b0c3d (the `bigint` and `undefined` types and `BigInt` are in their own entry).
- An opt-in screen writer (D624): with `terminal.screenWriter` set to `"writer"` in the global settings file, or `PIG_TUI_SCREEN_WRITER=writer`, fullscreen mode sends the terminal only what a frame changes on the screen, through a screen writer under the terminal's write. Pi sends every row a frame writes, and so does PiG in 0.8.0 when the writer is not selected. With the writer on, a row that already shows what the frame writes is not written; a row whose cells change is written in place, from its first cell through its last changed one, where that leaves the terminal the line the frame's own bytes leave it, and whole otherwise (a row as wide as the screen that changes through its last cell is written whole); a frame that changes nothing is not written; the rows the frames rewrote and the writer did not write whole are written whole once 250 ms pass without a frame. Frames are translated only while autowrap is known to be off, and regular mode, print, JSON and RPC mode are sent the bytes as they are written. In a replay of the recorded streams at 160 by 48 the writer sends 89.2 % of the bytes of a long streamed answer and 19.8 % of those of a file write. A raw capture of the output (`script`, `tmux pipe-pane`) holds other bytes than Pi's for the same frames. The lines tmux 3.4 and 3.6 keep are those of Pi's bytes (51 cases, asked of tmux itself by the tests). `PIG_TUI_SCREEN_WRITER=pi` sends the terminal Pi's bytes whatever the setting says; `PIG_TUI_SCREEN_WRITER_LOG=path` records every write as it came and as it was sent.
- `pig extension init <path> --lang node` scaffolds a TypeScript extension (`package.json` and an `index.ts` default-export factory with a ping tool, a command and a status) like the Go, Python, Rust and Lisp scaffolds. `--isolated` is refused for Node, which has no SDK for an executable script to speak the wire with.
- A tool renderer in the Go, Rust, Python and Lisp SDKs receives `ToolRenderContext.lastComponent` (`LastComponent`, `last_component`, `tool-render-context-last-component`): what the renderer of the same phase of the same card returned on its previous run (its lines, or its kit view), nil on the first run and after a run that failed, as Pi's `lastComponent` is the component the renderer returned before. The Node runtime already passed Pi's component. The conformance suite binds its `render_probe` rows to the value in every SDK.
- A Go extension handler can read the key order of an event's objects with `Context.ObjectKeys(object)`, as a Pi handler reads `Object.keys`: the order the host wrote them. The Node, Rust, Python and Lisp SDKs already iterate objects in that order and need no call. (D273)
- A Provider object an extension registers (`pi.registerProvider(provider)` in TypeScript, `Provider.RefreshModelsAuth` in Go, `refresh_models_auth` in Python and Rust, `provider-refresh-models-auth` in Lisp) now carries Pi's `refreshModelsAuth`. With `"configured"`, a catalog refresh of that provider runs its network phase without a credential and no longer refreshes an expired OAuth login first, so a stale login (`invalid_grant`) no longer fails the catalog refresh. An extension that reads another extension's Provider (`getRegisteredNativeProvider`) sees its `refreshModelsAuth` in every SDK and in Node.
- A provider config's `oauth.modifyModels`, `refreshModels` and `oauth.usesCallbackServer` now work from Go, Rust, Python, Lisp and Node extensions, as in Pi 1.5.2. `modifyModels` runs in the extension with the provider's chat models and the stored OAuth credential (Go `OAuthProvider.ModifyModels`, Rust `modify_models`, Python `modify_models`, Lisp `:modify-models`) and its error is the model listing's error. `refreshModels` runs in the extension with Pi's refresh context and its `context.publish({persist, update})` calls reach the host's refresh (Go `ProviderConfig["refreshModels"]` as `sdk.ProviderRefreshModelsFunc`, Rust `ProviderOperations::refresh_models`, Python `config["refreshModels"]`, Lisp the `"refreshModels"` config key). `usesCallbackServer` is forwarded to the registered config and, as in Pi, changes nothing. Before, the host dropped all three. <!-- feat: sdkprovidergaps -->
- Extension SDKs: an explicit `null` for an optional member of a session entry. Node `null`; Go `json.RawMessage("null")`, and `SendMessageOptions.Details` for a message's details; Python `pig_sdk.NULL`; Rust `Context::append_entry_opt` and `Context::send_message_with_details` with `Some(Value::Null)`; Lisp `:null`. The empty value of each language (`nil`, `None`, `Value::Null`, `NIL`) leaves the member out, as before.
- Extension SDKs: `setLabel` without a label and with `null`. Node `pi.setLabel(id)` and `pi.setLabel(id, null)`; Go `Context.SetLabelValue` with `nil` and `json.RawMessage("null")`; Python `set_label(entry_id)` and `pig_sdk.NULL`; Rust `Context::set_label_opt` with `None` and `Some(Value::Null)`; Lisp `ctx-set-label` without a label and with `:null`.
- Rust SDK: `SetupSessionManager::append_custom_entry_opt` and `append_custom_message_entry_opt` write an explicit `null` for the `data` and the `details` of a setup session entry.
- Each release now publishes PiG Standard as its own artifact: `pig-standard-<version>-<os>-<arch>` archives (`.tar.gz`, `.zip` on Windows) for linux, darwin and windows on amd64 and arm64, separate from the Stock `pig-<version>-<os>-<arch>` archives. Each holds the Piglet Binary that `pig piglet build piglets/standard/pig-standard.yaml --format binary` builds on a native runner for its target. They carry their own SBOMs, vulnerability scan, checksums (in the release `SHA256SUMS`), build-provenance attestation and Sigstore bundle. A smoke run on every target extracts the archive and starts the Binary offline, and requires `pig-standard version` to report the release version, `pig-standard verify --json` to report that version as its Piglet release, and `pig-standard status` to name `pig-standard` as the active Piglet. Termux has no PiG Standard archive. The Binary reports `build: dev`, so each archive also ships its Piglet build record (`-build-record.json`) with the source commit it was built from. `make set-version` now writes the exact release version, not a `-dev` one, into `piglets/standard/pig-standard.yaml`, so a release-prepared tree builds Standard.
- A `ctx.ui.custom` component is told when the host's screen is invalidated (a theme change, a cell-size report, a change of image support) in every SDK, as Pi calls a component's `invalidate()`: Go `Invalidate()`, Python `invalidate()`, Rust `RemoteComponent::invalidate` / `ViewComponent::invalidate`, Lisp the `:invalidate` function of `make-custom-component`, beside Node's `invalidate()`. The method is optional; the component is drawn again either way, and it sees the new theme when the method runs.
- The terminal draws the views extensions mount (`ui.view`, D614) when the active Piglet sets `viewClient: terminal`; PiG Standard sets it. Views mounted in `widget-above` and `widget-below` appear above and below the editor and `panel` views directly above it. F6 moves the focus to a panel, Escape returns it to the editor, and choosing a list item, changing a setting, submitting an input or clicking a mouse region raises the intent the extension bound to that node. Stock PiG attaches no view client: a mount still fails with `unsupported`.
- Piglet manifest key `viewClient` (`none` or `terminal`), inherited down an `extends` chain and replaced by naming it.
- The terminal view client states its size to extensions as claims (`size.columns`, and `size.rows` for each slot), so an extension can send an alternative that fits.
- In the terminal, the keys an extension binds on a view work while that view holds the focus: F6 enters the view, even when nothing in it takes keys, and a bound key the focused list or input does not use raises the extension's intent with the binding's argument. A binding is never global, and one row under the focused view names the bound keys that have a name. Gestures and keys bound on a widget view are not offered in the terminal; the extension is told once.
- In the terminal, Escape in a dialog whose extension declares a `dismiss` intent asks the extension to close it: the intent is raised with `{}`, and the dialog closes when the extension hides or ends its view. Escape asks once: a second Escape in a dialog that is still open returns the keys to the editor and folds the dialog into its row above the editor, as Escape does in a dialog without a `dismiss` intent, so Escape reaches the editor and interrupts within three presses, whatever the extension does.
- In the terminal, a view an extension mounts in the `dialog` slot is drawn in a titled frame centred over the screen, eight tenths of the terminal's columns and rows, with the keyboard: its list, its input and the keys it binds answer, and the panels and the editor under it keep their state. Only the extension closes a dialog. Several dialogs are stacked, the last shown on top. A frame is on the screen only while a dialog has the keyboard, so it never covers what you type: Escape returns the keys to the editor and folds the dialogs into one row above it (`<title>: F6 to enter`), F6 opens them again, and a dialog shown while you type in the editor waits on that row. The terminal states a dialog's size to extensions as the claims `size.columns` and `size.rows` of the slot.
- An extension lets the user close a dialog or an overlay it mounted: one intent of a mount may be declared `dismiss`. When the user dismisses the mount, a client raises that intent with `{}`, and the extension's handler closes the view. It names no node and its argument accepts `{}`; the host answers `invalid` otherwise, and for a second such intent. Without one, Escape leaves the mount and it stays open until the extension closes it. In a slot that is neither `dialog` nor `overlay` the member has no effect.
- The member is in the Go, Node, Python, Rust and Lisp SDKs with the same name and checks (`Dismiss`, `dismiss`, `:dismiss`). One conformance row proves it in every SDK: the host holds the mark on the intent the extension named, and raising the intent reaches the extension's handler.
- Piglet manifest key `viewEndpoint` (`none` or `socket`). With `socket`, an interactive session serves the `ui_view` carrier on a Unix socket in the agent directory (`view-endpoint/<pid>.sock`), so a view client outside the process, such as the reference web client, attaches to the same session as the terminal: both show the same mounts, and an intent raised in one is redrawn in both. Only the same user can connect, and a client can draw views and raise their intents and nothing else. Stock PiG and PiG Standard serve no socket.
- A view that an extension mounts can show a photograph in the terminal. The terminal view client draws the `image` node of a mount (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP) in a panel. In kitty and Ghostty it is a real image that is sent to the terminal once and then moves, scrolls and disappears with the view. In other terminals with the Kitty graphics protocol and in iTerm2 it is an inline image. In a terminal without an image protocol, tmux included, it is drawn with half-block characters in the terminal's colours; an image that cannot be decoded is one line of text that names it. The image is prepared in the background, so the interface stays responsive while a large photograph loads. `maxWidthCells` and `maxHeightCells` size it, and it is never taller than its slot.
- A mounted view can carry a `title` (at most 64 bytes on one line), which a client uses as the label of its tab or of its row in a list of views. It is part of the content, so an update replaces it.
- An extension lets the user open a view it hid: one intent of a mount may be declared `whenHidden`, and it is the only intent a hidden mount takes. A client lists such a mount, and choosing it raises the intent; the extension's handler shows the view.
- A focus record can ask for the keyboard on an update (`request: "update"`) as well as at mount. The client decides; when it does not give the focus the extension reads an `unfocused` notice from `ui.view.diagnostics`.
- The three members are in the Go, Node, Python, Rust and Lisp SDKs with the same names and checks. A tool an extension registers can mount, show and focus its view; one conformance row proves it in every SDK.
- In the terminal, the views extensions mount in `panel` are tabs: one row lists them by title, the front tab is drawn, and F6 walks from tab to tab and back to the editor. A view its extension hid is listed too when the extension lets the user open it; Enter on it opens it.
- A view an extension shows comes to the front when you are in the editor. While you work in another view its tab is marked with `*` instead, and nothing moves under your hands.
- Extensions are told when a viewer arrives, changes or leaves (D614): `pi.onViewAbilities((abilities, ctx) => ...)`, Go `Extension.OnViewAbilities`, Python `ext.on_view_abilities`, Rust `Extension::on_view_abilities`, Lisp `on-view-abilities`. The handler runs when the first client attaches, when the abilities change and when the last client leaves, and a mount it makes succeeds, so a client that attaches to an idle session is shown the extension's views without a prompt. With several clients attached the value is the merge of their abilities.
- `chordview.Views.Follow` mounts the chord panels when a client arrives.
- An extension binds keys and gestures to the intents of a view it mounts: `bindings [{key | gesture, intent, arg?, name?}]` on `ui.view.mount` and `ui.view.update`, in the Go, Node, Python, Rust and Lisp SDKs (at most 32). A key is a key id as `registerShortcut` writes it (`d`, `shift+left`, `ctrl+shift+p`); a gesture is `swipe-left`, `swipe-right`, `swipe-up` or `swipe-down`. A binding raises an intent that names no node, with a constant argument, and several bindings may raise one intent with different arguments. A binding is never global: a client fires it only while the mount holds the focus and the focused node did not take the key. The host refuses a key bound twice and the reserved keys (`escape`, `tab`, `f6`, and `ctrl` with `c`, `d` or `z`) with `invalid`, and sends every client the bindings as part of the content its digest covers. A client that cannot honour a binding reports it, and the extension reads the notice with `ui.view.diagnostics`. The reference web client and the terminal client do not fire bindings yet. One conformance row, `TestConformance_UIViewBindings`, runs in every SDK and realization.
- Plugin views: a `grid` node, a calendar-style grid of equal columns whose cells are data (a value, a label, a today mark, a dim flag, a colour and up to eight coloured chips with a count of events left out), so a month with three chips a day is three nodes instead of several hundred. The terminal draws it in equal columns cut by terminal cells, fits the chip lines to its slot, moves a cursor with the arrow keys, Home and End, and raises the node's intent with the cell's value on Enter, Space or a click. The host refuses a grid with a member the record lacks or one past a bound with code `invalid`. The other SDKs' builders and the web client's drawing follow.
- Plugin views: every SDK builds the `grid` node. Go `kit.Grid`, Rust `kit::Grid`, Python `kit.Grid` and Lisp `kit-grid`, each with its cell and chip records, and in Node the plain object, typed by `PiGViewGrid`, `PiGViewGridCell` and `PiGViewGridChip`. A member you do not set is not sent, and the host stays the one validator: a grid one past a bound, with an unknown mark or with a member the record lacks fails with code `invalid` in every SDK.
- The reference web client of plugin views (`examples/ui-view-web`) lets the user open a view its extension hid: a hidden mount that declares a `whenHidden` intent is a button with the mount's title in a list above the prompt, and choosing it raises that intent with `{}`. Before, the page did not offer a hidden mount.
- The reference web client raises the `dismiss` intent of a dialog or overlay mount with `{}` when the user presses Escape in it or the browser asks to close the dialog. The page still closes no mount itself, and a mount that declares no such intent stays as it is.
- The reference web client has a colour for every colour token of Pi's theme schema: 56 `--pig-<token>` properties, each set from the page's neutral tokens, so a text or a shape of a drawing coloured `mdLink` or `mdHeading` is drawn in the accent or the text colour.

### Changed

- A request to Anthropic or an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint allocates fewer objects when it is encoded: the encoder state that carried each large string through the request is kept from one request to the next instead of being built again, and dropped when a request fails or the session releases its request caches. The body is the same bytes.
