- SDK: `CreateAgentSessionServicesOptions.ModelRuntimeSignal` bounds only the creation of the model runtime, as Pi's `modelRuntimeSignal` does. A resource reload still running when the signal fired made `CreateAgentSessionServices` fail, and the model refresh after the extensions loaded was skipped; both now run to their end. <!-- fix: 3cb88affbc991262f1b745aa2109a7e5cc49be53 -->
- Startup prompts (project trust, the missing-directory choice, startup text input) keep reading the terminal until the prompt has been cleared and 25 ms have passed, as Pi does. The terminal was handed back to line mode before the prompt was cleared, so keys typed in that moment could be echoed onto the screen. <!-- fix: 3cb88affbc991262f1b745aa2109a7e5cc49be53 -->
- A new file that pig writes (`settings.json`, `trust.json`, `keybindings.json`, the MCP config, the credential files) now gets the mode its writer asks for with your umask taken out, as in Pi. The replacing write gave it exactly the requested mode: an MCP config could be created `rw-rw-rw-` under umask 022, and a settings, trust or keybindings file `rw-r--r--` under umask 077. `settings.json`, `trust.json` and `keybindings.json` now ask for Pi's mode (0666 before the umask). A file that exists keeps its mode. <!-- fix: 24de75207481, 65de6ddd866a --> <!-- cause: the helper chmodded the new temporary file to the requested mode, which no umask touches, and no test crossed the requested mode with the umask -->
- Rewriting a file in a directory that has a default ACL no longer gives it an access ACL it did not have: the replacement kept the entries it inherited from the directory, so a user named only by the directory could read a `0640` file that never granted it. <!-- fix: 5e106cc28d3a --> <!-- cause: the helper copied the attributes the replaced file has and never removed what the new file inherited, and no test put a default ACL on the directory -->
- A write whose directory entry could not be flushed (an I/O error) now fails instead of reporting success; a file system that has no directory flush is still accepted. A symbolic link to a file that does not exist is followed and the file is created, as Pi does, where the link used to be replaced by a regular file; a link that goes round in a circle or names a missing directory fails as Pi's write does. <!-- fix: 3e06d84430e8, 085dad13a226 --> <!-- cause: the directory flush answered a value its only caller dropped, and the link was resolved with filepath.EvalSymlinks alone, which has no answer for a missing target -->
- Reading an extended attribute that is set between the size query and the read no longer panics, and on Windows a failed replacement leaves the existing file untouched instead of deleting it. <!-- fix: a1c68e2bebdb, 58e14d8f3f1a --> <!-- cause: the read retried on ERANGE only, which a zero-length buffer never gets, and the Windows replacement previously used ReplaceFileW without a backup before switching to single-call MoveFileExW -->
- A new file that pig writes (`settings.json`, `trust.json`, `keybindings.json`, the MCP config, the credential files) now gets the mode its writer asks for with your umask taken out, as in Pi. The replacing write gave it exactly the requested mode: an MCP config could be created `rw-rw-rw-` under umask 022, and a settings, trust or keybindings file `rw-r--r--` under umask 077. `settings.json`, `trust.json` and `keybindings.json` now ask for Pi's mode (0666 before the umask). A file that exists keeps its mode. <!-- fix: 9b91740704, c7b4ed4b93 --> <!-- cause: the helper chmodded the new temporary file to the requested mode, which no umask touches, and no test crossed the requested mode with the umask -->
- Rewriting a file in a directory that has a default ACL no longer gives it an access ACL it did not have: the replacement kept the entries it inherited from the directory, so a user named only by the directory could read a `0640` file that never granted it. <!-- fix: 41120c0e67 --> <!-- cause: the helper copied the attributes the replaced file has and never removed what the new file inherited, and no test put a default ACL on the directory -->
- A write whose directory entry could not be flushed (an I/O error) now fails instead of reporting success; a file system that has no directory flush is still accepted. A symbolic link to a file that does not exist is followed and the file is created, as Pi does, where the link used to be replaced by a regular file; a link that goes round in a circle or names a missing directory fails as Pi's write does. <!-- fix: 541820ef23, 4dfa69b67e --> <!-- cause: the directory flush answered a value its only caller dropped, and the link was resolved with filepath.EvalSymlinks alone, which has no answer for a missing target -->
- Reading an extended attribute that is set between the size query and the read no longer panics, and on Windows a failed replacement leaves the existing file untouched instead of deleting it. <!-- fix: ee5045c2d1, ea2e967070 --> <!-- cause: the read retried on ERANGE only, which a zero-length buffer never gets, and the Windows replacement previously used ReplaceFileW without a backup before switching to single-call MoveFileExW -->
- On Windows, saving `auth.json`, the settings, trust, keybindings and MCP files, or any other file pig writes through a temporary file, now leaves the whole security descriptor and user-settable file attributes (`HIDDEN`, `SYSTEM`, `NOT_CONTENT_INDEXED`; `ARCHIVE` stays set on rewritten content) of the file as they were, as Pi's in-place write does. The access (the DACL entries with their flags, and the protected flag) is carried onto the temporary file before anything is written to it and read back, then verified again before moving the temporary file over the target in one `MoveFileExW` call; a file system that cannot take the access gets the in-place write, as before (divergence D651). <!-- fix: 1f4ce560a8c2, 950803e7b7da --> <!-- cause: the helper previously relied on ReplaceFileW merging and copied only the DACL with its protected flag, and no test compared the whole descriptor before and after a write on Windows -->
- durable harness: `ConversationTranscript.LoadEarlier` and `FillGap` waited for good once an entry loader had panicked: the load that call ran stayed registered and never ended. A load whose loader does not return is now settled, as Pi's shared promise settles when its loader throws: the calls that share it fail with `ConversationTranscript: the entry loader panicked`, the next call loads again, and the panic still reaches the caller whose call ran the loader. <!-- fix: 7d34ee2c6c1528e96cb6abc9c7156da99cd216a1 -->
- env: closing a connection at the moment its daemon was being started left that daemon process unreaped, a zombie holding its pipes, until PiG exited. The start that finds the connection closed now waits for the daemon it has just signalled. <!-- fix: a3391bc58e0bed3079666cbb6665373cba45f0fe -->
- durable harness: closing a Harness on one goroutine while a commit was being published on another could start a scheduler pass after the close had waited for the scheduler's passes. The pass ran unjoined, and the close could panic with `sync: WaitGroup is reused before previous Wait has returned`. A pass now joins the scheduler when it is scheduled, so the close waits for it. <!-- fix: bc5d1adb08b7a87d64d5258a9f5df949d9374886 -->
- tui: after quick terminal resizes a subprocess extension could be left rendering for a width the terminal no longer had, and what it pushed for that width was not painted until the next resize. On the main screen and with a frontend, the resize callbacks ran on a goroutine each, so two resizes could reach the extension host out of order, or after the renderer had stopped. They now run one at a time, in render order, as they already did on the alternate screen: a size replaced while the listener is busy is skipped, the last one always arrives, and a stop discards what is pending. <!-- fix: f003f0a6d1cf6d8ed0c4b9ebaa359b9a48359ac1 -->
- Quitting while an OAuth token refresh is in flight no longer loses the new token. If pig exited after the token request went out but before the new token was written, `auth.json` kept the refresh token the provider had already spent and the next request failed with `invalid_grant`; an RPC client that stopped pig right after startup, while the background catalog refresh refreshed an expired login, hit this. Interactive, print, JSON and RPC mode now wait for a refresh that has started to be saved before the process exits, with no timeout beyond the 15 s refresh and the 30 s auth lock wait; a second signal exits at once in RPC and print mode. The wait comes before pig stops its extensions, and a refresh that has started (a subprocess extension provider's, in the catalog refresh or at request time, or the Radius gateway's) is no longer cut or discarded when its caller is cancelled, as Pi main does (D237). <!-- fix: 7febcec6be -->
- Two pig processes that reach the same `auth.json` through different paths, such as an agent directory whose `auth.json` is a symlink to a shared file, now take one lock instead of two, so they no longer refresh the same single-use OAuth token at the same time and fail with `invalid_grant`. The lock of `auth.json`, `models.json` and `mcp-auth.json` now follows symlinks to the real file, as Pi main does (D236), and resolves the path as Node's `fs.realpath` does: a `..` step cancels a directory that need not exist, and on Windows the case and 8.3 short names (`RUNNER~1`) of components that are not links stay as given, so a lock error names the path as Pi's does. <!-- fix: 1724c9e834, 72e19b38b8 -->
- Saving `auth.json` (or another state file pig replaces through a temporary file) when the path is not an ordinary file, for example a device such as `/dev/null` or a named pipe, no longer swaps that node for a regular file. pig writes such a target in place, as Pi does, so the bytes reach the device and a full-device error is reported; no temporary file is made for it. <!-- fix: cb4481fdbc --> <!-- cause: the shared writer treated every existing target as a regular file and replaced it by rename, which removed a device or pipe and left an ordinary file with the node's mode. -->
- Saving `auth.json` (or another state file pig replaces through a temporary file) when the path is not an ordinary file, for example a device such as `/dev/null` or a named pipe, no longer swaps that node for a regular file. pig writes such a target in place, as Pi does, so the bytes reach the device and a full-device error is reported; no temporary file is made for it. <!-- fix: f1f2471bd --> <!-- cause: the shared writer treated every existing target as a regular file and replaced it by rename, which removed a device or pipe and left an ordinary file with the node's mode. -->
- Text typed before the extensions are bound (for example while an extension's `session_start` handler is still running) no longer opens the slash-command or `@` file menu, and Tab no longer completes a path there; the editor gets its completion provider when the bind ends, as in Pi. An editor an extension installs from `session_start` is installed with no provider and gets the provider when the bind ends or, if the host had already built it, when the host installs the editor, as Pi's `setCustomEditorComponent` does. This has been so since 0.2.0. <!-- fix: d016fe9ce4, 104cf63578 --> <!-- cause: the editor was given its autocomplete provider when it was built, without checking that Pi installs it only after bindExtensions returns, so input read before the bind finished reached completion code Pi has not armed yet; and a remote editor built before the provider existed was installed by the host after the provider was built, a case where nothing handed it the provider -->
- ai: an Azure OpenAI Responses base URL that already carries the full Responses endpoint path with a query string (such as `https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/responses?api-version=2025-04-01-preview` or a gateway `.../responses?api-version=...`) now reaches the endpoint, as in Pi, instead of appending `/responses?api-version=...` onto the query string and failing the request. <!-- fix: ca83bfc373 --> <!-- cause: azureResponsesEndpoint.resolve built the URL by string concatenation (`strings.TrimRight(config.BaseURL, "/") + "/responses?api-version=" + url.QueryEscape(config.APIVersion)`) instead of the openai SDK's `client.buildURL("/responses")` with `defaultQuery: { "api-version": apiVersion }` --> <!-- tests: ai/azure_request_url_oracle_test.go::TestAzureResponsesRequestURLMatchesSDK ai/azure_request_url_test.go::TestAzureResponsesRequestURL -->
- Tests: the read barrier, which lets a fixture server write its next record only when the client is reading the socket again, counted bytes per client address. Linux gives one local port to live connections to different servers, so two parallel fixture servers could see the same client address; one of them then waited until its test's deadline, or wrote two records into one read. `TestRPC33AzureTickOrder` failed that way in about one run in a hundred, more often on a loaded machine. The barrier now counts per connection (client and server address). <!-- fix: 8b15be354a87d6daa1923f581af9613b43da8501 -->
- On macOS and the BSDs, a chord app's watch of its base code puts back the watch of a directory that was moved away and back (a base directory, or one holding a recorded file). The system's file watcher (kqueue) held the directory again for its own rename alone, so nothing made in it was reported and `base` never changed; the watcher now adds that directory again when an event names it, as Pi's FSEvents watch of a path follows the path. <!-- fix: 47e7748062 -->
- A resumed session takes the model its registry lists for the saved provider and id, with that listing's API, window and limits, instead of building it a second time from its name. <!-- fix: bc0594500 --> <!-- cause: restore followed the old BuildModel contract, which made a model from any provider and id, so it re-resolved what it had already resolved -->
- After `/new`, `/resume`, `/clone` or `/fork` in the interactive mode, the model selector, an extension's `setModel` and the post-login selection build the model from the new session's registry, not from the registry the program started with. Before, picking a model of a provider that the new session's extension registers gave a model with a context window of 0 and no reasoning: the footer showed `0.0%/0 (auto)` and the thinking level went to off. <!-- fix: b214a4c12 --> <!-- cause: the per-session bindings of a replacement were swapped one by one and the model builder was left out of the list --> <!-- tests: TestInteractiveModelAfterSessionReplacementKeepsRegisteredMetadata, TestInteractiveModelAfterSessionReplacementProviderShapes, TestInteractiveModelAfterNewAcrossSDKs, TestInteractiveExtensionSetModelAfterNewKeepsRegisteredMetadata, TestRPCSetModelAfterNewSessionKeepsRegisteredMetadata -->
- The bash tool no longer returns no output, with a footer like `[Showing lines 3-2 of 2]`, when a command's output ends in one line longer than about 100KB, such as a `grep` match in a minified file; it shows the end of that line, as Pi does (upstream #12092). <!-- fix: 1ad65fe04f2b54091a977a9f4c9f4760d9a649e8 -->
- Bedrock: with `HTTPS_PROXY` or `HTTP_PROXY` set, an AWS SSO / IAM Identity Center profile could not fetch role credentials (`GetRoleCredentials`) or refresh an `sso_session` token (`CreateToken`), and an `aws login` / `login_session` profile could not refresh its Signin token (`CreateOAuth2Token`), because those calls bypassed the proxy and went direct. Bedrock now routes SSO, SSO OIDC, and `login_session` Signin credential calls through the same proxy resolved for the Bedrock endpoint, alongside the Bedrock runtime and STS (`AssumeRole` / `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`) calls, while IMDS, container credentials, `credential_process`, bearer tokens, `AWS_BEDROCK_SKIP_AUTH`, and static environment keys keep their existing direct behavior. Affects v0.7.0. <!-- fix: 52310a47489a40458df54bd8b6ccd1fa191d4fa3, c014a03de29fae8feaa949e871ffbdfdc469cb9d --> <!-- cause: loadBedrockConfig passed a proxy-free HTTP client into awsconfig.LoadDefaultConfig and only overrode the STS client with runtimeHTTPClient, leaving SSO, SSO OIDC, and login_session Signin on the direct client (matching Pi before be269f57b1b707399edd86f5f718d1a907ffea8b / #12365) -->
- A second termination signal during print or JSON mode's shutdown now ends the process with the code of the signal that repeated (143 for SIGTERM, 129 for SIGHUP), as Pi's per-signal handler does. A SIGHUP that followed a SIGTERM could end with 143. <!-- fix: 62aaa5e7d9 -->
- Markdown rendering matches Pi for five more shapes of text. A paragraph whose last line is only spaces no longer gets an extra blank row under a default text color. An ordered list item with nothing after its delimiter (`2)`) renders as `2.` when list markers are preserved. In a quote narrower than three columns, lazy list lines followed by one blank line no longer add a blank row. A bare `-` under a list item's text is a setext underline (a heading) instead of a nested empty item, also while the text streams. A list item that starts with an empty line and is followed by a blank line ends there, and a bullet up to three spaces in after it is the next item. <!-- fix: e9e4fc5ff2, 93daca1d47 -->
- A task list item whose text starts with emphasis, a code span or a link (`- [ ] **bold** text`) no longer shows an empty styled span in front of it under a text color or style, and delimiters that open the item's text (`- [ ] **`code`**`) are parsed as emphasis like Pi does. <!-- fix: af56fab3a1 -->
- A list item at a marker indent of three spaces or more (`   - d`) followed by a line indented four spaces (`    - e`) continues the item's text with up to four spaces removed instead of rendering a code block, as Pi does. <!-- fix: af56fab3a1 -->
- Rendering Markdown at width 0 gives the rows Pi gives instead of padding them to one cell. <!-- fix: af56fab3a1 -->
- Markdown rendering matches Pi for more block shapes. A quote whose list takes lazy lines no longer swallows the quoted line after them, and an empty nested quote drops the lines after it as Pi does. Display math that starts a line after a paragraph line (up to three spaces in) clips the paragraph like Pi, and a paragraph ended by a pipe line and a dash line merges with the next one when display math follows later in the text. Nested lists followed by blank lines or trailing spaces inside a list item keep their empty row, a list item's text starts a setext heading at any line, lazy lines of a quote are lexed apart from the quoted lines before them (HTML blocks, tables, display math and setext headings no longer read across them), and an unclosed fence keeps a partial closing fence line when its text ends in a newline. <!-- fix: f238db7efe -->
- Markdown quotes, lists, paragraphs, tables and display math now lex exactly as Pi's marked lexer does: the block lexer is a port of `Lexer.blockTokens` with the `blockquote`, `list`, `paragraph` and `table` tokenizers and the display-math clipping of paragraphs. This closes every remaining difference from Pi that the random-document comparison found, among them a quote whose nested quote is empty and swallows the lines after it (`>>` then `b`), lazy lines after a quoted list, an item with an empty first line followed by indented content, a list followed by spaces and a blank line, a table delimiter row or display math on a lazy line, an indented line after a lazy line, a list item whose lazy line starts with an astral character, and a quote line that holds a carriage return. <!-- fix: b09867998c, b058711ea5, 1b82ede629 --> <!-- fix: 1b82ede629 -->
- Accepting an autocomplete suggestion after the cursor moved off the typed text (a word move, Home or End) cuts the line where Pi does when the text before the cursor holds non-ASCII characters, instead of a few bytes away, where it could split a character. <!-- fix: 532a0099a8 -->
- Typing a space or a letter such as `é` right after a slash command whose arguments have completions no longer opens the argument popup unless Pi opens it. Pi opens a closed popup only for `/` at the start of the message, for a trigger character, and for a letter, digit, `.`, `-`, `_` or CJK character in a slash command or trigger context. <!-- fix: 24b67ccb05, e790f48f58 -->
- Typing fast into an `@`, `#` or provider-trigger token, or while a slow autocomplete provider is still working, no longer loses the popup: a character that triggers nothing (a space, `é` or `/` after `@al`) leaves the pending request alone, and the request asks the provider about the text the editor holds when it starts, as Pi does, instead of asking nothing. <!-- fix: 74c3fde97e -->
- The `@` file search of a tui editor that has a file-search provider but no task owner (an embedder's; no pig surface is one) takes the text current when its debounce ends when the editor has an owner loop, as Pi does, so a space, `é` or `/` typed right after `@al` no longer loses the search; with no loop the search leaves its answer for the caller's goroutine to publish instead of writing the editor from its own. <!-- fix: a1be5452a3, f294c50ce3, 37a8d53c8c -->
- An extension autocomplete provider that watches its abort signal no longer sees it fire when the user types a character that triggers no request (a space, `é` or `/` after `@al`, `x` after Tab): as in Pi, the request in flight finishes and its answer is dropped, and only a new request or a cancel aborts it. <!-- fix: 4ffcd59e5d -->
- Markdown removes the indent of a line of an indented code block that follows a Unicode line separator (U+2028) or paragraph separator (U+2029) inside the block, as Pi does. <!-- fix: bf1905dd40 -->
- Interactive mode follows Pi's agent events more closely: `agent_end` removes a message that is still streaming, `message_end` of an assistant message requests a frame, and a user `message_end` does nothing. <!-- fix: c4628883bc -->
- A prompt rejected while the messages queued during compaction are flushed (for example no model selected) now puts the whole queue back and shows "Failed to send queued message(s): ..." as Pi does, instead of dropping the messages. <!-- fix: c4628883bc -->
- The terminal progress indicator and the working status start at the run's first turn, as in Pi, so a run writes the progress sequence once, and Escape in a retried run aborts the run. <!-- fix: ed07745fa8 -->
- A queue change, a thinking-level change and the end of a run now update the pending messages, the editor border and the footer from the session events, and an extension's `ctx.shutdown()` during a run ends the session when the run settles instead of mid-run. <!-- fix: ed07745fa8 -->
- Custom entries, displayed custom messages and compactions that an extension appends at a turn boundary now draw in the transcript as they do in Pi. <!-- fix: ed07745fa8 -->
- A finished response shows the thinking-drop notice before the cache-miss notice, an aborted or failed response shows neither, and a message update or end that arrives with no streaming message draws nothing. <!-- fix: ed07745fa8 -->
- Messages queued during an overflow compaction now go through the input handlers and prompt template expansion when the retry turn takes them, and an extension command among them runs instead of being queued as text, as Pi does. <!-- fix: 2492caeaa0 -->
- Flushing the messages queued during compaction no longer moves the output of `!` commands that ran during a run into the chat; only a prompt you submit does that, as in Pi. <!-- fix: 2492caeaa0 -->
- Messages restored after a rejected flush stay queued until the next compaction ends instead of being sent with your next submission, as in Pi, and a flush that fails at one message no longer sends the messages behind it. <!-- fix: 2492caeaa0 -->
- Startup now paints the resumed transcript before the startup diagnostics, the models.json error, the model fallback message and the crash notice, and shows the changelog notice before the transcript, as Pi orders init() and run(). <!-- fix: 68457ed2d2 -->
- Startup now records the changelog version, and each extension package's version, before the UI and the extensions start, as Pi's `init()` does: a `session_start` handler that reads `settings.json` finds `lastChangelogVersion`. A resumed session that holds no message now records it and shows "What's New" like a new session, because Pi skips the changelog only for a session with messages. <!-- fix: dd09fd446a -->
- Extension commands now run one after the other where Pi awaits each prompt: among the positional startup messages, among the prompts you type while a command runs, and among the messages queued during compaction. The prompt after a command waits for its handler to return, and a queued prompt joins a run an earlier command started with its queued mode. <!-- fix: da65d9a454 -->
- Ctrl+C clears the draft (a second one exits) and Ctrl+D on an empty editor exits while startup is still finishing, for example during the first `fd` and `rg` download, as in Pi; the other application keys stay inactive until startup is done. <!-- fix: da65d9a454 -->
- `pig config` no longer clips `  No resources found` and the `(n/total)` scroll row to the terminal width, as Pi does not; the selector's rows still fit every width at which Pi's fit. Declared Package members whose file is absent stay listed with a `  missing` suffix, recorded as D230. <!-- fix: 825b4ab1a6 -->
- `pig config` names the key bound to `tui.input.tab` in its "switch mode" hint, as Pi does, instead of always printing `tab`; an unbound action prints no key. In the global scope the selector no longer toggles an item whose scope is `project`, and a toggle updates the first item of the same path and resource type in the current scope's groups too, as Pi's `ResourceList.updateItem` does. <!-- fix: c5d6b43342 -->
- The extension editor consumes the external-editor key even when no editor handoff is bound, as Pi's `handleInput` does, instead of typing it into the text. <!-- fix: c5d6b43342 -->
- An extension's message_end replacement of a custom message that has no `content` now writes `content` after the replacement's other members, in the session's message, in the message_end event and in what RPC and JSON consumers read, as Pi does; the replacement's own member order is kept whatever the original's was. <!-- fix: 2307f4e5e8 -->
- A `message_end` handler that returns a system message with missing or null content now keeps that content, as Pi does, instead of getting an empty string. <!-- fix: cfe05f8aaf -->
- A row that fills the terminal and holds an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate, for example text cut inside an emoji, no longer stops the interface with "Rendered line N exceeds terminal width". The surrogate is measured as zero cells and written to the terminal as U+FFFD when the frame is written, as in Pi, instead of being widened to U+FFFD before the row was measured. <!-- fix: 21cdff7cc7 -->
- A model's `bash`, `powershell`, `grep`, `find` or `ls` call is now drawn by the tool's built-in card, as Pi does and as `read`, `write` and `edit` already were. The interactive mode took the plain card for those calls unless an extension registered the tool, so a collapsed bash preview at a narrow width wrapped its "earlier lines" hint with other colour resets, an image in the result drew nothing, and the elapsed time past a minute stayed in seconds. <!-- fix: 0c7d23f052 -->
- The session picker reads its tab, sort, path, delete, rename and key-hint bindings from the process-wide keybindings and only the named-filter binding from the manager the component was built with, as Pi does. <!-- fix: 56e30a4a0d -->
- A selected session row with no text no longer draws an empty bold span. <!-- fix: 56e30a4a0d -->
- The `/tree` key-hint rows keep Pi's one-cell wrapped rows in a zero-width terminal instead of drawing empty rows. <!-- fix: 9f7111a870 -->
- The read, write, edit and ls cards draw their call fallback, as Pi does, for a path argument whose `file:` URL cannot be resolved (a URL that names a host or holds an encoded `/`) when the terminal supports hyperlinks; they used to show the path unlinked. <!-- fix: 4cf6069a9b -->
- The read card's truncation warning prints a count the result does not carry as `undefined` and keeps a stored limit of 0, as Pi does; it printed `0` and the default limit. <!-- fix: 4cf6069a9b -->
- A streaming tool call's card is drawn again from the rows of its last frame: a `write` card at 160 columns now re-wraps, measures and pads only the lines whose text changed (its collapsed preview changes one line, the "... (N more lines" hint) instead of all of them, which halves the per-frame cost of the card in an in-process benchmark (178.7 to 89.5 us per frame for a 50 KB file, 121.7 to 43.0 us for 200 KB). The rows drawn are those of a fresh card. The rows kept are bounded (4096 rows of the last text), so a text of many thousand lines does not retain a memo as large as itself. <!-- fix: 72fdd1ee1 -->
- Interactive mode is ready to type about 10 ms sooner when the recorded "what's new" version differs from the running version without a newer release to show (a downgrade, or a settings file that carries a later version). The startup check inflated the whole bundled changelog (about 1 MB) before drawing the first frame; it now decodes the changelog only as far as the releases newer than the recorded version extend, which is a few kilobytes here. What's New, the recorded version and the install report are unchanged. <!-- fix: 3838d0b70 -->
- A `write` tool call that streams a large file no longer leaves the UTF-16 units of its last highlight warm-up in memory after the call is done: each finished card held up to 1.7 MB (a 400 KB file) in the highlighter until later warm-ups pushed it out. The units are released when the call completes, when its card is disposed, and by a warm-up that ends after either; the lines the card draws are unchanged. <!-- fix: 672bed754b67cb31d4a1d927e0ff63b2d16d05a4 -->
- A `write` tool call that streams a large file keeps the highlight of the whole file warm in steps of 4 KB that each cost what they add, so the 99th percentile of the gap between frames while a 200 KB or 400 KB file streams in is 17 ms where it was 18-20 ms, and the CPU is not above. The highlighter keeps the UTF-16 units of the text it has seen from one step to the next and converts only the text a step adds; the lines the card draws are those of a run over the whole file, as before. <!-- fix: 65eafc14a27de87a2d292d419b6e0373066fdf2d -->
- A code block that begins like an earlier streamed block and then differs, such as a file rewritten with its last lines changed or a second fence that repeats the start of the first, is highlighted as a whole run highlights it, in every language. The highlighter restarted from a state of the earlier block that only matched the text before its resume point, and highlight.js reads past that point, so the new block could take a state it does not hold: python, bash, SQL, Kotlin and about 70 other languages showed it, and JavaScript and TypeScript would have with the resumable highlighting of the same release. <!-- fix: e38ea7c9db -->
- After an answer, interactive mode no longer draws three more frames that repaint nothing and only move and hide the cursor (two direct renders at the end of the turn and one requested by `agent_settled`). Pi ends its output with the frame that carries the end of the reply; PiG now does too, which also stops a terminal multiplexer or a script that waits for output to go quiet from waiting a frame longer after every answer. <!-- fix: 18e3b43f1bc06e704351f3d1c193b5367a90ff72 -->
- A `write` tool call that streams a large file no longer stalls a frame while the highlighting of the whole file is kept warm: that work (20-30 ms a step for a large file) now runs on a worker the card owns instead of inside the frame it falls in, and ends with the call, the card or the session. The lines the card draws are unchanged. <!-- fix: 912dc45d6dcc155ca8d4b634988fa0c87abd9e2a -->
- Changing the output padding now applies at once to the branch-summary, compaction-summary and skill-invocation cards already in the transcript. Their padding change reached the card's box without telling the transcript, which kept showing the card at the old padding until the card changed for another reason. <!-- fix: 69c667b1ea19576a74b9d3a02c025a06843642ca -->
- The bug fix ledger no longer puts a fix in the wrong impact class because a word of its release note contains a keyword of that class: a note that says an image is redrawn "when it closes" was classed with fixes of user data, and a note about a `border` with fixes of ordering. Each keyword of the impact and platform classes counts only as a whole word, and `make bug-ledger` reads the class of every committed entry again, so no class outlasts the rule that chose it. <!-- fix: 051ca70445 --> <!-- cause: The impact and platform rules were unanchored patterns that matched inside longer words, and regeneration kept the class of a committed entry as it was. --> <!-- tests: TestImpactAndPlatformKeywordsMatchWholeWordsOnly, TestAKeptEntryTakesItsImpactFromTheRulesAsTheyAre -->
- The bug fix ledger no longer gives a wrong root cause for a fix, the paragraph of its commit message that reports how the fix was tested, and no longer lists as a test of the fix a test that the message only mentions. The cause is what the changelog bullet or the fix commit states outright, or else a paragraph of the message that says why; the tests are the ones the bullet or the commit names as regression tests, or else the ones the fix commit adds or edits. <!-- fix: 051ca70445 --> <!-- cause: Any paragraph of a commit message that held a cause word such as "did not" was taken for the cause, and every test name in the message was taken for a test of the fix. --> <!-- tests: TestTheCauseIsNeverAParagraphAboutHowTheFixWasChecked, TestTheSubagentsRaceFixListsTheTestItAddsAndNoSighting, TestOnlyANamedRegressionTestIsListed, TestABulletStatesItsCauseAndItsTests, TestTheCheckAsksForTheCauseOfANewFix -->
- `make bug-ledger` writes the same ledger in every clone of a commit, and an entry no longer keeps the hash of a commit that a rebase or a re-pick replaced: the fix marker of its changelog bullet decides, and `make bug-ledger-check` names the entry and the fragment while one of them names a commit `HEAD` does not reach. Before, a clone that still held the replaced commit resolved a marker that a fresh clone refused, and a scratch copy of a test file in an ignored directory could remove a test from an entry. <!-- fix: 051ca70445 --> <!-- cause: A committed entry that named a commit missing from the history was kept over a fix marker that names a commit of the history, commit names were resolved against every object of the clone, and the test index walked the directory instead of the files git knows. --> <!-- tests: TestARebasedFixIsRecordedUnderTheCommitThatReplacedIt, TestTheLedgerOfASquashedFixIsTheSameInEveryClone, TestAFixTitledSquashJoinsTheEntryItLandedWhenTheMarkerNamesAnotherCommit, TestAnIgnoredCopyOfATestFileDoesNotChangeTheLedger -->
- `make generate` / `make bug-ledger` could fail on a loaded host with a bare `signal: killed` when a git invocation hit the generator's 120s timeout; the hang guard is now 15m and a timeout names the git subcommand, the bound, and that the host or output reader is slow. <!-- fix: b80d98b1f140c12fefa12ae5048d5e1cb360459c --> <!-- cause: repo.git and repo.gitLines used a 120s context timeout and formatted every cmd error without checking context.DeadlineExceeded, surfacing timeouts as bare signal: killed -->
- Accepting an autocomplete popup of awaited command-argument completions after the cursor moved applies the popup at the cursor as Pi does, instead of dropping it, and a cursor placed before the start of the popup's prefix splices the completion as Pi's string slice does. <!-- fix: 495e25b434 -->
- A compaction that completes with an empty summary, such as one an extension answers `session_before_compact` with, now shows the `[compaction]` block and rebuilds the transcript like any completed compaction, and the RPC `compaction_end` event carries its `result`. The interactive mode and the RPC encoder took an empty summary for a missing result. <!-- fix: 495e25b434 -->
- Quitting during startup (Ctrl-D, or Ctrl-C twice, while the tools download or the terminal colours are queried) in a session started with an initial message, such as `pig "/hello"`, ends the session cleanly instead of crashing or starting a prompt with no session bound. <!-- fix: 4db62b64ea -->
- The footer's context percentage includes the prompt as soon as it is sent, for the whole reply, as Pi shows it; it was stuck at the previous value until the reply finished. <!-- fix: a2fad25d8a -->
- A custom message's `message_start` event keeps the members it started with, in their order, when a `message_end` handler replaces the message; the replacement no longer reaches the start event a listener may still be reading. <!-- fix: 6c31af7a58 -->
- Tooling: `make test-carried-oracles` (the CI step "Run the oracle tests of carried Pi work") passes again and no longer changes the tree. Since Pi's durable packages are vendored, `durable/interop` holds the pin's packages at every pin, so the run, which compares with a later Pi commit, failed (`TestWakeRecordMemosMatchPi`: `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED './session-resources'`) and compared the scripted sessions with the pin's Pi Durable. The run also pointed `extensions/sdk-ts/node_modules` and `.upstream/current` at the later commit, and a run that was killed left them there for the next gate. It now reads that commit's Pi in the build store (`pin.py override-tree`, handed to the tests as `PIG_PI_OVERRIDE_TREE`) and writes nothing in the tree, so `pin.py point-current` is removed. A carried test fails instead of skipping when that Pi lacks the work. `make test-carried-oracles-guard` runs the target to its end, failing and killed, and requires the tree's own Pi to be what it was; `pin.py check-vendored --installed durable/interop` checks the installed packages against the vendored packs. <!-- fix: ee9dfad46efcc493aae48371852950a7642405c1 -->
- The model catalog is now the live one. It was the snapshot the published Pi 1.5.2 package shipped on its build day (1643 chat, 66 image and 64 classifier models); it is Pi's own catalog generator over a committed recording of the live sources taken on 2026-11-15 (1663 chat, 72 image and 72 classifier models: 38 chat models added and 18 removed, 71 records with a changed limit, price or capability), so models released since 1.5.2 can be selected and priced. The recording is data in `automation/gen/catalog-source`; `make model-catalogs` replays it offline and `make model-catalogs-live` is the only target that fetches, so a refresh is a reviewed data change that needs no test edit. <!-- fix: 23b801cc09 -->
- Chord: the surfaces' and bases' build goroutines are joined by `App.Wait`. It is bounded by its context and returns the context's error when that ends first (the builds finish on their own and what they finish after the close is dropped); a surface whose build had not started never starts it. `App.Close` does not wait for them, as Pi's `#close` does not. <!-- fix: 09587d27180574d0864d4a7f7608911d2655765e -->
- Chord's active-language and active-theme followers could miss the user's pick for good: the pick's watch was opened from a goroutine after the hold bound, so a pick chosen in between (a language picked right after the page loaded) was folded into the watch's first value, which the follower never reads, and the page kept the device's language until the next change. A watch of a member that never had a value is now opened in the turn that binds its reference, as in Pi, and the followers start the pick watch from it. <!-- fix: 2e95347143 -->
- Chord's heartbeat closed every link after the process had slept (a laptop's sleep) or blocked its event loop, before reading what the peer had sent meanwhile. Time the process did not run no longer counts as silence: after such a pause each open link pings at once and closes only if its peer stays silent for `close - ping` (15 s by default). <!-- fix: 31312ab0f6 -->
- Chord's workers no longer leave an address failed when a running worker loses its link (the heartbeat, a protocol error, the worker closing its own link): the worker is stopped, `WorkerLinkLostError` (`worker_link_lost`) is reported, and its holders get a new worker. A second lost link within a minute of the last recovery still fails the address (public error `worker lost its link`). Crashes, `fatal`s and failed starts still stay failed until `Retry` or a rollout. <!-- fix: 31312ab0f6 -->
- In the Go Chord v2 workers (`chord/nextnode/workers`), `Workers.Retry` and a plugin rollout no longer leave a crashed worker stopped when they run after the failed automatic resolve of the worker's address has read the failure the workers recorded (the crash a start finds, or the failure of an address that is already failed) and before the route has handled the rejection: the route started nothing for the retry because the address was still resolving, then forgot the address with the rejection, and the worker stayed down with no state until the next hold. The route now remembers a retry that finds the address's resolve running, and the workers' rejection of a recorded failure tells it whether that failure was ended since: the route handles such a rejection as usual and resolves the address once more, so the worker starts once. Any other rejection, the application's own start failure included, takes the retry with it, as in Pi (one resolve, one `resolve_failed` report, one start, the address failed); a resolve that succeeds takes the retry with it and a healthy worker is not restarted. <!-- fix: 4463d9e40b, c1619c666d --> <!-- cause: the route treated a retry that found its address resolving as satisfied by that resolve, which holds in Pi where a rejection and its handling are one chain of microtasks no retry can enter, but not in Go where the answer is handled in a later section a retry can precede --> <!-- tests: chord/next/host/host_route_retry_goonly_test.go::TestRouteHandleRetryWhileTheResolveRunsThatThenRejectsASupersededFailureResolvesOnceMoreAfterTheRejection, chord/next/host/host_route_retry_goonly_test.go::TestRouteHandleRetryWhileTheResolveRunsThatThenRejectsAFailureThatIsNotSupersededTakesTheRetryWithIt, chord/next/host/host_route_retry_goonly_test.go::TestRouteHandleRetryWhileTheResolveRunsThatThenRejectsWithAPlainErrorTakesTheRetryWithIt, chord/next/host/host_route_retry_guard_goonly_test.go::TestRouteHandleRetryWhileTheResolveRunsThatSucceedsIsNotRememberedForTheRejectionOfALaterResolve, chord/next/host/host_route_retry_guard_goonly_test.go::TestRouteHandleRetryWhileTheResolveRunsIsNotRememberedOnceTheAddressIsSuspendedAgain, chord/next/host/host_route_retry_guard_goonly_test.go::TestRouteHandleRetryWhileTheResolveRunsIsNotRememberedOnceTheLastHolderReleasedAndTheAddressIsForgotten, chord/nextnode/workers/workers_retry_resolving_test.go::TestARetryThatEntersAfterTheStartReadTheCrashAndBeforeTheRouteHandledItsRejectionStartsTheWorkerAgainOnce, chord/nextnode/workers/workers_retry_resolving_test.go::TestARolloutThatEntersAfterTheStartReadTheCrashAndBeforeTheRouteHandledItsRejectionStartsTheWorkerAgainOnce, chord/nextnode/workers/workers_retry_resolving_test.go::TestARetryThatEntersAfterAFailedAddressAnsweredANewHoldAndBeforeTheRouteHandledItsRejectionStartsTheWorkerAgainOnce, chord/nextnode/workers/workers_retry_resolving_test.go::TestACallToTheRoutesRetryThatEndsNoFailureOfTheWorkersIsNotFollowedByTheRejectionItEntersBefore, chord/nextnode/workers/workers_retry_failing_start_test.go::TestARetryDuringAStartThatThenFailsOnItsOwnIsOneResolveOneReportAndTheAddressStaysFailed -->
- `TestNodeTheCompileCacheIsWrittenBeforeTheProcessExits` no longer counts the probe's own module as a write on the exit path: the host replies to a load before it writes the load's cache entries, so the test now waits for that write with one more request, and its probe loads 300 modules so a count that did not wait fails on every run. The host's comment states what its exit can still write (modules a plugin's call compiled after the last load or reload). <!-- fix: 606a74fef -->
- Chord: a reload whose new factory pins a keyed member of another object (`ref.keyed.at(key)`) no longer fails the whole plugin with "is valid only in the factory". The recording self a reload runs the factory on handed out references with no dependent. <!-- fix: a79074ec58 -->
- Chord's terminal launcher no longer ends the session when a stop and continue (Ctrl+Z, then `fg`) interrupts the termios ioctl of raw mode: macOS reports that as EINTR, and Node's `setRawMode` retries it, but the launcher's `SetRaw` called `x/term` directly and failed with `interrupted system call`. Entering and leaving raw mode now retries the ioctls on EINTR. <!-- fix: ff6b95eb25, aadacbc03e -->
- A chord app's `Close` kept going after a step failed and joined the errors; it now stops at the first failing step and returns that error, as Pi's close chain does (the steps after it, the data directory's lock release included, do not run). <!-- fix: 4477a81c13 -->
- Chord sync: a store whose outbox was turned off and on again after it committed could not upload any more (`UploadSession` failed with `OutboxUnavailableError` on every attempt) because the commits between what the remote held and the outbox start were gone. `UploadSession` now creates an archive slot after the remote head (the store `Export`), so the session history continues from a full copy; `RemoteHistoryOf` and `PullSession` restore from the newest archive slot along the chain (copies behind it get `HistoryUnavailableError` and restore fresh), and `FoldSession` folds every unfolded slot covered by the snapshot including those before an archive slot (follows Pi `f472efdc1`). <!-- fix: d0eb79648d --> <!-- cause: UploadSession only exported an archive slot when synced == LogStart && outbox.Floor() > 0, so toggling the outbox off and on after a prior upload left outbox.Floor() > synced > 0 and failed with OutboxUnavailableError on every retry. -->
- Chord sync: a `PullSession` restore whose `store.ImportStore` failed before reading the archive body (such as on a cancelled context or non-empty backend) left the remote body file open, and concurrent closes of a `FileSystemSyncRemote` body raced on a plain bool. `PullSession` now closes the body on the `ImportStore` error return and `fileBody.Close` is once-guarded (follows Pi `434dc5e4d`). <!-- fix: 3b0319bcde --> <!-- cause: PullSession omitted body.Close() on the ImportStore error return and fileBody.closed was an unguarded bool under concurrent background close. -->
- Chord store/sync: cancelling a store import while it waits for input triggered a data race under the Go race detector (no wrong result is known). `DecodeJsonl` and `DecodeSnapshot` now synchronize their close flags and close the underlying source once so background cancellation closes safely alongside an in-flight read. <!-- fix: f0f349cb03 --> <!-- cause: importEach calls parts.Close() in a background goroutine on early exit while parts.Next(ctx) may still be running, but jsonlDecoder.finished and gunzipBody.done/reader were unguarded against concurrent Close. -->
- A chord client's watch callback returned at once and let a newer script set be delivered while an update ran, which left a stale retry armed and doubled the next retry pause; the callback now waits for its update, as Pi awaits it, so the newer set is delivered after the update ended. <!-- fix: ec409c76ea -->
- Chord: a plugin update's retry that a newer set replaced is cancelled even when the newer set arrives while the retry's timer is being set; the client kept the replaced set's timer pending. <!-- fix: d6464d301b5 -->
- `host.Registry` with a short `ReadyTimeout` no longer fails "did not become live" when the machine delays the waiting goroutine past the deadline: in Pi the wait's publication, lookup and first usable check run before any timer, so the deadline reports why the registry cannot be read (`contract_mismatch` for a version the provider cannot serve, `unavailable/undeclared` for a registry nobody serves). A deadline that finds the host published and the first check not yet made now lets that check run first. <!-- fix: e676d48779 -->
- Chord's workers on macOS and the BSDs: a worker killed by a signal (the grace's or the start timer's SIGKILL) left its lock's socket file, and every later start of its address failed with `... is a stale lock file`, `retry` too, until the file was removed by hand. The workers component now removes a lock socket file nobody accepts on before each start and after a child's exit by a signal, in the address's queue. `ProcessLock` on macOS no longer spins until its context ends when a regular file sits at the lock's path (`ENOTSOCK`); it fails closed naming the file, as for a socket file nobody listens on. <!-- fix: ea921ca80b -->
- Chord store: `Close` now waits for the `OnCommitted` announcement of the last commit before it closes the backend. A listener could be called after `Close` had returned, or not have been called yet when it returned. <!-- fix: 19f9ce245e -->
- Chord: a contract with an event member that crosses between a Go host and a Node host as data is rebuilt with its event member; it was rebuilt as a method and refused with a fingerprint mismatch. Until events are delivered across the plugins bridge, `NodeHost.Get`, `NodeHost.Hold` and a bridged Go core facet fail for a type with an event member with an error that says events do not cross the plugins bridge. <!-- fix: 7c9ce6f31f -->
- Chord surfaces: a client holds the scripts object by the time `StartClient` returns, as in Pi. The hold was made in the background, so it could be missing right after the start. <!-- fix: 862a8f7a90 -->
- Chord's objects no longer answer a call `not_ready` during a reload while the caller sees them `live`: a call over a link to an object whose restart had drained, sent while its hold was still bound to the old instance, got `not_ready: ... not live yet`. Such a call now waits for the object's new attempt (live, failed or ended), bounded by `readyTimeout` (`unavailable/park_timeout`); a parked attempt showing `failed { waiting }` rejects it with that cause. <!-- fix: f5efecf629 -->
- `chord/nextnode/plugins`, `chord/nextnode/app` (Pi `app.test.ts` "round-trips a worker's documents, tables and files", `worker.test.ts`): a TypeScript plugin can `get` the app kit's `Files` and `FilesFolder` on the server and on a worker, as Pi's plugins can (the divergence record of this limit retires). The plugin bridge copies a keyed member of a Go core facet (`Files.summary`) to the plugins' Node host as a keyed document handle of the proxy object: the object goes live with every document the Go member holds, each later commit reaches the copy in the Go host's commit order, a Go facet that reloaded is read again, and a method's answer follows the commits it made, so a plugin that awaited `files.put` reads its summary. A plugin reads it as a reference's keyed member (`get`, `watch`, `at`). New Go API: `documents.KeyedSlot.Observe` and `host.ReferenceKeyed.Snapshot` (the bridge's observer and read of a keyed member). <!-- fix: fbd59e3aff -->
- chord: a client's active theme or active language could end on an older value than the newest: when the user's pick changed at the moment the client's mode or device languages changed, the two changes could be delivered in the opposite order to the one they were decided in, and the older theme (or language) stayed until the next change. The followers now deliver in the order they read their state, so the last delivery is the current one, as in Pi. <!-- fix: 6138d199ae6 --> <!-- cause: the follower read its state under a lock and queued the change after releasing it, assuming the two steps were one, so two goroutines could queue in the opposite order to their reads -->
- Reading, watching, or listing a keyed state document while its object restarts or reloads no longer races the new attempt's state hydration. Handle and reference lookups now read the slot's active definition inside the object's serialized section, keeping key-validation errors ahead of ended-handle errors as in Pi. <!-- fix: f93a8f2b117da2fee5037cda1066f0a4fc56756f --> <!-- tests: chord/next/documents/keyed_slot_hydrate_race_test.go::TestKeyedSlotSealedHandleGetWhileHydrateWritesDoesNotRaceDefinition, chord/next/documents/keyed_slot_hydrate_race_test.go::TestKeyedSlotSealedHandleSiblingsWhileHydrateWritesDoNotRaceDefinition, chord/next/documents/keyed_slot_hydrate_race_test.go::TestKeyedSlotEndedHandleRefusesWrongKindKeyBeforeEndedPinsPiOrder -->
- A Chord host's link no longer drops the messages its transport delivered before closing when the close arrives while the link's listener is still being handed the messages queued for it: a host that set its listener with messages already waiting (a worker's IPC link queues until its start message) lost the rest of that queue and was told of the close first. The listener now gets them in order and the close after them, as in Pi, where the hand-over is finished before a close is heard; a link closed from its own side still drops what it has not delivered. <!-- fix: adc27a4cbe -->
- A Chord host's IPC or WebSocket link no longer hands its listener a message that arrived while earlier queued messages were still being handed over ahead of them: a hold could reach a relay worker before its hello and end the link with `handshake: hold before hello`. <!-- fix: 4fc2ad082d033ddb9a3ace79c40a76e656aef0f3 -->
- `chord/next/surfaces` (Pi `translations.ts` `canonicalLocale`, `language.ts` `directionOf`): a locale tag is canonical as Node's `Intl.getCanonicalLocales` has it for the value aliases of `-u-` keywords and `-t-` fields (`ca-islamicc` is `ca-islamic-civil`, `ks-primary` is `ks-level1`, `kb-yes` is `kb`, `m0-names` is `m0-prprname`) and for the alias rules of several subtags (a language with a region or script, such as `sgn-BR`; `Qaai` is `Zinh`), so the `lang` and `dir` of a page and the locale chosen for a client no longer differ from Pi's for those tags. The tables are generated from the pinned Node by `testdata/locale_tables.mjs` and checked against its Intl. <!-- fix: fbd59e3aff, 618af0a411, 7ddb7c1a27 -->
- `chord/next/surfaces`: a locale tag is canonical as Node's `Intl.getCanonicalLocales` has it for the time zone aliases of six letters and more (`tz-hongkong` is `tz-hkhkg`, `tz-usnavajo` is `tz-usden`, `tz-factory` is `tz-unk`), for the languages Node aliases only when they are not written all in lower case or are the source language of a `-t-` extension (`TW` and `en-t-tw` are `ak`, `BH` is `bho`; `tw` alone stays `tw`), and for a lone `true` or `yes` in a private use or another extension (`en-x-true` is `en-x`). The generator asks Node for the zones' names and for every six letters that begin with a region, and fails when a `-t-` source language is neither an alias nor in its table. `TestLocaleTablesMatchIntl` covers these classes. <!-- fix: 7ddb7c1a27 -->
- Chord (Go): a watch, an observer or a subscriber of a registry value or a writable that was registered from outside the host's loop is told of a change committed while it registered. The read and the registration were two steps, so such a change reached nobody and the follower kept the older value until the next change (seen as a p2 session worker that failed to start with `p2.harness-host: did not become live within 60000 ms`). <!-- fix: 7369b8f86377c7633e76c160b6ea0f8670ae2b99 -->
- Chord (Go): the observer of a followed source has `Section`, which runs a runtime's read and its advance as one section of the host's loop. A runtime that told of its changes from several goroutines could publish an older read last, and the followed value stayed stale until its next change. <!-- fix: 4f75f7758134ee64db2bdb89d3f3119db8502b29 -->
- On macOS and the BSDs, after a Chord server is hard-killed in the middle of an import or delete, the next start now undoes the interrupted import or finishes the interrupted delete once the dead server's stale lock file is removed (as in Pi); previously the address stayed blocked on its own stale lock file. <!-- fix: 0024f22d1e --> <!-- cause: startup intent recovery was written and tested where process locks are Linux abstract sockets that disappear when their holder dies, so the start never cleared a stale socket-file address lock before taking it -->
- `chord/nextnode/plugins`: the copy of a Go core facet's keyed member a plugin reads (`Files.summary`) is applied in the order the Go host committed. The documents are the first frame the Go side sends, the commits made while they were read follow them (before, a commit that reached the Node host in the same chunk as the documents was applied first and then retired or overwritten by them), a slot that ends while it is read is read again, and a document change refused because the object ended is not reported as a fatal error of the Node host. <!-- fix: 7ddb7c1a27 -->
- `chord/nextnode/plugins`: the directory the plugins' Node runtime is extracted to is named by the manifest and every file of the runtime beside it (`host.mjs`, `proxy.mjs`, `bridge.mjs`, ...), not by the manifest and `host.mjs` alone. Two builds with different `proxy.mjs` or `bridge.mjs` shared one directory under the user cache and repaired each other's files in place while a process of the other build was reading them, so a test run could start the Node host with another build's proxy (a run of the keyed-member bridge failed with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'type')` from an old `proxy.mjs`). <!-- fix: 618af0a411 -->
- On Windows, a message a Chord plugin or worker sent just before its Node process exited was lost: the Go side dropped the cut frame without an error. Each frame is now written in a single `socket.write` call, as Pi's transports send it. A frame larger than the pipe's free buffer (64 KiB per direction), or one sent while an earlier write is still pending, can still be lost if the process calls `process.exit()` without waiting for the write's callback. Affects 0.7.0. <!-- fix: 95274a3c73, 8b53e7c413 --> <!-- cause: on Windows named pipes libuv's uv_try_write always returns UV_EAGAIN so the first socket.write (the 5-byte header) stayed asynchronous in Node's Writable and buffered the second socket.write (the payload) in JS memory until the first completed; process.exit() abandoned the buffered payload, delivering only the 5-byte header so Go framedPort.read hit io.ErrUnexpectedEOF and silently ended the channel --> <!-- tests: TestFramedPortWritesEachFrameInOneSocketWrite, TestFramedPortDeliversAFrameSentRightBeforeProcessExit --> <!-- evidence: mechanism proven red on Linux by TestFramedPortWritesEachFrameInOneSocketWrite (a socket that completes no write synchronously); loss observed on Windows twice through example 76's old step (a report sent just before exit never arrived: runs 44880357753 and 44884991326); Windows-run tests TestFramedPortDeliversAFrameSentRightBeforeProcessExit and TestFramedPortWritesEachFrameInOneSocketWrite have not been seen red on Windows (red and green there are not the same test) -->
- A terminal client's device pairing ended its wait between polls at a cancel; it now settles when the poll interval ends (at most 2 s later) with the cancellation's cause and no further poll, as Pi's bare timeout does. <!-- fix: 9e72f22abd -->
- A terminal client's device pairing counted the poll interval from the start of the previous poll, so a slow poll was followed at once by the next; it now waits the whole interval after each poll was answered, as Pi does. <!-- fix: f105c622cd -->
- `chord/next/surfaces`: a locale tag whose `-u-` extension is only `true` or `yes` keeps it as Node's `Intl.getCanonicalLocales` does (`en-u-true` and `en-u-yes` are attributes); the lone `true` or `yes` of another singleton is still dropped. `TestLocaleTablesMatchIntl` covers both tags. <!-- fix: 308d2802ce -->
- `chord/nextnode/plugins`: a Go facet that reloads twice in a row no longer leaves the copy of its keyed member on the slot of the first reload (the mirror stopped resyncing after it queued the reset, so an end of the next slot in between was lost), and a method called while the copy is read again answers after the frames of its commits were sent, so the plugin reads what it wrote. <!-- fix: 308d2802ce -->
- The terminal sandbox failed to start when the temporary directory had a symlinked ancestor, such as macOS's default temporary directory. It resolves the directory before starting, as Pi does; the sandbox's read access stays the one script. <!-- fix: a9ff67595 -->
- A WebSocket that receives an oversized frame is left closing while its handlers run, as Pi's is, so the peer receives its 1009 close frame; the server side reports close code 1006, as Pi does. <!-- fix: e35933ead2 -->
- In the unreleased app kit, a plugin's contribution to `Translations` (server and worker) or `Themes` (server) was seen by no one, and a plugin object that read `self.registry(Translations)` or `self.registry(Themes)` never became ready (`registry chord.translations: no plugin serves it here`); a worker's plugins had no translations registry at all. The plugins' Node host now loads Pi's own `translationsFacet` (server and every worker) and `themesFacet` (server only, as Pi's worker has none) before the plugins, as Pi's one host does, so a contribution and a read meet in one registry, an unloaded or reloaded plugin's catalogs follow it, and a plugin that serves `Translations` again is refused as in Pi. The Go host's own registries keep the app's Go facets' contributions (the divergence record of the kit's facets says so). <!-- cause: the kit's facets were split to the Go host on the assumption that a registry could be served beside a plugins' host in another process, but a registry is per host and no link carries one, so the plugins' own host had no translations or themes facet; the app kit is new since v0.7.0 --> <!-- fix: 0f62ff2091 -->
- CSS module mappings are what Node's `vm` gives, as Pi's (key order of integer-like names, no `__proto__` key, template-literal names): `ScopeCSSModule` now takes the Node options and a context (the component's builds share one Node subprocess for the mappings), and `ScopedCSS.Classes` is the mapping's JSON text; a CSS module is decoded as UTF-8 like `TextDecoder`. A chmod of a recorded base file is compared like a write, and the base watches are renewed only when the directory is another one (inode and birth time), as Pi's. <!-- fix: 7e42a6a5f6e -->
- On macOS (kqueue), the watches of a base directory moved away and back are put back, and a watch that cannot be put on one entry (a protected or vanished one in a watched directory) no longer stops every watch. <!-- fix: 6fdf59fc088 -->
- The watcher of the plugins component closes the system watcher outside the host's lock, so a failure to watch no longer holds the host while the system (kqueue: one watch per entry) is slow to close; `Plugins.Close` still waits for it. <!-- fix: ad883911f06 -->
- A Chord registry value source reads its composition in a section of the host's loop (inline when the caller is in one): `Value`, `Start` and `Current` from another goroutine (a native's open callback, a request) no longer race a contribution added as an object goes live or a waiter registering. <!-- fix: 0a8ecd3702b -->
- A reload that retries an object whose earlier restart is still parked behind a call running on its old attempt, in the same reload that adds the plugin serving the type the object waited for, reported the object as `parked` with the stale cause `waiting for <type>`; it reports it as `retried`, as Pi does. <!-- cause: the report read the earlier restart's readiness cause before the reload's publication woke the request of that readiness that waited for the type, where Pi reads it after; the restart readiness is new since v0.7.0 --> <!-- fix: a4f9a5907f -->
- A Chord rollout lists every failed worker it retried. A worker whose address already had a start running when the rollout retried it (the route starts one itself when the worker's link closes) was left out of the rollout's list although its start went on, so the app saw one worker fewer than the rollout had brought up; the list now carries the start the address has after the retry, whoever began it, as Pi's does. <!-- fix: 2ca1d45bb497e59c8749c371ea6446dc15ee240f --> <!-- cause: the rollout kept a retried worker's entry only when its own Retry answered that it had started the resolve, assuming a start on a failed address was always its own; Pi lists whatever start the address has after the retry (workers.ts:598-601) -->
- A Chord rollout lists every failed worker it retried. A worker whose address already had a start running when the rollout retried it (the route starts one itself when the worker's link closes) was left out of the rollout's list although its start went on, so the app saw one worker fewer than the rollout had brought up; the list now carries the start the address has after the retry, whoever began it, as Pi's does. <!-- fix: 982a52a9f96927651c76e5a4c3df0bbe270b5a3f --> <!-- cause: the rollout kept a retried worker's entry only when its own Retry answered that it had started the resolve, assuming a start on a failed address was always its own; Pi lists whatever start the address has after the retry (workers.ts:598-601) -->
- A Chord worker rollout no longer lists a retried failed worker twice or sends it a duplicate reload for the scripts it just started with, and no longer sends a duplicate reload to a starting worker waiting on a stale lock when a rollout ships the same script set (since v0.7.0). <!-- fix: 296ad4db9c5 --> <!-- fix: 1adf8da8a48 --> <!-- cause: Workers.Rollout released the component loop around c.route.Retry without skipping retried addresses in its reload loop, and startChild set spawned.shipped after options.Lock and ClearStaleLock instead of directly after Plugins.Scripts. -->
- Chord plugins (internal, the tests' seam): a tree the plugins component's file watcher watches on request (`Plugins.WatchTree`, which only the tests' barrier `pluginstest.Settle` calls) stays watched across discoveries until the component is closed. A discovery dropped it with every tree that is no root's, base's or linked plugin's, so the build of an apply that ran beside a test's edit could take the barrier's watch away between the barrier's request and the event it waits for: `TestARolloutAcrossHostsEndsTwoRolloutsBackToBackOnTheSecondsCodeThePageFollowingWithoutFailing` then failed with `timed out after 15s waiting for the watcher to handle a directory made after the edits`, in about one run in ten. No product path calls `WatchTree`: the trees of the roots, of the base code and of linked plugins are watched and released as before. <!-- fix: 114f1954538 -->
- A terminal sandbox chunk holding valid frames before a malformed one delivered the valid messages before failing; it now delivers none of that chunk's messages, as Pi does. <!-- fix: db8955f3f6 -->
- A chord session's `lastUsed` touch was written even when its request had been cancelled; it is now cancelled with the request (a disconnect or the server's close), as Pi's write on the request context, and a request that finished normally still lands it. <!-- fix: ecf6db94d8 -->
- A Chord singleton state document's handle reads its value in a section of the host's loop, as its watch does: Go code that reads it from a job's goroutine no longer races the object's own commits and its seal when the host closes. <!-- fix: d80cb241f77 -->
- The Chord app kit gives its plugins component the web surface's assets path (`/_chord/web/assets/`), as Pi's app does: a web plugin's `import icon from "./icon.svg?url"` evaluated to a root-relative file name that no route served, and now to the URL the surface serves it at. <!-- fix: 4a33ec6bf7 -->
- The Chord terminal launcher holds the sandbox's frames from the moment a request that asks the user arrives, not once the goroutine answering it runs: a frame the sandbox wrote right after its request could be drawn over the launcher's prompt. A second prompt request while one is open is refused at once (`terminal: a prompt is open`), and the launcher sets its resize and signal restores on its loop, where a finishing launcher reads them. <!-- fix: 4a33ec6bf7 -->
- The Chord terminal launcher no longer ends when the sandbox closes a link socket while it is still connecting and then sends on it (`send on closed channel`): every state change and close of a link socket runs on the launcher's loop, a dial that finishes after the close is closed at once, and a send on a socket that is not open is dropped, as in Pi. <!-- fix: d8c67842e9 -->
- A terminal client whose sandbox stops reading its input and floods messages can be stopped again (Ctrl-C, `Stop`): the sandbox's end no longer waits on the launcher's full event queue from the loop itself. The terminal is no longer left in raw mode when the sandbox ends while the launcher is starting. <!-- fix: d8c67842e9 -->
- The terminal's frame and bundle limits count bytes, as Pi's `Buffer.byteLength` checks do, again. <!-- fix: 45794934c0 -->
- The app kit gives the HTTP component the app's telemetry store (as Pi's `startServer` does), so each request is recorded as a `chord.http` trace of the server. <!-- fix: d06b3d225b9 -->
- Chord: `FormatNumber` and `FormatTime` format in ICU's root locale when neither the tag nor the platform locale has data, as Node does (a `LANG=xx_YY` prints `14:05`, `xx_US` `2:05 PM`, a variable set to the empty string is the locale `und`), and apply CLDR's compound legacy aliases (`hy-arevmda` is `hyw`, `zh-hakka` is `hak`, `zh-xiang` is `hsn`) before the lookup. <!-- fix: 0950d13d68 -->
- Chord's surfaces: a language or theme follower stopped before its pick watch bound no longer crashes the process ("Watch is stopped"); a follower's callback may call `SetDevice`, `SetMode` or `Stop` on it without deadlocking; `Message(key)` with no arguments sends `params: []`; `CanonicalLocale` and the text direction of a locale follow Node's `Intl` (`en_US`, `i-klingon` and `zh-min-nan` are refused, `cmn` is `zh`, `mo` is `ro`, `sam` is right to left). <!-- fix: 2f7f6929c0 -->
- Chord's `TuiScope`: a holder that releases its own `Hold`en reference before the scope's watch of its state started no longer crashes the process. <!-- fix: 2f7f6929c0 -->
- Telemetry: a rendered trace keeps a lone surrogate beside an escaped control character. <!-- fix: 2f7f6929c0 -->
- A running worker's data export (`HostData.exportTo`) holds both of its stores at one point: the kit's store (`kit.sqlite`) keeps its commit queue from before the plugins' store (`store.sqlite`) is copied, SQLite copies that file at one instant, and both archives are written from those. It packed `store.sqlite` through a second handle and `kit.sqlite` after it, holding neither, so a write between the two showed in one archive only. <!-- fix: 5291c9268f -->
- `StartServer` refuses a worker kind without `Authorize` or `Start` with a start error instead of panicking at the first worker start. <!-- fix: 5291c9268f -->
- A worker's `.host-data.mjs`, which holds the start's secret token, is removed when the worker closes. <!-- fix: 5291c9268f -->
- The server no longer keeps a worker's telemetry host entry for every address it ever started: the entry ends when the workers component forgets the address. <!-- fix: 5291c9268f -->
- chord: a message sent to a worker that had just ended no longer discards what the worker wrote before it ended. The failed write closed the connection under its reader, so messages not yet told (a `fatal` report with the worker's reason) were dropped. As Node's `send`, a failed write now only tells its sender; the reader ends the channel after it told what the worker wrote. <!-- fix: 30a10edfb2b5b5b4848eb0fcb7aff63775582ee5 -->
- chord: a worker's exit is no longer held by a process that outlives it. A process the worker started in a session of its own survives the kill of the worker's process group; when it held the worker's stdout or stderr, the server waited for the stream's end and told the worker's exit only when that process ended, so the worker's session never learned that its worker had died (and since the fix of a worker's last messages, a holder of the worker's channel did the same). As Node, which emits `exit` when the process ended, after what it wrote, and `close` when its streams did, the exit is now told once everything the worker wrote before it ended was read and told, and waits for no stream's end. What such a process writes later is still told (output, the stderr tail, control messages, link frames) and is recorded on the worker that exited, never on a worker started after it. The server reads those streams on, three descriptors and goroutines per exited worker at most, until they end or the workers component closes, which now ends them. Limits: on Windows the exit is still told when the worker's streams ended (its pipes have no read that does not wait, and the worker's job object ends them with it): built and vetted, not run; not run on macOS. <!-- fix: 48ba73df55ced82cc6fdb7b5c4015f7921d6475a -->
- chord: a worker that fails right after it started now reports its reason. The server could handle a worker's exit before it had read, or before it had handed over, the last messages the worker wrote (its answer to a waiting holder and its `fatal` report); it then closed the connection and recorded the fixed `worker failed to start` (in p2, under load: a session whose worker dies at its start showed that text where Pi shows why, for example `Unknown model`). As in Node, which emits a child's messages before its `exit` event, the exit is now told after the channel's reader took and told everything the worker wrote. Limits: not run on Windows, where a worker that ends before the server accepted its pipe connection can still lose its last messages. <!-- fix: 60cc9c5bd314b0fd2f655fb8e6976d986bd3e16d -->
- On Windows, a Chord worker sending its last message (such as `fatal`) before exiting no longer blocks when the parent's reader is busy, which could leave the worker hanging until a timeout killed it without receiving the error. The worker IPC pipe now buffers 64 KiB in each direction, matching Unix socketpairs and the Chord plugin listener. Affects 0.7.0. <!-- fix: 48530e80f6 --> <!-- cause: prepareChannel in workers_channel_windows.go created the named pipe with zero InputBufferSize and OutputBufferSize, so CreateNamedPipe blocked every write until the peer read it; a worker exiting in sendControlThen's write callback stalled whenever the parent reader was busy running message listeners -->
- Chord: a `Writable.Set` from outside a section of its owner's loop enters one, so its commit and the derives it causes run on the loop and never race the batch; a Set inside a section is the plain call. <!-- fix: b0ab4cd2563 -->
- Chord: a wait on a promise that a context's abort also ends (`awaitWithContext` in Pi) now delivers the abort in the section that made it, ordered with the promise's own settlement, as Pi does (the abort listener runs inside `abort()`, the settlement's continuation is a microtask). Before, the abort was delivered by `context.AfterFunc` on a goroutine of its own and could lose to a settlement that came a moment after it. The visible case: an attempt sealed while it waited for the previous attempt's drain (a decision change, or a reload, that sealed the successor as the old drain ended) could still run its factory once the drain ended, so a plugin saw the factory of an attempt that had been abandoned run (`[a:write a:write]` where Pi has `[a:write]`). `chord/context` gains `OnAbort`, the listener that runs inside the cancel function, in the cancelling section; an abort made from another goroutine is queued on the host's loop as an event when it is observed. <!-- fix: 6c69d7b4c38aeac73f5a993e82ff856cce23863c -->
- Chord: an abort listener of the host (a call's wait, an event subscription's stop, a reference's `until`, a root scope's seal, a routine's sleep and `on` watch, a consumer's outgoing call, the end of a blocked route settle) now runs inside the cancel and hands its work to the host's loop at once, as Pi's abort listener runs inside `abort()`. Before, the work started on a goroutine of its own after the cancel, in no order against the cancelling section, so a settle could return between a cancel and the work it caused. <!-- fix: 537249aa9f819d7cf51aea5c654218aa2eb246e6 --> <!-- fix: 80406e92df04ef72f5d1ca15a4f84caad6435d25 -->
- Chord: a parked call whose caller aborts is rejected inside the abort, and a flush that runs in the same section no longer sends the cancelled call. <!-- fix: 58c30eca5c196916ad664bb7c6fd3b31808f6fe2 -->
- Chord: a peer that held and released origins faster than the host tore their objects down could make the host keep one pending teardown (a parked goroutine and the object it pinned) for every release: 14,626 pending tasks and 111 MiB at 20,000 origins of one identity, 73,430 and 568 MiB at 100,000, 294,528 and 2,265 MiB at 400,000. An ending now waits for the identity's previous one as a reaction (no goroutine parked on it), and a link's reader waits, after each frame it read off the transport, until the teardowns that frame started have ended or wait for something outside the host (Pi runs the microtasks an ending queued before its next frame), so the same churn leaves at most 2 pending at every size. A teardown that waits for something only a later frame releases does not stop the reader, and the endings queued behind it still pile up without bound, as in Pi. Reply order, teardown order per identity and abort and close order do not change; the reply to a ping sent after a release now comes after the teardown that release started. <!-- fix: 37dad5849b8dc034379218c6c72fe83341c1cf0c --> <!-- cause: the endings of one identity each parked a goroutine on the previous ending and the link's reader read the next frame without letting the ending of the last one run, which Pi's microtask checkpoint does --> <!-- tests: chord/next/host/host_pace_test.go::TestPaceBoundsTheEndingsAPeersUnmarkedChurnLeavesPending, chord/next/host/host_pace_test.go::TestPaceDoesNotHoldTheReaderForATeardownParkedOnALaterFrame, chord/next/host/host_pace_test.go::TestPaceTwoHostsChurningToEachOtherOverABlockingTransportBothFinish, chord/next/host/host_pace_test.go::TestPaceWakesWhenTheLastRunningPacedTaskParks, chord/next/host/host_pace_test.go::TestPaceInTheLinkReaderReturnsAtOnceWhenTheHostOrTheLinkCloses, chord/next/host/host_endings_order_test.go::TestEndingsOfOneIdentityTearDownInTheOrderTheyWereMadeOneAtATime -->
- Chord: waiting for a host to settle now waits for the rest of a handler that parked (a method handler's or a route's `resolve` after its first wait), for the continuations of every unawaited promise of the host (the close tail, host-data turns, flushes and retries of an object, a reference's follow and release, a root scope's handler, a routine's wait, a job's record) and of the documents.
