Before, the rest of such a handler ran on a goroutine the settle did not count, so a check made right after the settle could see a state from before it. <!-- fix: fe0d5a32cefd8fba59b26d68c87e8e944bbc724a --> <!-- fix: f0020ca3a433cafe3d035b8d4ad18b42d3fc766c -->
- Chord: a context derived by `chordctx.WithAbortSignal` from a signal that is a context made by `chord/context` is now cancelled inside the cancel function of its source, before that function returns and before any abort listener (`OnAbort`) of the source runs, as `AbortSignal.any` marks its composite aborted in Pi. Before, `WithAbortSignal` cancelled it with `context.AfterFunc`, on a goroutine of its own, so code that ran right after the cancel could still see a context derived from the cancelled signal live. `OnAbort` now also runs listeners in Pi's order: the aborted context's own, in the order they were added, then those of the contexts derived from it, in the order those were created. Before, a listener added to a child first ran before one added to its parent. A source from another package (a deadline, the standard library's cancel) still reaches the derived context on a goroutine of its own, and `OnAbort` reports `exact` false for such a context. An embedder of `chord/context` can see all of it; no change was found through the Chord host. `git tag --contains` names v0.7.0 as the first tag with the code. <!-- fix: cb409e6c3 -->
- Chord: a context linked from two abort sources now reports the reason of the source that aborted first when one of the sources is derived from a `chordctx.WithoutAbortSignal` context: the host's linked abort signals do, and so does `chordctx.OnAbort` on a context derived by `WithAbortSignal`. Before, the abort order (`chordctx.AbortOrder`) walked through the `WithoutAbortSignal` context into its parents, so the abort of a parent that never reached the derived context counted as the derived context's own, and its reason won over the other source's although that one aborted first. As in Pi, where `withoutAbortSignal` leaves the context no abort signal, the walk now ends at a `WithoutAbortSignal` context. Released in: v0.7.0, and every release since (the walk came with 0b76ae5e5, which `git tag --contains` places in v0.7.0; a probe at the v0.7.0 tag ranks `WithCancel(WithoutAbortSignal(x))` before an independent source that aborted earlier). <!-- fix: 873f87dc7 --> <!-- cause: abortSources and AbortOrder each walked a context's parents on their own, and only abortSources stopped at a WithoutAbortSignal context, so the two functions disagreed about which aborts reach a context. -->
- Chord: the rollout Step of a published script set now lists removed plugins in UTF-16 code unit order, as Pi does, instead of UTF-8 byte order; names outside the Basic Multilingual Plane no longer sort differently. <!-- fix: 2f8638b9498101639722008b729aca56d9187ac6 -->
- Chord: the HTTP listener now parses the Host header and the request target with the WHATWG URL algorithm, as Node does, instead of an approximation. <!-- fix: 2f8638b9498101639722008b729aca56d9187ac6 -->
- Chord: the HTTP listener answers 400 for a request target that contains bytes Node refuses, where it used to pass the request to the component. <!-- fix: 2f8638b9498101639722008b729aca56d9187ac6 -->
- Chord: a table read made while its object ended no longer races with the end. <!-- fix: 7160ad4291 -->
- Chord: an abort listener that ran leaves every source it listened to, and an emptied listener set is dropped. Before, a context that outlived its waits (a link's or a host's) kept every wait that had ended by an abort, and the memory of its busiest moment. <!-- fix: 7e9a4bc8f5e5bfccd4b1cb59e296082932935e06 -->
- Chord: the loading and paging of a list and of a tiling are tasks of the host's loop that waiting for the host to settle counts. Before, they ran on goroutines that only a test helper joined, so a settle could return while a page was still loading. <!-- fix: 1a00b075b6e8b4ab1367070a4b654f4ac19e0f2b -->
- Chord sync: the batch decoder scanned the whole unfinished line for a newline on every 64 KiB chunk (quadratic: 128 MiB took 9.4 s); it scans only the new bytes now. <!-- fix: 04e62295ce8 -->
- Chord: the reloads of a changed binding are owned tasks of the store's reads index, so a binding that changes while a query is made is reloaded in order and waiting for the host to settle waits for them. <!-- fix: 674e3b98693590395be118d765adac76bfad3ff8 -->
- Chord: a query reader opens its read in the section of the move that created it, as Pi does, so what it reads follows the move in the same section. <!-- fix: 6d4e10cfcf11fad2b41f16c3ac1b82bcbb860b28 -->
- Chord: a table read from a handler's goroutine (`handle.Get`, `Page`, `Count`) while its object ended was a data race: the check that the object is still live read the object's documents state outside the host's sections while its end wrote it. The check now takes a section of its own. <!-- fix: 18e7372b98 -->
- Chord: a worker's exit is published after its link closed and after the commits its calls queued in the server's store settled, and a stop resolves only once the exit was published; the app gives its workers the server's store for this. Before, an exit could be published while the commits of the worker's last reports were still queued, and a worker that reported and exited in one turn could have its reports committed after its exit. A worker process closes its link at its exit, before the exit is told, as neither a lost nor a closed link. <!-- fix: 3e66246870f63df797347f38a1280cc929724b74 --> <!-- fix: d3f63d62e9f6b41b4f72d0a368e73930d517c317 -->
- A host whose parent link had closed before `Connect` registered it (a server that refused the WebSocket at once, a proxy that reset it) no longer keeps the dead link as its parent: its references wait for the next link, a hold with no other route fails at once with `no route to server`, and the next good `Connect` holds the references again. The host used to keep the dead link, bind every hold to it and wait on it, and the next `Connect` left a hold that was already set where it was. A WebSocket link made over a socket that had closed already is a closed link too; it used to stay open over the closed socket. <!-- fix: 4ee52b8b9b --> <!-- cause: a Go link closes on its own goroutine, between any two statements of its creator, where Pi's connect() runs to completion before any socket event: a link closed before the host registered it ran its close handler before the connection was the host's upstream, so the handler had nothing to clear and Connect then kept the dead link as the parent; likewise a WebSocket link read nothing of a socket that had closed before its close listener existed, so it stayed open over the closed socket -->
- A Chord WebSocket link made over a socket that closed while the link registered its listeners is a closed link too; it used to stay open over the closed socket, because the close came after the link read the socket's state and before its `close` listener existed. <!-- fix: 647a44808aeb4c1e62c7009848a6d1ba6030c6e1 -->
- CI only: the nightly run on main, a push to a `release/**` branch, a merge group and a dispatch run the full job set again. The `Pre-flight verdict` job ran only on a pull request, and a skipped job skips every job behind it, so every such run since the pre-flight landed ran `Changed paths` and `Bookkeeping` only and failed `CI result` on the verification jobs it skipped. The verdict job now runs on every event and waits for the pre-flight only on a pull request. Released versions: none (CI only). <!-- fix: 23994a396e --> <!-- cause: the verdict job's job-level `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` skipped it outside a pull request, GitHub skips the jobs that need a skipped job transitively (Bookkeeping's `!cancelled()` did not carry over to the jobs that need Bookkeeping), and the CI result test expected the verdict to be skipped outside a pull request, so no test ran a non-pull-request plan through the job graph -->
- CI: the Linux parity shards install the pinned SBCL as the test and portmap shards do, so the Lisp scenario `75-robust-notes-lisp` no longer fails with `exec "sbcl" not found in PATH` on whichever parity shard runs it. <!-- fix: f6d681159b -->
- Text of a pull request that the pre-flight prints (a path, a ledger reason or cite, a commit subject) could start a workflow command on the runner, in the `::command::` form and in the legacy `##[command]` form. Every line the tool prints is now inert. <!-- fix: 363faed088 -->
- The pre-flight `test-expectation` check admits a reviewed ledger row only when the named commit changed that file, as the line lint requires, so the two gates judge alike. <!-- fix: 546133acb5 -->
- The pre-flight `test-expectation` check skips the tooling directories of `test/testdata-provenance.toml` on main, as the line lint does, so a ledger row for such a file is no longer required by one gate and stale for the other. <!-- fix: a058b99ea8 -->
- A shortened notice of the pre-flight is no longer stored as a complete verdict: the record keeps the whole text and only the printed line is cut. <!-- fix: 2844ff315c -->
- When a report was too long for its comment, the next unchanged run reused the shortened record and printed no warnings or notices; it now recomputes. <!-- fix: 730c233072 -->
- Text of a pull request shown in the pre-flight's comment table (the reason of a verdict, a file of a warning) and in its alert comment can no longer break out of its cell: a fence, a mention, an HTML tag, a link or a pipe in it stays text, and a backtick in it cannot close the code span. <!-- fix: eade544cc1 -->
- In fullscreen mode, a click on a message or entry that an extension renders is no longer lost when it arrives before the extension has drawn the card. Until the extension answers its first render request the card is shown as the placeholder `[<type>]`, and a click on that row did nothing: on a slow start or a loaded machine the card stayed closed. The click now waits for the card, and the frame that draws the card gives it the click; several clicks reach the card in the order they were made. A click on a placeholder whose extension never answers still does nothing. <!-- fix: c7c99c68c -->
- `console.*` output and thrown non-Error values in Code Mode scripts print `NaN`, `Infinity` and `-Infinity` as `text()` prints them, not as `null` (so `throw NaN` reports `NaN`). A number nested in an object or array still prints as `null`, as `JSON.stringify` and `text()` print it (Pi #11901). The cause was that the script prelude's `format()` sent every number through `JSON.stringify`, which writes `NaN` and `Infinity` as `null` because JSON has no such numbers; Pi 33cd7e507 prints a number with `String()` first. <!-- fix: 62339c464299bc73839815a2821c62610ce15db8, 36579e48924d36809e3dec8fd91fc9274488648f, f352c2af4bc23110237eab2b90db4b7fd5746012 -->
- Changing the thinking level mid-conversation on GPT-6 models with the OpenAI Codex provider (`openai-codex-responses`) no longer invalidates the prompt cache: thinking level changes (including switching to `off`, sent as `none`, across direct `StreamSimple` and `ModelRuntime` paths, while ignoring any caller-supplied raw `ReasoningEffort`) are now sent as `configuration_update` input items with a fixed `reasoning.effort` of `medium`, and `maxTokens` is forwarded as `max_output_tokens` (at least 16) unless `compat.supportsMaxOutputTokens` is `false`. <!-- fix: e6df1cddad, a5e3bdecaf, eae538553e, 2c7391d451 --> <!-- cause: Codex did not enable supportsMidConvoEffort on GPT-6 models or emit configuration_update items, did not forward maxTokens to max_output_tokens, allowed raw ReasoningEffort to leak into StreamSimple, and only applied the off-to-none rule in direct StreamSimple rather than the shared ModelRuntime simple-stream preparation. -->
- The OpenAI Codex provider (`openai-codex-responses`) now gets prompt cache hits for the system prompt on GPT-6.2 models instead of invalidating the cache on every turn: the system prompt is sent as the leading `developer` input item and top-level `instructions` is omitted (`ConvertResponsesMessagesOptions.IncludeSystemPrompt` is removed). <!-- fix: 9486493968 --> <!-- cause: Codex placed the system prompt in top-level instructions rather than as the leading developer input item, and GPT-6.2 appends instructions after input so every turn changed the prefix before it. -->
- A Codex WebSocket stream whose caller cancels its context right after reading the result no longer closes the connection the provider keeps for the session, so the session's next request reuses it (one connection for sequential requests, as Pi) instead of failing on a closed connection and dialling a new one. <!-- fix: 801d08c8ba --> <!-- cause: the abort-close registration of a WebSocket stream outlived its terminal frame, so a cancel after the result raced the release that keeps the connection and closed it -->
- A Codex WebSocket session whose requests name no transport (a caller of the `ai` package with `StreamOptions.Transport` unset, or a pi-ai helper that passes none) now sends the full context on its later requests, as Pi's do, instead of the delta of a cached context (one new item and a `previous_response_id`). The transports `auto` and `websocket-cached` still send the delta and `websocket` still sends the full context. PiG's `Agent` and `Session` name `auto` when no transport is set, as Pi's do, so the requests of the CLI are unchanged, and an extension's model calls through the host no longer add the settings' transport, as in Pi. The Codex provider has treated an unset transport as `auto` since v0.2.0. <!-- fix: 351b869062 --> <!-- cause: the Codex WebSocket provider read an unset transport as Pi's default "auto" in the cached-context decision, on a comment's claim that Pi does the same, where Pi defaults the option only to choose the WebSocket path and decides the cached context from the raw option, and no test compared a request with no transport against Pi's -->
- The startup prompts (the project-trust and extension selectors, the extension text input and first-time setup) now load the `keybindings.json` of the agent directory, as Pi's startup UI does. They took whatever keybindings the process held before, so a remapped `tui.select.confirm` or `tui.select.cancel` was ignored by them. <!-- fix: 6d3043e50bac375e834e3c5a617bc7359652b2a8 -->
- The startup prompts (the project-trust and extension selectors, the extension text input and first-time setup) now load the `keybindings.json` of the agent directory, as Pi's startup UI does. They took whatever keybindings the process held before, so a remapped `tui.select.confirm` or `tui.select.cancel` was ignored by them. <!-- fix: ecfaad1026bf485d83930b69d152776fc8a52672 -->
- Rendered diffs keep the indentation shared by a removed and an added line when text is inserted at the start of the line. <!-- fix: 1aaf60fd8e -->
- The edit tool keeps the line endings of the lines it does not touch in files with mixed CRLF, LF or lone CR endings, and computes its diff and patch before writing, around the changes only, so a diff failure leaves the file unchanged. <!-- fix: 3b9c7daf85 -->
- Prompt template arguments keep apostrophes inside words, treat a quote with no closing match as text, and accept a backslash-escaped quote inside a quoted argument. <!-- fix: 41226f3eea -->
- A model request that is cancelled while its setup runs, for example the request after an abort during a tool call, ends as aborted instead of as an error. <!-- fix: 563f896e3f -->
- grep takes its context lines from ripgrep instead of reading each matched file, reports the match limit only when another match exists, keeps a lone CR inside a line, and matches a glob relative to the searched directory. <!-- fix: 68fd735480 -->
- A prompt can no longer start while tree navigation or a branch summary is running, tree navigation is refused while a prompt is in its input hooks, and the live thinking level is recorded on the branch before each prompt so a resume after /tree restores it. <!-- fix: b8a8fe5551 -->
- The read tool streams a text file instead of loading it whole: only the lines it can show stay in memory, so a one-line read of a very large file no longer costs the file's size, and an abort stops the read. <!-- fix: c5edfc4dbc -->
- The find tool on Windows returned no results for patterns with Windows separators such as `src\**\*.ts`, and for every path pattern such as `src/**/*.ts` with fd 10.5.1. A Windows path pattern now matches the same way with every fd version: `src/**/*.ts` also finds files directly in `src/`, and `src/*.ts` no longer finds files in subdirectories. <!-- fix: 55a52447fc1 -->
- A find call aborted while the tool looked for a `.git` directory above the search path no longer starts fd. <!-- fix: 55a52447fc1 -->
- The powershell tool no longer reports `Command exited with code 1` under Windows PowerShell 5.1 when a native command succeeded but its stderr was redirected, as in `git push 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 3`; such commands report the exit code PowerShell 7 reports. <!-- fix: 8ac653e9b23 -->
- An extension command that awaits `ctx.reload()` now goes on after the reload when the reload removes another member of the command's shared Go, Rust, Python or Lisp process, as it does in Pi, where the old extension instance outlives the reload its command awaits. The reload stopped the shared process while the command still ran, so `await ctx.reload()` failed with a lost connection, the command stopped half way, and the calling extension was gone after the reload (an RPC session with two extensions of one shared process, one of which removed the other's file and reloaded), in the Go, Rust, Python and Lisp SDKs alike. Node extensions were not affected. Present since 0.4.0. <!-- tests: coding/extension/host/subprocess/reload_caller_packed_cell_test.go::TestPackedGoCommandGoesOnAfterAReloadThatRemovesAMemberOfItsCell, coding/cli/rpc_reload_resumes_test.go::TestRPCCommandGoesOnAfterAReloadThatRemovesACellMember, test/extension-conformance/sdkscenario_test.go::TestSDKScenarios --> <!-- fix: 33aa6ec15e -->
- Aborting a compaction while extensions were being told it finished no longer keeps the extensions after the first from hearing about it. `session_compact` now reaches every extension, in order, as in Pi, whichever of them calls `abortCompaction()` or has the compaction aborted while its handler runs; the saved compaction still completes. <!-- fix: 79194ebd9f -->
- Aborting a compaction while extensions were being told it finished no longer keeps the extensions after the first from hearing about it. `session_compact` now reaches every extension, in order, as in Pi, whichever of them calls `abortCompaction()` or has the compaction aborted while its handler runs; the saved compaction still completes. <!-- fix: 030982080e -->
- A compaction, branch summary or bug report summary no longer fails with "Summarization failed: 401 Unauthorized" when the short-lived token it started with (a GitHub Copilot API token lives about 30 minutes) expires before its last request: after a retry's backoff, or on a later chunk. A Session started from the command line resolved its credentials once, when the summary began, and sent that token with every request of it. Each request now resolves its own credentials when it is sent, as a turn does and as Pi's sessions do. <!-- fix: 15b13fcae5f93175152234595b75ffe1fad879df -->
- A compaction, branch summary or bug report summary no longer fails with "Summarization failed: 401 Unauthorized" when the short-lived token it started with (a GitHub Copilot API token lives about 30 minutes) expires before its last request: after a retry's backoff, or on a later chunk. A Session started from the command line resolved its credentials once, when the summary began, and sent that token with every request of it. Each request now resolves its own credentials when it is sent, as a turn does and as Pi's sessions do. <!-- fix: 9e95660e7d6185fff8d31df8ebd61a491cee7812 -->
- A session whose model has no known context window (a model an extension registers without a `contextWindow`, or one an embedding program builds without `ContextWindow`) no longer compacts its history after every reply: a window of 0 is unknown, not used up, so the threshold check is skipped for it and a known window is checked as before. PiG had compacted after every reply for such a model since 0.2.0, which cost a summariser request and the history of each turn; Pi still does (D660). Fix from #548 by @Cpt-Falcon. <!-- fix: 87ea4f926e95b30091295ba946c1716e3d8cb260 -->
- OpenAI-compatible (chat completions) requests write the objects a model entry or the caller supplies with their members in the order the source lists them, as Pi does; PiG wrote each sorted by key. This holds for `chat_template_kwargs` / `chat_template_args` (compat `chatTemplateKwargs` / `chatTemplateArgs`), for `provider` and its nested objects such as `max_price` (compat `openRouterRouting`), and for the sampling parameters at the top level of the request (`samplingParams`, `samplingParamsByThinkingLevel` and a request's own). The content was the same. The order is kept from `models.json`, from a provider an extension registers and from a request an extension streams with; a provider entry's compat merged with a model's and with a model override's follows Pi's spread (the base's members in the base's order, an overridden member in its place, new members after them). The sampling parameters of OpenAI Responses and Azure OpenAI Responses requests follow the same order. Go callers: `ai.Model` and `ai.StreamOptions` gain `SamplingParamsOrder` (`ai.Model` also `SamplingParamsByThinkingLevelOrder`) beside the maps, and `ai.MergeOpenAICompat` merges two compats as Pi's `mergeCompat` does; a caller that sets only the map still sends its members sorted. <!-- fix: 3fe81801cc -->
- Ports Pi's fix b82477b7b (#12134): Groq Qwen reasoning models no longer fail with `400 Unexpected message role` when their chat template rejects the `developer` role, because `openai-completions` now defaults `supportsDeveloperRole` to `true` only for provider `openai`, `api.openai.com` endpoints, and bare `OpenAIConfig` defaulting to `openai` / `api.openai.com`. <!-- fix: 58c210c508, 6e265d4046, 855a70ed39 --> <!-- cause: detectOpenAICompletionsCompat defaulted supportsDeveloperRole to true for standard OpenAI-compatible hosts and OpenRouter openai/anthropic models instead of limiting the developer role default to provider openai and api.openai.com. --> <!-- tests: TestOpenAICompletionsInstructionRoleDefaultsToSystem, TestOpenAICompletionsInstructionRoleRealPathsWithoutCatalogCompat, TestCatalogOmitsRedundantSupportsDeveloperRole, TestToPiModelOmitsRedundantSupportsDeveloperRole, TestOpenAICompletionsCompatSupportsDeveloperRoleDescription -->
- When a provider's server resets or closes the connection before it answers, the retry notice and the turn's error now name what happened the same way every time, as Pi does: `Connection error.: read ECONNRESET` for a reset and `Connection error.: other side closed (UND_ERR_SOCKET)` for a close. A reset that arrived while the request was still being sent was shown, depending on timing, as a bare `Connection error.`, as `other side closed (UND_ERR_SOCKET)`, as `write ECONNRESET` or as `write EPIPE`; with a large request that was nearly every time. The turn was retried in each case and still is. <!-- fix: 1662063665 --> <!-- cause: net/http returns the request body write's error and drops the read side's, and the error mapping named only the "write" and "read" operations, not the vectored "writev" of a request body -->
- A `context` handler that edits a message of `event.messages` in place and then throws now leaves the edit in the request, as it does in Pi, where the handler works on a copy of the list over the one set of message objects: an edit to a message stays and a change to the list does not. Until now the failed handler's reply was dropped and the edit was lost, in every extension SDK. The loss was present in every release since v0.2.0. <!-- fix: 83928e2246 -->
- Go SDK: the stack of a panic the SDK recovered in a settings storage's `WithLock`, an MCP credential store's `WithRefreshLock` or a custom editor component (a queued task, a guarded call such as `HandleInput`) was written to the extension process's stderr, which the host forwards to the terminal, so it painted over the interactive screen. It now goes to the extension's log, as the stacks of the SDK's other recovered panics do; the user still sees the one-line error (Pi shows one line for a throwing callback and writes no stack to the console). <!-- fix: f7dbf5424d -->
- GitHub Copilot models on the Responses API (GPT, Grok, MAI-Code) no longer fill omitted optional tool arguments with empty strings or invented values. Their tools were sent without `strict`, which Copilot treats as strict mode; they now send `strict: false`, or `strict: true` for tools with JSON-schema constrained sampling. Affects 0.7.0. <!-- fix: 81f580b72d -->
- A login refresh that took more than fifteen seconds while another pig process opened the credential file lost its lock, and the refreshed login was thrown away. The lock is now renewed every five seconds, so a slow refresh keeps it. Divergence D651 (approved by the owner, 2026-11-14T14:10:39Z "proceed"): Pi renews its async auth lock every 15 s (proper-lockfile stale/2) while its sync readers take any lock older than 10 s; pig renews every 5 s. Why: a live holder is never taken over, so a rotating refresh token is not spent twice. Remove when: Pi renews faster than its sync stale window. <!-- fix: fbe92b66a0 --> <!-- cause: the async lock heartbeat (stale/2 = 15 s) was longer than the sync acquirers stale window (10 s), so a live holder looked stale to them. -->
- A login refresh that took between ten and fifteen seconds while another pig process opened the credential file was thrown away, and the next request asked you to log in again. pig now saves the refreshed login for that provider into the file as it is at that moment, leaving every other provider's entry as the other process wrote it; for that provider the refreshed login replaces what the file holds, a later login or logout of it by the other process included, as in Pi. This holds while the lock's own renewal has not yet noticed the takeover: once it has, the refresh still fails with the lock error and writes nothing, as in Pi. <!-- fix: 0635f2339b --> <!-- cause: Modify treated a lock taken over while the refresh ran as a failure of the whole write, though the refreshed credential, possibly the only copy of a single-use refresh token, was already in hand. -->
- A login refresh that took between ten and fifteen seconds while another pig process opened the credential file was thrown away, and the next request asked you to log in again. pig now saves the refreshed login for that provider into the file as it is at that moment, leaving every other provider's entry as the other process wrote it; for that provider the refreshed login replaces what the file holds, a later login or logout of it by the other process included, as in Pi. This holds while the lock's own renewal has not yet noticed the takeover: once it has, the refresh still fails with the lock error and writes nothing, as in Pi. <!-- fix: 93b5de031b --> <!-- cause: When another process took auth.json's lock while a refresh was in flight (the sync lock goes stale after 10 s, a slow refresh outlasts it), Modify returned the compromise error and dropped the credential the refresh had obtained, which may have spent a single-use refresh token. While the lock's heartbeat has not yet reported the takeover, Modify now writes that provider's entry alone, under a lock of its own, into the file as it is then; what the other process wrote stays, and Pi persists the credential in that case. Once the heartbeat has reported the takeover, Modify still returns the lock error and writes nothing, as Pi throws. An fn that fails still writes nothing. -->
- A full disk or a killed process during a credential write could sign you out of every provider. `auth.json` was rewritten in place, so a write that stopped half way left it empty or cut short, and the next login or token refresh then saved a file holding that one provider. The file is now replaced as a whole through a temporary file in the same directory, so where it can be replaced a failed write leaves the old file untouched. A file that exists keeps its mode, owner (where pig may set it), extended attributes (the POSIX ACL on Linux, the user's attributes on macOS) where the file system takes them, exactly the access it had (an ACL the directory would hand a new file is not added), a symlinked `auth.json` and, on Windows, its access rights; a file that does not exist yet gets the mode that is asked for with your umask taken out, as in Pi. pig replaces a file only when that changes nothing but the file itself: where a credential file cannot be replaced atomically, for example a single file mounted into a container, a file in a directory pig cannot write into, a file with more than one hard link, a file whose extended attributes cannot be carried over, or a device or named pipe, pig writes it in place as before, as Pi does, and the debug log (`PIG_DEBUG`) says so. That guarantee does not cover an in-place write: one that fails half way can still leave the file empty or cut short, as before. <!-- fix: 4ec88b40bc --> <!-- cause: auth.json was written in place (opened, truncated, written), so a full disk, a size limit or a killed process during the write left it empty or cut short. It is now replaced through a temporary file in the same directory (private from creation, fsynced, renamed over the file, directory flushed), so such a failure leaves the old file whole. The mode, the owner where the process may set it, and the extended attributes (the POSIX ACL on Linux, the user's attributes on macOS) where the file system takes them are kept; a symlinked auth.json is followed; on Windows the security descriptor and user attributes are carried onto the temporary file before MoveFileExW replaces the target. A read-only auth.json is refused as before. A file with more than one hard link, or whose extended attributes cannot be carried over, is written in place as before, as in Pi, and so are a single file mounted into a container, a file in a directory that cannot be written, and a device or named pipe. -->
- A full disk or a killed process during a credential write could sign you out of every provider. `auth.json` was rewritten in place, so a write that stopped half way left it empty or cut short, and the next login or token refresh then saved a file holding that one provider. The file is now replaced as a whole through a temporary file in the same directory, so where it can be replaced a failed write leaves the old file untouched. A file that exists keeps its mode, owner (where pig may set it), extended attributes (the POSIX ACL on Linux, the user's attributes on macOS) where the file system takes them, exactly the access it had (an ACL the directory would hand a new file is not added), a symlinked `auth.json` and, on Windows, its access rights; a file that does not exist yet gets the mode that is asked for with your umask taken out, as in Pi. pig replaces a file only when that changes nothing but the file itself: where a credential or settings file cannot be replaced atomically, for example a single file mounted into a container, a file in a directory pig cannot write into, a file with more than one hard link, a file whose extended attributes cannot be carried over, or a device or named pipe, pig writes it in place as before, as Pi does, and the debug log (`PIG_DEBUG`) says so. That guarantee does not cover an in-place write: one that fails half way can still leave the file empty or cut short, as before. <!-- fix: 74be4056e2 --> <!-- cause: the credential store wrote auth.json with os.WriteFile, which truncates the file before it writes, so a write that failed after it began left an empty or cut-short file that the next process read as holding no credentials. -->
- `--model <provider>/<id>` with an id the catalog does not know, under a provider an extension registers with its own models or a provider `models.json` defines, started with none of the provider's model data. The footer showed a context window of 0 (`0.0%/0`), the turn cost nothing, images were not accepted and the provider's compat flags were ignored; the request the provider received asked for almost no output (`max_completion_tokens: 1` on openai-completions, `max_output_tokens: 16` on openai-responses, where Pi sends the model's limit) and addressed a reasoning model with a developer message even where the provider declares `supportsDeveloperRole: false`. In print mode a reply cut short for length then ended with exit status 1 and the partial answer on stdout, where Pi recovers and ends with status 0. Under a built-in provider whose default model `models.json` overrides, the id took the catalog's values instead of the overridden ones. As in Pi, such an id now starts as a copy of the provider's default model, or its first model, under that id: its window, output limit, prices, input kinds and compat flags, with the provider's own request headers. Present since 0.7.0. <!-- fix: aa954ac08f, e261af0cdc, 84e1fdeeea --> <!-- cause: Start-up discarded the model its selection returned for the id, a copy of one of the provider's models, and resolved the provider and id a second time: they name the provider's connection and no model. The request path did the same where no credentials were resolved for the provider. --> <!-- tests: coding/cli/custom_model_fallback_rpc_test.go::TestRPCCustomModelIDKeepsTheProvidersLimitsCostAndCompat, coding/cli/custom_model_fallback_test.go::TestStartupCustomModelIDIsACopyOfTheProvidersModel, internal/codingagent/model_registry_fallback_test.go::TestResolveFallbackModelKeepsTheModelAndResolvesTheProvidersConnection, test/parity/scenarios/model-resolver-selector/31-custom-model-id-extension-provider-print.toml, coding/cli/custom_model_fallback_footer_test.go::TestInteractiveFooterOfACustomModelIDShowsTheProvidersWindow, coding/startup_copy_request_model_test.go::TestUnauthenticatedRequestModelOfAStartupCopyIsTheCopy -->
- Go, Rust, Python and Lisp extensions: a bash tool built on `createLocalBashOperations()` now says `The shell exited with code C after S seconds, but background processes it started kept writing output until the timeout.` when a command timed out after its shell had already exited, as Pi 1.5.1 does. The local operations of these SDKs reach the host over `builtinTool.localExec`, whose error reply carried only `timeout:N`; it now carries Pi's `shellExit` (the shell's exit code and run time), which the SDK passes on when its exec returns that error unchanged. An error wrapped around it, or a new error with its message, gives the plain `Command timed out after N seconds`, as in Pi. <!-- fix: 123827b998d68c0daa1b7633ecf647a4c41846c8, 01d8d08b3124e0110aaed8b7c9c5400a54038f34 -->
- Closing the terminal of an interactive session (a closed window, `tmux kill-session`, a dropped connection) now gives extensions `session_shutdown` with the reason `quit` before the exit, as Pi does when the hangup reaches it as SIGHUP. PiG's input reader saw the dead terminal before any signal and exited 129 without the event, and it killed the extension processes under an event the signal path had already started, so an extension lost its last write (reported for a fused Piglet extension whose session log ended without its shutdown record). The exit waits for the handlers for at most one second, writes nothing new to the dead terminal, stays 129 and leaves one `exit.log` line; a session without a `session_shutdown` handler exits as fast as before. D186 records the differences from Pi, which waits for a slow handler without a limit, cuts a working session's handler at its next terminal write, and emits nothing when its event loop is empty. <!-- fix: 5b36a5f599baa42fccb554fbea75d7f2c07c116f, aef7184ef313f3d4bbd3254d4cfb7ce01e773c30 -->
- Node extension runtime: a `message_update` or `tool_execution_update` handler failed with `Maximum call stack size exceeded` from about 2500 levels of nested arrays (about 4960 levels of nested objects), because the runtime copied each event payload recursively for its handler; Pi's handler gets the object. The payload is copied without recursion now, so a handler receives it up to where its own `JSON.stringify` runs out of V8 stack, as in Pi. <!-- fix: 3ebb3155aacd3c28b0e45b05ede33d45fdf9e172 -->
- Extension SDKs: tool arguments nested thousands of levels deep no longer fail or end the extension, in any SDK or on any supported Python (3.11 and later). The host sends arguments nested up to 10000 levels, and Pi's own runtime fails the call with `Maximum call stack size exceeded` only where V8 runs out of stack for `JSON.stringify` (about 4400 levels on Node 24; it moves with the Node version). The Python SDK failed the call from about 1000 levels (`maximum recursion depth exceeded`), and from about 990 on Python 3.11; the Lisp SDK ended its extension from 4000 levels; the Rust SDK ended its extension past 4096 levels and its `Context::tool_params` returned `None` from 128; the Go SDK ended its extension from about 9995 levels. Each now returns the object for every frame the host can send, a request nested past what an SDK reads fails with that error while the extension answers the next call, and a notification nested past it (a `model_stream_event` with deep tool arguments reads fine) is dropped with a line on stderr. The Rust SDK also ended its connection on a `message_update` (a tool call in the partial message) or `tool_execution_update` whose delta carried a value nested past 128 levels; both are read now. The Lisp image is built with a 64 MiB control stack per thread (address space, not resident). The difference from Pi's depth-dependent limit is recorded as D268. <!-- fix: c551a6348dff9de55e14a1143f471c868ea43c1f, e2ea65cfa34d3cd2961b2c9d0b2259c2d1a87e8a -->
- An interactive start now prints the warnings about extensions still in a deprecated directory, with the migration guide and documentation links, and waits for one key before the TUI starts, as Pi does. Before, the warnings were computed and dropped. <!-- fix: 0ca206e73e -->
- `pig docs show divergences` lists every active divergence in one table, each once. A blank line inside the table and rows added after the page's last section had left 80 of its 143 rows outside the table, and D540 and D605 each had two rows with different wording. <!-- fix: 3bf80808ee -->
- A telemetry span of a failed provider request kept a 500-character cut of the provider's error message that still pointed into the whole message, so a 4 MB error body stayed in memory for as long as the recorded span did. The cut is copied now. <!-- fix: b50a5abb5c565c5700b67230fc31deed6b5c6c34 -->
- Draining a model collection while it refreshes no longer starts provider work after the drain began, and a streaming request's blocked auth callback no longer holds the drain. `ai.Models.Drain` now stops the collection admitting owned work under the lock the work is admitted under, so a refresh with providers still queued starts none of them, a publication made afterwards writes nothing, and no worker is added to the group the drain is waiting on. A stream's auth callbacks run outside the work `Drain` joins, as a login's do, while the credential write of a stored OAuth refresh, which a cancelled stream leaves running, is joined. <!-- fix: 44803aac4d07fd4c63d3ccb5fac7934db304c194 -->

A stream's auth callbacks run outside the work `Drain` joins, as a login's do, while the credential write of a stored OAuth refresh, which a cancelled stream leaves running, is joined. <!-- fix: 86376a77778aaf9bd4a025856512f722d853d2b7 -->

- A Durable core's warm turn waits exactly the microtask passes Pi's does. The Cloudflare host's section effect resolved the agent a second time for the section's input, four passes more than Pi's `await section.render()` on each model call (+36 per turn of eight lookups); it now renders with the agent the `resolveAgent` hook last answered, as generation.ts passes the agent it resolved. The contract rows `F-ticks-warm-node` and `F-ticks-warm-gate` and the host test `warm-ticks.test.ts` pin Pi's counts. <!-- fix: 1e64d3f44e -->
- Closing a durable Harness releases the pi-ai resources of the provider sessions its tasks used, after the running task invocations joined and before Storage closes, so a legacy OpenAI Codex WebSocket no longer keeps the process alive after `Harness.close()` returns. The cleanup is scoped to the closing Harness (another live Harness in the process keeps its resources), runs also when the Harness fails, leaves the persisted provider session IDs for a reopened Harness, and a failing cleanup is reported as a `host_error` for `models` without stopping Storage from closing. <!-- fix: 8e2123081c -->
- A Durable value that holds a lone UTF-16 surrogate is stored as Pi stores it. Task states and outcomes (checkpoint, result, error message, reason), entry drafts, context edits, document contents, tool controls, compaction `modelOverrides` keys, a tool call's checkpoint arguments, extension and tool selections and view documents went through Go's `encoding/json`, which writes the unit as U+FFFD where `JSON.stringify` writes `\ud800`, and read the escape back as U+FFFD. Two document kinds that differ only in such a unit also got one `AddressId`. SqliteStorage read a stored record's escape as U+FFFD as well. `ownedTasks` returned a task's kind, input and checkpoint with U+FFFD for such a unit, and a nested call key's error quoted the key with Go's escaping (`\u003c` for `<`, U+FFFD for the unit) where Pi's `JSON.stringify` does not. Pi's own `JSON.stringify`, `documents.ts` `addressId` and `tool.ts` `checkKey` answer for the encoders in the new tests. <!-- fix: bbccefdf7f, 7c3789482b, e37b86562b, adad5282ac, a639c9afb2, d7367de40 -->
- Durable's SQLite storage stores a lone UTF-16 surrogate in a row of more than 8 Ki characters as U+FFFD, the text Pi's bound insert (node:sqlite) stores, instead of its raw WTF-8 bytes (rows of up to 8 Ki characters keep the bytes of Pi's JSON route, as before); the row's size is measured as Pi measures it, in UTF-16 units of the text with each ill-formed UTF-8 subpart as one U+FFFD. A test compares the stored bytes with Pi's own insertRows (statements.ts under Node) at 8 Ki characters and either side of it, for lone high and low surrogates, pairs, and ill-formed UTF-8. <!-- fix: d818c2140 -->
- Durable contract CLI (`durable/contract/cli/contract.mjs`, `durable/contract/cli/robust.mjs`): `-j N` is now parsed as the concurrency option instead of being treated as scenario ids, and `contract all` / `contract run` now exit non-zero on unknown options, unknown scenario ids, or selections that match zero rows (previously CI passing `-j 4` ran zero scenarios and exited 0). <!-- fix: f01e5a14c4af0a9fee4bb4a224c1664c924975e4 --> <!-- cause: contract.mjs looked up every option with two dashes (--j) and forwarded every leftover token as a scenario id filter where matching zero rows exited 0, so -j 4 silently matched nothing. -->
- `durable/contract/tools/setup.sh` now populates the Pi reference checkout's generated provider catalogs (`packages/ai/src/providers/data`) from the committed vendored `@earendil-works/pi-ai` tarball in `third_party/pi-packs` whose `manifest.json` commit equals `durable/contract/PIN` `main`, re-syncing whenever the pack digest stamp or any imported catalog is missing, and fails loudly naming any missing catalog file or manifest mismatch. - Closing a durable Harness releases the pi-ai resources of the provider sessions its tasks used, after the running task invocations joined and before Storage closes, so a legacy OpenAI Codex WebSocket no longer keeps the process alive after `Harness.close()` returns. The cleanup is scoped to the closing Harness (another live Harness in the process keeps its resources), runs also when the Harness fails, leaves the persisted provider session IDs for a reopened Harness, and a failing cleanup is reported as a `host_error` for `models` without stopping Storage from closing. <!-- fix: e99d1a7ca372e7ddd8ab8fc76827a51bf2eb9a5d -->
- durable/harness: a host embedding `durable/harness` could be ended by Go's `concurrent map read and map write` when a registry change refreshed blocked reasons concurrently with commit publication, could hit a data race when a task graph or conversation view observer attached during commit publication, and could see a task graph observer show a task blocked for a definition that had just been installed until the next registry change. Present since 0.7.0. <!-- fix: d1a4d01571 --> <!-- fix: 388aed919e --> <!-- fix: deb3251294 --> <!-- fix: 7f55f03889 -->
- Group-commit publication no longer publishes the next part of a storage call before a wait's continuation has run for waits carrying a `Continuation`. `SessionImpl.Park` previously had two race gaps: it called `enter(continuationOf(ctx))` before inserting the new `*Parked` entry into `session.parks`, and it checked whether `done` was closed before acquiring `parkMu` to insert into `session.parks`, allowing a publication's `awaitReadied` scan (which runs under `parkMu` after deferred wakes close their channels) to miss the wait and letting the next part's `Hop` proceed early. `Park` now holds `parkMu` across the `done` check and the map insert, then releases `parkMu` before calling `enter`. <!-- fix: b5a660ac5c --> <!-- fix: 84b5913537 --> <!-- cause: SessionImpl.Park checked done outside parkMu and called enter(continuationOf(ctx)) before inserting into session.parks, letting a publication close done and run awaitReadied before the wait was in parks and letting deliverLoop go idle while the wait was still entering Park --> <!-- tests: TestGroupCommitParkEnterBeforeInsertWindow, TestGroupCommitParkCheckBeforeInsertWindow, TestParkWithPendingParkedOnSameContinuationDoesNotDeadlock -->
- Durable agent turns whose provider call failed with a node-fetch network error of the form `request to <url> failed, reason: ...` were not retried since v0.7.0 because the Durable core regex engine did not implement the `\S` non-space character class; they are now retried, as in Pi. <!-- fix: 83992d88018dacbc7e68b5874f3c030c1dd058fd, ce5cdf98237ed5b5252d12c015e736abdf46dd75 --> <!-- cause: durable/core/turn/rx.go only handled \d and \s after a backslash and fell through to literal characters for every other escape, so \S in patterns.go silently matched literal S. -->
- Durable: a task change deep in a long ownership chain no longer costs time proportional to the chain's depth: finding the conversations whose idleness a change can affect starts at the task's own conversation, as Pi does (Pi 628d8ab52ce2), instead of walking every owner task up to the conversation. <!-- fix: 577d66446d30694aab1c06fc85bb2814fc60da4c -->
- Durable: a task change deep in a long ownership chain no longer costs time proportional to the chain's depth: finding the conversations whose idleness a change can affect starts at the task's own conversation, as Pi does (Pi 628d8ab52ce2), instead of walking every owner task up to the conversation. <!-- fix: 91d3edcb1c07b12434de3b63d20da1be412d0dad -->
- A Durable session on a Chord store no longer races the host's loop when a commit is published: the publication of each commit now runs as a section of the host's loop instead of on the writer's goroutine, which touched the host's batch while the loop ran its own commits (a data race, seen under `-race` when a p2 server reloads a plugin while a worker streams). A caller that blocks on a durable commit from inside a host section now waits for itself; commit from a goroutine of its own. <!-- fix: 07f40724ef -->
- A Durable entry record is written and read as Pi's JSON.stringify and JSON.parse do for every UTF-16 string. A lone surrogate in an entry's kind or in a data value that is not an object was written as U+FFFD by `EntryRecord.MarshalJSON` (Pi keeps the escape `\ud83d`); a lone surrogate in a message, kind or data string read back as U+FFFD (Pi reads the unit); a surrogate pair held as two adjacent lone halves was written as two escapes by the Chord `Object` (Pi writes the character). `MarshalJSON` and `AppendStringify` now write the same text, which a Node differential test over random UTF-16 strings (lone, paired and reversed surrogates in the kind, the messages, the edits and every data string and key) compares with JSON.stringify and JSON.parse; the general encoder path (`json.Marshal` of an entry) writes a float -0 as 0, as JSON.stringify does; SQLite stores the escape, so rows of up to and above 8 Ki characters hold the same text. <!-- fix: 7570ee804d -->
- A wait of the durable harness (`Submission.Wait`, `WaitForTask`, `WaitForIdle`) whose context was cancelled before its result settled it now fails with the cancellation, as it does in Pi, not with the result. Pi rejects a wait at the abort itself (`Waiters.add` runs the abort listener there), so a later resolve never reaches it; PiG's cancellation reaches the wait on its own goroutine (`context.AfterFunc`), and a result that settled the wait in between was returned instead. A tool that waits for a subagent's submission, aborted with its parent's conversation, could get the child's `unanswered: aborted` record as an ordinary result, not the abort error; the harness's own test for it hung once in 2041 passes on a loaded runner. The durable library's embedders can see it (stock `pig` does not link `durable/harness`); `git tag --contains` names v0.7.0 as the first tag with the code. <!-- fix: a8428a1f79 -->
- A wait of the durable harness (`Submission.Wait`, `WaitForTask`, `WaitForIdle`) whose context was cancelled before the harness closed, or before its Session failed, now fails with the cancellation, as it does in Pi, not with `ErrClosed` or the Session's failure. Pi rejects a wait at the abort itself (`Waiters.add` runs the abort listener there), so a later `rejectAll` never reaches it and the first rejection wins; PiG's cancellation reached the wait on its own goroutine (`context.AfterFunc`), and a close that came in between gave it the close error. The idle pass also counted a wait whose context was cancelled until that goroutine ran. The wait now listens with `chordctx.OnAbort`: for a context made by `chord/context` it is rejected and out of the set when the cancel returns. A context of another package (an embedder's own `context.WithCancel`, a deadline) still reaches the wait on a goroutine of its own, and the harness reads that context's error where the order matters. The durable library's embedders can see it (stock `pig` does not link `durable/harness`): `git tag --contains` names v0.7.0 as the first tag with the code. <!-- fix: 6d4cba03d -->
- A durable `Submission.Wait` or task wait whose context was cancelled while earlier commits were still publishing returns the cancellation cause as the error of that call; a regression test with a slow `Storage.Publishing` (Pi `d9d535b6c9e4`, #11963, #11820) pins it. Pi needed a fix so Node reported no unhandled promise rejection; Go has none, so no Go source changed. <!-- fix: 93cc26e553039e668b45a3ec915c50e57c43588d -->
- A key bound to two editor actions now performs the action Pi performs. The editor checked copy, undo, the autocomplete selection keys, deletion, kill ring, history, movement, newline, submit and paging in an order of its own, so a shared key such as one bound to both undo and cursor left, or to selection cancel and up, did the wrong one. A newline typed while a forced file popup is open closes it, Tab with no completion available ends there instead of acting as another key, and accepting a popup applies it as shown instead of asking the provider again at the new cursor. <!-- fix: 35be5ca502 -->
- An extension editor that fails to take the autocomplete provider no longer ends the session. When the editor installed with `setEditorComponent` throws from `setAutocompleteProvider`, pig now does what Pi does on each path: adding a provider, installing an editor and `/reload` show an extension error (`/reload` shows `Error: Reload failed: <message>` and hands the input back to the previous editor) and the session continues, a settings change raises the uncaught exception, `/new` reports `Error: Failed to create session: <message>` and exits with status 1, and the startup raises the uncaught exception; a bind or a reload now also waits until the editor a `session_start` handler installed is in place, so that editor hears the provider exactly as often as in Pi. Present since 0.3.0, the release in which the host first sent the provider to an installed editor. <!-- fix: f68d3295ea, 5e8dbeb17a -->
- A prompt you submit again, or one restored when you switch branches (`/tree`, `/fork`, `/clone`, `/resume`), no longer appears twice in the up-arrow history; it moves to the front instead of duplicating older entries and pushing history past the 100-entry limit. Affects v0.2.0 through v0.7.0. <!-- fix: 9d587e873d --> <!-- cause: Editor.AddToHistory skipped only a consecutive repeat (inputHistory[0] == trimmed), matching Pi before commit 06a20368a7 (#12370), so re-adding an older prompt appended a duplicate. -->
- Enter on a Tab menu for an absolute path (for example after `look at /tmp/x/fi`) or on a menu of command arguments that start with `/` completes the text and keeps it in the editor; it used to send the unfinished prompt as well. Enter on a command name still runs the command, as in Pi. <!-- fix: 159e2a1922 -->
- The waits that keep upstream's one-thread order no longer return early for a goroutine the Go runtime has stopped for its own work. `entered.Await`, `entered.Go` and `entered.AwaitUnless` took a goroutine that allocates while a collection marks (it waits for assist credit) or scans its stack, or that a trace or a heap dump stops, for one parked in a wait of the program's, and `entered.AwaitBlocked` also took the world lock of a collection that is starting for one. What a caller could see: `chord/output.AwaitCaller` (`SettleInOrder`, `SettleAndAwait`) went on to settle the next `details()` waiter of a commit before the caller of the one before had run to its next await, so the continuations ran out of Pi's order; `durable/codemode` `spawnEntered` returned before the tool call it started was running, so the call that followed it, or the end of the script that aborts it, could come first; and the chord host's `goEntered` closed its channel before the handler had run to its first wait. It needed a collection or a trace at that instant, so it was rare. The first release with it is 0.5.0: `git log --diff-filter=A v0.5.0 -- internal/entered/entered.go` names 9080668e4ab, `git tag --contains` that commit lists v0.5.0 first, and v0.4.1 has no such package. `entered.Classify` is now the one place that reads a goroutine dump entry, and the durable harness's test barrier uses it too, which also ends the intermittent failure of `TestIncrementalIdleStateEqualsAFullRecomputeAfterEveryStepOfRandomNestedWork`. <!-- fix: ad24cdf7f, 8303e4c98 --> <!-- cause: entered.Parked took every state of a goroutine dump except running, runnable, syscall, copystack and preempted for a wait of the program's, so a goroutine the runtime itself had stopped (assist credit, a stack scan, a trace or heap dump stop; for AwaitBlocked also the world lock of a collection) read as parked -->
- The pi-env daemon ended by SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP could end with status 1 and a stray `pi-env: read /dev/stdin: file already closed` instead of 128 plus the signal number (143 for SIGTERM). The signal exit gives the daemon's stdin back by closing the descriptor the serving loop is reading; the loop returned that read error to `main`, which ended the process with status 1 whenever it got there before the signal exit did (a loaded or slow-to-wake host, macOS most often). The signal exit now claims the process first, and the serving loop waits for it to end it. <!-- fix: 6785b03919 -->
- The pi-env daemon on macOS: a small reply (an `lstat`, a ping) could come after megabytes of queued command output, more than a client buffers, where Pi's daemon answers between output frames. The writer now flushes after every frame as Pi's does instead of holding up to 1 MiB, and the daemon waits on its inherited stdin and stdout through the runtime poller, so a request that arrives while the runtime is busy with the output no longer waits up to 10 ms for a worker. <!-- fix: 7fc9ec365 -->
- Windows: the environment daemon's `taskkill /F /T` runs with the `SystemRoot` it resolved for its path (`C:\Windows` when the variable is empty or unset) instead of inheriting an empty one, with which taskkill did not run and left the killed program's tree alive. <!-- fix: 30cdab4dca7d53826a7c440631c6e6599e90bd71 -->
- The pi-env daemon left its stdin and stdout non-blocking for whoever shared them when it ended by SIGTERM or by its silence limit: it moves them into the runtime poller while it runs, which sets O_NONBLOCK on the open file descriptions a parent shell or a wrapper also holds, and only the normal return gave the mode back. Every exit does now, and a thread-panic message written to a stderr that shares a full stdout pipe waits for room instead of being lost. <!-- fix: e77c2e2da -->
- The pi-env daemon ended by SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP could end with status 1 and a stray `pi-env: read /dev/stdin: file already closed` instead of 128 plus the signal number (143 for SIGTERM). The signal exit gives the daemon's stdin back by closing the descriptor the serving loop is reading; the loop returned that read error to `main`, which ended the process with status 1 whenever it got there before the signal exit did (a loaded or slow-to-wake host, macOS most often). The signal exit now claims the process first, and the serving loop waits for it to end it. <!-- fix: f4cc20bae428518080b4cafde1e1fa8cc02d1406 -->
- The pi-env daemon no longer loses the end of a program's output when the program exits while the link is backed up: `process` (and the terminal) ended their wait 100 ms after the exit even though a reader still waited for the link with output left in the pipe, so up to one pipe buffer went missing. Reading now continues while a reader is held (Pi b48c675a912f). <!-- fix: 7c6d3f98216e83d30b07ae3b33829f84d397f4fb -->
- The pi-env daemon no longer loses the end of a program's output when the program exits while the link is backed up: `process` (and the terminal) ended their wait 100 ms after the exit even though a reader still waited for the link with output left in the pipe, so up to one pipe buffer went missing. Reading now continues while a reader is held (Pi b48c675a912f). <!-- fix: 951b35a6af82cdc47099cec0e5b0ef99e3e30f11 -->
- `TestDaemonRepliesBeforeBulkOutputLikePisDaemon` failed on a loaded machine because it started to read before the daemon had queued the reply it measures, so it counted command output that its own reading drained as output "ahead of the reply" (2.7 MB against Pi's own daemon in one CI run). The defect was the test's: no daemon changes. Both daemons send a small reply ahead of the command output still in their queue, and the test bounds the output that arrives ahead of that reply. It read as soon as it had sent its request, or as soon as the request's effect (a `mkdir`) showed, which leaves the time until a worker of the daemon is scheduled to queue the reply: with the `mkdir` wait, 1.57 MB arrived ahead of the reply of PiG's daemon once in 400 runs on a loaded machine. The reply now answers the first of two chunk writes to one handle and the test reads once the second chunk is in the file: a daemon runs a handle's chunk writes in order, so the first reply is queued by then, and exactly one 64 KiB frame is ahead of it on both daemons. The command prints numbered lines instead of zeros, so the test also fails when output is missing, repeated or out of order. <!-- fix: 041d8b85d2 -->
- `TestDaemonRepliesBeforeBulkOutputLikePisDaemon` failed on a loaded machine because it started to read before the daemon had queued the reply it measures, so it counted command output that its own reading drained as output "ahead of the reply" (2.7 MB against Pi's own daemon in one CI run). The defect was the test's: no daemon changes. Both daemons send a small reply ahead of the command output still in their queue, and the test bounds the output that arrives ahead of that reply. It read as soon as it had sent its request, or as soon as the request's effect (a `mkdir`) showed, which leaves the time until a worker of the daemon is scheduled to queue the reply: with the `mkdir` wait, 1.57 MB arrived ahead of the reply of PiG's daemon once in 400 runs on a loaded machine. The reply now answers the first of two chunk writes to one handle and the test reads once the second chunk is in the file: a daemon runs a handle's chunk writes in order, so the first reply is queued by then, and exactly one 64 KiB frame is ahead of it on both daemons. The command prints numbered lines instead of zeros, so the test also fails when output is missing, repeated or out of order. <!-- fix: 88cf2855e3 -->
- Stop and timeouts end remote calls at once while the host is down: a request cancelled while the connection starts ends with `aborted` instead of waiting for the start, a sent request settles as `aborted` when the daemon does not answer its cancel within a second, `RemoteExecutionEnv.Exec` enforces its timeout locally, file operations stop waiting for the connection when cancelled, and `ssh` uses `ConnectTimeout=15`. Follows Pi main c96e368e2 ahead of the pin. <!-- fix: 8c3339c527 -->
- A `turn_end` handler's in-place edit of `event.message` (an `agent_end` handler's of `event.messages`) no longer races with the consumer of `Session.Events`, and no longer reaches the `message_end` and `turn_end` events published before it. The session publishes those two events with the message as it was when the event was published, which is what Pi's listeners, running at the event, see; the transcript, the saved entry, the events published after the edit and the payloads of the extensions follow the edit as before. The consumer reads on its own goroutine and held the one message object the edit overwrites: the race detector reported it (`go test -race`, `TestInPlaceMessageEventEditsMatchPi/subprocess-node-packed/turn_end/deep`), a message serialized during the edit could mix the old and the edited content, and the edit of a custom message clears and refills its member map, a map read while it is written, which is a fatal error in Go. <!-- fix: 1e2d25f16124c04e4bcb618c222f56b1fe438d02 --> <!-- cause: ReplaceMessageInPlace (introduced by 0bed50c8ff) overwrites the members of the one message value the transcript, the saved entry and the message_end and turn_end events hold, and Session.publishAgentEvent sent those events to the consumer of Events, which reads them on its own goroutine, with that same value; a handler's edit at turn_end ran while the consumer read the events published before it. --> <!-- tests: TestEventsConsumerReadsMessagesAsPublishedAcrossLaterInPlaceEdits, TestEventViewIsNotChangedByAReplacementOfTheMessage, TestEventViewIsRaceFreeWithAReplacementOfTheMessage, TestInPlaceMessageEventEditsMatchPi -->
- `pi.exec`: when a command's output exceeds `maxBuffer`, the output pipes are now closed before the command is signalled, as Pi does. PiG signalled first, so a command that was still writing always reported code 143; it now reports 141 when its next write met the closed pipe first (SIGPIPE) and 143 when the SIGTERM came first, as Pi does; the code 1 Pi can still report there is D631. A command that had already exited keeps its own code, 1 for a 0. <!-- fix: 6da170c870d6af4344932b372354f9d94d6d4b7f -->
- The frame that the exit key itself asks for is painted inside the exit's drain now, as Pi paints it, not before the exit starts. Pi's `shutdown()` turns the color scheme reports off, drains the input and only then stops, and the frame requested by Ctrl+D, `/quit`, a second Ctrl+C or a signal's dispose is rendered on the next tick, which falls inside that drain: `?2031l`, the keyboard protocol pop when it is on, the frame, the progress clear, the renderer's stop. PiG painted that frame first, so a recording of the exit showed `frame ?2031l ... progress clear`. The exit holds the renderer's frames from the moment it is decided, and the one requested frame is flushed after the drain, before the active selector is disposed and the progress is cleared. No screen differs for a user; a terminal that records or replays the bytes, and the per-exit-path parity scenarios, saw the order. Present in v0.7.0 (checked by tag: v0.7.0 paints in the key's dispatch, before the exit starts). <!-- tests: internal/codingagent/interactive_exit_frame_flush_pty_test.go::TestExitFrameRequestedByTheExitIsPaintedInsideTheDrain --> <!-- fix: 01c9e0b8fa --> <!-- cause: the input dispatch painted the frame of every key right after the key, and the exit's own key was no exception, although Pi renders it on the next tick, after shutdown() has ended the color scheme reports and while it drains -->
- The terminal progress indicator (`OSC 9;4;0`, with `terminal.showTerminalProgress` on) is turned off when PiG ends after the terminal's color scheme reports are off and the keyboard protocols are popped, as it is in Pi: Pi's shutdown writes those and drains the input before `stop()`, whose first writes are the selector dispose and this clear. PiG wrote the clear first, so a recording of the exit saw it ahead of `CSI ?2031l` and `CSI <u`; the screen a user sees is the same. The order was introduced by the commit that made the exit clear the progress; no release has it. <!-- tests: internal/codingagent/interactive_exit_drain_order_pty_test.go::TestStopInteractiveTuiWritesTheProgressClearAfterTheDrainAsPiDoes --> <!-- fix: e07e1a737a -->
- PiG's raw mode is the one Pi's terminal is in now (libuv's `UV_TTY_MODE_RAW`, which Node's `setRawMode(true)` uses), not the `cfmakeraw` mode of `golang.org/x/term`. While the TUI runs, the kernel turns a line feed into carriage return plus line feed again, as under Pi: a bare `\n` written to the terminal by a child process that shares it (an extension's stray console output, a program the bash tool starts on the terminal, a Go runtime message) returns to column 0 instead of moving straight down and leaving the next text where the previous line ended (the staircase). The input flag `INPCK` is cleared now (PiG left it as the terminal had it), `IGNBRK`, `PARMRK`, `INLCR`, `IGNCR` and `ECHONL` stay as the terminal had them (PiG cleared them; a terminal configured with `INLCR` or `IGNCR` keeps what they do to Enter, as under Pi), and the mode is applied after the output already written has drained, as libuv does. On Windows the console input mode is exactly `ENABLE_WINDOW_INPUT` plus `ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT`, as under Pi: selecting text in the window no longer pauses PiG's output (the quick edit flag is cleared); this part was built and vetted for Windows but not run on a console. The terminal mode the shell gets back at exit is unchanged. Present in every release from v0.2.0 through v0.7.0 (checked by tag: each calls `term.MakeRaw`). <!-- tests: tui/terminal_raw_output_unix_test.go::TestRawModeKeepsTheKernelsNewlineTranslationAsLibuvDoes, tui/terminal_raw_output_unix_test.go::TestRawModeIsTheModePiRecorded --> <!-- fix: 92adb39502 -->
- A Piglet frontend that draws the run no longer has the session resume line (`To resume this session: ...`) written over or under its exit screen: the host writes nothing to the terminal after the frontend closes. The ANSI renderer prints the hint exactly as before, and a run that fell back from the frontend to the ANSI renderer still prints it. <!-- fix: 6334aa7405e70486993af326459936fd79940785 -->
- A SIGTERM or SIGHUP that arrives while PiG is still starting up (the session_start handlers of an extension, the terminal color query, the bind of the session) ends PiG with status 0, as it ends Pi, instead of printing `Error: context canceled` and exiting with status 1. The signal's shutdown ran, and the startup step it interrupted then reported the cancelled root context as a failure. Present in v0.3.0 through v0.7.0 (checked by tag: each runs the signal's shutdown before it cancels the root context and returns the startup error from the run). <!-- tests: internal/codingagent/extension_ui_phase_shutdown_test.go::TestStartupEndedByASignalShutdownIsNotAnError, coding/cli/interactive_signal_stalled_terminal_linux_test.go::TestInteractiveSignalWithAStalledTerminalDeliversShutdownAndEndsOnTheResume --> <!-- fix: 0e061942a9 -->
- The exit's terminal restore is one uninterrupted sequence of writes now: a title an extension sets, an OSC 52 copy and the terminal progress keepalive, which three other goroutines wrote at any moment, no longer land inside the stop's bytes (between the cursor show and the bracketed paste off, between the alternate screen's leave and the transcript print) and, when SIGTERM or SIGHUP ended the session, no longer follow them. Pi's `stop()` is one synchronous call on a single thread, so nothing of its own event loop writes inside it and, after a signal, `process.exit(0)` follows it at once. A recording of the exit, or a terminal that handles the bytes in order, saw an `OSC 0`, an `OSC 52` or an `OSC 9;4` between PiG's reset sequences or after the last of them; the screen a user sees is the same. A write requested before the stop begins is still written, before it (a copy requested just before quit reaches the clipboard); one requested while it runs waits for it and, for a quit by keys, follows it as in Pi (the title Pi's dispose sets); one requested after a signal's stop is dropped, as the exit drops it in Pi. An external editor's or a suspend's stop holds the terminal the same way and gives it back when the TUI starts again. Present in every release from v0.2.0 through v0.7.0 (checked by tag: v0.2.0 and v0.7.0 each write the title, the progress keepalive and the OSC 52 copy from goroutines of their own, outside the restore). <!-- tests: internal/codingagent/interactive_exit_storm_pty_test.go::TestExitStopSequenceHoldsNoWriterOfAnotherGoroutine, internal/codingagent/terminal_stop_transaction_test.go::TestHostWriteRequestedBeforeTheStopIsWrittenBeforeIt, internal/codingagent/terminal_stop_transaction_test.go::TestHostWriteMadeAfterTheStopIsDroppedForASignalOnly, tui/stop_transaction_test.go::TestSealedStopDropsTheForeignWritesMadeDuringItAndAfterIt, tui/stop_transaction_test.go::TestForeignWriteStormHoldsNoByteInsideAStop --> <!-- fix: 83ee534a7d -->
- interactive mode: when it ended, PiG wrote an empty terminal title (`ESC ] 0 ; BEL`) and a clear of the terminal progress indicator (`ESC ] 9 ; 4 ; 0 BEL`) whatever `terminal.showTerminalProgress` said, and on a quit it wrote both after the renderer had stopped. Pi writes no empty title, and clears the progress indicator only when the setting is on, before the renderer stops. PiG now writes the same: on ctrl+d, ctrl+c twice, `/quit`, SIGTERM and SIGHUP the terminal receives the session title once, and the progress clear only with the setting on. Present in releases 0.2.0 to 0.7.0. <!-- fix: 770a98ad1e121d07ddbaaa300ab1e00e28512984 -->
- The terminal title that a session sets (the session name, or an extension's title) is written where Pi writes it when PiG ends: for a quit by keys (Ctrl+D, Ctrl+C twice, `/quit`) before the "To resume this session" line, and for SIGTERM and SIGHUP before the terminal is restored. PiG wrote it only when the runtime closed, after the exit had restored the terminal and, for a quit, after the resume hint, so a terminal or a recording of the exit saw the title last. A signal that arrives while the quit's last steps are running, or a terminal that has stopped taking output, no longer holds the title write or the exit behind each other. Present in v0.3.0 through v0.7.0 (checked by tag: each runs the title hook only when the runtime closes). <!-- fix: 154d2c5776 -->
- A fullscreen or inline exit writes the cursor show and bracketed paste off (`CSI ?25h`, `CSI ?2004l`) in Pi's order now: before the alternate screen is left (`CSI ?1049l`) and, for a fullscreen exit that prints the transcript, once more after it, with no further cursor show after the last bracketed paste off. PiG wrote them only after the alternate screen was left and added a trailing cursor show. A terminal that handles the resets in order, or a recording of the exit bytes, now sees Pi's order; the screen a user sees is the same. Present in every release from v0.2.0 through v0.7.0 (checked by tag: v0.2.0, v0.5.3 and v0.7.0 each stop the renderer first and write the bracketed paste off in the terminal restore after it). <!-- fix: 71e0f20510 -->
- `/export` HTML no longer shows raw terminal hyperlink escape codes around links in custom tool output; http, https and mailto links are clickable and other escape sequences are dropped, as Pi does (upstream #12052). <!-- fix: 4669953e23 -->
- `/export` HTML no longer shows raw terminal hyperlink escape codes around links in custom tool output; http, https and mailto links are clickable and other escape sequences are dropped, as Pi does (upstream #12052). <!-- fix: 909154b71765513ecb374dc6d35e599aa4f97f4d -->
- An extension that calls `ctx.abort()` from an event handler in interactive mode no longer stops the session from answering. The abort action waited for the turn to end, and the turn waited for the handler that made the call, so the call never returned: the turn stayed open and no later prompt was answered. The call now starts the abort and returns, as in Pi, for extensions of the Node, Go, Python, Rust and Lisp SDKs, and the run's `ctx.signal` is already aborted when it returns, even while the interactive loop is busy with earlier work. An extension that needs the turn to have ended cannot wait for it inside the handler the turn awaits, because the turn is waiting for that handler: it waits outside it, with `ctx.waitForIdle()` in a command handler (Pi offers that call on the command context only) or by acting from an `agent_settled` handler. Present in 0.2.0 through 0.7.0. <!-- fix: 6dddc19157, a289ab6116, a14dd43d7b -->
- Checking for available package updates now queries at most four npm registries or Git remotes at a time, as Pi does, instead of five. <!-- fix: 5213caba73 -->
- A line an extension wrote to its stderr or stdout just before pig ended could be lost: with `--mode rpc` (stdin ended, a signal, `ctx.shutdown()`), with Ctrl+C in the interactive mode, when the terminal went away, and when a replaced session's extension was still running at exit, pig stopped the extension processes and exited without waiting for the copy of their output to reach its own stderr and the extension's log. Seen as a failing listener's `Event handler error (...)` line that was sometimes missing from the output of a docs example. Pig now waits for that copy, for Node, Python, Go and Rust extensions alike, isolated or packed. The wait ends after five seconds for all extension processes of all sessions together, so an extension whose descendant keeps the output open cannot hold pig back; pig then prints one line saying how many extension processes had not finished and that their undelivered output is dropped. The extension's own log file gets the same lines. The ordinary quit paths (print mode, an interactive quit by keys, `/quit`) already waited for the processes and are unchanged. <!-- fix: 1147e7735a0204c5ca2b546728f7e99f62a0188d -->
- After an external `kill -TSTP <pid>` (from a supervisor, `pkill -TSTP`, or another pane), pig stops without resetting the terminal, so mouse tracking, hidden cursor, Kitty keyboard flags, bracketed paste, the fullscreen alternate screen, and under `dash` raw terminal settings stay active at the shell prompt until `fg`; previously, `fg` also left the terminal in the shell's state without re-entering or redrawing the TUI. Interactive mode now re-arms raw mode, paste, keyboard, mouse, and screen modes on `fg` (forcing a full redraw on fullscreen and regular ANSI renderers and resuming the session on frontend surfaces, which draws what changed), including during startup once the terminal is armed, after a background `bg` (which re-stops pig until `fg`), and under shells that restore saved raw terminal settings on `fg`, while leaving external-editor handoffs and `Ctrl+Z` unchanged (follows Pi `e4f50d76`, `3107a58d`; record D661). <!-- fix: f36632c6eed5f18a4ff765418d15ba48a34228dd --> <!-- cause: interactive mode had no SIGCONT re-arm handler tied to process-terminal ownership, so resuming after an external SIGTSTP left the terminal in the shell's state without re-entering or redrawing the TUI -->
- A failed extension load could report a less specific error than the extension's stderr gave. When a Go, Rust, Python or Lisp runner failed its only member and exited at once, the host read the stderr log before its copy had forwarded the runner's last line, so a factory that returned nothing after a host helper call was reported as a bare "connection closed before register", while the same factory in a shared cell reported "factory returned nil". The host now waits for that copy to end, within two seconds, before it reads the cause. <!-- fix: 536faf0fb -->
- When `/new`, `/fork`, `/resume` or `/reload` ends in a fatal error ("Failed to create session" and its kin, exit status 1), `pig` now ends the replacement session's extension processes before it exits, as its signal and RPC exits already did. They used to be left to end on their own for a moment after `pig` had gone (since v0.5.0), so a script or a test that removed `pig`'s home directory right after the exit could fail with "directory not empty": a Node extension writes its compile cache when its process ends. <!-- fix: 52f29278c2 --> <!-- cause: the exit that follows a fatal runtime error released only the startup extension host, so the processes of a replacement session's host, started later by the session factory, were never ended by it. -->
- Typing `@` in the editor, the `find` and `grep` tools and the tools status no longer treat a program that is not fd or ripgrep as one. Debian's `fdclone` package installs a file manager as `/usr/bin/fd`; it opened `/dev/tty` and took over the terminal, and it hid a real fd installed as `fdfind`. A system `fd`, `fdfind` or `rg` is now used only if `<bin> --version` exits 0 and prints `fd `, `fdfind ` or `ripgrep ` first; otherwise PiG tries the next name and then downloads its own, and the tools status no longer counts the impostor as installed. The check runs once per binary (cached by path, modification time and size), in a new session with stdin on `/dev/null` and a 5 s bound, and starts the program the way the searches do. The `@` search also runs fd in a new session, and on Windows without a visible console window. Pi has the same bug. <!-- fix: 4d731f2eec, 39b6e4dbe3 -->
- The find tool no longer returns no results for patterns that start with `./`, such as `./src/*.ts`; the leading `./` is dropped, as under Pi (upstream #12020). <!-- fix: 2b29409f01b0b6937a4572c237164e474ed30bd3 -->
