- The find tool no longer returns no results for patterns that start with `./`, such as `./src/*.ts`; the leading `./` is dropped, as under Pi (upstream #12020). <!-- fix: ac7ebbf1a5 -->
- An interactive start in a project whose AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md is large no longer keeps three copies of the system prompt in memory. The CLI, the Session and the interactive mode each rendered the same prompt text and each kept it; the Session and the interactive mode now keep the CLI's string when their rendering is equal, so the live heap at the first frame is 130 KB smaller in this repository (2,155,000 B before, 2,025,000 B after, `process.interactive_first_frame.heap_live_bytes`). The prompt text is unchanged. <!-- fix: ce4df6b13ca7 -->
- After a Radius sign-in, accepting the offer to configure the Radius MCP server updates the chat (its notices, the reload status and the last paint) on the interactive loop, as Pi's single-threaded TUI does, and no longer from the login's own goroutine, where it raced the loop's status line (a data race the nightly race job reported). <!-- fix: c6fb79537 -->
- Interactive mode: when the first message flushed from the compaction queue was rejected (a `before_agent_start` handler that fails, a missing model, an input handler error), a message queued behind it could start a run of its own if the rejection had already ended the first run, and be rejected for the same cause, so "Failed to send queued messages" was shown twice. The rejection is now recorded when the run finds it, and a message behind it is neither sent nor queued; the whole queue comes back with one failure shown. <!-- fix: f81ce001e32 -->
- `/resume` no longer selects an unrelated session while its list reloads after a session is deleted or renamed: the selected session stays selected through the partial lists of the reload. <!-- fix: 7838047e30 -->
- Kitty and iTerm2 images no longer cover an overlay drawn over them. An image that an overlay overlaps by row and column is removed while the overlay is open and drawn again when it closes, on the main screen and in fullscreen mode; an image beside an overlay, such as a sidebar, stays visible. <!-- fix: 959646e66a -->
- A Node extension start no longer loads pi-tui's text-width module; it loads when an image line is first measured. Cause: the Node runtime loads pi-tui's terminal-image module at every start (the runtime hands it the host's terminal capabilities, and the theme's colour mode reads them from it), and the backport of Pi 787005a40 made that module import the width module for its image-line extent, so the merge that brought the backport loaded the width tables at every start. No released PiG had this: the import arrives with that merge. <!-- fix: 6f949d9716 -->
- `enabledModels`/`--models` warnings such as `No models match pattern "github-copilot/nope"` are reported with the other startup diagnostics: in the chat in interactive mode, where they were a raw stderr line printed before the TUI started, and on stderr in print, JSON and RPC modes, after the settings and extension diagnostics. A pattern given twice is reported once (Pi #11973). <!-- fix: 8a4185de22 -->
- The find tool matched path patterns through folders above the search path: with the project in `~/src/app`, `src/**/*.ts` returned every `.ts` file in the project (Pi #12066). <!-- fix: f0c8b9662f -->
- `/copy`, the copy key, RPC `get_last_assistant_text` and a child session's `getLastAssistantText` now skip a turn that ended without an answer. After Esc during a tool call or after a provider error they copy or return the previous answer; before, `/copy` said `No agent messages to copy yet.` and RPC returned `null` while the answer was on screen. An assistant message without text is skipped when its turn did not end normally (aborted, failed, only tool calls, or cut at the length limit); a reply that ended normally without text is still the last reply. Follows Pi #12121 (ede360e4d). <!-- fix: 4f6214356835a674ca9370bf2b9309cca21b3533 -->
- A Node extension that draws Pi's `ToolExecutionComponent` for a tool that renders itself (`renderShell: "self"`) no longer fails with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` when the tool's result draws about 125,000 rows or more: the bundled Node runtime carries Pi's fix (Pi #12145). PiG's own interactive screen draws tool cards in Go and never had this limit. <!-- fix: 37c6264b53 -->
- A Codex turn that hits the backend's 60 minute WebSocket limit (`websocket_connection_limit_reached`, "Responses websocket connection limit reached") after output has started, for example during long thinking, is now retried by the agent's auto-retry on a fresh connection instead of failing the turn: you see the retry notice, the interrupted response is redone from the start with the full context, its partial output stays in the session file and on screen but is left out of the retry's context, and no tool runs twice. The retry classifier is shared, so durable and compaction recover the same way. New requests also stop reusing a cached WebSocket after 45 minutes instead of 55, so a long response is less likely to reach the limit; this costs one full-context request per rotation, at most once per 45 minutes (since v0.2.0 the limit was not retried mid-stream). An error after the first WebSocket event, a leading `codex.rate_limits` included, now ends the message in an error that the agent retries, as in Pi; before, PiG reconnected or fell back to SSE inside the provider (since v0.3.0), which a user saw as a silent second request and no retry notice. Follows Pi bb1a2b3542b5: Fixed the OpenAI Codex WebSocket 60-minute connection limit failing the turn when it hit mid-stream, for example during long thinking. The error is now retried on a fresh connection, and new requests stop reusing a cached connection after 45 minutes instead of 55, so a long response is less likely to reach the limit (#12124). <!-- fix: e098b6491f50ea0447e0a0f2975c096e7d387c1c -->
- `read` no longer stores a note that the current model does not support images, which was replayed to the model as stale text after a switch to a vision model. The image is still replaced with a placeholder per request for a model without image input; the read result names that model in `details.imageUnsupportedByModel`, and the read card shows `[<model> does not support images; it saw a placeholder instead]` from it, collapsed and expanded. A session that already holds the old note keeps it as written. The durable `read` no longer adds the matching `info` diagnostic and names the model in its details the same way (Pi 4be4cb4f5e9c, #12139). <!-- fix: dec362c82f -->
- A connection failure with no status or body keeps its cause in the error message, for example `Connection error.: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:8080` on `openai-completions`, `openai-responses` and `anthropic-messages` (`fetch failed: connect ECONNREFUSED ...` elsewhere), instead of only the generic text. <!-- fix: 2d3121b71c -->
- A gateway's `cut short after the reply had begun` stream error is retried like other dropped streams. <!-- fix: 2d3121b71c -->
- A response stream dropped mid-run reports `terminated: other side closed (UND_ERR_SOCKET)` on `openai-completions`, `openai-responses`, `google` and `anthropic-messages`, as Pi does, instead of `terminated (cause: ...)`. <!-- fix: 8f241ca2fd -->
- Requests through the built-in HTTP client refuse the ports the Fetch standard blocks (for example 1, 25, 6000) with `fetch failed: bad port`, as Node's fetch does. <!-- fix: ac42ce189e -->
- A `pig_strip_codemode` build no longer links the code mode sandbox or wazero through tool search. <!-- fix: 083db0c482 -->
- `pig auth login` reports "Login cancelled." for any login that fails with that message, as Pi does, including the providers that create their own cancelled error. <!-- fix: 40b12101e0 -->
- A custom message or a compaction summary drawn live (`pi.sendMessage`, an extension's boundary compaction) hands Markdown transformers no `messageId` or `timestamp`, as Pi does; only a restored transcript carries the entry's. <!-- fix: 40b12101e0 -->
- Custom messages, skill blocks, summaries and the changelog run extension Markdown transformers off the render loop, so a slow extension no longer stalls a frame, and they are only redrawn each frame while an extension registered a transformer. <!-- fix: 40b12101e0 -->
- A finished MCP sign-in whose single-use verifier could not be removed afterwards is still reported as authorized. <!-- fix: 40b12101e0 -->
- MCP credential files that are symlinks are written through the link, and the directory is synced after the replace. <!-- fix: 40b12101e0 -->
- A custom message renderer is called once, not twice, when a message is drawn. <!-- fix: 54660cf133 -->
- chord: `Plugins.Build` discovers again when a named plugin is unknown to discovery or a file discovery found for it is gone, so a plugin deleted (or written) just before a build is removed (or added) even when the watcher's events lag (Pi 822b37a27). <!-- fix: dd06fc5665 -->
- chord tutorial: chapter VI waits for the app's base code to be watched before it adds the Harbor plugin, so file events dropped while a watch is added no longer leave it waiting (Pi f2bd84a51). <!-- fix: dd06fc5665 -->
- chord: base bundles collect the fonts and images their stylesheets name: a base stylesheet with `url()` fonts, images or WebAssembly no longer fails to build with "No loader is configured"; they are files under `assets/`, named by their content (Pi da44c4df3). <!-- fix: 6005946dcd -->
- chord: a client starts without its server (a page renders offline, from a service worker's kept page): `StartClient` follows the scripts object in the background, a failure reported as `update_failed`, and `Client.Stop` ends and joins it; the set the scripts object shows when following begins is applied too, so a set published while the client started is no longer missed (Pi 3c771bd18). <!-- fix: a24f919546 -->
- ai: a non-strict Anthropic tool schema keeps its root `additionalProperties` (false, true or a schema), so Claude is told whether extra arguments are allowed; root `anyOf`, `oneOf` and `allOf` stay out (Pi aa47cedce, #12100). <!-- fix: f51de47842 -->
- A turn that ends with a provider error that reports only a socket error code, such as `read ECONNRESET`, `write EPIPE` or `connect ETIMEDOUT`, or with `connection reset by peer`, is now retried automatically like other dropped connections, instead of stopping with the error; this is what Amazon Bedrock reports when a connection fails before a response. The same applies in the extension SDKs' `isRetryableAssistantError` (Go, Python, Rust, Lisp and the Node runtime). <!-- fix: 386b88c3b69 -->
- Pressing Esc during a batch of tool calls left the calls that had not started yet without a result in the session: the transcript held an assistant message with tool calls that no tool result answered. Each of those calls now gets its start and end events and an "Operation aborted" error result, and extension `tool_call` handlers are not asked about a call that will not run. A call whose `tool_call` handler in an extension process was still deciding when the run was aborted now reads "Operation aborted" too, where it read "event tool_call: context canceled". `ctx.executeTool` answers an aborted run the same way, before it looks the tool up. A session that an older build left with unanswered calls still opens and continues as before. Follows Pi 4438c58ba ([#9986](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9986)). <!-- fix: 2653e628346be00041b278e63003cbbdb20ad3ea -->
- chord: a client whose link dropped while it was away (a laptop or phone woken, a network changed) reconnects at once instead of first waiting for its `CanRetry` check: with a check that takes 3 s, the next attempt went 3 250 ms after the wake and now goes at 0 ms. The wait happened because the connection loop scheduled its next attempt only once `CanRetry` had answered. `KeepConnected` now asks `CanRetry` beside the next attempt, one question at a time (a link that drops while a question is open asks nothing more); a late `false` still stops the loop and ends the attempt made meanwhile, which is reported `waiting`; a drop within 26 s of a wake is retried at once, once per wake, and the replacement of a silent socket no longer waits a pause. `StartClient` stops the loop before it calls `Outdated`, so the app starts over with the link already ended. The vendored page and plugin runtimes carry the same change (Pi 21e4cb80d: `surfaces/connection.ts`, `surfaces/client.ts`, `web/page.ts`). The old loop is in v0.2.0, v0.3.0 and v0.7.0. <!-- fix: acc14924dfa886d3ce2b1914293cc757906cce54, 6e061374e278c20fadb251fd4cbae1b613e3fa60 -->
- chord: a server that is still loading its plugins refuses requests and links with 503, as Pi's does, instead of answering them. A page that reconnected to a restarted server in that time (about 220 ms in the run that found it; the page's first retry comes after 250 ms) was connected, shown the scripts object's empty set, took its base for another one and reloaded: what the page held was lost (the server's state was kept). This happened because the Go server host loads its own facets first and its plugins after, in the Node plugin host, and its HTTP component answered once the first of the two were loaded, where Pi's one host loads both in one `load` and its HTTP component refuses until that ended (`not_ready`). The HTTP component now sees the server host's registries only once the plugins are loaded. The fix is commit aa77aa9c2f1d3eccb4597259bdf1440915b97215; its message names the divergence of the server's two hosts (number 605 in docs/parity/DIVERGENCES.md) because the defect exists only where those two hosts exist, and the fix does not close or change that divergence. In no release: the app kit (`chord/nextnode/app`) is in none of v0.2.0, v0.3.0 and v0.7.0. <!-- fix: bedd7ec384b07d94b5b28e1aa685b4e800ca33ca -->
- GitHub Copilot's chat-completions models with effort levels (Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini 3.8 Flash and Kimi K3) now receive the selected thinking level: the request carries `reasoning_effort`, where before the level was never sent and the model always ran at its default; these models now offer their own levels (low, medium and high for the Gemini models; low, high and max for Kimi K3). Reasoning tokens that a chat-completions provider reports at the top level of `usage` (`usage.reasoning_tokens`, as GitHub Copilot does) are now counted in the usage's reasoning figure instead of showing as 0; output tokens, total tokens and cost are unchanged. Follows Pi #12110. <!-- fix: 77e64cd2af4 -->
- chord: a watched derive that was read between two changes of its source in one commit published two frames, the first diffed from the value read in between; over a link that was the protocol error `member twice in one state`, which closed the link (Pi f6600b58f347). It publishes one frame per commit now, diffed from the value before the commit. A failure read in between and again at the end now reaches its watches. <!-- fix: 6acd45c40ca1 -->
- chord: a list or live query whose value was set several times in one commit (a list's row moving from one loaded page to another) published one frame per set; over a link that was two entries for one member in one state message, the protocol error `member twice in one state`, which closed the link (Pi 36c709e720b6). It publishes one frame per commit now: its last value, diffed from the value before the commit. <!-- fix: 94a2516ddeb8 -->
- ai: Mistral Large 4 tool calls no longer stall for minutes. The model went silent before a tool call when the tools carried `strict: true`, which PiG sent on every Mistral request since 0.2.0; with strict off the call arrives in seconds (Pi 2c2a77f9f3ab, #12148). <!-- fix: 9b302729ad --> <!-- cause: buildChatPayload passed true as the strict-tools default to toFunctionTools, so every Mistral tool that asked for JSON-schema constrained sampling carried strict true and a converted schema, and Mistral Large 4 spends minutes before a call to a strict tool; the default is now the model's compat.supportsStrictMode, false when absent. --> <!-- tests: ai/mistral_tool_schema_upstream_test.go::TestMistralToolsAreNonStrictUnlessTheModelEnablesStrictMode, ai/mistral_test.go::TestMistralToolsWithoutStrictMode, ai/mistral_strict_mode_oracle_test.go::TestMistralStrictToolsRequestBodyMatchesPi -->
- Follows Pi c47ad0432bb8 (#12115, related to #11264): problems found when the session is replaced with `/new`, `/resume`, `/fork`, an import or RPC `new_session`, `switch_session` and `fork` (and an extension's `ctx.newSession()`, `switchSession()` and `fork()`) were never shown: the runtime kept the diagnostics of the replacement and only the startup read them, so a project extension that fails to load after `/resume` into another project, invalid settings of that project, or an `enabledModels` pattern that matches nothing after a settings change gave no chat line, no stderr line and no event. Interactive mode now shows them in the chat, print, JSON and RPC modes write them to stderr (RPC never writes them to stdout), and a problem already reported is not repeated. The new `AgentSessionRuntime.takeUnreportedDiagnostics()` (Go `TakeUnreportedDiagnostics`, Rust, Python and Lisp `take_unreported_diagnostics`) gives an SDK host each diagnostic once at startup and after each replacement. <!-- cause: the runtime stored the replacement's diagnostics and no mode read them after startup; present since v0.5.1 (the runtime's Diagnostics field); the report is new with the change --> <!-- fix: 6f6f6bab9a --> <!-- tests: TestTakeUnreportedDiagnosticsReturnsEachDiagnosticOnceAtStartupAndAfterReplacements, TestRPCReportsADiagnosticThatFirstAppearsOnNewSessionOnStderrOnce -->
- Follows Pi beffcde92dea (#12230, #10470): in RPC mode `new_session`, `switch_session`, `fork` and `clone` run an extension's `session_start` handlers once for the new session, with the old session's `session_shutdown` before it, as Pi's RPC mode does since this commit; before they ran twice (the runtime's rebind callback, then the command handler's own rebind), so an extension that started a timer in `session_start` and cleared it in `session_shutdown` leaked one timer per replacement and `appendEntry` in `session_start` wrote its entry twice. The RPC mode also subscribes to the session's events before the extensions are bound, at startup and on replacement: the events a `session_start` handler emits (`entry_appended`, `session_info_changed`, a message it sends) now reach the client, in the order they happen and ahead of the command's response; before the client received none of them at startup and a replacement's first bind wrote nothing. The same for every extension SDK (Node, Go, Python, Rust and Lisp, isolated, packed and fused). Pi's CHANGELOG line: "Fixed RPC `new_session`, `switch_session`, `fork` and `clone` running extension `session_start` and `resources_discover` handlers twice for the new session. RPC clients now also receive events emitted by `session_start` handlers, such as `entry_appended` for entries they append (#10470)". The bug has been in PiG since v0.3.0. <!-- cause: PiG ported Pi's rpc-mode (as of v1.5.2), whose command handlers called the rebind a second time after the runtime's rebind callback had already run it (rpcHost.rebindAgain), and which subscribed to the session events only after the extensions were bound, so the second bind ran session_start again and the first bind's events had no listener --> <!-- tests: coding/cli/rpc_session_start_once_upstream_test.go::TestRPCNewSessionRunsSessionStartOnceUpstream, coding/cli/rpc_session_start_once_upstream_test.go::TestRPCSwitchSessionRunsSessionStartOnceUpstream, coding/cli/rpc_session_start_once_upstream_test.go::TestRPCForkRunsSessionStartOnceUpstream, coding/cli/rpc_session_start_once_upstream_test.go::TestRPCCloneRunsSessionStartOnceUpstream, coding/cli/rpc_session_start_once_upstream_test.go::TestRPCStreamsEntriesAppendedByTheStartupSessionStartUpstream, coding/cli/rpc_writer_after_session_start_test.go::TestRPCWritesSessionStartEmissionsOnceInEverySDK, test/extension-conformance/rpc_session_start_once_test.go::TestRPCSessionReplacementRunsSessionStartOnceInEverySDK --> <!-- fix: 4da149a9792aa51240e2282c6b22f43e7cf598c7 -->
- Follows Pi 6aab551a79ba: `--mode json` dropped the events emitted by extension `session_start` handlers, such as `entry_appended` for entries they append, `session_info_changed` for a name they set and the `message_start` and `message_end` of a custom message they send, at startup and after an extension replaces the session (`ctx.newSession()`). The JSON writer now subscribes before the extensions are bound, so these events follow the session header and come before the prompt's events. The fault is in v0.7.0. <!-- fix: c28880ae3e71 -->
- Follows Pi e03dca7a3843: `Session.Reload` (and the reload of every SDK's `AgentSession`) did not emit `session_start` to the extensions when the host had bound them with `BindExtensions` and no bindings (the Go counterpart of `bindExtensions({})`), after it had already emitted `session_shutdown`. Extensions that start work in `session_start`, such as the MCP extension connecting its servers, stayed stopped after a reload. A reload now restarts the extensions of every session whose host called `BindExtensions`; a session that was never bound behaves as before, and the print, JSON, RPC and interactive modes were not affected. The fault is in v0.7.0. <!-- fix: 7236618f972d -->
- Follows Pi c8c456c85c6e (#12234, same class as #12115): when the saved model of a session you resume, fork or continue no longer exists or has no login, the model Pi falls back to is now reported in every mode and after every replacement. The warning `Could not restore model <provider>/<id>. Using <provider>/<id>` was shown only at interactive startup; `/resume` and `/fork` into such a session, and RPC `switch_session` and `fork`, changed models without a word, and print, JSON and RPC mode never showed it even at startup. Interactive mode now shows it in the chat, above `Resumed session` after `/resume`, and print, JSON and RPC mode write `Warning: <message>` to stderr (RPC never writes it to stdout); a message already reported is not repeated (a second `/resume` into the same session shows nothing, a fallback to a different model shows its own line). The fallback model rule is unchanged (the saved model if it has a login, else the default model, else the first available model of the shared provider order). <!-- cause: the fallback message was read only by interactive startup through the modelFallbackMessage option; the runtime recomputed it on each replacement and nothing reported it, and the print and RPC runtime inputs never carried it; present since v0.3.0 (the startup model's ModelFallbackMessage) --> <!-- fix: 8f2ed99753 --> <!-- tests: TestRPCSwitchSessionReportsTheModelFallbackOnStderr, TestRPCStartAndForkReportTheModelFallbackOnStderr, TestPrintAndJSONReportTheModelFallbackOnStderr, TestNoModelsAvailableIsReportedOnceAsAWarning -->
- Follows Pi 18e99051be24: an extension's `pi.events` handler that threw was printed on the terminal behind the TUI (`Event handler error (<channel>)`), which corrupted the interactive screen. It is now reported like the error of a `pi.on` handler, in every SDK: in the chat in interactive mode, as `extension_error` in RPC mode and as `Extension error (...)` in print mode, with the extension's path, the event `events:<channel>`, the message and the stack. The error of a handler that fails after its session was replaced, or after a failed reload left its runner stale, is dropped, as is one that fails before the mode attaches its error listener. Every release since 0.7.0 has the fault. <!-- fix: 52a25ee0669c -->
- In the interactive mode, an extension's `pi.setModel` whose extension has `model_select` handlers could leave the footer on the previous model's context window until the next keystroke. The model changed at once, but the footer was pushed only after the handlers replied, so a frame drawn in between (a key press, a stream tick) came from the cached footer and no render followed. The footer now changes in the same owner-loop unit as the session's model, and the handlers are awaited after it, off the owner loop. This has been so since v0.7.0 (the first tag with the extension `setModel` path). <!-- fix: 0b5f9bd080 --> <!-- cause: the extension setModel path awaited the model_select handlers between the session's model change and the footer push, and the push only invalidated the footer without requesting a render, where /model and model cycling push it in the same owner-loop unit --> <!-- tests: TestInteractiveExtensionSetModelShowsTheNewWindowWhileItsHandlersAreStillReplying, TestExtensionSetModelOnMainMutatesInsideTheDispatcherAndAwaitsTheHandlersAfterIt, TestInteractiveExtensionSetModelAfterNewKeepsRegisteredMetadata -->
- The footer no longer shows `0.0%/0 (auto)` for a model the remote model catalog carries and the bundled catalog lacks (for example `github-copilot/claude-fable-5.2`). A resumed session, a `/model` switch and an extension's `setModel` built such a model without its context window and prices, so the context estimate was unknown and automatic compaction had no window to compare against; the startup model took the window and prices of the provider's default model. Every path now builds the model from the catalog entry the model runtime returns, with the remote catalog's window, limits and prices. <!-- fix: 72f75e5e7 -->
- `FormatTime` returns an options error for an instant outside JavaScript's Date range (more than 8.64e15 ms from the epoch), where Pi's `Intl.DateTimeFormat.format` throws a RangeError; it printed a clock time for it before. The ends of the range are still formatted. <!-- fix: 5e006747d9 --> <!-- cause: D465 recorded the out-of-range instant as formatted because Go has no invalid Date, but no range check on the time value was ever added. -->
- In interactive mode the frame that draws a reply could leave the Working indicator on screen for a second frame to take away, where Pi draws both in one frame: the 16 ms frame timer could fire between two events of the end of a response. The events that Pi's event loop handles in one task (the part of a response its provider delivered in one run, and behind it `message_end`, the tool starts, `turn_end` and `agent_end`) are now applied together, so a frame draws all of them or none. Print mode, RPC mode and SDK consumers of `Session.Events` receive the events they received before. <!-- fix: db38fad50e14e6d46ccf9df95fbe0559dd8a8f3d -->
- In interactive mode a frame that changed no row could follow the frame that carries a reply, when the frame timer fired before the clean-up at the end of the turn reached the screen loop. The clean-up now paints only a frame that is still owed or rows it changed. <!-- fix: 99faf6640197823f981b69bb8b8ad35d31a6225f -->
- Sessions built with both caller-supplied custom tools (`SessionOptions.Tools`, `SessionOptions.CustomTools`, or `SessionStartOptions.ExtraTools`) and extension-registered tools saw a tool-prefix mismatch between a fresh session (`[built-ins, caller custom tools, extension tools]`) and its clone or post-reload session (`[built-ins, extension tools, caller custom tools]`), causing a provider prompt-cache miss; fresh sessions now declare tools in Pi's order (`[built-ins, extension tools, caller custom tools]`) and `Session.Clone` seeds the clone with the source session's active tool order. Existing persisted sessions keep their transcript's recorded tool order and an unchanged tool prefix on resume with no tool-state churn record. A session created with its own active tool order (InitialActiveToolNames) and cloned before its first prompt now keeps that order in the clone; before, the clone listed the same tools in registry order. Affects 0.3.0, 0.3.1, 0.4.0, 0.4.1, 0.5.0, 0.5.1, 0.5.2, 0.5.3, and 0.7.0. <!-- fix: 6a5633658b --> <!-- cause: createSessionToolRegistry appended caller custom tool names to activeNames before extension tool names, and Session.Clone did not pass InitialActiveToolNames to preserve the source session's active tool order --> <!-- tests: TestFreshAndCloneToolOrderMatchesPi -->
- Fullscreen scrolling in long sessions no longer re-renders the whole transcript on every wheel event and key press ([#9549](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9549)). <!-- fix: 0d09de822e -->
- Containers no longer copy every rendered line of every nesting level on every frame ([#9549](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9549)). <!-- fix: f4700463a2 -->
- Column slicing of printable ASCII text is faster, as in Pi ([#9549](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9549)). <!-- fix: 008b787556 -->
- A Piglet Binary with a fused extension no longer leaves a log file in the temporary directory after the session ends, and creates none unless an extension handler fails. <!-- fix: c96c624b89 -->
- A Gemini 3 or later model addressed by a prefixed ID (such as `google/gemini-3-pro`, `models/gemini-3-flash`, `publishers/google/models/gemini-3.1-pro`, or `randomprefix-gemini-4-argon`, as through a gateway) now gets tool-call IDs, strict tool sampling (`VALIDATED` mode), and nested multimodal function responses like the unprefixed ID, while prefixed Gemini 2.x IDs keep separate user turns for tool-result images; a custom Google Generative AI or Vertex model can also declare `compat.supportsStrictMode` to override version-based strict-tool detection. Affects v0.2.0 through v0.7.0. <!-- fix: 07a11152c4b47c1cbd727c8601900d7cede5bff0 --> <!-- cause: c318b7716369e00310092c987a9243c9a8d4a1a3; Pi fe8a6f5dc741e9214a20f70f359c68c72b494d1e (#12371) -->
- Google (`google-generative-ai`): a request that fails before the response starts is reported with its cause, as Pi 1.5.2 does: `fetch failed: read ECONNRESET` for a connection the server reset, `fetch failed: other side closed (UND_ERR_SOCKET)` for one it closed, `fetch failed: bad port` for a base URL on a port that fetch refuses. It was a bare `fetch failed` in each case. <!-- fix: 1662063665 --> <!-- cause: the cause detail was switched on only for the stream builder made after the response headers, so a failure before them was formatted without it -->
- The Go SDK's start-order tests no longer fail on a loaded machine since v0.5.2 (a test-claim fix: the SDK is unchanged). The SDK guarantees the order in which handlers are invoked: a handler is invoked only after every earlier request's handler was invoked or its request ended without one. The tests asserted the order of the handlers' first statements, which is more than that, and a goroutine the operating system holds back after its place was released is overtaken by the handlers behind it, so one of 300 runs failed under one-CPU pressure. The tests now read the order where the SDK keeps it, and a new test holds one handler back to show that the invocation order stays intact while the first statements do not. <!-- fix: 1d5b4bb0fe --> <!-- cause: the tests asserted first-statement order, which is more than the SDK's invocation-order contract, and a goroutine descheduled between the release of its place and its handler's first statement is overtaken --> <!-- tests: TestEventAndCommandHandlersStartInArrivalOrder, TestToolCallHandlersStartInArrivalOrder, TestOvertakenHandlerKeepsItsInvocationPlace -->
- A Pi extension that starts the harness again (`process.execPath process.argv[1] ...`) and ends it with SIGKILL no longer leaves the PiG binary running, which 0.7.0 always did: the harness entry cannot forward SIGKILL, so it starts a small supervisor that runs the binary and kills it when its channel to the entry closes. The binary exists only as the supervisor's child, so no instant has a binary without something to end it: a SIGKILL right after the binary starts, and a SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP before the entry has installed its handlers, end it as well. Signals sent to the entry still reach the binary, and stdio, process group, environment and exit status are unchanged; a harness-launched binary starts about 40 ms later. Windows ends the binary by its handle. Two limits remain: a supervisor process that is itself killed directly leaves its binary running, and processes that the binary started are not ended by the kill, which ends the binary only (the same on Unix, where the signal goes to the one process). When the binary ends by SIGUSR1 the entry ends with code 0 without raising the signal on itself, so it no longer opens Node's inspector and writes no inspector notice. <!-- fix: 59c181494e, f5af42b553 -->
- `pig extension preview-login` did not enable editor views or `TuiAltScreen`, so an editor in a view of the previewed extension was rejected with `editor views are not enabled in this program`. Every `pig` command now enables them before it runs. <!-- fix: 0749ea17ba963df29f9008111518533d00575c88 -->
- After ctrl+c, SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP while a quit was held by a native extension command (a Go, Rust, Python or Lisp command still running when you quit with ctrl+d, beside another extension whose shutdown never finishes), pig could exit with status 0 instead of the signal's status (130, 130, 143, 129), as Pi's process does; in about one run in 120 of the held-quit tests the shell saw 0 while `exit.log` said `received SIGINT (exit 130)`. The signal's exit ends the extension processes, the host read the end of the process that held the quit as an empty event loop and started the exit of a drained quit (status 0) beside it, and whichever of the two reached `os.Exit` first ended pig. The signal's exit now claims the end of the process before it touches the extension processes, and every other exit waits behind it (D102); the wait for the extension processes to end is the one it was (D56). No release has this: the held quit of a native command is not in 0.7.0 or earlier. <!-- fix: 69c19c31617f7e44d708fd4d406e584c00400f87 --> <!-- cause: exitAtSignal ended the extension processes before its os.Exit, which made the host run the exit of a drained quit (exitProcess(0)) on a goroutine of its own; the two exits raced to os.Exit, and the 0 won when the scheduler ran it first --> <!-- tests: TestSignalExitAtAHeldQuitIsNotOvertakenByTheDrainedQuitExit, TestSecondSignalExitBlocksBehindTheFirst, TestInteractiveHeldQuitOfANativeCommandEndsOnTheKeyAndTheSignalsPiEnds -->
- Unscoped syntax-highlighted code (plain identifiers, operators, spaces, and punctuation) now takes the active theme text foreground instead of inheriting the terminal default foreground, keeping code readable when the terminal and PiG use contrasting themes. <!-- fix: 6389d4475 --> <!-- cause: cliHighlightTokens omitted the default highlight.js scope, so unscoped tokens emitted no foreground SGR and inherited the terminal default foreground. --> <!-- tests: tui/syntax_highlight_default_token_upstream_test.go::TestSyntaxHighlightDefaultTokenUpstream, tui/highlight_test.go::TestHighlightCode_ColorsEachLineOfPythonDocstringsIndependently -->
- A `before_provider_request` handler that edits `event.payload` in place and returns nothing now changes the request the provider receives, as it does in Pi, in the Go, Node, Python, Rust and Lisp extension SDKs, and so does an edit made before the handler throws. A `before_provider_headers` handler's in-place edit of `event.headers` is kept the same way when the handler throws, and in the Go, Python, Rust and Lisp SDKs when it returns normally (the Node SDK already kept it then). Until now only a payload a handler returned took effect, so an edit in place was lost, for every provider, in every SDK. Each SDK sends back the payload as the handler left it when it differs from the one it received, in the member order the handler's object has. The loss was present in v0.7.0. <!-- fix: 556f2b00a1 -->
- An extension that is restarted automatically after a crash could lose a registration its new process made right after it was ready. The host started the loop that serves the new process's calls before it adopted the new registration into the extension its runner holds, so a command, shortcut, flag or renderer registered late (`registerDeclaration`), a tool registered late (`registerTool`), an event handler subscribed late (`event.subscribe`) or the claim to own thinking runs (`ownThinkingRuns`) was written into the held extension and then replaced by the registration the new process had sent before its ready. The call was answered with success and the registration was not served: the command did not run, the tool or the handler was never called, for as long as that process ran. The restart now adopts the registration before the loop starts, so every call the new process makes after its ready is applied on top of it. The first load of an extension is not changed. No report of this was received; a test holds the adoption and shows each of the four calls lost. The restart adoption that rewrites the held extension dates from v0.7.0 (`6af0806f7a`). <!-- fix: 0d8601423d --> <!-- cause: adoptConn started the loop that serves the connection's calls before it adopted the restarted registration into the held extension, so a call made after the ready was written into the registries the adoption then replaced, and no test made a registration between the ready and the adoption --> <!-- tests: TestRestartKeepsWhatTheNewProcessRegistersAfterItsReady -->
- A restarted extension kept the Markdown transformer its first process registered. After an automatic restart a transformer that only the new process registered did nothing, one the new process no longer registered went on being asked, and the surfaces the new process listed were ignored in favour of the old list. The restart now replaces the transformer with the new registration, as it does for commands and renderers. Tool renderers were already correct: a restarted extension resolves them from its new process. The restart adoption that left the transformer behind dates from v0.7.0 (`6af0806f7a`). <!-- fix: 986c5a7e86 --> <!-- cause: adoptRestartedExtension did not adopt Extension.MarkdownTransformer, so the first registration stayed --> <!-- tests: TestRestartedExtensionTakesItsNewMarkdownTransformer, TestRestartedExtensionResolvesToolRenderersFromItsNewProcess -->
- An extension that is restarted automatically after a crash could keep a stale list of the host's commands until its next call. The restart's ready frame is built before the host adopts the new process's registration, so it carried the command catalog of the process that crashed beside the new process's flags, and nothing pushed the state again after the adoption. The host now pushes the state on the new connection once the adoption is done. A packed cell's member is started again as a new extension and was never affected. The ready frame and the automatic restart date from v0.2.0. <!-- fix: 23dfe7d7ad --> <!-- cause: the restart adopted the new registration after its ready frame was built and bumped neither state counter, so no push followed the adoption, and no test read the state an extension holds after its restart --> <!-- tests: TestRestartPushesTheStateOnceItIsAdopted -->
- An extension that is restarted automatically after a crash could be read half replaced: the host adopts the restarted process's registration while a state push, a flag lookup, a command, tool or event call or a status reader runs on another goroutine. The adoption wrote the flag names and defaults, the session-log and model-registry requests, the runtime kind, the process it runs in and the held extension in place with no lock, so a reader could take the new flag names beside the old defaults, or the process of one generation with the link of another, and a registration that failed validation left its flag names behind. The race detector reported each of them in a gate run; no crash was reproduced. The flag names and defaults and the two requests are now one value that the adoption replaces whole once the registration validates, so a reader sees the registration that was running until the new one is adopted and a refused registration replaces nothing; the process fields join the lock that already guards the process handle. The unlocked writes date from v0.2.0 (flag names, the session-log request, the held extension), v0.3.0 (flag defaults, the runtime kind, the process share) and v0.7.0 (the model-registry request). <!-- fix: 0e2d7f4bb4 --> <!-- cause: the restart adopted the new registration field by field with no lock on the supervisor's goroutine, although the readers of those fields run on other goroutines, and no test restarted an extension beside each kind of reader --> <!-- tests: TestRestartReplacesRegistrationBesideEveryReader, TestFailedRegistrationKeepsTheOldRegistration, TestStatePushReadsOneRegistration, TestProcessLinkChangesWithItsHandle -->
- An extension that is restarted automatically after a crash could be judged stopped by the host, or not, from a half-replaced record. The restart rewrote the context its new process runs under and the owner context whose end means the host stopped the extension, while a failed command, shortcut or event call read the owner context from its own goroutine; the race detector reported the pair once in a gate run. The two now change together under the lock that already guards the process handle, and every reader copies them under it. No failure a user could see was reproduced: the worst outcome of a read at the wrong moment was a failed call at the instant of a restart judged by the old owner. <!-- fix: 4cc22fbce1 --> <!-- cause: the restart wrote cancel and parentCtx of a published extension with no lock, although procMu already guarded the process handle beside them, and no test ran a call that reads the owner context while a restart replaces it --> <!-- tests: TestRestartReplacesTheStartContextBesideItsReaders -->
- A Chord activation that waited at the host data gate while an import or delete ran no longer crashes the host when its object ended meanwhile (a reload that no longer serves the type, a close). Its documents were gone, and the activation dereferenced a missing slot. It now ends as Pi's does, as the abandonment of the ended object (Pi's `#broken` returns the abandonment before a failure), and releases the keys it pinned. <!-- fix: 5b36301b3937a5e544bbcefa135c20f0f1659d6a -->
- A Go, Rust, Python or Lisp extension's `stdout` and `stderr` now reach the terminal as Pi's `console.log` and `console.error` do, in print, JSON, RPC and interactive mode: stderr always on stderr, stdout on stderr in the headless modes (in one pipe, so the two keep the order the extension wrote them) and on stdout in interactive mode. Only Node extensions did before: the others' stderr went to a log file removed unless a load failure named it, so a notice such as Posthorse's automatic-rollover failure report never reached the user. A packed runner's failure cause is still read from the log: the host flushes the output pipe before it reads. <!-- fix: bb1c920e97 -->
- The Go SDK's `EstimateTokens` counts an unpaired surrogate as one UTF-16 unit, as Pi's `estimateTokens` does, and as the six-character escape inside a tool call's arguments. A message with eight unpaired surrogates sized 6 tokens where Pi gives 2, and one inside a tool call argument sized less than Pi's `JSON.stringify` length. The Python and Lisp SDKs were right and now have the same table of Pi's numbers; the Rust SDK cannot receive such a string. <!-- fix: dd2f4cb404 -->
- Two tool calls of one parallel batch that took the file mutation queue after different numbers of host calls (a write and an append of one note) could register in the other order in a Go, Rust, Python or Lisp extension, where Pi registers them in call order. Each SDK's context now has the ordered form, `Context.WithFileMutationQueue` (Go), `ctx.with_file_mutation_queue` (Rust, Python), `pig:ctx-with-file-mutation-queue` (Lisp) and `ctx.withFileMutationQueue` (Node): the host registers the call after the extension tools before it in its batch (D187). The free `withFileMutationQueue` is unchanged and registers in the order the calls reach the host. <!-- fix: 760ab0dcf4 -->
- A Go, Rust, Python, Lisp or Node extension's SDK no longer prints its own diagnostics on the terminal. Since the host forwards an extension's stderr as Pi's console does, the Go SDK's recovered-panic report with its goroutine stack, Rust's default panic message for a caught handler panic and the Python, Lisp and Node reports of a failed handler or host call overprinted the interactive frame, where Pi reports a throwing handler as one line and writes no stack. Every SDK now appends them to the extension's log (`PIG_EXT_LOG`, the file the host's load and crash diagnostics read), bounded at 1 MiB per process, and writes to stderr only when no host started it. What the extension's own code writes to stdout and stderr still reaches the terminal. <!-- fix: 54eb0309c7 -->
- A `message_start`, `turn_end` or `agent_end` handler that edits the event's message in place and returns nothing now changes the message the next handlers, the saved session entry and the next provider request hold, as it does in Pi, in every extension SDK: the `message` of a `turn_end` event and a member of its `toolResults`, a message of an `agent_end` event's `messages`, and a user or system message at `message_start`. An edit of the assistant message at `message_start` reaches the later handlers of that event only, as in Pi, where the event holds a copy of the partial. Until now the edit stayed in the handler's own copy of the event and was lost, for every out-of-process handler of these events, in every extension SDK. Each SDK sends back the messages as the handler left them when they differ from the ones it received, and the host refuses a malformed edit before it applies any. The loss was present in every release since v0.3.0. <!-- fix: 18e1649ef2, 6f3ca3d155, 10c7dc1da2, 75f10dda50 -->
- A ctrl+c, SIGTERM or SIGHUP that arrives as a quit by keys (ctrl+d, ctrl+c twice, `/quit`) hands the terminal back now ends PiG at once, as it ends Pi: Pi removes its signal handlers in the same call that restores the terminal, so no signal finds a quit that is still to dispose. PiG marked the quit as disposing only after the terminal was restored, so a signal in between waited a second (ctrl+c) or for ever (SIGTERM, SIGHUP) for a lock the pending quit holds. The window was introduced by the unreleased change that made these signals end a pending quit at once; no release has it. <!-- tests: internal/codingagent/interactive_quit_dispose_after_stop_unix_test.go::TestQuitByKeysIsMarkedDisposingBeforeTheTerminalTurnsCooked, internal/codingagent/interactive_quit_dispose_after_stop_unix_test.go::TestQuitSignalAtTheTerminalHandBackEndsThePendingQuit, internal/codingagent/interactive_quit_dispose_after_stop_unix_test.go::TestQuitByKeysThatEndsInACrashIsNotMarkedDisposing --> <!-- fix: 4246f80e83 -->
- Quitting interactive mode with ctrl+c twice, ctrl+d or `/quit` while a turn is streaming now ends the turn first, as Pi does: the interrupted assistant message is written to the session file as the provider's stream ended it (for a built-in provider the text received so far, with stop reason `aborted`), and extensions receive `message_end`, `turn_end` and `agent_end` before `session_shutdown`. PiG exited at once: the interrupted turn was missing from the session file, and extensions saw `session_shutdown` in the middle of the turn. A `!` command that is still running is not waited for, and nothing of the interrupted turn is drawn after the screen was restored. PiG 0.2.0 through 0.7.0 have the defect. <!-- fix: 4d65734a52 -->
- Quitting interactive mode with ctrl+c twice, ctrl+d or `/quit` while a turn is streaming now ends the turn first, as Pi does: the interrupted assistant message is written to the session file as the provider's stream ended it (for a built-in provider the text received so far, with stop reason `aborted`), and extensions receive `message_end`, `turn_end`, `agent_end` and `agent_settled` before `session_shutdown`. PiG exited at once: the interrupted turn was missing from the session file, and extensions saw `session_shutdown` in the middle of the turn. A `!` command that is still running is not waited for, and nothing of the interrupted turn is drawn after the screen was restored. PiG 0.2.0 through 0.7.0 have the defect. <!-- fix: 4ef5612c00, e477852b5b -->
- When SIGINT ends interactive mode (exit status 130), PiG now ends its extension processes before it exits. The runtime process of a Node extension whose event loop was still alive, for example one that holds a timer, stayed behind. Nothing more is written to the session file at that exit. PiG 0.2.0 through 0.7.0 have the defect. <!-- fix: ab68fb7b65, 851af29834 -->
- When SIGINT ends interactive mode (exit status 130), PiG now ends its extension processes before it exits. The runtime process of a Node extension whose event loop was still alive, for example one that holds a timer, stayed behind after a quit by keys that was still waiting for an extension's session_shutdown handler. Nothing more is written to the session file at that exit. PiG 0.2.0 through 0.7.0 have the defect. <!-- fix: cc061a0b2, f522a9c34 -->
- A custom editor installed by a Go, Rust, Python or Lisp extension no longer ends the interactive session with `autocomplete provider is no longer available` when the install ran before the autocomplete rebuild that follows `session_start` (and on a later `/reload`). The host reports each rebuild to the editor's runtime, and those SDKs answered the notice with an error that the host raised as an uncaught exception; they now accept it, as the Node runtime always did. <!-- fix: 5d60aa5d36 -->
- `pig piglet remove <name> --source` now deletes the prompt file `pig piglet add` copied for that Piglet, so an edited Piglet of the same name adds again instead of failing with `destination .../piglets/prompt.md already exists with different content`. Add records each copied file and its SHA-256 digest in `<name>.files.json` beside the registered YAML. Remove keeps, and reports, a copied file that another registered Piglet lists or references, or whose content changed after it was copied; it never deletes a file it has no record of. A leftover record whose YAML was deleted by hand lets `add` of the same name replace its unchanged files, and an add that still conflicts names the Piglet that owns the file or says that no registered Piglet copied it. A prompt copied by 0.7.0 or earlier has no record: delete that file yourself or use another relative prompt path. Replacing a source Piglet is `pig piglet remove <name> --source` and then `pig piglet add` (#417, reported by @Cade-Peterson). <!-- fix: 27e5b1e20c -->
- MCP stdio servers now start in a session of their own, as Pi's stdio transport does (`detached` in Node's spawn is `setsid`): a server, or a child of it, no longer keeps PiG's controlling terminal and cannot take the terminal's foreground process group from PiG. The server still leads its own process group, so closing the transport still ends its children (#427). <!-- fix: 8392c2900 -->
- Chord workers now start in a session of their own, as Pi's `detached: true` fork does, so a worker no longer keeps the launching terminal as its controlling terminal. The worker still leads its own process group, so killing the group still kills everything it spawned (#427). <!-- fix: 8fbbd2da1 -->
- An interactive shell run by the bash tool or by a `!` command no longer suspends PiG with `suspended (tty input)` on the next key press. PiG started the shell in its own process group but in PiG's session, so the shell kept PiG's controlling terminal: `zsh -f -i -c true; true` opened `/dev/tty`, made its own process group the terminal's foreground group and left it so when it exited, and PiG's next read from the terminal raised SIGTTIN. `bash -i -c true; true` stopped itself and the tool call never returned. The shell now starts in a session of its own, as Pi's `detached: true` does (Node's spawn calls `setsid`), so it has no controlling terminal: `/dev/tty` cannot be opened and `bash -i` reports `no job control in this shell` and returns. The shell still leads its own process group, so abort, timeout and the exit cleanup still end every descendant (#427, reported by @asp345). <!-- fix: dc7d547ec -->
- A Go, Python or Lisp extension with a tool that has a `prepareLoadout` hook no longer hangs PiG when a tool of the same extension is registered after loading (`registerTool` in a `session_start` handler or a tool call, `setToolRenderers`, `toolPromptSnippet`). The hook now runs inside the call, as in Pi. <!-- fix: 5a88cb4140 --> <!-- cause: the SDK held its tool-table lock across the registerTool call to the host, and the host asks every tool prepareLoadout hook before it answers that call while the hook lookup, on another thread, takes the same lock; the fault is in tag v0.7.0 -->
- A Node extension with a `prepareLoadout` tool no longer hangs PiG when it, or another extension in the same process, registers a tool after loading (in a `session_start` handler, as pi-extensible-workflows does) or calls `setActiveTools` and then a synchronous API such as `getActiveTools`; a parallel batch of tool calls no longer gets a `prepare_loadout` extension error. The hook now runs inside that call, as in Pi. <!-- fix: 8aaa7309c1 --> <!-- cause: the Node runtime sat in its synchronous host call while the host asked tool_prepare_loadout before answering registerTool or setActiveTools, and served requests only between its calls, so the extension and the host waited on each other; present since the host asked the hook inside those calls, in tag v0.7.0 -->
- A Python extension that sets renderers on a tool with `tool_renderers` after registering it no longer loses the tool's `prepare_loadout` and `reaches_tools` hooks: the host asked for hooks the extension had dropped and kept the registered description, and the tool's `reaches_tools` calls failed. <!-- fix: 497aa275b2 --> <!-- cause: tool_renderers registered the tool again with its renderers and passed only the prepare_arguments handler along, so the registration dropped the tool's prepare_loadout and reaches_tools handlers while its declaration still asked the host for them; the fault is in tag v0.7.0 -->
- `--mode json` no longer writes what an extension's `session_shutdown` handler emits after `agent_settled`: the `entry_appended` line for `pi.appendEntry`, the `session_info_changed` line for `pi.setSessionName` and the `message_start` / `message_end` lines for `pi.sendMessage` are saved in the session file and not written, as in Pi, which detaches the JSON stream before it runs `session_shutdown` handlers. The stream ends with `agent_settled`, in a normal run and after a termination signal; lines already queued still reach a slow reader, and an extension error from the handler still goes to stderr. The bug has been in every release since v0.3.0. <!-- fix: 1886bcbfd3 --> <!-- cause: the normal teardown detached the JSON writer after closing the runtime (session_shutdown), and the entry_appended line was written outside the subscription without checking that the writer was detached -->
- The ordered-object JSON readers keep two object names apart when `JSON.parse` does. `"\ud800"`, `"\ud801"` and the raw bytes `ED A0 80` are three keys in JavaScript; the readers read each as U+FFFD and merged them into one entry (last value wins). A name with a lone surrogate or ill-formed UTF-8 is now keyed on the string JavaScript has (`jsonopts.ReadName`): an escaped lone surrogate is its WTF-8 bytes, and ill-formed raw bytes become one U+FFFD per maximal subpart, as Node decodes them. `internal/orderedjson` writes a lone-surrogate key back as its escape. The readers that hand the key to `encoding/json` still hold it as U+FFFD. <!-- fix: 2a83c43014 -->
- A nested `RawMessage` or `MarshalJSON` output, and an agent message or content block written by the SDK encoder, no longer lose a quote, newline, backslash or other two-character escape that stands before the letters `fffd` (`"say \"fffd\""` was written as `"say �"`): only the `\ufffd` escape itself is written as the replacement character. <!-- fix: 030f512fd6 -->
- A custom provider named exactly `ollama` in `models.json` with no `apiKey` was sent requests in print mode (`pig -p`) and interactive mode, where Pi answers `No API key found for ollama.` and PiG's own RPC mode did too: PiG exempted that one provider name from the check for configured credentials (releases 0.2.0 to 0.7.0). PiG now applies Pi's one rule to every provider in every mode: a provider without configured credentials is refused before any request is sent, whatever it is called and whether or not `OLLAMA_HOST` is set. **If your local Ollama provider has no key, add one line to it in `~/.pig/agent/models.json`: `"apiKey": "ollama"`** (any text works; Ollama ignores it). That is the form the models and custom provider pages of PiG's docs and Pi's `docs/models.md` show, and a setup that already has it is unchanged, as is a keyless provider under any other name (it was always refused). The same name no longer passes the other credential gates either: selecting the model reports `No API key for ollama/<model>`, an extension's `setModel` answers `false`, a virtual model route to it fails with `which has no credentials.`, and a model object an extension builds for the provider gets no request. <!-- fix: f1fc6abc88eb7f661593d49746b3c913e2bc2684 -->
- The provider id `ollama` no longer has a base URL of its own. `coding.BuildModel` and the request path gave an OpenAI-compatible model of that provider without a base URL the value of `OLLAMA_HOST`, or `http://localhost:11434/v1`; Pi has no such default and never reads `OLLAMA_HOST`, so that model is now addressed like a model of any other provider without a base URL (the OpenAI client's default, `https://api.openai.com/v1`). **If you relied on the default, state `"baseUrl": "http://localhost:11434/v1"` (or the value of your `OLLAMA_HOST`) in the provider's entry in `~/.pig/agent/models.json`**, as the models and custom provider pages show. A `models.json` provider that defines models already had to state its `baseUrl`, in PiG as in Pi; the Go SDK's `BuildModelFromEntry` and a model object an extension builds for the provider without a `baseUrl` are the callers that change. <!-- fix: f56733c5a40f1dcdbc5c50c13a54bc6a895d26ec -->
- Fullscreen Kitty images no longer disappear after a full redraw such as a window resize; the redraw deletes the placements and keeps the uploaded image data instead of clearing the screen, as Pi does (upstream #12047). <!-- fix: 030a083ada -->
- Fullscreen Kitty images no longer disappear after a full redraw such as a window resize; the redraw deletes the placements and keeps the uploaded image data instead of clearing the screen, as Pi does (upstream #12047). <!-- fix: 97711dbbc6c5608a8254be3a7039bd47f943eb3c -->
- LaTeX math that holds a lone UTF-16 surrogate (`$x\ud83d$`, a script, fraction, root, accent, `\text{}`, matrix or cases, inline or display) keeps the unit as one character of its own instead of rendering three replacement characters. <!-- fix: 2a0b22db2e -->
- LaTeX math renders two surrogate halves that end up side by side in one argument (`\vec{\ud83d{}\ude00}`, `x^{\ud83d{}\ude00}`, `\not{...}`, `\frac{x}{...}`) as the one character they spell, so the script, fraction, accent and `\not` layout matches Pi instead of treating them as two. <!-- fix: f0eace4daf -->
- LaTeX math reads an unbraced astral argument (`\vec😀`, `\frac😀x`, `\sqrt😀`, `\not😀`, `x^😀` in display mode) as Pi does, one UTF-16 unit: the high half is the argument and the low half is the next character. <!-- fix: f0eace4daf -->
- LaTeX math treats two surrogate halves that end up side by side in a fraction, a root or next to a named operator (`\sqrt{\ud835{}\udc9c}`, `\frac{x}{\ud835{}\udfce}`, `\ud835{}\udc9c\sin x`) as the one astral letter or digit they spell, so the parentheses and the spacing match Pi. <!-- fix: f40cd6b547 -->
- `pig piglet build` planned a Common Lisp extension as packed into the Piglet Binary but did not embed its SBCL image: it warned `[not-embedded]`, a Piglet with no other member to fuse failed with "nothing to embed or fuse", and a Piglet with a fused member built a Binary that exited at startup with `baked Piglet Binary binary-packed extensions do not match its plan: missing [<extension>]`. The build now builds the Lisp image and embeds it, the Binary starts it without SBCL, and a Piglet whose only extensions are Lisp extensions builds. <!-- fix: 20b9d0592b -->
- `pig piglet build` planned a Common Lisp extension as packed into the Piglet Binary but did not embed its SBCL image: it warned `[not-embedded]`, a Piglet with no other member to fuse failed with "nothing to embed or fuse", and a Piglet with a fused member built a Binary that exited at startup with `baked Piglet Binary binary-packed extensions do not match its plan: missing [<extension>]`. The build now builds the Lisp image and embeds it, the Binary starts it without SBCL, and a Piglet whose only extensions are Lisp extensions builds. <!-- fix: ffe1cf3473 -->
- Loading a packed Lisp cell no longer hangs when two of its extensions each make a host call, such as a `pi.events` subscription, while their factories run. The host serves a cell's connections in order, so the second extension's first call waits for the first extension's register; the first extension's run needed the lock that call held to take its connection, and when the second factory reached its call before the first run took its connection, neither could continue and the load never ended. A factory-time call now holds only the lock of its own connection. <!-- fix: 9ee5c21f2 -->
- Loading a packed Python cell no longer hangs when its second extension's factory makes a host call before the first extension's run has taken its connection. The Python SDK had the same lock order as the Lisp SDK: a factory-time host call held the lock `run` takes while it waited for the host, so neither could continue. A factory-time call now holds only the lock of its own connection. <!-- fix: dd7613e75 -->
- `listDir` of the local execution environment leaves out an entry whose name is not valid UTF-8, as Pi does (Node decodes the name with replacement characters, so its `lstat` finds nothing and #12055 skips the entry); the remote environment already matched. <!-- fix: 2d2259d899cb11de276d564ce5efd9e3c5d5ddd3 -->
- `listDir` of the local execution environment leaves out an entry whose name is not valid UTF-8, as Pi does (Node decodes the name with replacement characters, so its `lstat` finds nothing and #12055 skips the entry); the remote environment already matched. <!-- fix: 3d492806e5 -->
- `listDir` of the local and remote execution environments leaves out an entry removed between enumeration and `lstat` instead of failing, so a read-only JSONL open beside a live writer no longer fails with `JSONL directory listing failed: ENOENT`, as Pi does (upstream #11994, #12055). <!-- fix: 1be82286e0 -->
- `listDir` of the local and remote execution environments leaves out an entry removed between enumeration and `lstat` instead of failing, so a read-only JSONL open beside a live writer no longer fails with `JSONL directory listing failed: ENOENT`, as Pi does (upstream #11994, #12055). <!-- fix: e6e4f9acc50b26111b6f83f48ea004ca1fa9927e -->
- chord: a host object reading a live query, a count or a list could stay loading for ever, and `Host.Load` with it, when the first run of its read was adopted between the reader's classification and the registration of the wake: the attempt checked the reader and followed it in two sections with a task between them, so the adoption made the reader ready and told nobody (one run in about 18,000 of a loaded test). Pi checks the reader and follows it in one turn (query-reader.ts, read-declarations.ts); the check now runs in the section that settles its await, before the attempt follows the reader. <!-- fix: 923604266 --> <!-- cause: reader.Open read the reading in a section of its own at the end of its blocking task and the attempt followed the reader in the next section, the one that settles the task's promise, where Pi has one turn; an adoption between the two found no wake to tell --> <!-- tests: TestOpeningReadersFollowsAReaderInTheSectionThatFoundItNotReadyNotAfterAnAdoptionCouldLandBetween, TestStartBarrierAHostObjectWhoseReaderWasAdoptedBetweenItsCheckAndItsFollowGoesLive -->
- A llama.cpp decision classifier whose server reports image input, such as Clef with its `mmproj`, now takes images: `models.classify()` sends them to `/v1/systemone` as data URLs instead of failing with "does not support image input". Decision models without image input and the next-token fallback for chat models stay text-only. <!-- fix: 64373deac1 --> <!-- cause: PiG registered every llama.cpp classifier model with input text only and no System One compat, as Pi did, so the classifier refused the images of a decision model the server had said accepts them. --> <!-- tests: TestProviderSendsImagesToDecisionModelsThatAdvertiseImageInputAsDataURLs, TestProviderRefusesImagesForClassifiersThatTakeNone, TestAIClassifierModelCarriesImageInputOfDecisionModels -->
- A login dialog could draw one frame half-updated while an OAuth or device-code sign-in was changing it: a prompt shown without its input row or its hint, a masked key preview built from the previous prompt's input, or the device-code hint row in its old state after the clipboard write had finished, until the next frame repainted it. The frame's change check read the dialog's prompt input and redaction state without the dialog's lock, while the sign-in's own goroutines (the provider's prompt and progress callbacks, and the clipboard writer of a confirmed device code) wrote them. The change check now holds the same lock as the dialog's render, and a source guard fails any component that embeds a container, has its own lock and skips it in `Render` or `IsDirty`. <!-- fix: 0f48556b87b1 --> <!-- cause: the dialog's lock was assumed to cover every way a frame reads it because Render takes it, but the settle scan added with the per-child render cache asks the embedded container's IsDirty, which renders the dialog's children without the lock -->
- `pig login` and `pig logout` end on Ctrl+C, SIGTERM and SIGHUP at the provider menu, the logout menu and inside a provider's login. Ctrl+C and SIGTERM were ignored there before; the process now ends by the signal after its cleanup, as Pi's does. `pig auth login` restores the terminal before ending on SIGTERM and SIGHUP (it left the terminal raw), and Ctrl+C still prints "Login cancelled." and exits 1. Affects 0.5.0 through 0.7.0. <!-- fix: 7d225e5e36 -->
- A failed interactive login now behaves as in Pi: the login dialog closes, the editor has focus again, and the transcript shows the error as `Error: Failed to login to <provider name>: <message>` in the error colour (for example `Error: Failed to login to GitHub Copilot: 401 Unauthorized: {"message":"Bad credentials"}`). Before, GitHub Copilot, OpenAI Codex and every other OAuth login kept the dialog open with `Login failed: <message>` inside it until Escape, and anything typed went nowhere. A credential that cannot be stored is reported the same way. <!-- fix: 3e66fd5b363dcd36dbf1ab786ddfa6d3b80d7722 -->
- A tool whose name, description or parameter schema holds a lone UTF-16 surrogate now reaches the provider, the session file, RPC output and an HTML export as Pi writes it. A JavaScript, Python or Lisp extension can register such a tool, and so can a Go extension that builds the string. PiG wrote U+FFFD in the unit's place (three for a name or a description, one inside the schema), so two tools whose names differed only in that unit reached the provider under one name, a property name no longer matched its `required` entry, and a call the model made by that name ended in `Tool ... not found`. Now the request of the Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, Azure OpenAI Responses, Google Generative AI, Mistral and Bedrock kinds holds the unit as the `\uXXXX` escape `JSON.stringify` writes, in the tools it declares and in a history that names a called tool or holds the unit in a call's arguments, also when the body is written from a payload a Go `OnPayload` hook handed back; the system message's session line and its RPC lines hold the same escape. The name of a called tool is read with the unit kept from the Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, Azure OpenAI Responses, Google Generative AI and Mistral streams, so the call finds its tool. A session Pi wrote with the escape is read and sent with it; a session an earlier PiG wrote with U+FFFD is sent as it is. ECMAScript specifies that `JSON.stringify` writes a lone surrogate as its escape, and Anthropic's prompt caching documentation says a cache hit needs an identical prompt prefix. No provider documents whether it accepts a tool name or description that holds such an escape, and this was not tried against a live provider. The Google Vertex and OpenAI Codex requests go through the same encoders as the Google Generative AI and OpenAI Responses ones and were not compared with Pi's. Not changed: an extension in a subprocess still receives U+FFFD in the unit's place in what the host sends it (so a payload its `before_provider_request` handler returns holds U+FFFD), tools of an MCP server are still read with U+FFFD, and so is the name of a called tool in the Bedrock stream. <!-- fix: 1a6b1ab3ed, e95b1a4f11 -->
- Markdown no longer shows HTML comments (`<!-- ... -->`) as text in Extension Updates, What's New, `/changelog` and messages. A comment-only block disappears with one of its blank lines, so no extra gap remains; an inline comment is skipped, so `See <!-- c --> the docs.` renders `See the docs.`; an unclosed comment stays hidden while it streams. Follows Pi main 54280c4ff. <!-- fix: 348a3a8859 -->
- Text after a multi-row inline image in Markdown no longer draws over the image when the image rows were joined with hard line breaks; the rows stay separate, as under Pi (upstream #12017). <!-- fix: 028c1a5b09899b4deb785ddc3a119d2b6b7edf11 -->
- Text after a multi-row inline image in Markdown no longer draws over the image when the image rows were joined with hard line breaks; the rows stay separate, as under Pi (upstream #12017). <!-- fix: d7dd9c5a19 -->
- MCP messages nested more than 10,000 levels deep (a tool `inputSchema`, `_meta` or `structuredContent` of a server that nests that far) are now read the way Pi reads them with `JSON.parse`, instead of being refused by Go's JSON decoder. <!-- fix: 3868dd514e -->
- `tool_search` (and its Durable copy) now finds a tool by property names and descriptions behind a local `$ref`, as in MCP input schemas that put their models in `$defs`; the codemode `resolves to` summary shows field names behind a `$ref`; and a `$ref` with a malformed percent escape renders as `unknown` instead of failing every codemode run. `codemode.SchemaToType`, `RenderToolSignature`, `RenderToolSample`, `RenderDeclarations`, `RenderToolOutputType` and `CreateDescription` no longer return an error. <!-- fix: 604e18084d -->
- `/mcp login` and `pig mcp login` no longer stay on "Connecting..." after a successful browser sign-in while the browser keeps an unused connection to the OAuth callback port: the callback server drops connections that have not sent a request when it closes. <!-- fix: 62b28a24c6 -->
- A sign-in wait that ends with its context no longer leaves its state pending, so a retry with the same state works, and a wait begun after the callback server closed fails at once. <!-- fix: 8d46bf82b6 -->
- `mcp-auth.json` is replaced through a temporary file and a rename, so a crash cannot leave a torn credential file, and the PKCE verifier is dropped once its code exchange succeeded. <!-- fix: 8d46bf82b6 -->
- Tool search and codemode resolve a local `$ref` in one pass over the schema instead of parsing it once per path segment. <!-- fix: 8d46bf82b6 -->
- Two pig processes opening the MCP OAuth credential file (`mcp-auth.json`) for the first time at the same moment, or reaching it while it was being replaced, could overwrite every stored MCP login with `{}`. The initial file creation used a truncating write after an unlocked existence check instead of exclusive creation, so a late create could land on top of a credential another process had already written; `mcp-auth.json` is now created exclusively with owner-only access (following dangling symlinks), so an existing file is never overwritten by the create. <!-- fix: 95a57fda36 --> <!-- cause: FileAuthStorageBackend.WithLock used unlocked os.Stat followed by truncating os.WriteFile("{}") before locking, so a concurrent caller seeing mcp-auth.json absent overwrote an existing credential file. -->
- MCP tools loaded by `tool_search` are no longer dropped on resume and `/reload` when an extension deactivates only its own tool at `session_start`, as Pi does (upstream #12054). <!-- fix: 4b6e822b66 -->
- MCP tools loaded by `tool_search` are no longer dropped on resume and `/reload` when an extension deactivates only its own tool at `session_start`, as Pi does (upstream #12054). <!-- fix: b562713f26fef66342f709edca8904ede4f1bdf6 -->
- extensions (MCP): a server an extension registers at run time (`pi.registerMcpServer` and its SDK forms) reached the built-in MCP extension only after the call had returned, and a second server registered while an earlier one was still connecting waited until that connection attempt had ended or timed out. Pi runs the first `mcp_servers_change` handler up to its first await inside the registering call, and every registration starts its own delivery: when `registerMcpServer` returns, the built-in MCP extension has listed the server, hidden the tools of a server it replaced and activated the discovery tool, and a server registered while another still connects starts connecting at once. PiG now does the same when the first handler runs in the PiG process (the built-in MCP extension, or a compiled-in Go extension). Still different from Pi: the handlers after the first run beside the registering code instead of after its synchronous run; and the call does not wait for a first handler that lives in a subprocess extension (possible only when the built-in MCP extension is replaced or disabled), nor when the registration is made on the interactive input loop. Affected release: v0.7.0, the only release with this code (it came with 3dd4d752e8; no earlier tag has `mcp_servers_change`). <!-- fix: 72bf4f2ebd5e8721bde804fd00fba33de81c2563 -->
- Markdown text that holds a lone UTF-16 surrogate (a paragraph, heading, emphasis, code span, link, table cell, list item, quote or link reference definition) now measures and wraps as Pi does: the unit is one code point of no width instead of three replacement characters, and a reference definition whose label holds one still resolves. <!-- fix: 20bdd2c341 -->
- A `message_end` handler that edits `event.message` in place and returns nothing now changes the message the next handlers, `turn_end`, `agent_end`, the saved session entry and the next provider request hold, as it does in Pi, in the Go, Python, Rust and Lisp extension SDKs, and so does an edit made before the handler throws. Until now only a message a handler returned took effect in those SDKs, so an edit in place was lost (the Node SDK already kept it in the unreleased line). Each SDK sends back the message as the handler left it when it differs from the one it received. The loss was present in every release since v0.2.0. <!-- fix: 83928e2246 -->
- The upstream mirror's provider data (`.upstream/current/packages/ai/src/providers/data`) is the snapshot the pin froze for its commit, checked against its digest, and no longer a copy of the installed pi-ai package, which carries the post-release fixes: a mirror made after a fix changed a provider list held the fixed list and the tests that read the mirror failed (`make upstream-mirror` now also ends with the check that every recorded fix still applies to the mirror once). <!-- fix: 8f816685ff -->
- Resuming or replacing a session whose saved model no catalog describes no longer continues on a blank model with no context window and no prices (a footer of `0.0%/0`). As in Pi, only a model the model runtime carries is restored; otherwise the session keeps the model it had. <!-- fix: 6691fb8df -->
- A custom model defined in `models.json` under a built-in provider that omits `api` or `baseUrl` now inherits the provider's composed defaults in `coding.BuildModel`, `--model`, saved default model startup, and RPC `get_state`, matching `ModelRuntime.GetModel` and upstream Pi. Before, a direct stream for a `models.json` custom model that set `api` and omitted `baseUrl` under a built-in provider with several APIs could send the request, with that provider's key, to another vendor's host (for example, `opencode-go` with `anthropic-messages` went to `api.anthropic.com`), while omitting `api` failed with `No API provider registered for api: undefined` and RPC `get_state` reported empty `api` and `baseUrl`. A `models.json` custom model under a provider whose base URL an extension overrides (without declaring extension models) now uses the extension's base URL in `coding.BuildModel` and `--model` too, as the model runtime and Pi do. Affects 0.7.0. <!-- fix: af90a4b18a --> <!-- cause: ModelRegistry.Resolve built custom models.json entries from the raw definition without filling omitted api and baseUrl from the provider's composed catalog defaults and dropped an extension provider's baseUrl overlay when dynamic.Models was nil --> <!-- tests: TestResolveCustomModelUnderBuiltInProviderInheritsDefaults, TestBuildModelCustomModelUnderBuiltInProviderInheritsDefaults, TestBuildModelOpenCodeGoAnthropicCustomModelRoutesToProviderHostNotAnthropic, TestSelectStartupModelCustomModelInheritsBuiltInDefaults, TestPrintModeCustomModelWithoutAPIReachesLocalEndpointAndPreservesMetadata, TestPrintModeEndToEndCustomModelWithoutAPIUsesInheritedDefaults -->
- A write to `models-store.json` that fails partway (a full disk, a size limit, the process killed) no longer leaves the file truncated and loses every provider's cached model catalog. The file is replaced through a temporary file in the same directory, and a failed write leaves the old content. <!-- fix: cdd5b98d3 --> <!-- cause: the store was written in place with os.WriteFile, which truncates the file before it writes, so any failure after that left a partial file -->
- Releasing a session's services no longer leaves the model selector's catalog refresh running. Before, the refresh the selector starts and the shared catalog operation behind it were not joined by anything, so with a file-backed registry the operation could still write `auth.json` and `models-store.json` in the agent directory after the registry's model tasks were closed. The selector's refresh is now an owned task of the interactive mode, which cancels and joins it when the mode shuts down, and the operation behind it is a task of the model registry, which cancels and joins it when the session's services are released (for example on session replacement); at quit the process exits, as Pi's does. The refresh result and the picker are unchanged. <!-- fix: bd9ac3b95 -->
