- Every strict and packed Go cell of the extension conformance suite (the theme, child-session, markdown, exec-abort and other rows) failed to build with `go: updates to go.mod needed` since the root module moved to an SDK pseudo-version: 23 in-tree fixture, example and bench modules still required the PiG and SDK modules at v0.7.0. They are pinned to the root's requirement, and `make module-pins`, part of `ci-bookkeeping`, now fails when one drifts. <!-- fix: 142baa38fb -->
- Interactive mode: the terminal stays live after `/name <name>` while an extension's `session_info_changed` handler runs. The input loop waited for the first handler to reach its first wait or to end, and a Go, Rust, Python or Lisp subprocess handler reports neither before its first host call, so no key echoed and nothing was drawn for as long as such a handler ran: 10 s for a handler that slept 10 s, where Pi 1.5.2 echoes at once while a handler awaits. The loop now starts the handler and goes on. Every release from v0.3.0 to v0.7.0 has the wait. <!-- fix: d63659241b8d167aaac409696f678822d5e352b6 -->
- The Python SDK now carries an event.messages list a `context` or `context_with_system` handler assigns, and an event.entries list a `turn_end` handler assigns, and the Lisp SDK the context list, as the Go and Rust SDKs already do (they have carried an assigned context list since v0.2.0 / v0.3.0 and turn_end entries since v0.3.0, Lisp since v0.7.0, so the behaviour stays and the other SDKs follow it); the Node runtime still follows Pi, which carries neither. A handler that assigns a bad list leaves what the same value returned leaves. <!-- fix: 5003f90812 --> <!-- cause: each native SDK was written alone: Go and Rust re-read the member after the handler, Python and Lisp kept the list captured before it, and no conformance row compared an assignment across SDKs -->
- Chord: a registry value's watch that ended through its context's cancellation could race with the host's close (a data race under `-race`); the watch now ends as a section of its host, like the rest of the code that touches the registry. <!-- fix: 62b2278409, e163ba898d -->
- `/new`, `/resume`, `/fork`, `/clone`, `/tree` navigation and a compaction no longer erase the terminal's scrollback. The text above the TUI (the `Installing ...` lines of a package install at startup, or what a wrapper script printed) and the older transcript rows that had scrolled above the frame stayed in Pi and were gone in PiG. The transcript repaint now clears the chat and renders normally, as Pi's does, and only the reload box forces the clearing redraw, as in Pi. A boundary compaction and a provider logout no longer erase it either, and after a `/fork` of a long session the footer sits where Pi leaves it. <!-- fix: ec8fbdc5a9 --> <!-- cause: rebuildChatFrom and renderCompactionResult called ForceFullRender, which writes ESC[2J ESC[H ESC[3J and replays the transcript from the top, where Pi's chatContainer.clear() plus renderInitialMessages() request an ordinary render that repaints only from the first changed row --> <!-- tests: TestSessionReplacementRepaintsDifferentially, TestReloadBoxForcesTheRedrawAsPiDoes -->
- A Chord host's IPC or WebSocket link no longer hands its listener a message that arrived while earlier queued messages were still being handed over ahead of them: a hold could reach a relay worker before its hello and end the link with `handshake: hold before hello`. <!-- fix: 349684cecf6ee8bcf6ea7814f3c20b74a75f7274 -->
- Searching a long session in `/tree` allocates as many objects as in 0.7.0 again, 30% fewer than with the regression: lowercasing text with non-ASCII characters (the search text of every row, model ids and names, and other callers of `jsstring.ToLower`) made a second copy of each text, which raised `BenchmarkTreeRecompute` by 43%. <!-- fix: 87d4c01443 -->
- `/fork` of a session that is not file-backed builds the clone's entries from the source's decoded messages again instead of decoding every record a second time, which doubled the allocations of that clone. <!-- fix: c60d6af727 -->
- Every frame the renderer paints allocates two fewer objects: the cursor's hide and show copied their escape sequence into a new slice, where they had copied it into a pooled buffer before dead-terminal handling routed them through `WriteToTerminal`. <!-- fix: c60d6af727 -->
- On macOS and the BSDs, a chord worker that found a lock file left by a crashed holder waited for it forever instead of failing with the "stale lock file" error that names the file to remove. Connecting to a plain file fails with ENOTSOCK there (ECONNREFUSED on Linux), and the waiter took that for a holder that was still releasing and retried without end. <!-- fix: ee0017ae81495ad4bbf1ab69fe2c181fe356f7c1 -->
- `pi.exec` reports `killed: true` for a command whose timeout fell due before the call settled, as Pi does, when the process was kept off the CPU past both the timer and the child's end; the result used to depend on which of two ready channels the watcher picked. <!-- fix: 1caec6e3a589500f6a2f37260ff04f3bccaf924d -->
- A codemode script that makes a tool call at the moment its execution ends (an abort, a timeout, `Sandbox.Close`) could have the call start after `Execute` returned, because the call was counted in the execution's wait group only after the check that the execution had not finished. The call is counted under that check now, so `Execute` returns only after every tool call it started has ended. <!-- fix: e3bc5f0f13a62f753c8c3a87a0bc6a2f786bf281 -->
- extensions: when the Node process that several TypeScript or JavaScript extensions share was killed or crashed, an extension could be reported twice: first as disabled (`packed member connection closed; /reload restarts it`), then as crashed and restarting, so one exit read as an error that asked for `/reload` and a warning that the extension restarts by itself. How many notices appeared depended on whether the host noticed the closed connections or the exited process first: two, three or four for two extensions, four in 86 of 100 kills. The host now reports the exit once for each extension, as restarting, in the order the extensions load, whichever it notices first. The extensions of a Go, Python or Rust cell that stops are reported in load order too, where the order varied from one exit to the next. Present in releases 0.3.0 to 0.7.0. <!-- fix: 7c24a924a9f3b784e3748673bb1982fc9bdb7b62 -->
- A Node extension whose file or package entry point is gone is now reported with the same error whether it runs in a process of its own or shares one with other Node extensions (`build "name": ...`, in the startup error and in the reload's issues); a member of a shared process was reported as `extension "name": stat ...` or `extension "name": package ... declares pi.extensions ... but none exist`. Present since 0.2.0. <!-- tests: coding/extension/host/subprocess/reload_member_unresolved_test.go::TestNodeCellLoadsItsOtherMembersWhenOneEntryPointIsGone --> <!-- fix: d13855f45b -->
- A Node extension whose entry point is gone no longer keeps the extensions that share its process from loading. The extension whose file or package entry does not resolve now fails alone, with its own error, and the others load, at startup and at a reload, as Pi reports one error per extension that cannot be loaded; before, every extension of the shared Node process was reported with the missing one's error and none was loaded. Present since 0.2.0. <!-- tests: coding/extension/host/subprocess/reload_member_unresolved_test.go::TestNodeCellLoadsItsOtherMembersWhenOneEntryPointIsGone --> <!-- fix: 27c81a52d1 -->
- A Piglet Binary with a TypeScript or JavaScript extension compares the extracted copy of the extension's sources with the archive inside the Binary at every start, as it compares an embedded Go, Rust or Python cell binary with its embedded bytes. Before, a later start reused the copy under `piglet-binary-cells/node/<digest>/sources` by its `ready.json` alone, so a file changed or deleted there, a file added that the extension would import, a `node_modules` or `package.json` beside the sources, a file or folder replaced by a link, or a widened mode reached Node and ran in place of the code the Binary was built with, until the `<digest>` directory was removed. Now a copy that differs is replaced from the archive, one warning line on stderr names the first difference (`pig: warning: the extracted Node sources in <folder> differ from the Binary's archive (changed: sources/greeter/index.ts); extracted them again`) and nothing reaches stdout, and two Binaries starting at once do not disturb each other. A `node_modules`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` or `jsconfig.json` in `piglet-binary-cells` or `piglet-binary-cells/node` stops the start and names the path; the PiG configuration directory and the folders above it are not checked. The check runs at startup, not at a `/reload`. It reads every extracted file, which adds 0.3 ms to a start with an extension of 10 to 13 files, 9 ms to one with 561 files and 1.9 MB, 16 ms to one with 1,064 files and 28.5 MB, and 73 ms to one with 3,665 files and 17.5 MB (Linux, median of 20 starts). A Binary built before this change has no check: build it again to get one. An extension keeps its data outside its extracted sources, in the agent directory. Present since 0.5.0. <!-- tests: coding/extension/host/cellpack/node_recheck_test.go::TestNodeCellStartExtractsTheArchiveAgainWhenTheTreeDiffers, coding/pigletbuild/node_binary_test.go::TestPigletBinaryRunsTheOriginalNodeSourcesAfterTheExtractedCopyIsEdited --> <!-- fix: 5fd39a75a5 -->
- A Node extension no longer sees PiG's own loader in `process.execArgv`. It held `["--import", "file:///…/runtime/register-loader.mjs"]`, where Pi's is the empty list Node was started with, so a child the extension forked with the default `execArgv` or with `[...process.execArgv, …]` started with PiG's loader too. Under Node's restricted-access mode (`--allow-fs-read` with only the child's own directory readable) that child died before it ran with `ERR_ACCESS_DENIED`, which is how every workflow of pi-extensible-workflows failed with `Workflow child exited with code 1`. PiG now starts the extension's process with a small bootstrap file (`node-cli.mjs`, `node-cell.mjs`) that registers the loader inside the process and then loads the runtime, so `process.execArgv` stays empty in an isolated extension and in a packed cell, and a forked child, a spawned `process.execPath` and a worker thread start as they do under Pi; none of them gets PiG's module hooks (the `@earendil-works/pi-*` specifiers resolve in the extension's process only, as they do under Pi). What the extension itself loads, and every other property it reads from `process` (`argv`, `execPath`, `title`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `cwd()`), are unchanged. The cache of built Node launchers and cells is rebuilt once after the update. <!-- fix: 698d040146 -->
- A Node extension handler's host effects are written before the RPC reply or interactive prompt drain that waited for the handler's first suspension, as Pi writes them. A `session_info_changed` or `thinking_level_select` handler that calls `ctx.ui.notify`, `ctx.ui.setStatus`, `ctx.ui.setWidget`, `ctx.ui.setTitle`, `ctx.ui.setEditorText`, `pi.appendEntry` or `pi.sendUserMessage` synchronously now has that effect written before the reply of `set_session_name` or `set_thinking_level` (RPC mode) and before the prompt drain releases its dialog answer. PiG wrote the reply first, so a client saw the reply and then the notification, status or widget that Pi writes before it (isolated and packed Node extensions, since 0.2.0, the first release with the call lanes that queue those calls). A notification that followed a refused call, such as a failed `pi.appendEntry`, could also be applied after the caller went on outside RPC mode. The host releases the caller only after every call the same extension sent before its report has been applied: the wait is per extension connection, has no timer, and ends with the request, so a handler that ends or goes on, a cancelled caller or a closing session releases it, and a dialog, a model request or a child process the handler starts never holds it. Go, Python, Rust and Lisp subprocess extensions already wrote in Pi's order; the same rows now pin them in isolated and packed mode. <!-- tests: coding/cli/rpc_handler_effect_order_test.go::TestRPCHandlerEffectsPrecedeTheReplyOfTheCommandThatEmittedTheEvent, coding/extension/host/subprocess/ack_hold_test.go::TestBlockedAcknowledgmentWaitsForTheCallsReadBeforeIt, coding/extension/host/subprocess/ack_hold_test.go::TestBlockedAcknowledgmentOfAnEffectCallWaitsForTheHandlersProgress, test/extension-conformance/handler_effect_bounds_test.go::TestConformance_HandlerEffectWaitEndsWithTheCallersContext, test/extension-conformance/handler_effect_bounds_test.go::TestConformance_HandlerEffectWaitEndsWithTheSession, test/extension-conformance/handler_effect_bounds_test.go::TestConformance_HandlerEffectsPrecedeTheReleaseUnderLoad, test/extension-conformance/handler_effect_order_test.go::TestConformance_HandlerEffectsPrecedeTheReleaseOfItsCaller --> <!-- fix: d2ab7d89f0 -->
- A full disk or a killed process while pig saved `keybindings.json`, `mcp.json` or the settings file during the legacy API-key migration could leave the file empty or cut short and lose your keybindings, your MCP servers or your settings. These files are now replaced as a whole through a temporary file in the same directory, so where one can be replaced a failed write leaves the old file untouched. Where one of them cannot be replaced atomically, for example a single file mounted into a container or a file in a directory pig cannot write into, pig writes it in place as before, and a failure half way through that write can still leave the file empty or cut short. <!-- fix: 8d4e7f2452 --> <!-- cause: these files were written with os.WriteFile, which truncates the file before it writes, so a write that failed after it began left an empty or cut-short file. -->
- Print, JSON and RPC modes: a stdout write that fails with ENOBUFS, EAGAIN or EWOULDBLOCK (a slow or non-blocking pipe) is now retried every 10 ms without losing or repeating bytes, as Pi does; any other write error still ends the process with exit code 1. <!-- fix: 07d55d47099d643bcb624453b45b7d34da7ce7fb -->
- Ordering `/fork`, `/new` or `/resume` while an extension's `session_start` handler (or any other event, command or shortcut handler of a subprocess extension) has not returned no longer shows `Extension "<path>" error: connection closed`. The swap stops the old extension process, and the connection answered the call still pending with its own "connection closed"; the host returned that answer as the handler's failure, so the runner reported it. It is now marked as cut short by the host, as the same call ended by a transport error already was, and nothing is shown, as in Pi, whose handler finishes. An error the extension answers itself, whatever its text, and a crash are still reported as before. The old process is stopped, so a handler in flight does not finish as it does in Pi (D70, in-flight handler clause). <!-- fix: 9315f493e3 --> <!-- cause: Conn.Close answered the requests still pending with a made-up response that Request returns as a plain response, and the response branches of the event, command and shortcut calls returned it without the classification their transport-error branches apply, and no test held a handler across a stop of its extension --> <!-- tests: TestAHandlerPendingWhenTheHostStopsItsExtensionIsNotItsFailure, TestAHostCloseAnswersPendingRequestsWithTheMark, TestSessionReplacementDuringAHeldSessionStartShowsNoExtensionError, extensions-runtime/113-fork-while-session-start-held -->
- `/reload` no longer hangs when extensions that share a packed process (Go, Rust, Python or Lisp) subscribe to the event bus with `pi.events.on` while their factory runs. The Host wrote the admissions of every retained member before it accepted the first connection. A runner starts each admitted factory on its own goroutine or thread and takes them in whatever order the scheduler picks, and a factory that calls the Host before it returns waits for the Host to serve its member's connection. When a later member took the factory turn first, the Host waited for an earlier member that could not start its factory, so the reload never returned. The Host now admits each retained member after the members before it have registered, which is the order Pi loads its factories in, and every listener hears an emit once after a reload. PiG 0.5.2 through 0.7.0 have the defect. <!-- fix: e67ba4d381 --> <!-- cause: the Host admitted every retained member of a packed process before it accepted the first connection, while a factory that subscribes to the event bus waits for the Host to serve its own member's connection and the Host serves the members in order --> <!-- tests: coding/extension/host/subprocess/retained_factory_bus_test.go::TestGoFactoryReloadWithFactoryTimeSubscriptionsCompletesAndDeliversOnce, coding/extension/host/subprocess/retained_factory_bus_test.go::TestGoFactoryReloadRetainedMembersBesideAChangedMemberDeliverOnce, test/extension-conformance/events_bridge_reload_test.go::TestNativeEventBusReloadKeepsEveryFactoryTimeListenerOnce -->
- `/reload` no longer hangs when extensions that share a packed process (Go, Rust, Python or Lisp) subscribe to the event bus with `pi.events.on` while their factory runs. The Host wrote the admissions of every retained member before it accepted the first connection. A runner starts each admitted factory on its own goroutine or thread and takes them in whatever order the scheduler picks, and a factory that calls the Host before it returns waits for the Host to serve its member's connection. When a later member took the factory turn first, the Host waited for an earlier member that could not start its factory, so the reload never returned. The Host now admits each retained member after the members before it have registered, which is the order Pi loads its factories in, and every listener hears an emit once after a reload. PiG 0.5.2 through 0.7.0 have the defect. <!-- fix: fcb3ef3f9d --> <!-- cause: the Host admitted every retained member of a packed process before it accepted the first connection, while a factory that subscribes to the event bus waits for the Host to serve its own member's connection and the Host serves the members in order --> <!-- tests: coding/extension/host/subprocess/retained_factory_bus_test.go::TestGoFactoryReloadWithFactoryTimeSubscriptionsCompletesAndDeliversOnce, coding/extension/host/subprocess/retained_factory_bus_test.go::TestGoFactoryReloadRetainedMembersBesideAChangedMemberDeliverOnce, test/extension-conformance/events_bridge_reload_test.go::TestNativeEventBusReloadKeepsEveryFactoryTimeListenerOnce -->
- A packed Rust cell whose two members both failed to build could report the second member's panic as the first member's load error. The runner started the next member while the failed one was still writing its line, so the panic output of the next member split the line, and the host, finding no line of its own for the first member, read the last panic in the log. The next member now starts after the failed member's line is written and the host's wait for it has ended, as the Go runner already did. <!-- fix: ecc923b099d -->
- A packed Go, Python or Rust extension whose factory calls a host helper (`parseFrontmatter`, `Date.parse`, a `pi.events` call) and then panics, raises or returns no extension no longer hangs its load until the caller cancels it: the runner closes the connection the helper opened, and the extension is reported as the load error it is while its siblings load. <!-- fix: 2cef1bf5e0 -->
- When two extensions of one packed cell fail to load, each load error carries its own cause, not the last one the shared process wrote to its log. <!-- fix: 2cef1bf5e0 -->
- A panic in a Go editor component call is reported as `editor <call> failed: <message>`, as the other SDKs report theirs, instead of ending the extension's process, and a `handleInput` that fails still finishes its key, so the editor does not stall on the next one; the Rust SDK reports a panic's value in that notice rather than a fixed text. <!-- fix: 2cef1bf5e0, 0a9002fb19 -->
- A panic in an MCP credential store's `WithRefreshLock` or a settings storage's `WithLock` (Go), and a failing `onError` callback of `ctx.compact` (Lisp), no longer end the extension's process, which in a packed cell serves other extensions: the call fails with the error instead. <!-- fix: 2cef1bf5e0 -->
- When a goroutine or thread that a packed Go or Lisp extension started itself ends the process the cell shares, only that extension stops, reported with its panic and the log that holds it, and a `/reload` runs it isolated. The other extensions of the cell start again together, instead of every one stopping until `/reload`; they run their factories again, so their in-memory state starts over, and a call in flight when the process ended fails with the connection error (D274). The blame comes from the panic that ended the process only, never from a panic the SDK had recovered earlier or text an extension logged in the form of a panic or a backtrace: the host reads the Go trace only when the process exited with status 2 and no fatal error follows the panic, and the Lisp backtrace only when SBCL's unhandled-condition quit line follows it. A crash whose trace names no one extension, names two, or does not exist (`os.Exit`, a runtime fatal error, a kill) still stops the whole cell. <!-- fix: 34f110f09d, 28042f4fa6, 6c9d6559f6 -->
- A Node extension's editor component whose `handleInput` (or another call the host makes) throws is now reported as `editor handleInput failed: <message>`, naming the call as the Go, Rust, Python and Lisp SDKs do, instead of `editor failed: <message>`. <!-- fix: d22ad24247 -->
- A Go extension whose factory panics (where the TypeScript factory would throw, for example on a malformed environment variable) no longer takes down the other Go extensions that share its runtime cell. The packed runner now reports the panic as that extension's own load error, as an isolated process does, with the stack in its stderr log, and every sibling keeps running; `/reload` lists only the failing extension. A factory that returns no extension fails the same way in a Go, Python or Lisp cell (`factory returned nil`, `factory returned None`), and a Lisp cell no longer hangs the load until the caller cancels it when a factory returns nothing. <!-- fix: eda66dd663 -->
- `pig config` in the default theme no longer draws the space after a dim checkbox, or the name of a project-owned enabled item, faint: its spans close the faint attribute as Pi's do. <!-- fix: 80191207cd -->
- Print and JSON mode: on SIGTERM or SIGHUP the interrupted run now settles before `session_shutdown` handlers run, as the pinned Pi's `runtimeHost.dispose()` does. The session file gets the killed tool's result and the aborted assistant message, no second model request is made, and text mode reports the aborted result on stderr after a throwing handler's error. <!-- fix: 01f1936690eb518d7c036f905065336a018242ef -->
- RPC: a `prompt` that starts a run, and a `prompt` that fails in preparation, answer one microtask later than before, as the pinned Pi's extracted `_preparePrompt` orders them, so `steer` and `follow_up` sent in the same input batch before the prompt are answered first. <!-- fix: df43f7bb53d889ef55c6214e12e5ef6c7e964f08 -->
- Ctrl-C at the secret prompt of `pig auth login` now drops the rest of its input chunk, so an Enter arriving in the same read can no longer submit the secret, as in Pi. <!-- fix: 7f5979c13 -->
- Chord: a registry value an app keeps past `host.close` (`host.registry`) no longer keeps the closed host alive; after the close it reads its last composition and holds nothing of the host. <!-- fix: c72462b3703acedca15f2c330cd05a01f75f22ea -->
- A Node extension's `message_end` event now carries the same message object that `ctx.sessionManager.getEntries()` returns in the matching session entry, as in Pi, also when a `message_end` handler returns a replacement: the object then holds the stored, replaced message, as Pi writes the replacement into the original object, and only a handler that ran after the replacement holds another object. A handler that edits `event.message` in place (a redaction extension) now has the edit kept, as in Pi: later handlers, `turn_end`, `agent_end` and the saved entry hold the edited message, where before the edit was never saved. The `message` of `message_start` (system, user and tool result messages), the `message` and `toolResults` of `turn_end` and the `messages` of `agent_end` are those same objects, and extensions packed in one process hold one object for one message. This holds for the events of the session's own run, and for the handlers of one emit of an `ExtensionRunner` that a Go, Rust or Python extension drives (every handler of one emit holds one message object, as in Pi). A message an extension passes on `pi.events` to a Node extension in another process is the object that extension holds for the message when it holds it. Extensions in different processes (isolated) otherwise each hold their own object for a message, and a Go, Rust or Python caller's own message object is not the one a Node handler holds (D541). An edit made outside a `message_end` handler (in `message_start`, `turn_end` or `agent_end`) stays in the extension's own object and is not saved to the session. An extension that finds an entry with `entry.message === message` found none in PiG. Paseo's Pi integration depends on that lookup: through PiG its timeline did not show the user's prompt until the session was reopened, and a conversation rewind was refused. <!-- fix: e99791bd8b -->
- `RpcClient.Start` in the Go SDK returns as soon as the agent process exits, instead of after the fixed 100 ms settle window: a child that fails at once (a bad flag, a missing file) is reported in about 5 ms, with the same error text and with its stderr already collected. A child that is still running at the end of the window is returned as before. <!-- fix: 2af9ecf583 -->
- `pig piglet build` of an ahead-of-time image no longer waits 200 ms per extension after each training run's registration, and no longer closes the training connection in the middle of a registration frame that arrives in more than one piece. <!-- fix: 471d6fb3bd -->
- Loading several source-based extensions (Go, Rust, Lisp or Node directories) hashes their sources together instead of one after another, so each Go extension no longer waits for the previous one to re-read the SDK it replaces: 16 Go extensions hash in 45 ms instead of 170 ms. Load and registration order are unchanged. <!-- fix: 87faba8e7d -->
- A command that writes to both stdout and stderr no longer keeps a reader spinning while the other stream's output is delivered, and on Linux and macOS an idle command no longer wakes its output readers every 10 ms (Windows still wakes every 10 ms through its finite timeout): the output readers of the bash tool and of `pi.exec` children wait on the runtime's poller, and a `pi.exec` child's stderr reader waits for stdout's delivery on an event. Output order is unchanged (stdout before stderr). Process CPU while a slow consumer held stdout fell from 25-34 ms to 11-14 ms in a 0.5 s run, and from 14-19 ms to 0.5 ms for two idle pipes over 2 s. <!-- fix: aa48a2557c -->
- A detached helper that resolves `@earendil-works/pi-ai` as plain Node does now finds the names Pi's modules export: `convertMessages` of `api/openai-completions`, `PiMessagesResponseError` of `api/pi-messages`, `api/google-shared`, the Codex WebSocket helpers `closeOpenAICodexWebSocketSessions`, `getOpenAICodexWebSocketDebugStats` and `resetOpenAICodexWebSocketDebugStats` of `api/openai-codex-responses` (they act on the provider-bridge child that serves the helper's streams), and the `lazy-bedrock-provider` and `lazy-oauth` subpaths (D74). <!-- fix: 6c3e63b94d, 7d26c9d83e --> <!-- cause: the D74 stand-ins exported only stream and streamSimple and the harness peer's exports list had no entry for two subpaths of Pi's package.json, and no test compared the export names or the subpath list with Pi's -->
- A `pi.events` listener's failure is reported before the command that emitted answers, as in Pi: an RPC client reads every `extension_error` line before the command's response (`E E E E R`, and `E R` for a listener that rejects after an await), and print and JSON mode write the error to stderr before the command's own output, whether the extensions share a Node process or each run in their own. Cause: a Node runtime writes the failing listener's `report_error` notification before the response, but the connection's read loop routed the response straight to its waiter while the notification went through the Host's loop; a shared Node realm sent the listener's report on the listener's connection and the emitter's response on another; and the quiesce that releases the emitter of a listener that rejects after an await was counted on the read loop before the Host's loop applied the report. The read loop now queues the response and the quiesce behind the unapplied report, and a shared realm sends the report on the emitter's connection, naming the listening extension (the Host takes the name only for an extension of the connection's own process and applies any other name's report as the connection's own). No released PiG has this: the `report_error` notification arrives with the same release. <!-- fix: 0aecafce0a, 447a4edc21, 6390f27ae9, 95a798f82a -->
- `pi.exec` no longer reports code 0 for a command that a signal ended. A command that timed out, was aborted, crashed or was killed from outside returned `code: 0`, which an extension checking `result.code === 0` took for a success; it now returns 128 plus the signal number as a shell does (143 for SIGTERM, 137 for SIGKILL), as Pi does (upstream #12089). <!-- fix: 0bb39707e5 -->
- agent (Go API): a message that a tool or an `AfterToolCall` hook of a parallel tool batch replaced in place in its context (`call.Context.Messages[i] = m`) never reached the run: with two or more calls each call wrote a copy, so the batch's other calls and the next model request did not see it. Pi hands every call of the batch one live context: the other calls read the new message and the next request carries it. Every call now receives the run's own messages, as the calls of a sequential batch do. The after hooks of a batch still run one at a time; the tools of a parallel batch run at the same time, so a tool that reads or writes a message another call's code may touch at that moment has to lock with it. No extension is affected: the hook context never reaches an extension. Of the releases, v0.7.0 has the lost write (its hooks receive a copy of the messages that the run never reads back; v0.2.0 and v0.3.0 hand hooks no context). The change also removes a data race of the per-call copy (the second call's copy was taken after the first call's goroutine had started), which was never released. <!-- fix: 49e7c6d8bc87e7251b89a5046b78b64bbea0a6f0 -->
- Building the compiled host with Pi-Bolt 0.7.4 crashed the compiler ("Segmentation fault at address 0x30", on the CI image and on the host) in the ahead-of-time step whenever the build's function order held any record, so `pig-bolt` built no image. Pi-Bolt 1.1.2 builds the same input; the Piglet pins it. <!-- fix: 9b33064ca0, a921aa3352 -->
- A build's training run ended on a 200 ms timer: every extension of every build waited 200 ms, and a registration larger than one read was cut and its runtime's next write failed with a broken pipe. It now ends on the registration frame (339 and 398 ms before, 150 and 197 ms after). <!-- fix: 0684c43cd0, b8b9af5e63 -->
- The training run's socket was in the build's work directory, whose path under a deep agent directory can exceed what a Unix socket address holds (108 bytes); every training run of such a build failed to listen, was logged and skipped, and the build's function order lacked each extension's startup. The socket is in a short directory of its own. <!-- fix: 0a0d27d74a -->
- A set whose file locates itself by a value of `import.meta` (`const meta = import.meta; readFileSync(new URL("./x", meta.url))`) was not refused and compiled to a silently wrong result. It is refused, and the set runs on Bun. <!-- fix: 91e6a2498b -->
- Stopping and continuing `pig` (Ctrl+Z, then `fg`) while it asks for an API key at the login prompt no longer ends the prompt with `interrupted system call` on macOS: the prompt enters and leaves raw mode through the same retrying calls as the main screen, as Node's `setRawMode` retries the call. <!-- fix: a397ee91ed -->
- Tooling: `make pin-bump` retires the carried oracle as it is built now. The retirement step still looked for the earlier mechanism (a Makefile block that ended in `carried-oracles-run`, a rewritten `suspendableOraclePackages`), so a bump to a Pi that contains the carried commit stopped at `Makefile: nothing to retire` and `make pin-check` failed in three tests of `automation/pin/test_carried.py`. It now deletes what exists only for the carried run: the Makefile block (`CARRIED_ORACLE_REF`, the two test lists, `test-carried-oracles`, `test-carried-oracles-guard`), the CI step that runs the guard, `automation/pin/carried_guard.py` and its tests, the three skips of the oracle tests (`skipWithoutSuspendableWork`, `suspendableOraclePackages`, `namespaceOracleSkip`), the reviewed decisions carried ahead of the pin, the paragraph on the carried run in `docs/parity/upstream-pin.md`, and the commit's frozen files. `pin.py override-tree` and `internal/pioracle` stay: they serve a run at any Pi commit. Three things changed in how it does that: every piece is looked up before a file is written, so a tree that lacks one stops the bump with `<file>: nothing to retire (<piece> is not there)` and no edit (before, the files edited up to that point stayed edited, and so did the backports script); the frozen provider data and closure of the carried commit are kept when the bump's target is that very commit, whose oracle build reads them (before, they were deleted and the new pin's first build would have hydrated live model data); and a rerun after a retirement reports `carried oracle: none`. <!-- fix: 8e49dba2413a866f335014456f69446483b5bddf -->
- A runtime API key (`--api-key`, `SetRuntimeAPIKey`) for a Radius provider now counts as its auth, as it does in Pi: the provider has configured auth, its models are in the available list and it counts as an available provider. Before, requests used the key but the Radius catalog was not listed. <!-- fix: a94dde31ede -->
- Windows: installing a plugin from npm extracts the packed tarball with a relative archive name, so the `tar` of Git for Windows (which reads `C:\...` as a file on host `C`) no longer fails with "Cannot connect to C: resolve failed". Pi passes the absolute path and fails there (D616, owner approved 2026-11-10). <!-- fix: 5043738f102ccc23820ceefcc241c2495b6a5e8f -->
- Windows: installing a plugin from npm also names the extraction directory relative to the pack directory (`-C ../<dir>`), so the `tar` of Git for Windows, which resolves a `-C C:\...` name against its working directory, no longer fails with "Cannot open: No such file or directory". Pi passes the absolute directory (D616 now names the archive and the destination). <!-- fix: 4812c0127bc6c2049a5c417ebc419edc355ea7bb -->
- Installing a Chord plugin works with npm 12: `npm pack --json` prints an object keyed by package name there, and the install now reads the member of the package it asked for instead of the first member (the list npm 11 and earlier print is read as before), as in Pi. <!-- fix: 2a0a44d8b02e0641c82373a6311a1fa754cf7585 -->
- When a session's working directory no longer exists, interactive mode now offers Continue, Fork or Cancel (Pi 1.5.2): Continue runs the session in the current directory without storing the choice, Fork copies it into the current directory as a new session so the next resume no longer asks. This applies at startup (`--session`, `--resume`), to `/resume`, to `ctx.switchSession()` from extensions and to `/import`; a failed `/import` removes the copy it made, and Anthropic OAuth requests report Claude Code 2.1.322. <!-- fix: 7ecacae312 -->
- CI: the pre-flight no longer rejects a pull request for the merge of `main` that GitHub's "Update branch" button adds. That commit is GitHub's and cannot carry a `Signed-off-by` line, so the `signoff` check failed every pull request kept current that way. The check now exempts it, and only it: two parents, committed and verified by GitHub, the second parent on the base branch, and the tree git's own merge of the two parents writes. A merge made by hand, a merge of another branch and a merge with a conflict resolution or an edit still need the line, as does every commit the pull request adds. <!-- fix: 349959b6ff -->
- A Piglet whose `discovery.extensions` leaves out `user` no longer runs the user's extensions before a project trust decision. When the project had config that needs one (for example `.pig/mcp.json`), the pre-trust pass loaded `~/.pig/agent/extensions` with a fixed user scope, so an ambient extension's factory ran in a Piglet that discovers none (it did not join the session), and a closed Piglet Binary built without the Node runtime failed to start. The pre-trust pass now reads the scopes the Piglet's discovery allows for an untrusted project; stock pig still loads user extensions there, as Pi does. <!-- fix: bddbf4c88 -->
- A `-p`, `--mode json` or `--mode rpc` run over a large session no longer sometimes keeps the Go GC target of 400 past 64 MiB live heap. The check that returns to the default 100 waited for a cleanup after each collection, and that cleanup could run late or miss the collection that found the large heap; on a 66 MB session about 1 run in 13 under CPU load exited at target 400 with a peak RSS 1.37-1.80x that of `GOGC=100`. A goroutine now reads the live heap every 5 ms (every second while no collection finishes), so the fallback fires once a read finds the latest finished collection's live heap above 64 MiB. A later collection can replace that value before the next read, so a read can miss a short-lived peak, but the fallback no longer waits on a cleanup. Output is unchanged. <!-- fix: 3fe5b201f0 -->
- A `-p`, `--mode json` or `--mode rpc` run over a large session no longer sometimes keeps the Go GC target of 400 past 64 MiB live heap. The check that returns to the default 100 waited for a cleanup after each collection, and that cleanup could run late or miss the collection that found the large heap; on a 66 MB session about 1 run in 13 under CPU load exited at target 400 with a peak RSS 1.37-1.80x that of `GOGC=100`. A goroutine now reads the live heap every 5 ms (every second while no collection finishes), so the fallback fires after the first collection that finds more than 64 MiB live. Output is unchanged. <!-- fix: 95db124c04 -->
- Interactive mode: a `before_agent_start` handler's edit of `systemPromptOptions` (for example `appendSystemPrompt`, `customPrompt` or `contextFiles`) is sent to the model also when a skill is loaded and the active tools do not include `read`. In that case the request kept the startup prompt and changed only its tool list and rules, so the edit was lost and the skills section still told the model to use the `read` tool. Print, JSON and RPC mode were not affected. <!-- fix: 45c0b46c0a40582190d677af1cebb573e1e9214a -->
- The write card and the expanded read card of a file whose extension is `constructor` or `__proto__` (for example `notes.constructor`) are the ordinary cards with the file's text, as for any extension without a known language. Pi looks the extension up in a plain JavaScript object, finds a member inherited from `Object.prototype`, its highlighter throws and Pi falls back to its generic card; PiG does not copy that defect (D645). This replaces the change of dd2727b68af, which had made PiG draw Pi's fallback for these cards and is in no release. <!-- fix: eabcdf054ae -->
- A Mermaid class named `__proto__` (`classDef __proto__ fill:#f00` with `class A __proto__` or `A:::__proto__`, in flowcharts, class diagrams and state diagrams) styles its nodes, as it does in Pi. PiG left the class out and drew the nodes without the style. <!-- fix: 1407bdfc738 -->
- For an extension written with the Go, Rust, Python or Lisp SDK, `Value.Check` and `Value.Errors` with `uniqueItems` no longer take two objects that differ only in a member named `constructor` for the same item. TypeBox leaves that member out of its hash; PiG hashes it like any other (D645). <!-- fix: eabcdf054ae -->
- `pig-evals` prints its report title in bold when `TERM` is `constructor` or `__proto__` and `COLORTERM` is set, as for any other `TERM` it does not know (D645). <!-- fix: eabcdf054ae -->
- A name that is also a member of JavaScript's `Object.prototype` (`constructor`, `toString`, `hasOwnProperty`, `__proto__` and the like) is treated as any other name in more places (D645). `pig mcp add constructor -- <command>` reports the server as added (it said `Replaced` the first time), `pig mcp add __proto__ -- <command>` writes the server to `mcp.json` (it was not written at all), and `pig mcp remove` of such a name that the file does not hold says there is no such server (it said `Removed`). A `keybindings.json` key so named is left as written: it was renamed to text such as `function Object() { [native code] }` and the file was rewritten. Pi 1.5.2 does the old things. In Node extensions, `ctx.ui.theme.fg`, `bg`, `getFgAnsi` and `getBgAnsi` throw `Unknown theme color: <token>` for a token so named, as Pi does and as the other SDKs did: `fg` threw `open.endsWith is not a function`, `bg` drew the text of a native function before the text, and the two getters returned a function. `ctx.ui.setStatus("__proto__", text)` is a status the extension's own footer reads back in the same turn, a provider registered under the name `__proto__` is read like any other provider, and `pi.getSettings()` hands the settings without any `__proto__` member. <!-- fix: 88bbdd2eaa5883a3b70bca3a7ad36f73339a5a72 -->
- For a provider built with `CreateProvider` (an SDK or natively registered provider, or a direct user of package ai) that fetches a large model catalog, every model lookup re-merged the provider's baseline and fetched catalogs on every read, slowing model selection and request setup for that provider; built-in providers were not affected; the catalog is now merged once when published (stored restore or network refresh) and cached, with public getters returning an owned copy and internal lookups reading the cached snapshot directly. Affects v0.4.0, v0.4.1, v0.5.0, v0.5.1, v0.5.2, v0.5.3, v0.7.0. <!-- fix: dc99069530 --> <!-- cause: 3dd4d752e8; upstream Pi 073b0bae8 (#12366, closes #12311) --> <!-- tests: ai/models_provider_catalog_merge_test.go::TestCreateProviderMergesCatalogOncePerPublishUpstream, ai/models_provider_catalog_merge_test.go::TestCreateProviderRestoredCatalogMergesOncePerPublish, ai/models_provider_catalog_merge_test.go::TestCreateProviderCatalogReadAllocs, ai/models_provider_catalog_merge_test.go::TestCreateProviderCatalogMergeMatchesLegacy, ai/models_provider_catalog_merge_test.go::TestCreateProviderCatalogConcurrentReadsDuringRefresh, ai/models_provider_catalog_merge_test.go::TestCreateProviderReplacedGetterBypassesCache -->
- The error for a provider with no credentials now reads `Provider is not configured: <id>` as in Pi, where it read `provider is not configured: <id>`, so a failed `/compact` or prompt after `auth.json` was emptied shows Pi's sentence. <!-- fix: 519554ac1db6 --> <!-- cause: the messages were written in Go error-string style (lowercase) instead of copied from Pi's ModelsError text, and their tests pinned the lowercase copy -->
- A `before_provider_request` handler that adds members to the Google, Vertex or pi-messages request it was handed sees them written in a fixed order: an array-index key (`"9"`) first, as Pi's object enumerates it, then the members the provider created in Pi's order, then the added members in byte order (a Go map keeps no insertion order). The order of the added members was decided by a sort of the map's iteration order before the fix, so it is the same on every call now. The unreleased change that gave a handler Pi's member order introduced the window; no release has it. <!-- tests: ai/hook_payload_order_extras_test.go::TestMarshalHookPayloadWritesAddedMembersInOwnKeyOrder --> <!-- fix: 7781c9298c -->
- A `before_provider_request` handler of a subprocess extension (Node, Python, Go, Rust, Lisp) now receives the request a Google, Vertex or pi-messages provider is about to send with its members in the order Pi's provider creates them (the model, contents and config of Google's parameters, the part members thought, text, thoughtSignature, functionCall before thoughtSignature), where it received them sorted by name. A handler that returns the payload unchanged now sends the same bytes as no handler. The Google and Vertex payload has been a map since v0.3.0 and the pi-messages payload since v0.2.0; before them Google's was a struct. The Google request body itself also writes a replayed part's members in that order. <!-- tests: ai/pi_messages_payload_oracle_test.go::TestPiMessagesPayloadMatchesPi, ai/google_replayed_part_order_test.go::TestGoogleReplayedPartsHavePiMemberOrder, coding/extension/host/subprocess/event_payload_order_test.go::TestBeforeProviderRequestWireKeepsPiMemberOrder --> <!-- fix: c13e751f73 -->
- Aborting a turn whose model is served by an extension provider (`registerProvider` with `streamSimple`) now keeps what the provider's stream does after the abort, as Pi does: the text already shown, the provider's own stop reason and error message, or its complete answer when it ignores the abort. PiG's extension host ended such a stream at the abort with a message of its own (empty content, `aborted`, `context canceled`), so the text the user had seen was gone from the turn, from the session file and from the next request's context. The abort now only aborts the signal the provider holds, in the Go, Node, Python, Rust and Lisp SDKs, and the provider's stream decides how the turn ends; a provider that never reacts holds the turn, as in Pi, and no time limit is added. In RPC mode, when stdin closes while a Node provider's aborted stream never reacts, the process exits 0 once the runtime's event loop is empty, as Pi's process does, and leaves no runtime process. PiG 0.3.0 through 0.7.0 have the defect. <!-- fix: cc05ab3196 -->
- OpenAI Responses requests replay a stored reasoning item as it was stored, and the items of a client tool search have Pi's member order. A replayed reasoning item was rewritten `type, id, summary, encrypted_content` and lost any member PiG does not know; Pi sends the stored object as the provider wrote it. The `tool_search_call` and `tool_search_output` items were written `type, status, call_id, ...` (Pi: `type, call_id, execution, status, ...`). This held for OpenAI, Azure OpenAI and ChatGPT (Codex) Responses. A stored reasoning signature that is not JSON now ends the request with the JSON error before anything is sent, as in Pi, where PiG dropped the block and sent the request; only a block of the same provider, API and model id with such a signature reaches this, which means a hand-edited or corrupted session. <!-- fix: 202aea01ba -->
- A Mistral request that names a function as its tool choice writes the object `type, function`, as Pi does; PiG wrote `function, type`. The content was the same. Only an extension or SDK caller that passes a tool choice object reaches this. <!-- fix: 4de6fbaf00 -->
- Azure OpenAI Responses requests hold the members Pi's Azure requests hold. PiG sent Azure three members Pi does not send: `prompt_cache_retention` (with long cache retention), `prompt_cache_options` (for a model with explicit cache mode) and `service_tier` (when one was configured). PiG left out two members Pi sends: `prompt_cache_key` when cache retention is `none`, and `max_output_tokens` for a model marked as not supporting it. <!-- fix: b7d2c0775e -->
- OpenAI Chat Completions request bodies now have the member order of the bodies Pi sends. A replayed assistant message that carries reasoning was written `role, content, tool_calls, reasoning_content` (Pi: `role, content, reasoning_content, tool_calls`; the same for `reasoning` and `reasoning_text`), and the z.ai `thinking` member was `clear_thinking, type` (Pi: `type, clear_thinking`). The content was the same. This held for every provider that uses the Chat Completions API. A request built from a transcript that converts to no message now sends `"messages":[]`, as Pi does, where PiG sent `"messages":null`; a first prompt and a compaction's own request cannot produce one; an extension whose `context` handler returns an empty message list can. Not yet in Pi's order: objects a model's catalog entry or a caller supplies (`chat_template_kwargs`, `chat_template_args`, the OpenRouter `provider` routing object, sampling parameters), which PiG writes with sorted keys. <!-- fix: ce136a8bd5 -->
- A Node extension's `refreshModels`, both as a provider config's callback and as a provider object's method, now receives the context object Pi builds (`packages/ai/src/models.ts`): its members in Pi's order (the login, the stored catalog, `publish`, `allowNetwork`, `force`, `signal`, `baseUrl`), every key present, and a member Pi has no value for (no login, no stored catalog, no `force`, no `baseUrl`) is `undefined`. The config form listed `allowNetwork` and `baseUrl` first and `publish` last and left the unset members out, so `Object.keys(context)` and `'force' in context` answered differently from Pi; the provider object listed `publish` last and gave the unset members `null`, so `Object.keys(context)` and an `=== undefined` check on an unset member answered differently from Pi. <!-- fix: 5e55e0d13 -->
- Closing an RPC client's input while a `bash` command is running, or quitting interactive mode with Ctrl+D while a `!` command is running and an extension's `session_shutdown` handler never settles (the drained-loop quit), left that shell command and its descendants running after `pig` exited 0. `pig` now kills tracked shell process trees before exiting on both paths, as it already does on `/quit`, and on Windows bounds the whole exit-path kill (taskkill, job termination, and waiting on job members) at 2,000 ms (following Pi 31b407dc63, #11889). Affects 0.3.0 through 0.7.0 (RPC input end; drained-loop quit was introduced after 0.7.0). <!-- fix: 867727906e8f7b8359bc98735a0a17eaa01cd096 --> <!-- cause: exitRPC in coding/cli/rpc_mode.go and exitAtDrainedQuit in coding/cli/interactive_build.go exited via os.Exit without calling tools.KillTrackedDetachedChildren, so os.Exit raced Session.Dispose's asynchronous AbortBash kill and left the shell's process group or Windows job alive --> <!-- tests: coding/cli/rpc_quit_kills_bash_unix_test.go::TestRPCInputEndKillsRunningBashTree, coding/cli/rpc_quit_kills_bash_unix_test.go::TestRPCInputEndKillsRunningBashTreeNoExt, coding/cli/rpc_quit_kills_bash_unix_test.go::TestRPCExtensionShutdownWhileBashRuns, coding/cli/rpc_quit_kills_bash_unix_test.go::TestListenConnectionEOFDoesNotKillSiblingConnectionBash, coding/cli/rpc_quit_kills_bash_windows_test.go::TestWin_RPCInputEndKillsRunningBashTree, coding/cli/interactive_drained_quit_bash_linux_test.go::TestInteractiveDrainedQuitKillsRunningUserBash, internal/codingagent/tools/taskkill_port_test.go::TestTaskkillCommandContextAllPIDs, internal/codingagent/tools/bash_group_windows_test.go::TestWin_KillTrackedProcessGroupsReapsJobDescendants, internal/codingagent/tools/bash_group_windows_test.go::TestWin_KillTrackedProcessGroupsBoundedExit -->
- CI: the nightly `-race` run no longer fails on the nested modules that only build inside a Go workspace (`apps/p2`, `apps/p2desktop`; `piglets/porter/extensions/pig-porter` builds and tests with `GOWORK=off` against its released dependencies and stays as it was): their entries in `automation/ci/race-packages.txt` carry `workspace`, and `test-race-nightly.sh` runs them without `GOWORK=off`. `race-coverage.sh` accepts only an empty or `workspace` third column on a group entry. <!-- fix: 05c7426135850e8d7bdcb3b863f13290caf41000 -->
- `pig --mode rpc --listen`: a connection that registered just after the server received SIGTERM was shut down while its session was still starting, and the shutdown read the extension runner while the start filled it, a data race. The shutdown now waits until the connection's first session start has bound the extensions (not for its `session_start` handlers). <!-- fix: 26787ff149eabe921bd663ef0bb9503bd78ac69d -->
- A session swap (`/new`, `/resume`, `/fork`, `Session.ReplaceInner`) no longer races with `/new`, a fork or a clone that reads whether the session has a file, and a routed request stores a virtual model's router state on the session it read the state from, not on one a swap installed meanwhile. <!-- fix: 4ed1d7213 -->
- `Session.ID`, `Session.Path`, `Session.CWD` and `Session.Inner` no longer race with a session swap (`/new`, `/resume`, `/fork`, `Session.ReplaceInner`): a host call that reads the session id while the swap runs sees the old or the new session, and the Go race detector no longer reports the read. <!-- fix: 4f3cc2e06 -->
- A credential read from read-only auth storage (`ReadOnlyAuthStorage`, used by `pig auth check --no-refresh`) now keeps the member order of the auth.json entry when anything prints or forwards it, as Pi does: an OAuth entry written `type, access, refresh, expires` is no longer returned as `type, refresh, access, expires`, and members the typed form does not model keep their place. Only the order changes, not which members are returned. Present since 0.2.0. <!-- fix: e0610029327 --> <!-- cause: the read-only decode built its credential from a map and never recorded the entry's member order, which the writable decode records, so marshaling fell back to struct order -->
- Shutting down a Session no longer leaves a provider's model refresh, or an auth check it had abandoned, running against the agent directory. Closing the registry's model tasks cancelled the native model collection's refreshes but joined their work on a detached goroutine, so the refresh could still be writing its catalog after `Close` returned and the owner removed the directory (which on Windows cannot delete a directory whose file is still being written). `ai.Models` gains `Drain`, which cancels active refreshes and waits for the work the collection runs for its own queries (a provider's refresh and its store write, auth resolution and checks, availability) but not for a caller's login or stream, and `CloseModelTasks` calls it before returning. <!-- fix: 2c7db1a65508be8e94a43ceb332ca986321338f8 -->
- Shutting down a Session no longer leaves a provider's model refresh, or an auth check it had abandoned, running against the agent directory. Closing the registry's model tasks cancelled the native model collection's refreshes but joined their work on a detached goroutine, so the refresh could still be writing its catalog after `Close` returned and the owner removed the directory (which on Windows cannot delete a directory whose file is still being written). `ai.Models` gains `Drain`, which cancels active refreshes and waits for the work the collection runs for its own queries (a provider's refresh and its store write, auth resolution and checks, availability) but not for a caller's login or stream, and `CloseModelTasks` calls it before returning. <!-- fix: ba5e8abb4e16a25468440932ba9804af45c6f4dd -->
- Shutting down a Session no longer leaves a provider's model refresh, or an auth check it had abandoned, running against the agent directory. Closing the registry's model tasks cancelled the native model collection's refreshes but joined their work on a detached goroutine, so the refresh could still be writing its catalog after `Close` returned and the owner removed the directory (which on Windows cannot delete a directory whose file is still being written). `ai.Models` gains `Drain`, which cancels active refreshes and waits for the work the collection runs for its own queries (a provider's refresh and its store write, auth resolution and checks, availability) but not for a caller's login or stream, and `CloseModelTasks` calls it before returning. <!-- fix: d73376b814100a3af5ea58fd72da70a9a75e2ed4 -->
- Release workflow: a run from a private repository now fails in its first step, with the reason, instead of building every archive and stopping at the publish job. Attestation is skipped for private repositories and `assemble-evidence.py` requires a Sigstore bundle for every archive. <!-- fix: d986ba346f284af97a9e6eb74a4b1e73e7dad1d6 -->
- Release workflow: the draft GitHub Release takes its body from `docs/release/<version>-release-notes-draft.md` when that file exists, and from GitHub's generated notes only when it does not. The publish job stops, before it creates anything, while that draft still has the generator's "Draft. Not published." banner. <!-- fix: d986ba346f284af97a9e6eb74a4b1e73e7dad1d6 -->
- Release workflow: the packaged smoke steps compare the `pig:` line of `pig version` with the release version, for the `pig` archives and for the `pig` inside each `pig-acp` archive. They checked only exit codes before. <!-- fix: d986ba346f284af97a9e6eb74a4b1e73e7dad1d6 -->
- `make changelog-fold` stops, changing nothing, while `## [Unreleased]` still holds entries, and names `set-version --move-unreleased`; `make changelog-fold VERSION=Unreleased` is refused with its own message. The fold moves fragments only, so an entry left under Unreleased (the 0.8.0 `klauspost/compress` Security entry) was missing from the release section. <!-- fix: 0223bea7e7c207ed182bae038ccd2f4a989a53fc -->
- `docs/project/PROVENANCE.md` named an earlier release of Pi, not the pin, as the upstream pin. It now states the pin from `.upstream/pin` (`1.5.1`, the release tag `v1.5.1`), and `make pin-sync` and `make pin-check` keep it current. <!-- fix: 4219d7aa50ec06651ed37fb99567a1ac3457cfe3 -->
- extensions: the animated loader of an extension's view kept running after its message or tool card was gone from the transcript. A transcript that is rebuilt (after `/reload`, a compaction, `/tree`) drops its cards, and each dropped view with a loader left a timer that asked the terminal to draw again on every tick and kept the view and its extension's connection for the rest of the session: fifty rebuilds left fifty timers, and a session that reloaded an extension drawing such views grew by about 27 KiB for each reload (54 KiB for two extensions in one cell). A loader is now animated while its view is drawn, stops within one tick once nothing draws it, and starts again with the next draw. Present in releases 0.5.0 to 0.7.0. <!-- fix: 36123ec15c1635385ccfe178a2ddcb009d40966e -->
- extensions: a widget that an extension set before `/reload` and did not set again stayed on screen for the rest of the session, for an extension process and for an extension of the host process alike. `/reload` now clears the extension widgets when it begins, as Pi does, and the reloaded extensions set their own. Present in releases 0.2.0 to 0.7.0. <!-- fix: 78f9ff1ba708ab9e09164c29c5b92b748f7267c3 -->
- extensions: `/reload` left on screen what the replaced extensions had set and Pi resets when a reload begins: keyed statuses (`ctx.ui.setStatus`), a custom footer and header, the working message and indicator, the hidden thinking label, overlays, and the terminal title; a terminal input listener (`ctx.ui.onTerminalInput`) of a replaced extension kept receiving every key, and `ctx.ui.getEditorComponent()` kept answering its editor factory. A session replacement (`/new`, `/resume`, `/fork`) kept the statuses, the footer and header, the title and the input listeners. Both now reset all of them, as Pi's `resetExtensionUI` does, and dispose the footer and header components; an extension that wants them after a reload sets them again in its `session_start` handler. Present in releases 0.2.0 to 0.7.0. <!-- fix: d1848ed259ba0c3557f81a0ef9f54b3bb988a742 -->
- `/reload` and every session replacement now install the configured git and npm packages that are missing and refresh the temporary `-e` git and npm packages, as Pi's resource loader does on every load: `/new`, `/resume`, `/fork` and the RPC `new_session`, `switch_session` and `fork` as well as startup. Before, only startup installed (since v0.3.0; `/reload` never did since v0.2.0), so a package added to `settings.json` in a running session stayed missing until the next start. In the interactive TUI the install runs while the reload message is shown and git and npm output stays off the screen, and a failure is listed under `[Extension issues]`. <!-- fix: 451287c12e -->
- A `/reload` that catches an extension command awaiting `ctx.ui.custom(...)` no longer lets the command go on. The reload closed the overlay's call with `undefined` when it retired the extension's old instance, so the code after the `await` ran in the replaced or removed instance, and a second command could start behind it; Pi removes the overlay and leaves the call pending, so the command never goes on (probed on Pi 1.5.2 for the extension replaced and removed). The overlay also stayed on the screen in isolated mode, where the old instance stays until its command returns; it now leaves the screen at the reload in both modes. The call ends with the session, with the extension's connection or with the component's own close. A closed connection also ends the dialogs (`select`, `confirm`, `input`, `editor`) its extension still awaited: they waited for an answer nothing would take after a graceful close. Node, Go, Python and Rust components alike. Present since 0.2.0. <!-- tests: coding/extension/host/subprocess/reload_pending_call_test.go::TestReloadLeavesPendingCustomCallPending, coding/extension/host/subprocess/reload_pending_dialog_test.go::TestReloadLeavesPendingDialogCallsPending, coding/extension/host/subprocess/packed_go_test.go::TestAC59PackedSDKFocusedComponentsOwnInput, internal/codingagent/remote_overlay_retire_test.go::TestRemoteOverlayRetireLeavesTheCallPending --> <!-- fix: 3da926800b -->
- An extension that registered a provider and is then removed (its file deleted, or taken out of the extension settings) keeps answering after `/reload`, as it does in Pi: the provider stays listed in `/model`, stays selectable, and a prompt to it is answered by the old extension, even across a second `/reload`. PiG stopped the removed extension and dropped its provider, so the model vanished and a prompt failed with "No API key found". A removed extension that owns a provider (also a bridged OAuth login or a virtual model) keeps its process and its registrations but loses everything else (tools, commands, handlers, widgets, MCP servers, events); its process ends with the session or when another extension takes its last name over. Present in every release up to and including v0.7.0. <!-- tests: coding/extension_provider_survives_removal_test.go::TestRemovedExtensionProviderStillAnswersAfterReload, coding/extension/host/subprocess/generation_linger_test.go::TestRemovedExtensionKeepsItsProviderAcrossTwoReloads, coding/extension/host/subprocess/generation_linger_packed_test.go::TestPackedGoMemberRemovedByAReloadKeepsItsProviderUntilShutdown --> <!-- fix: 90890e61c1 -->
- A key received after a /reload had completed could be dropped by the input loop; the editor now receives it, in the order typed. Keys typed while the reload runs are still dropped, as in Pi. <!-- fix: 8ed6366ca3b2468bef84bac9a6a9047d50f29341 -->
- extensions: a session leaked one goroutine and the state of the replaced generation (about 14 KiB for an extension in its own process, about 30 KiB for a cell of two) for every `/reload` of an unchanged subprocess extension, until the extension's process ended. A reload keeps that process and runs the extension's factory in it again; each generation it replaced kept a goroutine that waited for the process to exit. The same goroutines removed the extension's stderr log the moment the process died, so the crash notice of a process that had been reloaded did not name its log. The end of a process is now handled once: over a hundred reloads the host's goroutines do not grow and its live heap stays within 512 KiB, for every SDK (Node, Go, Python, Rust, Lisp), isolated and packed, and the crash notice names the log as it does for a process that was never reloaded. Present in releases 0.3.0 to 0.7.0. <!-- fix: 1b699a5442ffcee3b1cec84f1cd64b92609ed599 -->
- A left click on a custom message or entry card now toggles it as it does in Pi: a message renderer receives the same message identity on every rebuild, the component it returns takes the mouse, and the extension keeps the card's state per message, and for an entry it keeps it across compaction, `/tree` and a resume, as Pi's renderer does for the session manager's one object per entry. The Node SDK runs Pi's own `WeakMap` and `MouseRegion` renderer unchanged, and the host hit-tests the `MouseRegion` rectangles the runtime finds in one walk over the rules by which Pi's dispatch hands an event down (a 4000-line card costs milliseconds, where asking Pi's dispatch about every cell took seconds), so a click on a card's padding falls through to text selection as in Pi and only a component with a hand-written `handleMouse` takes the click as a whole (D277); the Go, Rust, Python and Lisp SDKs get `options.state` and `MessageViewEvent`/`EntryViewEvent` handlers for the clicks on their view's mouse regions. A click does no IPC on the TUI loop, and a transcript container now redraws a component whose handler changed it without telling the container. <!-- fix: 44f93fea88 -->
- A Node extension's handler that wrote the session (`pi.setSessionName`, `pi.setLabel`, `pi.sendMessage`) after an `await` read back a session log without the entry it had just written (`ctx.sessionManager.getEntries()` still ended in the earlier entry), and the replicated log later lost all but one entry, where Pi's in-process log shows every write to the next read. Every handler of an extension that registers `pi.onLoaded` is such a handler: its requests first await the loaded handlers. The runtime applied the host's state push for a write after the push for the next write, because the receive loop that held the first push (handed to it while it waited, or taken from its queue) is unable to read it during the synchronous call that follows an `await`. The runtime now applies the state in the order the host sent it. <!-- fix: 2173cc13ed -->
- Resource reload: an extension load hook or project-trust callback that reloads the resources with the context it received no longer deadlocks on the loader's operation lock; the nested reload runs inside the outer one, as Pi's unlocked reload does. <!-- fix: 2dc09ec10c05368947da2869f0d20a9e2f6d3a85 -->
- Resuming a session (`pig -c`, `--resume`, `--session`, and the SDK's `CreateAgentSessionFromServices`) whose saved model is gone no longer picks a model that your account does not list. The fallback chose from every model of a provider that had credentials, so an account that lists only some models (GitHub Copilot's list of models for your plan), or a provider whose own filter hides a model, was given a model it cannot use, where Pi gives it only a listed model, or none when none is listed and shows "No models available". The fallback now reads the same models `/model` offers. It was present in v0.7.0 and, in the startup path, in v0.3.0. <!-- fix: 60285d7fbd --> <!-- cause: both fallback selectors listed available models as the composed catalog filtered by provider auth, not the published availability snapshot, which applies each provider's per-credential model filter -->
- A turn that ends with a provider error reading `Connection closed.`, such as a gateway cutting a stream with an `api_error` event, is now retried automatically like other dropped connections, instead of stopping with the error; the same applies to the agent proxy's `Connection closed by proxy server before the response completed` error, in the extension SDKs' `isRetryableAssistantError`, and for durable agents (upstream #12093). <!-- fix: be8900bb344095aad0d8a8edfa61bead5dcd18a3 -->
- After a reload that failed (an extension that no longer loads, or a settings file the resource loader rejects), the session goes on with the extensions of the old load, as in Pi: the next prompt reaches their input, before_agent_start, tool_call and tool_result handlers, their tools run, and a handler that reads its stale ctx gets an extension error while the prompt goes on. PiG ended the first event after the failed reload with the stale error instead: `pig -p` exited 1 with "This extension ctx is stale ...", and an RPC prompt never ran. Present in every release since v0.2.0. <!-- cause: every emit method of the in-process runner asserted the runner active on entry (since v0.2.0), where Pi's emit methods never check staleness (runner.ts:1135-1560), so the first event of the next prompt after a failed reload returned the stale error to the session --> <!-- tests: coding/extension/host/inproc/stale_emit_delivery_test.go::TestEveryEmitDeliversToAnInvalidatedRunner, coding/extension/host/inproc/stale_emit_delivery_test.go::TestEmitInputAndToolCallOnAnInvalidatedRunnerHonourTheHandlers, coding/session_reload_old_runner_emit_test.go::TestAFailedReloadLeavesTheSessionDeliveringToTheOldInstance, coding/cli/headless_reload_prompt_test.go::TestPromptsAfterAFailedReloadRunOnTheOldInstance --> <!-- fix: cb54cf290b -->
- After a failed `/reload` in the interactive mode, the API that the old extensions captured is stale, as in Pi: in v0.7.0 a compiled-in extension kept using it and its event-bus subscriptions stayed. The next `/reload`, or an embedder's retry of `Session.Reload`, now loads on a live runtime again: it built its extensions over the stale one, so their registrations threw the stale message. <!-- cause: the interactive reload invalidated the old runner but kept its runtime active, where Pi's runner.invalidate() invalidates the runtime too (runner.ts:729-735), and a host that keeps one runtime across reloads never made it active again, where Pi's loader creates a new runtime for each load --> <!-- tests: internal/codingagent/reload_failed_runtime_test.go::TestFailedInteractiveReloadInvalidatesTheOldRunnersRuntimeAndTheNextReloadWorks, coding/session_reload_runtime_reactivate_test.go::TestAReloadAfterAFailedOneRunsOnTheSharedRuntimeAgain, coding/extension/runtime_state_test.go::TestRuntimeReactivateEndsStalenessButNotTheEndedSubscriptions --> <!-- fix: b30b8aa06d -->
- A title an extension sets (`ctx.ui.setTitle`, or the session name an extension sets), the OSC 52 sequence of an extension's `copyToClipboard` and the progress indicator's keepalive are written between frames now, as in Pi: Pi writes each of them with `terminal.write` (the keepalive from a `setInterval` callback) on its one event loop, so each is before the bytes of a frame or after them. PiG wrote them from the extension host's call or the keepalive's ticker goroutine, so they could land between two writes of a frame, and the race detector reported the writer. The interactive mode's loop writes them now. Released in v0.7.0 and earlier. <!-- fix: 1ceb9fb95a15 -->
- In RPC mode, a termination signal that arrives while the mode starts or tears down no longer skips the extensions' `session_shutdown`: the shutdown the signal started is now run by the mode itself when no signal hook was left to run it. A signal that was ignored during a running shutdown, followed by a stdout write failure that ends the mode, now leaves its `exit.log` line ("received SIGTERM during shutdown, which the mode's end cut off (exit 143)") and always exits 143 (D234). <!-- fix: 05102adc73 -->
- In RPC and print mode, a shutdown that has started now finishes. Closing standard input and sending SIGTERM or SIGHUP together, as a supervisor does, no longer kills PiG in the middle of the dispose (a pending MCP token refresh was lost); a later stdin end, `ctx.shutdown()` request or single signal does nothing, and the process exits with the code of the first trigger. A second signal exits at once with 128 plus its number. Print mode keeps its signal handlers through the final cleanup. This follows Pi main ace560c30 (D234). Two signals delivered back to back can reach PiG as one, because the Go runtime merges a pending signal; send a forcing second signal a short moment after the first. <!-- fix: 5b8189f98a -->
- In RPC mode, `exit.log` no longer says "received SIGTERM" for a single signal that arrived during a shutdown that stdin's end or `ctx.shutdown()` had started and that finished with exit status 0. The line now reads "received SIGTERM during shutdown, which completed (exit 0)", and a repeated signal's line reads "received SIGTERM again during shutdown (exit 143)". The cleanup, the log line and the process exit of an RPC exit now run once, so a repeated signal that arrives while another exit is already past its stdout wait no longer repeats them (D234). <!-- fix: caae28ae1c -->
- RPC mode: an extension dialog whose signal is already aborted now resolves its default without writing an extension_ui_request, as Pi does; the client no longer sees a dialog it cannot answer. <!-- fix: 6f9cf779f76ef93316e92d264a62b2ce084fc3dd -->
- The RPC usage probe that checks Pi's stdout ordering no longer dies on an unhandled `write EPIPE` when the CLI under test stops reading its stdin before the probe sends the prompt; it reports that the CLI wrote no frame, and any other failure to write the prompt still fails it. <!-- fix: e57eef0e6d -->
- An RPC prompt whose Node `input` handler awaits a timer, I/O or another real wait no longer holds the next stdin line: `get_state` and every later command are answered while the handler waits, as in Pi, in an isolated and in a packed runtime alike. The runtime reported a wait only for commands and the settle tail, so the host held the line until the handler returned. The hold has been there since v0.5.1. <!-- fix: 939416539e --> <!-- tests: coding/cli/rpc_settle_wait_test.go::TestRPCCommandDuringInputHandlerNetworkWaitAnswersAcrossSDKs, coding/cli/rpc_settle_wait_test.go::TestRPCNodeInputHandlerWaitSemanticsComparedWithPi, coding/cli/rpc_settle_wait_test.go::TestRPCNodeInputEndDuringInputHandlerWaitComparedWithPi -->
- The same for a Node `before_agent_start` handler: a `get_state` sent while it awaits I/O is answered at once, before the run starts, as in Pi. It has been held since v0.5.1. <!-- fix: bd00797bde --> <!-- tests: coding/cli/rpc_settle_wait_test.go::TestRPCCommandDuringBeforeAgentStartHandlerNetworkWaitAnswersAcrossSDKs -->
- An RPC prompt that runs a Node extension command which only chains microtasks (never yielding to the event loop) no longer lets the next stdin line overtake the command's response: the runtime took any command whose Promise was unsettled one microtask after the call to be waiting, where Pi's loop reads no line during such a command. The report has existed since v0.3.0 and the hold it releases since v0.5.1. <!-- fix: 7506dc78b8 --> <!-- tests: coding/cli/rpc_settle_wait_test.go::TestRPCNodeHandlerThatOnlyRunsMicrotasksHoldsStdin -->
- An RPC prompt whose `before_agent_start` handler, written with the Go, Rust, Python or Lisp SDK, awaits I/O no longer holds the next stdin line for the whole wait, for ever when the handler never returns: the line is admitted once the handler outlives the 250 ms quantum that already bounds those runtimes' command, input and settle handlers. The hold has been there since v0.5.1. <!-- fix: c485b4e675 --> <!-- tests: coding/cli/rpc_settle_wait_test.go::TestRPCCommandDuringBeforeAgentStartHandlerNetworkWaitAnswersAcrossSDKs -->
- `events.off` on an extension listener that had migrated to the routed event bus panicked on a nil untrack. <!-- fix: ada701819cf5aa940ce24da7b6d759ce6af52520 -->
- RPC mode: a prompt written right behind an extension command that calls `ctx.reload()` is read after the reload, runs on the reloaded extension and answers after that command, as in Pi. PiG read it while the reload ran: it ran on the extension being replaced and answered first, and with a TypeScript extension neither prompt was answered and the stream stayed silent until stdin closed. A client that waits for each response before it writes the next record was not affected. Present since 0.5.2. <!-- fix: d04750891b39f6d01f26116bac727542e213c003 -->
- RPC mode: a prompt read while a `session_start` handler of a reload waits runs on the reloaded extension; it ran on the replaced one, whose `ctx` was stale. <!-- fix: d04750891b39f6d01f26116bac727542e213c003 -->
- Extensions: a host call that a handler of a TypeScript extension makes while a reload is replacing that extension is answered with Pi's stale-context error, from the point the reload has run the `session_shutdown` handlers; a call that was already waiting for its answer keeps it. PiG dropped such a call while the replacement was loading, so the handler's command never finished and, in RPC mode, its prompt got no response. <!-- fix: 095939f576f8ffc10909e11ac7770dba3f4c58e4, bf60a5312160b533cdf49ef288b38d7a43f5269e, de7a83636fa9c44713bae9132534712af2ed94e4 -->
- Extensions: a call that a handler of a TypeScript extension makes just before a reload invalidates the extension is served, as a call made before Pi's `invalidate()` is. The host marked the extension stale when it sent the notification, before the extension's runtime had read it, so the call was refused; a call the handler does not await, such as `ctx.ui.notify`, was dropped with a diagnostic where Pi throws, and in RPC mode the command's prompt answered with no `extension_error`. The reload now waits until the runtime has acknowledged the invalidation. <!-- fix: a31c30a42a3a283ad1e8f7e0f70096ec8028efba -->
- RPC mode: a dialog answer read in the same stdin chunk as a prompt, while a reload runs, is delivered after the lines of its chunk, as Pi delivers it, so the notifications and responses of the two commands come in Pi's order. PiG delivered the answer at once and the order was a race: the reloading command could answer before the prompt of its chunk, or the prompt could answer without its notification. <!-- fix: 2a1edc2dc00b64e92b96e8c24de75f956c959658 -->
- Interactive mode: a `/reload` that fails leaves the old extension instances stale, as in Pi: their captured `pi` and `ctx` throw the stale-context error, and a later `/reload` that succeeds loads live instances. PiG left the old instances in service after the failure. <!-- fix: 83d0c737059d6b0f610f800d175a5cb9183b95bb -->
- In RPC mode `ctx.reload()` loads the extensions that are on disk, as it does in Pi and in PiG's print and interactive modes.
