RPC mode reloaded the extensions it had started with, so an extension command that removed a sibling extension's file and awaited `ctx.reload()` left the removed extension configured, and, when the two shared a Node process, the missing file failed the load of the calling extension as well: the caller was gone after the reload. An extension file added before the reload was never loaded. Present since 0.2.0. <!-- tests: coding/cli/rpc_reload_membership_test.go::TestRPCReloadDropsAnExtensionRemovedFromDisk, coding/cli/rpc_reload_membership_test.go::TestRPCReloadLoadsAnExtensionAddedToDisk --> <!-- fix: 994aab45cb -->
- Ending an RPC session while a response is running (stdin closes, an extension calls `ctx.shutdown()`, or pig gets SIGTERM or SIGHUP) now settles that run before the `session_shutdown` handlers run, as Pi does. The aborted tool call's result and the aborted assistant message are saved to the session file, extensions receive the run's remaining `turn_end`, `agent_end` and `agent_settled` events first, and a `session_shutdown` handler that throws no longer leaves the tool call unanswered. A run that waits on a dialog the client can no longer answer ends the process without `session_shutdown`, as Pi's does when its event loop drains. <!-- fix: d06e6cfbc9 -->
- A pig in RPC mode that ended normally, on the end of its input or on SIGTERM, left one `h<number>` directory in the temp directory for every session that started an extension: RPC mode ends with `os.Exit` after it killed the extension processes, as Pi ends with `process.exit`, so the Host's private socket directory was never removed. The host process now removes that directory when it terminates its processes, and a generation that asks for a socket path while the process exits no longer makes a new one, whether or not the Host had already made a socket path. <!-- fix: 338965f248a20f883de41ef33b933c96c3c13853, a782807087c164469d1422f91db7e05c43d2b474 -->
- A pig in RPC mode that ended normally, on the end of its input or on SIGTERM, left one `h<number>` directory in the temp directory for every session that started an extension: RPC mode ends with `os.Exit` after it killed the extension processes, as Pi ends with `process.exit`, so the Host's private socket directory was never removed. The host process now removes that directory when it terminates its processes, and a generation that asks for a socket path while the process exits no longer makes a new one, whether or not the Host had already made a socket path. <!-- fix: 567c58b9dd576b451a638224048f76e50073dace, c4b0c55b1f3fabaca91ed235c2dbdd8547973e12 -->
- `AgentSessionRuntime.dispose` in the Go, Python, Rust and Lisp extension SDKs now settles a run still in flight (it aborts the current session first) before it emits `session_shutdown`, as Pi's `dispose` does; the run's `agent_end` reaches the extension before the shutdown. <!-- fix: 98f0403ec4 -->
- `pig --help` in a build that strips a built-in no longer shows the `pig --tools +codemode` example when `codemode` is stripped. <!-- fix: 98f0403ec4 -->
- A build with `pig_strip_codemode` no longer links the codemode engine through tool search. <!-- fix: 65d2ac1eee -->
- Tool arguments for a `bigint` or `undefined` parameter are converted, not rejected: a JSON `"42"` or `42` for a bigint parameter and `null` for an undefined one validate, as TypeBox converted them. The arguments' JSON writes a bigint as `"42n"`, as Pi's validation probes do, and leaves out an undefined member. Follows Pi main af79b0c3d. <!-- fix: 967def653d -->
- A schema whose root `$id` is a relative path with a directory, such as `schemas/tool.json`, resolves its local `$ref`s: the `$id` was applied twice, so compiling failed with `Unresolved $ref` and tool arguments were rejected under `UnresolvedRefsReject`. The same holds with `unevaluatedProperties` and `unevaluatedItems`, when explaining errors under nested resources and on the first coercion of a schema with `$dynamicRef`. Follows Pi main 2bd2c2d0a ahead of the pin. <!-- fix: 91a0cfd13d -->
- A `number` or `integer` schema no longer accepts NaN or an infinity, with or without bounds, and an error names it (`expected number, got NaN`), as TypeBox does. Follows Pi main 55a5c6914 ahead of the pin. <!-- fix: 91a0cfd13d -->
- A Python or Lisp `session_before_compact` or `session_before_tree` handler dispatched after the operation was aborted can now make host calls, such as a notification on its first line, as Pi's handler can. The handler still starts with its signal aborted. <!-- fix: d93f8bccf09, f8180c331b0 -->
- A `turn_end` or `agent_before_settle` handler that returns a `context_edit` draft without the `replacement` member now stops the run as it does in Pi, with Pi's message that the replacement "must be null or contain string/array content": nothing is appended and the run does not continue. Before this fix, PiG took the absent member for null, left the target out of model context and continued. The cause: the host decoded an absent member and a null one into the same value. <!-- fix: c05aa12b6c, 65a97c7f91 -->
- Extension SDKs: `send_user_message` / `sendUserMessage` with no delivery mode now behaves alike in every SDK and as Pi does. The Python and Lisp SDKs defaulted the mode to `"followUp"` (since 0.7.0), so an extension that sent while the agent was running got a queued follow-up where Pi, a Node extension and a Go extension get Pi's refusal. Python `send_user_message(content)` and Lisp `(ctx-send-user-message ctx content)` now send no `deliverAs`: an idle agent runs the message at once, and a running agent refuses it with `Agent is already processing. Specify streamingBehavior ('steer' or 'followUp') to queue the message.`, reported as the extension error `send_user_message` while the call returns. The Python signature changes from `send_user_message(content, deliver_as="followUp", ...)` to `deliver_as=None`, so an author who relied on the default now gets Pi's refusal while the agent runs; the old behaviour is `deliver_as="followUp"` (Lisp `:deliver-as "followUp"`), and `steer` and `followUp` are unchanged. Interactive mode now reports a refused `sendUserMessage` and a failed `sendMessage` as those extension errors instead of returning the error to the extension, as print, JSON and RPC mode do, and the Lisp `host-call-error` prints `CODE: MESSAGE` as the other SDKs write a host error. <!-- fix: b8293216578c1689f576fedda27f68a93cdaff2f -->
- A provider written with the Go extension SDK whose `streamSimple` request the host cancels is now always answered with the cancellation's error. The SDK chose between that error and the stream's result with a `select` on the request's context and the stream's end; a provider that ends its stream when it sees the cancel makes both ready, and Go then picks at random, so the cancelled request was answered with the provider's result now and then (5 of 30 runs with the extension loaded in process, 1 of 30 as a subprocess), where the Rust, Lisp and Python SDKs answer the abort. PiG's host stops listening to such a request at its cancel and shows the stream as aborted either way, so the wrong answer was on the wire only. The window has been in the SDK since 0.3.0. A cancel that arrives after the stream ended and was forwarded still leaves the result. <!-- fix: 5425648cb7 -->
- The Go extension SDK no longer forwards a provider stream event that the provider pushed after the cancel of its request. The forwarder read the request's cancellation before it took the next event, so a cancel and a later push that both landed between the two sent the host one more event; it now reads the cancellation again once it has the event, as the Rust, Lisp, Python and Node SDKs do. The window was two statements wide (no run of the conformance row showed it) and has been in the SDK since 0.3.0; PiG's host has ended its own stream at the cancel, so the extra event was on the wire only. <!-- fix: 98a2e8d071 -->
- A Go, Rust, Python or Lisp extension can now set the Kitty image id of an image node of a view, as a Node extension could: Go `kit.Image.ImageID`, Rust `kit::Image::image_id`, Python `kit.Image(image_id=...)`, Lisp `(kit-image ... :image-id n)`. The host has read `imageId` of an image node (upstream `ImageOptions.imageId`; absent, the host allocates one) since the node was added, but those four kits had no member for it and sent none. The Go, Python and Rust kits have had the image node since 0.5.1 and the Lisp kit since 0.7.0. <!-- tests: test/extension-conformance/ui_view_image_id_test.go::TestConformance_UIViewImageID, extensions/sdk/internal/kitwire/encode_test.go::TestEncodeMatchesTheHostViewPayload --> <!-- fix: 1e2fa7e4a6 -->
- A Lisp extension's host call that the host had already answered no longer fails with `host-call-cancelled` when the request is cancelled before the waiting thread wakes, so a `ctx-notify` in a handler cancelled at that moment no longer ends the handler with no result. <!-- fix: 0c4a06b0e4d, f8180c331b0 -->
- A provider written with the Python extension SDK whose `streamSimple` request the host cancels is now always answered with the abort error. The SDK's read loop ended the request's provider stream before it set the request's signal, and the request's thread, when it ran between the two, answered the request with a null result and no error, where the Go, Rust and Lisp SDKs answer the abort. PiG's host stops listening to such a request at its cancel and shows the stream as aborted either way, so the wrong answer was on the wire only. The window is older than the push snapshot of provider stream events (the release line had the same order before this change) and a few bytecodes wide: none of 150 unforced runs of a cancel in the middle of a push burst hit it, and holding the signal back by 0.3 s hit it every time. <!-- fix: adddfb8a1a -->
- A provider written with the Go, Python or Lisp extension SDK now reaches the host with each stream event showing the partial message as it was when the provider pushed the event, and with the stream's result as it was when the provider ended it. The SDK queued the event the provider pushed and a goroutine or thread encoded it later, so a provider that appended to its shared partial message right after a `Push` could have the host receive the later text (under load every `text_delta` showed the finished message), and in the Go SDK the encoder's read of the provider's map was a data race with the provider's writes. `Push` and `End` now take the event, and the result, at the call (the Go SDK encodes the event on the provider's goroutine; the Python and Lisp SDKs queue a copy), so the host sees each event as it was at the push, which is stronger than Pi's own guarantee (D615): Pi's consumer reads the shared message at its own turn, so after a synchronous burst of pushes or between microtask awaits it shows later changes. The event and the message the provider reads back (`Events()`, `result()`) are still its own objects, and a value of a kind JSON has no copy of (a lock, a cycle) ends the request instead of raising in the provider's `Push`. The Rust SDK takes the event by value and is unchanged. <!-- fix: 57f113ba40 -->
- A provider written with the Go, Python or Lisp extension SDK now reaches the host with each stream event showing the partial message as it was when the provider pushed the event, and with the stream's result as it was when the provider ended it. The SDK queued the event the provider pushed and a goroutine or thread encoded it later, so a provider that appended to its shared partial message right after a `Push` could have the host receive the later text (under load every `text_delta` showed the finished message), and in the Go SDK the encoder's read of the provider's map was a data race with the provider's writes. `Push` and `End` now take the event, and the result, at the call (the Go SDK encodes the event on the provider's goroutine; the Python and Lisp SDKs queue a copy), so the host sees each event as it was at the push, which is stronger than Pi's own guarantee (D615): Pi's consumer reads the shared message at its own turn, so after a synchronous burst of pushes or between microtask awaits it shows later changes. The event and the message the provider reads back (`Events()`, `result()`) are still its own objects, and a value of a kind JSON has no copy of (a lock, a cycle) ends the request instead of raising in the provider's `Push`. In the Python SDK the guarantee holds for a stream that uses the SDK's own `events()` and `result()`: a Python subclass that overrides either one is read as Pi's consumer reads it, so the host receives what the override yields or returns when the host asks, including later changes to a message the override shares. The Rust SDK takes the event by value and is unchanged. <!-- fix: 924fe2818c -->
- A TypeScript extension that sends the bytes of an image in the `images` list of a plugin view (`{ ref, mimeType, data }`, with an `image` node that names the `ref`) now compiles: `PiGWireView` has the optional `images` member, `PiGViewImage` types its records and `PiGViewImageNode` types the node. The host accepted this view, as the `ui-views` page says, but the types rejected the object literal as one with an unknown member, so a Node author had to cast it. The plugin view API is unreleased and no release has the type. The type test is `extensions/sdk-ts/typecheck.ts`, which compiles a view with `images` and four wrong shapes that must fail (`make test-sdk-ts`). <!-- cause: PiGWireView declared only root, focus and theme, so the optional images list that the host reads from a view was not a known member, and no type test compiled a view with images --> <!-- fix: f633b88012 -->
- The `root` of a TypeScript `PiGWireView` is typed against the node kinds the host builds (`PiGViewNode`) and no longer accepts any object: a misspelt kind, a member of another kind, a select-list without its id or a string `imageId` is a compile error and no longer a refused mount at run time. The plugin view API is unreleased and no release has the type. <!-- cause: PiGWireView.root was Record<string, unknown>, which no type test could fail --> <!-- fix: 194a2b1b70 -->
- The Node extension runtime now serves Pi's `ModelRuntime.settleCredentialWrites` and pi-ai's `setBedrockProviderLoader`, and the Go, Rust, Python and Lisp SDKs gain `SettleCredentialWrites`/`settle_credential_writes`/`runtime-settle-credential-writes`, so an extension can wait for a started OAuth refresh to be saved before it exits. <!-- fix: 30e4a9808d -->
- `durable/core/budget/tinygo-install.sh` retries the TinyGo download when the release host answers with a transient error (HTTP 408, 429, 5xx). A single 504 from GitHub's release CDN made the `wasm-tinygo` row of the Durable contract job fail with "tinygo not found" in CI. <!-- fix: f927290d26 -->
- Go extensions that receive large event payloads (`before_provider_request`, `agent_end`, `turn_end`) now decode them about four times faster and allocate about half as much. They were slow because the Go SDK and the host scanned and copied each frame five times: a byte-at-a-time validity scan, a second scan to skip a request's arguments, a copy of them, and two more validations and scans to hand the event to a handler. On a 43 MiB provider payload, the read and decode of one request frame fell from about 600-800 ms to about 225 ms and from 181 MB to 101 MB allocated, and the host's read of a frame an extension sent rose from about 130 to about 500 MB/s. Malformed frames end the connection with the same message as before, and every value decodes to the same Go value. The Lisp SDK decoded a frame with many strings containing escapes in time quadratic in the frame (a 16 MiB frame took 20 s, now 0.15 s). <!-- fix: 10818f5661 -->
- The embedded Node runtime and the packed Go, Rust, Python and Lisp SDK bundles were not regenerated when `sendUserMessage` gained `expandPromptTemplates` and the Node theme gained `sourceInfo`, so shipped Node extensions saw no `ctx.ui.theme.sourceInfo` and the packed Lisp SDK rejected `:expand-prompt-templates`. They are regenerated, and the theme row now compares a real `SourceInfo`. <!-- fix: 5efaf92237 -->
- `pi.sendUserMessage(content, { expandPromptTemplates: true })` and the same option on a `withSession` context now reach the Session from Go, Rust, Python, Lisp and Node extensions (`Context.SendUserMessageWith`, `send_user_message_with`, `expand_prompt_templates=`, `:expand-prompt-templates`). The host used to drop the option, so a message such as `/my-command` or `/skill:name` was sent to the model as plain text. `ctx.ui.theme.sourceInfo` is now set on the Node runtime theme. <!-- fix: abc54d0438 -->
- A Go extension no longer re-sorts the JSON keys of objects it hands back to the host. The Go SDK held an event's objects as maps and wrote every reply with the members sorted, so an extension that left another extension's `turn_end` draft entries alone (the SDK echoes `event.entries` on every `turn_end`), dropped a `context` message, or returned the `before_provider_request` payload, a `tool_result`'s `details` or a `message_end` message unchanged rewrote their member order: the saved session bytes and the provider request bytes, tool-call arguments included, changed every turn, which a Node extension under PiG and Pi itself do not do. The SDK now writes those objects in the order the host sent them; the Rust, Python, Lisp and Node SDKs already did. <!-- fix: d918706fbc40b6e92c82051fd29723989cfbce7d -->
- A custom message draft proposed at a turn boundary keeps the member order of its `content` blocks. The host read a draft's `data` and `details` in order but built `content` as a Go map, so the blocks of a content array (`{type, text}`, `{type, data, mimeType}`) were stored with their members sorted, for every SDK. <!-- fix: d9833433d2c75147671f886833abf11afb13be3d -->
- A custom message keeps the member order of its `content` blocks everywhere the host holds it. `pi.sendMessage`, `appendCustomMessageEntry`, a session entry read back from a file and a custom message read from the wire took the content from a Go map, so the blocks of a content array (`{type, text}`, `{type, data, mimeType}`) were stored, written again and shown to extensions with their members sorted, for every SDK. <!-- fix: 402f61c2205adc5c2253437ad59cc8111d18d24c -->
- A Go extension that reorders, filters, sorts, copies or edits the objects of an event in place (the content blocks of a message, a provider request's `tools`, a list of messages or entries, a string of a message) and hands them back no longer re-sorts their keys, so tool-call arguments, tool schemas and message members reach the session and the provider in the order the host sent them. The Go SDK records the member order of every object while it decodes the event and knows each object by its own map, so no object is ever given another's order and a reply reads nothing of the event's text. `Context.ObjectKeys` lists integer-like keys first and ascending, as `Object.keys` does. <!-- fix: 3de4b8e877c8fc4d3b7bedafa5e8ae8cbad7161f -->
- A view node of every kind can carry an id in the component kits of the Go, Rust, Python and Lisp SDKs (Go the field `ID`, Rust `.id("…")`, Python `id=`, Lisp `:id`). Before, only the kinds that need an id took one there, so an `a11y` record, a `focus` record or a drawing's `node` of a mounted view could not name a container, box, text, truncated text, markdown, spacer, dynamic border, image, loader, stack, lines, user message or diff node, while a Node extension, whose view is a plain object, could. A `text` or `box` node has no `color` member in any SDK: its colour is `bg`, and the host draws no `color` it is sent on those kinds. <!-- fix: fb93e7325dfa51d8c2c32843ef26e21a1f831870 -->
- A Provider object registered from an extension process ignored `refreshModelsAuth`: its network refresh always resolved (and so refreshed) the stored credential. <!-- fix: 0ff9f4a443 -->
- An extension that declared one provider name in several `registerProvider` calls while it loaded kept only the last call on the host: `refreshModels` or `oauth` declared first and the other fields declared second lost the first. Pi pushes every call onto an array and applies each in order through the registry, which merges the defined values over the earlier registration (`loader.ts:221-231`, `runner.ts:471-487`, `agent-session-services.ts:158-169`, `model-runtime.ts:965-986`), so the host now queues every declaration of a name in order, which fixes it for Go, Rust, Python and Lisp extensions. Node extensions were never affected: the Node runtime merges the registrations of a name before it sends them. Tools, commands, shortcuts, flags and renderers still keep the last of a name, as the Maps of Pi's loader do. <!-- fix: 9910d0091 -->
- A Node extension's `ctx.getContextUsage()` returned the value of the host's last dispatch, so a timer between requests, or a handler after `waitForIdle`, `compact` or `navigateTree`, read a stale usage where Pi reads it live. It now asks the host, like the Go, Rust, Python and Lisp SDKs, and the host no longer scans the session branch for the usage on every state push. <!-- fix: e4b9bd554e -->
- After an extension's own `registerProvider`, `unregisterProvider`, `registerVirtualModel`, `unregisterVirtualModel` or `refreshModelRegistry`, the next read of the model returned the previous model object in the Go SDK and the Node runtime, where Pi refreshes the Session's model before the call returns. The host now sends its state before the reply of those calls, the Go SDK waits for it, and the Node runtime refreshes its model from its registry view. <!-- fix: b3b5ae8b6f -->
- A reader that learned a host change through a host call, for example the usage a new model or session moves, could read an older replicated model, session id, name or file afterwards, because the host's own state push is asynchronous. The host now pushes before any call result while a change has not reached the extension, the Go SDK waits for the state that precedes each result, and the Node runtime applies the queued state before it settles a synchronous call. <!-- fix: b3b5ae8b6f -->
- The Go, Rust, Python and Lisp SDKs asked the host on every read of the model object, the session id, the session name and the session file, which cost a round trip each (about 55 µs in the Go SDK); they now read the host's state snapshot, as the Node runtime does. <!-- fix: a16d8b4900 -->
- A Node extension loaded in a TUI could lose `ctx.ui` (every widget, status and footer call became a no-op) when the host's state update reached it while it was handling the ready frame, because the update applied before the older state of the ready frame, which then replaced it. The queued update is now applied only after the ready state. <!-- fix: 2e8dcc1eea -->
- A host call that read a change of the model, session id or name between the change and its report to the extensions, and the first `watchSessionLog` read of a replaced Session, could reply ahead of the state that names it. The Session now brackets each such change, and the host flushes its state before every reply while one is in flight, and under the cursor lock for `watchSessionLog`. <!-- fix: 6e789bbd91 -->
- Registering a native provider did not refresh the Session's active model from the registry, as Pi does after `registerNativeProvider`; the registry's observers are now told, and the Node runtime refreshes its model view too. <!-- fix: c1290084cb -->
- A Go extension's footer branch callback (`FooterData.OnBranchChange`) that made a host call, including the SDK's own report of a panicking callback, stopped the extension from serving any further request, because the callback ran on the message loop inside the state update that changed the branch and the call waited for that update. The callbacks now run on a worker, one change at a time in the order the branch changed, so a callback can call the host as it can in Pi. <!-- fix: ec1e0b68ca -->
- The README installed `@michaelkinsy/pig-extension-types` from the source tree as a link, and the compiler then resolved the package's imports from the folder: the PiG-only members, `ctx.ui.setLogin` of the README's own example among them, were missing from Pi's types. The install command is now `npm install --install-links`, which copies the folder, and the README names `preserveSymlinks` for a project that keeps a link. <!-- fix: 849f5f9c8d -->
- `registerMarkdownTransformer`'s `context` and `ui.onThemeChange`'s `theme` were `any`: `index.d.ts` named `MarkdownTransformContext` and `Theme` without importing them. <!-- fix: 849f5f9c8d -->
- CI only: a pull request's secret scan now stops, with one error line, when it cannot compute the range of commits to scan. The range script printed an open-ended `..<head>` and exited 0 when the base had no merge base with the head (unrelated histories, or a clone too shallow to reach the fork point), so the scan could cover no commits and pass; a missing or empty argument or a ref that is not a commit was not checked either. A pull request that adds no commit over its base is now reported as having nothing to scan. Released versions: none (CI only). <!-- fix: 55fbbcbe12 --> <!-- cause: secret-scan-range.sh took the merge base inside the arguments of printf, where a failing command does not trip set -e, so a failed git merge-base left an empty first sha and the script still printed the range and exited 0; no test ran it without a merge base. -->
- CI only: a pull request's secret scan now covers what the pull request adds over its base (the merge base to its head) instead of everything from the parent of its oldest commit. A batch pull request that merged member branches cut from an older main used to fail the scan on secret-shaped test values already on main, and, because the scan followed only the first parent (`--first-parent`), the commits inside a merged member branch were not scanned at all. Released versions: none (CI only). <!-- fix: e3f150557b --> <!-- cause: gitleaks-action scanned `<oldest pull request commit>^..<newest>` with --first-parent, which reaches back into main's history for an older-based member and skips every commit behind a merge, and no test built a batch of merged member branches -->
- chord: a list could show the older of two reads' rows, or a tiling installed on a list that had detached: `Open` tested `detached` in one section and installed its tiling after it, and a rebinding decided that a tiling was pending or current under a lock and read again in a later section, where a read for newer arguments that ran between was replaced by the older target. Pi decides and acts in one turn (list.ts `read`, `#rebound`); each is now one section. <!-- fix: e9902cbc2a --> <!-- cause: list.Open and list.rebound decided in one section or under a lock and acted in a later section, where another read or a detach could run --> <!-- tests: TestListOpenInstallsNoTilingOnAListDetachedWhileItsCheckWaitedForTheSection, TestListRebindsNothingWhenANewerReadTookThePendingPlaceWhileItWaitedForItsSection -->
- chord: a list that retired a page while that page's failed first run was waiting to be adopted could be failed by it: the store's read tested that it was still open and then adopted the failed run in a section of its own, so a close between the two handed the closed read's sink a failure. Pi tests `closed` and adopts the failed run in one turn (open-query.ts); the test and the adoption are now one section. <!-- fix: 2324030101 --> <!-- cause: OpenRead.failCompile decided closed and the compile error outside the section that adopts the failed run; a close that ran in the gap still reached the sink --> <!-- tests: TestReadsFailedCompileIsNotAdoptedByAReadClosedWhileItWaitsForItsSection -->
- chord: a worker could be forked into a component that a `Close` had begun to close: a start looked at the component and forked in two steps, and a Close between them found no child to stop. A worker spawned that way showed as `starting` for a moment, was killed by the start's cleanup, and the late fork re-armed the idle timer Close had stopped; a fork failing in that window reported worker_failed on a closed set. Pi checks `closing` and forks in one synchronous step (workers.ts); the check, the base's file and the fork are now one section. <!-- fix: a8b5e75eb3 --> <!-- cause: the start checked closing on its goroutine and forked in a section of the loop of its own --> <!-- tests: TestCloseLandingAtTheEntryOfAStartsForkSectionForksNothingTheStartFailsClosed -->
- Searching in `/login`, `/logout`, `/scoped-models` and `/resume` highlights the best match when you type a query after scrolling down, so Enter picks it and not the entry at the row you had scrolled to; and moving the text cursor in the search field with Left, Right, Home or End no longer moves the highlight back to the first entry in `/model`, `/settings`, the searchable settings submenus and `pig config`. Follows Pi 37b74c546921 and 5bcf370a5293. PiG 0.2.0 through 0.7.0 have the search-highlight defect. <!-- fix: 82903dace 204f9bb05 --> <!-- cause: selector search handlers clamped the scrolled selection index instead of resetting to row 0 on a non-empty query, and unconditionally re-ran filtering on every delegated key even when the query text did not change -->
- Extensions: a refused `sendUserMessage` or `sendMessage` is now reported as the extension error `send_user_message` or `send_message` after the run of the code that made the call, as Pi does, instead of when the call arrived (since 0.2.0). Pi reports from a catch callback on the Promise the Session method returns, so the error comes after every effect of the sending code: the `queue_update` of a steer or follow-up sent later in the same handler, an appended entry, a notification. A handler that sent a refused message first and a steer after it now sees the queue updates before the error, in print, JSON, RPC and interactive mode and in every SDK. Inside a handler or request the report is made when the run ends (a Node run at its next microtask checkpoint, a Go, Python, Rust or Lisp handler when its request returns, fails or is cancelled, or at its yield), and an extension that exits before that has its reports made at the connection's end, in call order. A Go, Python, Rust or Lisp thread that sends outside any request has no run boundary, so its refusal is still reported at once. <!-- fix: dddc1064cab785801295b51db1a635c364e37a41 --> <!-- cause: the Session reported a failed send from the call that made it, and the host had no point at which the sending code ends its run -->
- A session entry member that an extension sets to `null` is written as `null` and read back as `null`, as in Pi: the `data` of `pi.appendEntry`, the `details` of `pi.sendMessage`, the `data`, `details` and `usage` of a `turn_end` or `agent_before_settle` draft, and the `details` and `usage` of a `session_before_compact` result's compaction and of a `session_before_tree` result's summary. PiG wrote no member, and a reader of the reloaded session got undefined. The cause: the host decoded a member written as `null` and a member left out into the same value, and the entry types leave out a member without a value. A session file that PiG wrote before this change has no member where Pi has `null`; it reads as Pi reads the same file. <!-- fix: 8b8b8d33b3 -->
- An extension's `SessionManager.branchWithSummary(id, summary)` without the `fromHook` argument writes a branch summary entry without a `fromHook` member, as Pi does. PiG wrote `"fromHook":false`. The cause: the entry type could leave the member out only for an entry it had read from a file. <!-- fix: cc387053a6 -->
- A custom message that an extension writes without `display` (`pi.sendMessage({ customType, content })`, a `custom_message` draft without the member) has no `display` member in the session file, as in Pi, and a draft without `content` has no `content` member. PiG wrote `"display":false` and `"content":null`. The cause: `display` was a Go boolean with no "not given" state, and the entry wrote a missing content as `null`. A session file that PiG wrote before this change keeps its `"display":false`. <!-- fix: f71a1836fc -->
- `setLabel` from an extension writes Pi's three label entries: no `label` member for a call without a label, `"label":null` for a null label and `"label":""` for an empty string. Each clears the label. PiG wrote the entry without a `label` member for all three. The cause: the host decoded the label as a string, and the binders of the session, the interactive mode and the session graph runner mapped an empty string to no label. An extension that clears a label with an empty string now writes `"label":""`, as the same call does in Pi. <!-- fix: 3063e768f4 -->
- A `usage` object that an extension supplies is written to the session file as the extension wrote it, as in Pi: its member order and any extra member. This applies to a compaction draft, to a `session_before_compact` result's compaction and to a `session_before_tree` result's summary. PiG wrote its own member order and dropped extra members. The cause: the host decoded the object into its typed usage and wrote the typed value back. Token and cost totals do not change: they use `input`, `output`, `cacheRead`, `cacheWrite` and `cost.total`, as Pi's do. <!-- fix: 1ea5c18bc2 -->
- A custom message whose `display` an extension sets to `null` (a `custom_message` draft, or `pi.sendMessage` from a JavaScript extension) keeps `"display":null` in the session file, as in Pi. PiG wrote `"display":false`. The cause: `display` was a Go boolean with no null state. Readers take the null for false, as before. <!-- fix: 47ef9ce797 -->
- `pi.sendMessage` with a `content` of `null` writes `"content":[]`, as in Pi, and so does a message without `content` that the interactive mode appends. PiG wrote `"content":null` for the first and no `content` member for the second. The cause: Pi's `sendCustomMessage` reads `message.content ?? []`, and PiG applied that default only to a missing content and only in one of its two paths. <!-- fix: 1b0a657da2 -->
- Python SDK: a `setup` callback of `new_session` that leaves out the `data` of `append_custom_entry` or the `details` of `append_custom_message_entry` writes an entry without that member, as Pi does. PiG wrote `"data":null` and `"details":null` into the session file. The cause: the Python `SetupSessionManager` sent the member on every call, and its default, `None`, is a JSON null. `pig_sdk.NULL` still writes the member as null. <!-- fix: 94bd9a58fe -->
- A Go, Python or Rust extension that used a session graph object (a `DefaultResourceLoader`, its loaded extensions, a `ModelRuntime`) in a later call could get "Unknown or released session graph object" from the host, at random and more often under memory pressure. The SDK released the host's object when its wrapper was collected or dropped, but the later call named the object by a handle string that nothing kept the wrapper alive for: `ExtensionRunner` built from the extensions a loader returned, a method call on the object's last use, and a model stream on a `ModelRuntime` the program had already let go of. An object now stays valid while anything that names its handle is still in use or in flight. Affects 0.5.2 through 0.7.0. <!-- fix: 60e15bd01eb37f0a3842f35cd70d324b96458f10 --> <!-- fix: 7cc188258ce3dd50ad625a439c9b252b775e1570 --> <!-- fix: 81cc293a905934dd625d4ba899cd6e56e161b08c -->
- A session-graph client's extension (an `ExtensionRunner` an extension builds, in the Go, Python, Rust or Lisp SDK) no longer lets a handler that kept a run's `ctx.signal` see the next run's abort, and the handler still sees its own run's abort when the next run began before the host read it. The SDK's `getSignal` answer now carries a run token (`run`, new for each signal object the client returns) and `endedAborted` (the previous run's signal had aborted), and the host makes a context for each token; an abort of a client that returns a new signal object on every call costs at most four reads of its `getSignal`. A client built before this change, or one that sends no token, behaves as before (D235). <!-- fix: b290bc068c, e01a57f90c, ae821f41fc, b1ed275cb9 --> <!-- cause: the getSignal answer carried only none, live or aborted, so the host could tell a new run only from an abort it had already read, and no SDK said which signal object a run was -->
- Closing a `coding.Session` that built its own `DefaultResourceLoader` now shuts down its Extension Host (D19) when the last Session sharing it closes, and a failed `NewSession` closes that loader before returning. Previously, child sessions created by an extension with no resources of their own (one Extension Host process per child stayed until the parent exited) and Go SDK embedders who create a Session without a loader leaked extension subprocesses past `Session.Close`, blocking directory cleanup on Windows. A `Clone` of a Session that was already closed and had built its own resource loader now returns an error (previously it returned a clone that ran on the closed Session's leaked Extension Host); clone before closing, or supply a loader (a Session with a supplied loader still clones onto the caller's open loader). Affects 0.7.0. <!-- fix: 649bef3ed6, e509719a18, 7d12dea47a, 8378518ec6, 791a02dc55 --> <!-- cause: resolveResourceLoader constructed a DefaultResourceLoader for Sessions without a supplied or Services-owned loader, and neither Session.Close nor NewSession error paths ever closed it, leaking its Extension Host subprocesses. -->
- A resumed session that could not make its private copy of the session file (no copy-on-write clone, no room or no right to write the copy, a failed first write) read its entries back from the live file, so a change another program made to the file afterwards reached the session: a branch, a tree, an export, a fork, or the prompt after a /tree switch could show other bytes, an error, or a prompt that had lost turns. Such a session now reads the whole file once and keeps its entries in memory, as Pi does, and never reads the file again. <!-- fix: 8013c00611 --> <!-- cause: without a snapshot the entries were located by the file offsets of their lines in the live file, and a load that made no snapshot, a snapshot write that failed and the first write of a new session were all left to read from that file -->
- A lone UTF-16 surrogate now keeps its unit through the coding paths that still went through `encoding/json`, which writes it as U+FFFD, where Pi's `JSON.stringify` and `JSON.parse` keep it: the text blocks of an extension's `sendUserMessage` (the persisted user message), the `tool_call` and `tool_result` input a handler sees and the arguments an edited call runs with (also when the handler runs in an extension process and edits another member), the arguments and structured content an in-process `tool_execution_*` handler sees, the content of an extension's custom message sent to the model, a `context` handler's change to such a message, the `entry_appended` event's usage entry (now the exact session-line bytes, with `<`, `>` and `&` literal), an `extension_ui_response` string value, the text of an RPC command field that a template literal coerces (`Model not found: …`, a non-string `bash` command), and the Go RPC client's typed decode of a response. <!-- fix: e2bbcc56cf -->
- An extension's `setModel` of a model id that a registered provider object does not list answered `model not found` in every SDK. It now switches to the model, as it does for every other kind of provider and as Pi does. <!-- fix: d5e4cbc53f -->
- A Node extension's `pi.setModel(model)` with an edited or hand-built model object lost every member of the object but the provider and the id: the session took the registry's model, or one with no context window. <!-- fix: 0392315da8, 66df6c8115 -->
- A full disk or a killed process while pig saved `settings.json` or the project trust store could leave the file empty, and the next change then saved it with that one setting or decision alone, so every other setting or trust decision was lost. Both files are now replaced as a whole through a temporary file in the same directory, so where one can be replaced a failed write leaves the old file untouched; the bytes written are the same. Where one of them cannot be replaced atomically, for example a single file mounted into a container, pig writes it in place as before, and a failure half way through that write can still leave the file empty or cut short. <!-- fix: 16c1901a48 --> <!-- cause: settings.json and trust.json were written with os.WriteFile, which truncates the file before it writes, so a write that failed after it began left an empty or cut-short file and the next change was saved on top of that. -->
- RPC mode: a Go, Rust, Python or Lisp extension's `agent_settled` or `agent_before_settle` handler, command or input handler that waits on the network or another blocking call no longer holds every later RPC command, `get_state` included, until it returns. The host takes such a handler to be waiting once it has run for 250 ms, as Pi's event loop serves stdin while a handler awaits; handlers that answer sooner keep their order. <!-- fix: a94c58f2279d7231792d6a98e8900260ab165e5b -->
- An extension process that dies while pig is quitting no longer produces a crash notice after the quit has returned, and `Host.Shutdown` now waits for the whole of every extension connection's read loop. A quit that coincided with a crash used to return while the loop was still reporting it, so the notice reached a session that was already gone, and a connection that no extension held as its current one (a second connection of an extension, one a reload replaced) was neither closed nor waited for at all. Shutdown now stops crash and disable notices first, closes every connection the Host reads, and waits for every loop for at most the bound of a process's stop; a loop that does not end in that time is named on stderr, as a process that does not end is. A crash notice that could not be shown, because the screen's queue was full and the interactive loop had ended, no longer holds the quit either: a post to the loop is released when the loop ends. Present in 0.2.0 and every later release. <!-- fix: 091224f508 --> <!-- cause: Shutdown waited for each loop's sight of its connection ending (a signal the loop gives before its crash report, restart and exit), and only for the loop of each extension's current connection, so a loop in its tail, or the loop of a connection no extension held as current, ran on after Shutdown returned --> <!-- tests: coding/extension/host/subprocess/host_loops_shutdown_test.go::TestShutdownWaitsForALoopThatIsReportingACrash, coding/extension/host/subprocess/host_loops_shutdown_test.go::TestShutdownDoesNotReportACrashItFindsAfterItBegan, coding/extension/host/subprocess/host_loops_shutdown_test.go::TestShutdownEndsTheLoopOfAConnectionNoExtensionHolds, coding/extension/host/subprocess/host_loops_shutdown_test.go::TestShutdownBoundsTheWaitForALoopThatDoesNotEnd, internal/codingagent/interactive_loop_end_test.go::TestPostToMainIsReleasedWhenTheOwnerLoopEnds, internal/codingagent/interactive_loop_end_test.go::TestRunOnMainAndWaitIsReleasedWhenTheOwnerLoopEnds, internal/codingagent/interactive_loop_end_test.go::TestOwnerLoopEndIsSignalledWhereTheInputLoopReturns, internal/codingagent/interactive_loop_end_test.go::TestQuitDoesNotWaitForACrashNoticeThatCannotBePosted -->
- `Value.Check` and `Value.Errors` of the Go, Rust, Python and Lisp extension SDKs follow TypeBox in three more cases. A schema keyword that has the wrong type (`{"minLength": "3"}`, `enum: 3`, `pattern: 5`, `multipleOf: "2"`, `maximum: null`) is skipped, so it accepts every value, as in Pi; it rejected values before, and `Errors` reported a limit that was empty. `const` and `enum` accept an object for an array that has the same indices and `length` (`{"0": "a", "length": 1}` equals `["a"]`). `uniqueItems` ignores an object's `constructor` member, so `{}` and `{"constructor": 2}` count as duplicates. <!-- fix: 4924f3a174, 62f99dccb6, 7071ef14e3 -->
- `Value.Check` and `Value.Errors` of the Go, Rust, Python and Lisp extension SDKs check a schema's `minLength` and `maxLength` in grapheme clusters, `multipleOf` with a tolerance of 1e-10, `uniqueItems` by TypeBox's hash (0 and -0 differ), and the `hostname`, `idn-hostname`, `idn-email` and `regex` formats with TypeBox's own checks, as TypeBox does in Pi. They counted code points, compared exactly and followed a JSON Schema library's format rules. <!-- fix: 4625b4cc3d -->
- A prompt sent after `/reload` no longer hangs when a command of the extension that asked for the reload was still running while the next reload staged its replacement: the old generation's stop removed the socket file at the path its extension's name mapped to, which was by then the path the staged generation listened on, so the staged extension process could not connect (a Python extension beside an edited one hit it) and the reload waited for a connection that never came. Every generation now listens on a socket path of its own and its stop removes only that file. <!-- fix: 6fe688207d8dee14cd2a64fbc01a4fb8278a2a7a --> <!-- cause: Every generation of an extension name listened on one socket path, so a retiring generation's stop removed the socket file that a staged successor generation had already bound. -->
- A prompt sent after `/reload` no longer hangs when a command of the extension that asked for the reload was still running while the next reload staged its replacement: the old generation's stop removed the socket file at the path its extension's name mapped to, which was by then the path the staged generation listened on, so the staged extension process could not connect (a Python extension beside an edited one hit it) and the reload waited for a connection that never came. Every generation now listens on a socket path of its own and its stop removes only that file. <!-- fix: ab0fedf5d2728298926e86941fcf13f09008ac90 -->
- A context an extension keeps past a Session replacement or reload now fails the theme, the terminal size, `setWidget`, the tool update and the SDK-extra `getSettings` with Pi's stale message, as it already did `cwd`, `mode`, `hasUI` and `model`. Before, these members kept working on the old context in the Go, Rust, Python and Lisp extension SDKs and a widget or tool update sent from it reached the new Session's host. In Go and Rust the theme and the size panic (`UITheme`, `Width`, `Height`; `theme`, `width`, `height`) and the calls return the error; Python raises `RuntimeError` or `HostCallError`; Lisp signals. `notify`, `setStatus`, `setActiveTools`, `abort` and the run signal in Go and Rust still answer on a kept context. <!-- fix: 482fdb2a239, 5f10e4f9cc2, 3fd07e39eb5, 481d6ff7f7c --> <!-- cause: each SDK checked only the members the first stale-context fix named (cwd, mode, hasUI, model), and every later member (theme, terminal size, setWidget, the tool update, getSettings, the renderer calls) was added without the check: Go Width, Height, SetWidget and OnUpdate since v0.2.0 and UITheme since v0.3.0, Rust and Python width, height, set_widget and on_update since v0.2.0 and theme since v0.3.0, Rust set_widget_view, set_widget_renderer, get_settings and register_tool_renderer and Python get_settings and set_widget_renderer and Go SetWidgetRenderer since v0.7.0, and every Lisp member since v0.7.0, the first release with the Lisp SDK -->
- A start whose first frame was slow, as on a loaded machine, no longer writes a third frame, a bare cursor placement, after the frame that shows the startup notice (for example "No models available"). Pi runs that frame after the syntax grammars have loaded and asks for one frame for both; PiG now keeps a due frame until the grammar load's repaint request has arrived and draws the same single frame. Nothing changes on the screen; only the bytes written to the terminal do. <!-- fix: e4583be5aa8 -->
- A start with a Node extension no longer writes the whole model catalog to the extension once per step of the start-up catalog refresh. The host sent the catalog (about 1.5 MB) when it bound the model operations and again after the refresh reloaded `models.json` and after it refreshed the catalogs, changed or not: three equal frames in interactive mode and two in RPC mode, each decoded and applied by the extension's process on the thread that answers the host. A frame equal to the last one sent on a connection is now left out when a registry notification asks for it; a changed registry and the answer to an extension's own registry write reach the extension as before. <!-- fix: 935b371168e0e6d42815bfa4713ea25db717aed2 --> <!-- cause: the registry notifies its observers after every commit of a refresh, changed or not, and the host forwarded each notification as a full catalog without comparing it with the frame the extension already held -->
- The Node extension runtime no longer starts the last step of its highlight.js load, which holds its thread for 25 to 60 ms, while the host waits for an answer. On a resume that step could fall between the host's first render requests for an extension's transcript cards and their answers, and the cards stayed placeholders for that time. The step now starts once a host request has been answered and none is outstanding, 250 ms after the grammars were imported when the host asks nothing, and at the latest 2 s after they were imported. <!-- fix: 0f669b1c95c295b4f6400d11dc4cb6920aac17dc --> <!-- cause: the runtime started the registration pass as soon as the grammars were imported, as if nothing waited for its thread after start-up, while the host asks for the renders of a resumed transcript at that time -->
- A `/login`, slash command or prompt typed while PiG is still starting no longer runs before the start-up notices: PiG reads no key typed ahead while it binds the session, as Pi reads none there, unless a `session_start` or `resources_discover` handler is running, and it then serves the terminal while that handler runs, as Pi does. PiG ran the whole bind through a loop that read typed input ahead of the bind's last owner step, so the command could run before the start-up warnings (such as `Warning: No models available. Use /login ...`), the loaded resources list and a resumed session's history were shown, and those appeared below its output, for example the warning below `Error: Failed to login to <provider>`. Every release from 0.3.0 to 0.7.0 has it; it shows only when a key is typed within the first moments of a start on a busy machine. <!-- tests: internal/codingagent/startup_bind_input_pty_test.go::TestInitReadsNoTypedAheadKeyBeforeTheStartupNoticesWhenNoHandlerPends, internal/codingagent/startup_bind_input_pty_test.go::TestInitReadsATypedAheadKeyWhileASessionStartHandlerPends --> <!-- fix: ab82b4db0c -->
- Starting the interactive mode no longer writes cursor placements between its frames or frames of its own that Pi does not write. A terminal that answers nothing used to see the header frame, two bare cursor placements (`ESC[<n>G ESC[?25l`), the window title, and the same again after each later frame: `frame, cursor, cursor, title, frame, cursor, frame, cursor, cursor`; it now sees Pi's `frame, cursor, title, frame, cursor, frame, cursor`. The start now builds the header, binds the extensions and paints one frame at the end of its start, as Pi does, and the notices that follow it (resource diagnostics, the model fallback message, the crash notice) each request a frame. A plain start also no longer waits on the built-in MCP extension: its `session_start` handler returns without awaiting what it starts, as Pi's does, and an extension handler can now say the same of itself, so the session binds without taking a turn of the event loop. A handler of a subprocess extension, which can always wait, keeps the wait. <!-- fix: 7c140b3c41, 5edf81f2ab, b4b67844c7 --> <!-- cause: PiG painted a frame right after binding the session and painted each startup notice, warning and status line at once, where Pi only requests a frame and lets the next one carry them; it also took a turn of the event loop for every `session_start` handler, because the registry could not tell a handler that returns without awaiting (the built-in MCP one) from one that can wait, and no test compared the kinds of write around the startup frames, only the bytes up to the first frame -->
- A reopened session drew a tool call's generic card (a tool with no renderer of its own, or a card that fell back) with the call's arguments in alphabetical order; Pi and a live PiG turn draw them in the order the model sent them. The transcript encoded the arguments from a Go map, which sorts its keys, instead of the stored member order. <!-- fix: 417e1e6158d -->
- The provider bridge (`pig` `--provider-bridge`), the Durable core's `model_context` effect and an extension host's `modelStream` call now send a `start` event whose partial is the pending, empty message the provider built, as Pi does (the durable generation task reads the same pending partial but skips content-less partials before its observer, so it publishes no start partial): Pi attaches its consumer before any response I/O can complete. Each created the provider's stream and read it from an ordinary goroutine, so under load the goroutine could start reading after the provider had filled the shared partial, and a `start` event reached the wire carrying the finished message (`toolUse`, the whole content and the final usage) where Pi sends `stopReason: "pending"` and no content. Each now creates the stream and reads it inside one stream continuation, as the Agent does; event content, order, cancellation and errors are unchanged. <!-- fix: b9de6a2def, 16f41f045e -->
- A subprocess `before_provider_headers` extension handler can no longer race the agent loop's continuation turn when `ModelRuntime.Stream` or `StreamSimple` starts request preparation while the agent turn is still active: previously the spawned request-preparation goroutine could receive the agent loop's `StreamObservation` from `StreamObservationFromContext` and detach its coroutine concurrently with `Yield`, dropping the injected headers with an `iter.Pull` handler panic, crashing `Session.Send`, or permanently deadlocking the turn. `StreamObservationFromContext` now requires the calling goroutine to own the active observation (matching `AssistantMessageEventStream.ResultContext`), returning `nil` to any other goroutine so it runs its wait directly. <!-- fix: 97d1dfec0e81afb2ea202c7130715e69936d6530 --> <!-- cause: StreamObservationFromContext, callbackObservation, and activeProducer returned the executor's active StreamObservation without checking observation.ownedByCaller(), so a spawned ModelRuntime.start goroutine inheriting the executor via ObservationContext grabbed and detached the agent loop's active continuationTurn concurrently with the owner's Yield. --> <!-- tests: ai/stream_observation_owner_test.go::TestStreamObservationFromContextReturnsNilToForeignGoroutine, ai/stream_observation_owner_test.go::TestForeignGoroutineAwaitExternalDoesNotRaceOrDeadlockOwner, ai/stream_observation_owner_test.go::TestForeignGoroutineDataRaceOnDeferred, ai/stream_observation_owner_test.go::TestStreamObservationFromContextReturnsNilToForeignGoroutineDuringProducerTurn, coding/session_provider_headers_foreign_observation_test.go::TestBeforeProviderHeadersForeignGoroutineKeepsInjectedHeaderAndNeverRaces -->
- A tool that requires strict JSON-schema sampling and has a schema node without a type (such as `items: {}`, an unknown or any value, or a bare `const`) is now refused with a clear local error, and one that only prefers strict sampling is sent without strict mode, where before the provider rejected the request with an HTTP 400 error; a node with only an `enum` stays strict, as under Pi (upstream #12049). <!-- fix: 2ed08134a2576304dcea061c394ad186cfe0fef9 -->
- A PiG that runs without a model API now says so when a request for that API carries no API key. A Piglet Binary whose `strip.apis` (D92) names `mistral-conversations` (build tag `pig_strip_mistral_conversations`), and Stock PiG running a Piglet file with that strip, answered such a request with `No API key for provider: mistral`; the request now ends with `Provider mistral: API mistral-conversations is stripped from this Piglet (strip.apis: mistral-conversations)`, with a key and without one, as it already did for `google-vertex` and `bedrock-converse-stream`. <!-- fix: ede518330cab29e170e47ab498c25f256e8a211f -->
- A Piglet built with any model API stripped no longer allocates on every model catalog lookup. The built-in chat catalog asked the strip state for a fresh copy of the stripped API list each time it was read, to see whether the list had changed; it now compares one counter that the strip state advances when it changes, and reads the list only to rebuild. A strip applied after the first lookup (a Piglet's strip list is applied at start-up) is still seen by the next lookup. Stock PiG strips nothing and is unchanged. The bug was present since v0.7.0. <!-- fix: 1162a57f06 --> <!-- cause: the catalog tested whether the strip state had changed by comparing a copy of the stripped list against the list it held, and pigstrip.IDs returns a new slice whenever anything is stripped, so the comparison itself allocated; the no-allocation contract of the lookup was only ever tested in a build that strips nothing, where IDs returns nil -->
- A PiG that runs without a model API no longer panics when a caller streams through pi-ai's compat functions. This affected a Piglet Binary whose `strip.apis` names `bedrock-converse-stream`, `google-vertex` or `mistral-conversations` (build tags `pig_strip_bedrock_converse_stream`, `pig_strip_google_vertex`, `pig_strip_mistral_conversations`), and Stock PiG running a Piglet file with such a strip. In such a Binary the provider bridge subprocess (the `provider-bridge` command of the PiG executable, the transport of an extension's detached helpers such as background runs of pi-subagents) exited with status 2 and `panic: Provider <id>: at least one of "api", "images", or "classifiers" is required.` on its first stream request, whatever provider the request named. In both, an extension's pi-ai `stream` or `complete` call failed with `internal_panic: panic in HandleCall for <extension>.modelStream: Provider <id>: at least one of "api", "images", or "classifiers" is required.`. The built-in provider collection behind those calls now leaves a stripped provider out: requests to the other providers run, and a request for a model on a stripped API ends with `Provider <id>: API <api> is stripped from this Piglet (strip.apis: <api>)`. `--version`, `--help`, `--list-models`, print mode, RPC `get_available_models` and a `--model` that names a stripped provider were not affected, and neither was a build that strips only extensions or features. The defect is in every release since 0.5.0. <!-- fix: c1292ecbab9f906915f4de1c41c5e25d5c7f82be -->
- A connection to an extension process ends when it is closed or fails even while the host's queue of incoming frames is full. When an extension had sent more frames than the host had taken and the reply to a `session_start` handler request or a tool call was read behind them, the connection's read loop waited to queue its dispatch marker until the host took a frame, and only the context of that request ended the wait. A connection that failed in that state stayed open for the host (its `Done` never closed), and `Close` of a live one did not return while the host's incoming loop waited for a call that only the close ends, such as a call held behind the embedder's background gate. The wait now ends with the connection as every other wait of the read loop does; a connection that is only retired keeps its replies ordered until the peer closed. <!-- fix: 0885ded590 --> <!-- cause: Conn.dispatchBarrier waits to queue its marker on the incoming channel in a select that ended only with the context of the request that made the call (dispatchBarrier came with 2f03eb55db in 0.5.2 for tool calls, and the session_start handler uses it since 33d17edd37), while every other wait of the read loop ends with the connection and Close and Done join the read loop, so a full queue with a host that did not take a frame held the read loop for good. --> <!-- tests: TestAFailedConnectionEndsItsReadLoopWhileItWaitsToQueueTheDispatchMarker, TestCloseEndsTheReadLoopWhileTheIncomingLoopWaitsForAHeldCall -->
- A data race between the connection read loop of an extension process and a handler whose request had ended without a reply is gone. When the extension process died (or the caller's context ended) after the host sent a `session_start` handler request or a tool call but before the reply was read, the handler goroutine read the dispatch mark that the read loop was still writing. The race detector reported it (`go test -race`, `TestRestartReplacesRegistrationBesideEveryReader`); a user could observe nothing by value, because the mark is read only to order the reply behind notices already sent. The mark is now handed over through an atomic pointer at both sites. <!-- fix: 3777b25640 --> <!-- cause: Conn.dispatchBarrier runs on the connection read loop through the request arrival callback and the goroutine that made the request received its result through a plain variable (the session_start slot of makeEventHandler, introduced by 33d17edd37, and the dispatched variable of toolExecuteFunc, introduced by 2f03eb55db in 0.5.2). A reply orders the two goroutines, but a request that ends without its reply returns while the read loop is still inside the callback, so the caller read a variable the read loop wrote. --> <!-- tests: TestSessionStartRequestEndedByAConnectionFailureLeavesTheReadLoopsMarkOrdered -->
- A lone UTF-16 surrogate is kept, as Pi keeps it, in what an extension is given and in what it hands back: the prompt, the system prompt and every system prompt option of `before_agent_start` and the system prompt a handler returns, the tool names, ids and results of the `tool_execution_start`, `tool_execution_update` and `tool_execution_end` events, the entries of `turn_end` and `agent_before_settle`, the model of `model_select`, the servers of `mcp_servers_change`, and the model name of a provider an extension registers. PiG wrote three U+FFFD in its place in these event frames and read one U+FFFD from a handler's reply. An extension written with the Rust SDK still receives U+FFFD, because that SDK replaces the unit when it reads a frame. <!-- fix: 11367633b5 --> <!-- cause: the extension event types and the provider configuration encode and decode their own JSON with encoding/json, which writes each byte of a lone UTF-16 surrogate as U+FFFD and reads its escape as U+FFFD, and no test sent such a string through every event type or through a handler of every SDK -->
- A lone UTF-16 surrogate in the text of an MCP tool result is kept in the session like the result of any other tool. PiG read it as U+FFFD. <!-- fix: 11367633b5 --> <!-- cause: the MCP content reader decoded a result's members with encoding/json, which reads the escape of a lone UTF-16 surrogate as U+FFFD, and no test sent such a text through an MCP server -->
- The record of the calls a tool made through `executeTool` keeps a lone UTF-16 surrogate of a nested tool's error text in the session file, in RPC events and in extension events. PiG wrote three U+FFFD in its place. <!-- fix: 11367633b5 --> <!-- cause: the nested call record encodes itself with encoding/json inside a message that is otherwise written with JavaScript string semantics, and no test put such a text into a nested call's error -->
- A character that a provider's server splits over two stream deltas, written as the escapes of its two UTF-16 halves (`"\ud83d"` ends one delta, `"\ude00"` starts the next), is one character again in the reply, in the session file, in RPC output and in the next request for Anthropic and Google models, in text, thinking and tool arguments, as it already was for OpenAI-compatible models. PiG read each half as U+FFFD, so the character was lost for good. A half that stays alone is kept in the session file and in RPC output and removed from the text of the next request, as Pi does. A Mistral reply loses such halves from its text, as it does in Pi, instead of showing U+FFFD, and keeps one in a tool call's arguments. <!-- fix: 5a0c595ce2 --> <!-- cause: PiG decoded the stream events of these providers, and joined the text of two deltas, with encoding/json and Go strings, which have no form for a lone UTF-16 surrogate and replace it with U+FFFD, where Pi reads each event with JSON.parse and joins JavaScript strings. -->
- A model of `models.json` whose id, name, provider name or `compat` holds a lone UTF-16 surrogate can be selected by the id the file gives, and the request, the session file and RPC output name it as Pi does. PiG read the unit as U+FFFD, so `set_model` with that id found no model, and a `compat.openRouterRouting` value reached the request as U+FFFD. The `compat` of a provider that an extension registers keeps the unit too. <!-- fix: 5a0c595ce2 --> <!-- cause: PiG read models.json and wrote the compat object with encoding/json, which replaces a lone UTF-16 surrogate with U+FFFD, where Pi uses JSON.parse and JSON.stringify. -->
- A character that a server splits over two stream deltas, written as the escapes of its two UTF-16 halves, is one character again in the reply, in the session file, in RPC output and in the next request for OpenAI Responses, Azure OpenAI Responses, OpenAI Codex, Amazon Bedrock and pi-messages models too, and the `text_delta`, `thinking_delta` and `toolcall_delta` events of RPC mode carry each half as Pi writes it. PiG read each half as U+FFFD in these streams. A half that stays alone is kept in the session file and in RPC output. <!-- fix: d2a1d9594e --> <!-- cause: PiG read these stream events and copied these values with encoding/json, which has no form for a lone UTF-16 surrogate and replaces it with U+FFFD, where Pi uses JSON.parse and the object itself -->
- A lone UTF-16 surrogate is kept, as Pi keeps it, in the content blocks that a `tool_result` handler of an extension returns, in the text and images that an `input` handler returns, in the content array of a custom message, and in the schema of a tool that asks for strict sampling. PiG wrote U+FFFD in its place: three in a tool result, in a custom message and in a strict schema, one in the transformed input. <!-- fix: d2a1d9594e --> <!-- cause: PiG read these stream events and copied these values with encoding/json, which has no form for a lone UTF-16 surrogate and replaces it with U+FFFD, where Pi uses JSON.parse and the object itself -->
- An extension that calls `newSession`, `fork`, `navigateTree`, `switchSession` or `reload` from an event, tool or shortcut handler, for example a `session_start` handler, no longer replaces the session in the middle of the emit, which made the built-in MCP extension panic on a stale context and `pig` exit 1. A handler that stores its event context and calls one of them after its request ended is refused as well. Pi gives these only to the command context, so its handler gets a `TypeError` there and the session goes on. In the Node runtime an event, tool or shortcut context has no such member (`typeof ctx.switchSession` is `undefined` and the call throws `ctx.switchSession is not a function`); the Go, Python, Rust and Lisp SDKs, whose `Context` type has the methods, get the error `not_a_command_context` and the host runs nothing (D617). A command handler and a `withSession` callback are unchanged. <!-- fix: 105a93fed13c1d1bfcc9817ae009c45b558310d9 -->
- An extension that calls `newSession`, `fork`, `navigateTree`, `switchSession` or `reload` from an event, tool or shortcut handler, for example a `session_start` handler, no longer replaces the session in the middle of the emit, which made the built-in MCP extension panic on a stale context and `pig` exit 1. A handler that stores its event context and calls one of them after its request ended is refused as well. Pi gives these only to the command context, so its handler gets a `TypeError` there and the session goes on. In the Node runtime an event, tool or shortcut context has no such member (`typeof ctx.switchSession` is `undefined` and the call throws `ctx.switchSession is not a function`); the Go, Python, Rust and Lisp SDKs, whose `Context` type has the methods, get the error `not_a_command_context` and the host runs nothing (D617). A command handler and a `withSession` callback are unchanged. <!-- fix: c99165dfe0c1a03a303cbccc426def3598e51fe2 -->
- The in-memory telemetry recorder stored two copies of each event's time, so the second and later events of a span read another event's time in stored traces. Each event keeps its own. <!-- fix: 6f74b7089f, fcccc8bc97 -->
- When `pig` exits while extension processes still hold their output open (for example, when a descendant keeps the pipe open), `pig` waits one five-second bound and prints on stderr how many extension processes did not finish ending; under load that count could be too small, or the line could be missing. Every such process is now counted. Not present in 0.7.0, which did not join extension output at exit. <!-- fix: f4ed81b362 --> <!-- cause: each process's own five-second drain timer (cmd.WaitDelay) could close its exit channel after the shared deadline before the shared termination timer woke awaitReaped, so checking only open channels omitted those processes --> <!-- tests: TestTerminateProcessesOfSeveralHostsSharesOneBound, TestAwaitReapedCountsProcessesReapedAfterDeadline -->
- `TestPlugin` reports a Go stub's setup failure and the tested plugin's own failure together in one `testPlugin: setup failed: ...` message, the stub's first, as Pi's one `host.load` does; it returned the stub's alone and never loaded the plugin. <!-- fix: 75a9caccf1 --> <!-- cause: the stubs were loaded on a Go host of their own first and its failure returned at once, so the plugin's own failure was never collected. -->
- A theme file in the agent directory's `themes/` now loads when it is selected by its file name although the name inside the file differs (`themes/proto.json` with `"name": "other"`, selected as `"theme": "proto"`, `--use-theme proto` or an extension's `ctx.ui.setTheme("proto")`). PiG refused it with `Theme not found: proto` and fell back to the system theme, where Pi loads it. <!-- fix: b637cd4647260ed2b9feef32a13cf16d7c54c8f0 -->
- When the selected theme's file exists but fails to load, the `Failed to load theme "<name>":` line and the result of an extension's `ctx.ui.setTheme` now give the reason, as Pi does: for example `Variable reference not found: nosuchvar`, the JSON syntax error, the validator's list of missing color tokens, or the file-system error for a file that cannot be read. PiG said `Theme not found: <name>` for every such file since 0.4.0; only a name without a file is still "Theme not found". <!-- fix: b637cd4647260ed2b9feef32a13cf16d7c54c8f0 -->
- The thinking-level shortcut now goes to the lowest level of the model when the current level is not one of its levels (`minimal` from `off` on a model that cannot turn thinking off, as Pi), and works for every model that reasons. <!-- fix: d0de44500754 --> <!-- cause: the interactive mode re-implemented the cycle with its own index arithmetic (an unknown index clamped to 0) instead of calling the Session's function -->
- On arm64 and other CPUs with a fused multiply-add, three products ported from Pi are now rounded before they are added, as in Pi: the running pig's puzzle clock, the modification time that orders sessions for `--continue`, and the one-decimal size in truncation notices. No visible change is known. <!-- fix: 77c0b8d4d6 --> <!-- cause: the three lines carried a port-lint fusedmuladd exemption whose stated reason did not hold, so each product could be fused into the add or subtract that follows it instead of being rounded first as JavaScript rounds it --> <!-- tests: TestPigLogoRunCycle, TestFindMostRecentSessionMatchesPi, TestFormatSize -->
- Chord: a list over another owner's set could lose the rows of a page for good when the first read of its query was slow: the read of the first load was made before a commit, the commit's run was adopted, and the load's older run was then adopted over it, so a page that held 10 and 20 showed neither (a list of 10, 20, 30, 40 showed 30, 40; seen as 9 failures in 42,000 runs of one test under load, and none in 36,000 after the fix). The load now checks that no commit's run overtook it in the same section it adopts in, as Pi's `load` does in one turn. <!-- fix: e8c1e17c8ff01c8dc69b7884cef86fe8ea51aca0 --> <!-- cause: OpenRead.load tested its generation before it waited for a section of the host to adopt in, so a commit's adoption of the same read could run in between and the older first-load run was adopted after the commit's; Pi's load checks and adopts in one turn (open-query.ts:202-207) --> <!-- tests: chord/next/store/reads_test.go::TestReadsLoadIsOvertakenByACommitThatAdoptsWhileItWaitsForItsSection -->
- A request that fails because the server's TLS certificate does not name the host now shows the reason after `Connection error.` (`Hostname/IP does not match certificate's altnames: ...`), as Pi does, for the Anthropic, OpenAI completions and OpenAI responses APIs. <!-- fix: baacd45fe9ef --> <!-- cause: nodeConnectionFailure mapped only dial, socket and EOF failures to Node's cause text; the TLS name mismatch had no message -->
- A pig that ended while an extension cell was still starting, or right after one had started, left an empty `pig-packed-*.log` file in the temporary directory: the exit killed only the processes it already knew of, and the removal of the log of a killed process ran in a goroutine the exit outran. The exit now ends every packed cell process, including one still starting, and removes its log before the pig exits; the log of a failure that was reported stays. <!-- fix: cc9cc2f3e -->
- In the Go extension SDK, a tool or command that the host cancelled right after sending its request could start with its context still open and its host calls sent: the cancel frame was read before the main loop armed the request and was applied only later. The SDK now keeps the cancel frames it reads for a request it has not armed yet and applies them when it arms the request, so the handler starts cancelled (or with its signal aborted for a signal-only cancel) and its host calls are refused. <!-- fix: 8defe805741 -->
- Aborting a run while an extension tool awaits a host call, such as a dialog, a notification, a session read or `exec`, no longer fails that call in the Go, Node, Python, Rust and Lisp extension SDKs. The abort aborts the tool's signal and nothing else, as in Pi: the pending call and later calls return their results, and only the tool's nested calls (`executeTool`, `builtinTool.execute` and `builtinTool.localExec`) take the abort as their signal. A tool that has not settled when the 3 s grace period ends (D111) is abandoned as before, and what it still awaits is cancelled then. <!-- fix: dafd5f5103f, 0821b337c27, 0c06e59b1f2 -->
- A `tool_result` handler that edits the event in place now has the edit seen by the next handler of the chain and kept for the result, as in Pi, in every extension SDK. Assigning `event.content`, `event.details` or `event.isError` is what the next handler reads; editing a block of the content or a member of the details in place also changes the result the tool returns, and an edit made before the handler throws holds as well. A member assigned another value reaches the result only through a result a handler returns, as in Pi. Until now only a result a handler returned took effect, so every in-place edit was lost, in every SDK, in every release since v0.2.0. The Go and Rust SDKs cannot tell assigning a new list or object from editing the one they received, and treat a changed list or object member as an edit of the received one. <!-- fix: 549df8005d -->
- The `find` tool no longer reports the result limit when exactly `limit` files match, and `limit: 0` in `find` and `ls` no longer returns every result or an empty listing; a limit below 1 means 1 and a fractional limit is floored. A custom `FindOperations.glob` receives `limit + 1` in the Go, Python, Rust and Lisp SDKs, and a glob that ignores the limit has its results cut to it with the notice (D253). <!-- fix: 04a8c5e9d3 -->
- A user `!` command whose earlier output was discarded from the rolling window, but whose remaining tail fits the limits, was reported as not truncated, so the model got no truncation notice and no path to the complete log that PiG had already saved. It now reports `truncated` and the path, for a completed and for a cancelled command (D244). <!-- fix: 2544a44b2b -->
- A bash or PowerShell command that timed out after its shell had already exited, because a background process it started kept writing to the shared output, now reports the shell's exit code as well: `Command timed out after N seconds. The shell exited with code C after S seconds, but background processes it started kept writing output until the timeout.` The model no longer reads a failed command as a slow one and retries with a longer timeout. A shell still running at the deadline keeps the plain timeout message, and custom operations that fail with `timeout:N` are unchanged (D243). <!-- fix: 3fe717aa8a -->
- Grep match lines, codemode output and previews, compaction summaries of tool results, and MCP server summaries and connection-error stderr tails no longer cut an emoji or other non-BMP character in half when they truncate: the whole character is dropped, so no lone surrogate reaches the session file, RPC and JSON clients, extensions or providers. `TruncateLine` of the Go, Python, Rust and Lisp SDKs follows, and a negative `maxChars` now keeps nothing of the line (D252). <!-- fix: a808864bf4 -->
- A handler of `message_start`, `message_update`, `turn_start`, `agent_start` or `agent_end` that assigns, reassigns or deletes a member of the event itself (for example `event.note = 1`, `event.type = "x"` or `delete event.turnIndex`) now changes the event that the later handlers of that dispatch receive, of the same extension and of other extensions, as it does in Pi, where every handler is handed the one event object. The change lives for that one dispatch only: the next event of the same type starts clean, and the session, its entries and the provider request keep what they had. Until now the member stayed in the handler's own copy of the event and was lost, for every out-of-process handler of these events. Each SDK sends back the members the handler changed, and the host refuses a malformed entry before it applies any. The Rust SDK finds the members a handler adds, deletes or changes as a scalar; it cannot tell replacing an object member such as `event.message` from editing inside it, so a Rust handler that replaces one is carried like an edit inside it for the events that already carried those. The loss was present in every release since v0.3.0. <!-- fix: 3e50072e2e, 8c8b498329, 059aac35c1, c745f9200d, 9871d212a3, 17f9d1389d -->
