- Session files with large tool outputs opened slowly when `/tree` navigated or the transcript repainted: a parallel read split its records by line count, so a session of few large records was decoded on one goroutine. The read splits by record bytes now; the cold context read of a 27 MB, 600-entry session went from 830 ms to 82 ms on 16 cores. <!-- fix: 22866b5c9dca8fa558814ab99d710590b20532da -->
- Interactive mode: after choosing an entry in `/tree` the chat first redrew at the old position and, about a second later on a large session, snapped to the fork point. The frames of the choice that starts the navigation are held until the transcript is swapped, so the prompt stays up and the first frame after it is the fork point. <!-- fix: 59693cd597bafac9b94662ce0d8d342583295849 -->
- A Go, Rust, Python or Lisp extension that shows its own alternate screen (`TuiAltScreen`) and re-sends a component it already showed with different members (it gains or loses `handleInput`, `handleMouse`, focus or `wantsKeyRelease`) no longer races the host's reads of those members: a call that named the component again stored them while a key, a mouse event, a focus change or a frame read them, with no lock between the two, so an input could be delivered or withheld by a half-stored value. The host now keeps the members of a component as one value that a call replaces whole. Present since 0.7.0, the first release with the subprocess `TuiAltScreen`. <!-- tests: coding/extension/host/subprocess/tui_alt_caps_race_test.go::TestARenamedComponentsMembersAreNotRacedByTheScreensReads, coding/extension/host/subprocess/tui_alt_caps_race_test.go::TestSetFocusAndInputOfAnExtensionScreenDoNotRaceTheComponentsMembers --> <!-- fix: 8b6eb224b8 -->
- A Go, Rust, Python or Lisp extension that shows its own alternate screen (`TuiAltScreen`) is now sent the callbacks of its components one at a time, as Pi runs them on one event loop: a component's `render` no longer reaches the extension while its `handleInput`, `handleMouse` or focus callback is still being answered, and a frame that a handler asks for with `requestRender` runs after the handler returns. Before, the host sent a frame from the renderer's timer goroutine or from the call that asked for it, and an input or mouse event from the call that delivered it, with nothing between them, so an extension that keeps state across the two could draw a half-applied input. Each screen now has one goroutine that sends every callback, runs the throttled frame and runs every call the extension does not make from a callback. Present since 0.7.0, the first release with the subprocess `TuiAltScreen`. <!-- tests: coding/extension/host/subprocess/tui_alt_owner_order_test.go::TestAnExtensionScreensInputAndRenderNeverRunAtOnce, coding/extension/host/subprocess/tui_alt_owner_test.go::TestAnInputHandlersRenderRequestRunsAfterTheHandlerAnswers, coding/extension/host/subprocess/tui_alt_owner_test.go::TestAScheduledFrameRunsOnTheOwner --> <!-- fix: ec9984ae6c -->
- An extension's overlay (`ctx.ui.custom` with `overlay: true`) that keeps colored rows until its `invalidate()` is called kept the old theme after a theme change, in the regular and the fullscreen screen, and after a theme change in `/settings` it was not drawn again at all, where Pi redraws it. PiG's `Invalidate` set a flag on the root of the screen and reached no component, where Pi's `TUI.invalidate` calls `invalidate()` on every mounted root and every overlay's component. It now reaches both, the host tells a subprocess extension's component (`ui.custom.invalidate`, after the new palette), the Node runtime calls its `invalidate()`, and a theme set invalidates twice as Pi's does. Extensions on the Go, Python, Rust and Lisp runtimes follow too: see the entry on the component's invalidate in every SDK. <!-- fix: 98d708f331 -->
- An extension component in the editor's place (`ctx.ui.custom` without `overlay`) was invalidated three times by one theme change where Pi invalidates it twice. The count is Pi's now. <!-- fix: 5f449b50d4 -->
- The components of an extension's own `TuiAltScreen` in the Go, Rust, Python and Lisp SDKs were invalidated twice per `invalidate()` where Pi invalidates them once. The count is Pi's now. <!-- fix: e84bbf2122 -->
- An extension that stopped reading its connection while its component was being invalidated could hold the delivery of that component's keys until the connection ended. Invalidations that cannot be sent are now sent as one message with their count, and the wait ends when the component closes. <!-- fix: e516ccd06b -->
- Cancelling the context of `tui.StartTerminal` now ends the terminal client as `Stop` does, as its documentation says: the loop used to stop on the cancelled context and nothing else, so the sandbox's Node child process kept running, the link sockets stayed open and the terminal was not given back (the child outlived the client until the embedding program ended). `Stop` and the exit code now wait for the client's end whoever began it. <!-- fix: 257263d016b1e41ad4bbae1c132ad8a770b0f01d --> <!-- cause: the terminal launcher's loop returned on its cancelled context without running the client's end, and Stop reaches the sandbox and the link sockets only through that end, so a cancelled context ended the loop and nothing else --> <!-- tests: TestCancellingTheContextEndsTheClientItsSandboxProcessAndItsSockets -->
- A terminal client no longer handles a message of its sandbox before it has installed the sandbox: a socket the sandbox opened in its first moments made the launcher post to a nil sandbox (a nil pointer panic that ended the embedding program), and a request it made then was dropped unanswered. The launcher holds what a sandbox sends while it is being started and handles it in order once installed, as Pi's `Sandbox.start` continuation does. <!-- fix: 347671fef856cb2214c21f11b529bbd5fe57687f --> <!-- cause: the launcher installed its sandbox on the loop after the sandbox had begun passing its child's messages to the loop, so a message could be handled with no sandbox installed, where Pi's launcher assigns the sandbox before any of its output is delivered --> <!-- tests: TestASandboxsFirstMessageThatComesBeforeItIsInstalledIsHandledWithItInstalled, TestAtMostAQueuesWorthOfMessagesAreHeldForASandboxThatIsNotInstalledYet, TestWhatASandboxSentBeforeARestartReplacedItIsNotHandledForTheNext -->
- A fullscreen start now writes its terminal setup in Pi's order: the alternate screen is entered first (`ESC[?1049h`), then bracketed paste on, the Kitty keyboard push and query and the Device Attributes query, with the Kitty flags pushed once, on the alternate screen's own stack. Before, PiG started the terminal on the main screen (bracketed paste, the Kitty push and the queries, so the flags went onto the main screen's stack), then popped them, entered the alternate screen and pushed them a second time (`?2004h >7u ?u`, then `<u ?1049h >7u`), and mirrored the wrap on leaving. A terminal that was killed between those writes kept keyboard flags on the shell's main screen, and a recorder or terminal multiplexer saw a pop and a second push that Pi does not write. A start after an external editor, `ctrl+z` or a renderer swap, and an extension's alternate screen, follow the same order. What the screen shows, and `ctrl+digit` and `shift+enter` in fullscreen, are unchanged. Since v0.7.0. <!-- fix: 7b36c4fdd -->
- A terminal that answers the start-up Device Attributes query at once no longer has `CSI > 4 ; 2 m` (the modifyOtherKeys fallback for a terminal without the Kitty keyboard protocol) written in the middle of PiG's start-up writes, between the cursor hide and the colour-scheme and colour queries: the reply is read once the start has written its last bytes, so the fallback follows them as in Pi. Since v0.3.0. <!-- fix: 6835163dd2 -->
- tui: stopping the renderer while a component asked for a frame from its own goroutine (the Loader's spinner, since 0.5.0) was a data race on the renderer's `stopped` flag: the stop wrote it while `RequestRender` read it without the render lock, on all three screens. It could show as a rare crash report under the race detector or as a frame asked for on a renderer that had just stopped. The flag is now atomic and still written under the render lock, so the geometry callbacks' rule that nothing is delivered after a stop holds unchanged. <!-- fix: 4967f7dca31d6632010e5760d4881301c38b15c6 -->
- tui: a frame request that lost that race to the stop no longer arms a frame timer on the stopped renderer, or hands a render to the owner loop after it; the request is dropped under the render lock. <!-- fix: 21d22277cb0b1a1676ca1be7b313530677b03f33 -->
- tui: a renderer that draws on its own frame timer (one with no render dispatcher: the `tui.alt` screen of an extension, a program that embeds the package) wrote a frame from the timer goroutine while `ShowOverlay`, `HideCursor`, `ShowCursor`, `WriteRaw` or a stop wrote from the caller: two goroutines were in the terminal writer at once, and a cursor or raw sequence could land among the bytes of a frame, between its rows and its cursor placement. Every write of a renderer now holds its writer lock and a frame keeps it from its first write to its last, so such a write is before the frame or after it, as on the one event loop of Pi; a write a component makes from its `Render` still goes before the bytes of its frame. The interactive mode of pig draws and calls from one loop and showed no fault. <!-- fix: c0d873133bd5b5e08639692e871dde3bc7b8b3a3 -->
- The model picker (`/model`) now shows a catalog-refresh timeout or failure as soon as it happens. It kept showing `Refreshing model catalogs...` until the next key press, because the screen reused the picker's last drawing; `SettingsList` value updates and `FilterableList` cursor moves had the same hole. A component that embeds a container now tells its parent about a change anywhere beneath it, so the per-child render cache can no longer show a child that Pi would redraw. <!-- fix: 7eb7d29c3f0ed478db4e88cfa8a627d6c8b58732 -->
- Changing the output padding now applies at once to the branch-summary, compaction-summary and skill-invocation cards already in the transcript. Their padding change reached the card's box without telling the transcript, which kept showing the card at the old padding until the card changed for another reason. <!-- fix: ebaa4b5e2da687d9a96c5d01e5d3871c90d8ce48, f2641e89066325f41b2ca323cd3a07d615b9d399 -->
- A throttled frame whose timer callback had already passed its generation check could still draw once more after a direct `Render()`, a forced render request or a `Stop()` had cancelled it: the check is made under the render lock and released before the frame takes it again. The frame now checks its generation again when it takes the frame lock and draws nothing when it lost it, as in Pi, where `renderNow` cancels the timer and nothing renders until the next request (`tui.ts` `renderNow`, `scheduleRender`). The extra frame was forced in a test with the frame parked at its first clock read; it was not observed in a real terminal. <!-- fix: 752aef5e2747d13d62ef8e3368a6d40dc642c4f9 -->
- A cursor marker no longer reaches the terminal when a line holds more than one or a marker sits on another visible or scrollback row, and a selection to the right of the caret no longer repeats the marker, so terminals that print the payload of an unknown APC sequence show no stray `pi:c` text. Follows Pi main 25490ea49 ahead of the pin. <!-- fix: fb4d32eb1c -->
- Fullscreen Kitty images show every row in terminals that keep an image in the cells it covers (Orca, WezTerm). The alt screen now draws images after clearing and writing the rows they cover on every Kitty-protocol terminal, not only WezTerm. Follows Pi main 4622edb79 ahead of the pin. <!-- fix: fb4d32eb1c -->
- A frame of a main-screen renderer that keeps its own frame timer, already under way when the screen stopped, could draw after the stop. Its hide of the cursor then undid the cursor show of the stop, and the shell prompt that followed was left without a cursor. The start-up pickers (`--resume` and the others in `startup_ui.go`) run on such a renderer; the interleaving is forced in a test with the frame parked at its first clock read, and it was not observed in a real terminal. As Pi's timer callback runs on its one event loop, where nothing runs between its `stopped` check and its render (`tui.ts` `scheduleRender`), a stopped screen now draws nothing: the frame lock checks the flag, as the alternate screen's already did. <!-- fix: 0b2baca2cebed4269df13e39aba2ea947cd62255 -->
- The `/tree` search line now shows a cursor while the selector is focused (Pi #9157, D248). <!-- fix: 01a63b933a -->
- Hyperlinks (OSC 8) now work in Alacritty, which sets `TERM=alacritty` or `ALACRITTY_WINDOW_ID` but not `TERM_PROGRAM` (Pi #11767, D259). <!-- fix: 36fd3b5939 -->
- A changelog version recorded with a prerelease or build suffix, such as `0.1.5-20261020.7`, no longer shows the `0.1.1` to `0.1.5` notes again on every launch: only its leading `major.minor.patch` is read. A recorded version without one shows nothing and is replaced by the installed version instead of showing the whole changelog (Pi #11703, D245). <!-- fix: 3b696c8a7f -->
- Images in steering and follow-up messages queued while the agent is busy (`steer`, `followUp`, a prompt sent while streaming, RPC `steer` and `follow_up`) are now resized when the message is delivered, like images in idle prompts, instead of being sent and saved at full size; an image-only queued message now leaves the pending queue display after delivery (Pi #11738, #8581, D249, D250). <!-- fix: 7056d2d9e1 -->
- An extension selector with more than ten options now shows a window of ten around the cursor and a `(selection/total)` indicator, so a long list no longer overflows the terminal (Pi #6688, D257). <!-- fix: 72fa7a7feb, 1628f742e1 -->
- Quitting through `Runtime.Close` or the interactive quit during a tool call now waits for the interrupted run to settle before `session_shutdown` and disposal, so the aborted tool result and the final assistant message are saved and extensions see `session_shutdown` after them. Print mode's termination-signal shutdown and RPC shutdown keep Pi 1.5.2's order (Pi #9124). <!-- fix: bd8849d729, c28332bfcb, 694685ee71 -->
- Files ending in `.dart`, `.nix`, `.groovy` and `.gradle` are now syntax highlighted in the read and write views (Pi #11643, D260). <!-- fix: c3656e595c -->
- Ctrl+P and Shift+Ctrl+P now cycle to the only model in scope when the active model is outside it, instead of saying "Only one model in scope", and cycling from outside the scope selects the first scoped model forward and the last backward instead of skipping the first (Pi #11806, D258). <!-- fix: d1785c847b -->
- A collapsed paste in the editor draft keeps its content when an extension installs or removes an editor, when an editor-slot custom UI closes, and when queued messages are restored above it, instead of coming back as the literal `[paste #N ...]` marker (Pi #9809, D251). <!-- fix: f43fb00cfc -->
- An RPC `set_session_name` or `set_thinking_level` no longer waits for an extension's `session_info_changed` or `thinking_level_select` handler written with the Go, Rust, Python or Lisp SDK: Pi replies at once because it does not await that event, but PiG's reply was held until the handler returned, for ever when the handler waited on a socket or a timer and never came back, and now waits at most the 250 ms that already bounds the other handlers a runtime cannot report waiting. A handler that computes for longer than that writes its own notification after the reply, where Pi writes it before; the handler's effect is not lost. The wait has been there since v0.7.0 and earlier. <!-- tests: coding/cli/rpc_unawaited_event_test.go::TestRPCUnawaitedEventAcrossSDKs, test/extension-conformance/unawaited_event_wait_conformance_test.go::TestConformance_UnawaitedEventDoesNotWaitForAWaitingHandler --> <!-- fix: 77a1d720d9 -->
- A provider or model whose `api` is not the name of a registered API is refused when its first request starts, with the message of Pi, `No API provider registered for api: <name>`, and nothing is sent. Before, PiG sent the conversation, the system prompt and the credential of the entry to its `baseUrl` as an OpenAI chat-completions request. Affects 0.3.0 through 0.7.0. <!-- fix: 3300e6d394b58b2723b581c0f82feb0e71915942 --> <!-- cause: the default branch of the api switch that builds a model's provider built an OpenAI chat-completions provider for any name outside the API constants, where Pi looks the name up in its API registry and refuses --> <!-- tests: TestStreamSimpleRefusesAnUnknownAPINameWithPiText, TestUnknownAPINameIsRefusedBeforeAnyRequest, TestRegisteredAPINameRunsItsImplementationUntilUnregistered, TestUnknownAPINamePrintSendsNothingAndReportsPiText, TestUnknownAPINameJSONModeSendsNothingAndReportsPiText, TestUnknownAPINameResumedSessionSendsNothing, TestUnknownAPINameRPCSendsNothingAndReportsPiText, TestUnknownAPINameInteractiveShowsPiTextAndSendsNothing, TestExtensionProviderWithAnUnregisteredAPIIsRefusedAcrossSDKs, model-runtime-store-catalog/33-unknown-api-name-refused -->
- The Go `ai.StreamSimple` reports `No API provider registered for api: <name>` for a model whose api has no implementation even when the request has no key, as `streamSimple` of Pi does; it reported the missing key first. <!-- fix: 033f100d9a2355a8e7045297ce98724b4f53f9a6 --> <!-- cause: streamSimpleAs resolved the key before it looked at the api, where Pi looks the api up first, and the earlier refusal of an unknown api kept the key check ahead of it --> <!-- tests: TestStreamSimpleRefusesAnUnknownAPINameWithPiText -->
- A model with no api (an empty api name) and a GitHub Copilot model whose api is not one the Copilot catalog lists are refused when the request starts, with `No API provider registered for api: undefined` for the empty name and the same text with the name otherwise, and nothing is sent. Before, a model with no api went to the default OpenAI host as chat completions with the provider's credential, and a Copilot model with such an api went out as chat completions to the Copilot endpoint with the Copilot token. <!-- fix: 30bc09cbdb3b4d1b602b5747252fda32a02a7554 --> <!-- cause: the Copilot branch of buildLeafProviderForEntry defaulted to chat completions for every api name, and the refusal of an unknown name printed a missing api as nothing where Pi reads it as undefined --> <!-- tests: TestEmptyAPINameIsRefusedAtEveryStreamEntry, TestBareModelIsRefusedAtItsRequest, TestCopilotModelWithNoCopilotAPIIsRefused, TestBareModelSendsNothingToTheDefaultOpenAIHost, TestProviderCatalogServesAPI -->
- The choice to build the GitHub Copilot provider for a model no longer names the provider in shared code: a provider with a stream of its own registers itself in `ai`, and `ai.ProviderHasOwnStreamFor` answers by that table and the provider catalog, as Pi's `getBuiltinProviderForModel` chooses from provider data. Behavior is unchanged: a Copilot model whose api the Copilot catalog does not list is refused when the request starts. <!-- fix: 4c0f5e533730d0b18c59fb09550b298cefe0f80b --> <!-- cause: the gate that kept the Copilot provider to the apis its catalog lists compared the provider id with a literal in shared code, where Pi has no provider special case --> <!-- tests: TestProviderHasOwnStreamFor, TestCopilotModelWithNoCopilotAPIIsRefused -->
- A provider or model whose `api` is not the name of a registered API is refused when its first request starts, with the message of Pi, `No API provider registered for api: <name>`, and nothing is sent. Before, PiG sent the conversation, the system prompt and the credential of the entry to its `baseUrl` as an OpenAI chat-completions request. Affects 0.3.0 through 0.7.0. <!-- fix: 9f893e05d0b67d44d6d069f0ac57c95b83cf5f50 --> <!-- cause: the default branch of the api switch that builds a model's provider built an OpenAI chat-completions provider for any name outside the API constants, where Pi looks the name up in its API registry and refuses --> <!-- tests: TestStreamSimpleRefusesAnUnknownAPINameWithPiText, TestUnknownAPINameIsRefusedBeforeAnyRequest, TestRegisteredAPINameRunsItsImplementationUntilUnregistered, TestUnknownAPINamePrintSendsNothingAndReportsPiText, TestUnknownAPINameJSONModeSendsNothingAndReportsPiText, TestUnknownAPINameResumedSessionSendsNothing, TestUnknownAPINameRPCSendsNothingAndReportsPiText, TestUnknownAPINameInteractiveShowsPiTextAndSendsNothing, TestExtensionProviderWithAnUnregisteredAPIIsRefusedAcrossSDKs, model-runtime-store-catalog/33-unknown-api-name-refused -->
- The Go `ai.StreamSimple` reports `No API provider registered for api: <name>` for a model whose api has no implementation even when the request has no key, as `streamSimple` of Pi does; it reported the missing key first. <!-- fix: b266326bd39f6a4dc383b9f2e4cd44417f27b0c4 --> <!-- cause: streamSimpleAs resolved the key before it looked at the api, where Pi looks the api up first, and the earlier refusal of an unknown api kept the key check ahead of it --> <!-- tests: TestStreamSimpleRefusesAnUnknownAPINameWithPiText -->
- A model with no api (an empty api name) and a GitHub Copilot model whose api is not one the Copilot catalog lists are refused when the request starts, with `No API provider registered for api: undefined` for the empty name and the same text with the name otherwise, and nothing is sent. Before, a model with no api went to the default OpenAI host as chat completions with the provider's credential, and a Copilot model with such an api went out as chat completions to the Copilot endpoint with the Copilot token. <!-- fix: f00666666b8dbf5381e4bf96bf22cd02be1c8508 --> <!-- cause: the Copilot branch of buildLeafProviderForEntry defaulted to chat completions for every api name, and the refusal of an unknown name printed a missing api as nothing where Pi reads it as undefined --> <!-- tests: TestEmptyAPINameIsRefusedAtEveryStreamEntry, TestBareModelIsRefusedAtItsRequest, TestCopilotModelWithNoCopilotAPIIsRefused, TestBareModelSendsNothingToTheDefaultOpenAIHost, TestProviderCatalogServesAPI -->
- The choice to build the GitHub Copilot provider for a model no longer names the provider in shared code: a provider with a stream of its own registers itself in `ai`, and `ai.ProviderHasOwnStreamFor` answers by that table and the provider catalog, as Pi's `getBuiltinProviderForModel` chooses from provider data. Behavior is unchanged: a Copilot model whose api the Copilot catalog does not list is refused when the request starts. <!-- fix: 6830edce78e1e5662a96d9d495316afc5f95b256 --> <!-- cause: the gate that kept the Copilot provider to the apis its catalog lists compared the provider id with a literal in shared code, where Pi has no provider special case --> <!-- tests: TestProviderHasOwnStreamFor, TestCopilotModelWithNoCopilotAPIIsRefused -->
- The error for a model whose provider is not known now reads `Unknown provider: <id>` as in Pi, where it read `unknown provider: <id>`. <!-- fix: a1b09915ffbb --> <!-- cause: the message was written in Go error-string style (lowercase) instead of copied from Pi's ModelsError text, and no test pinned it -->
- A view's `title`, its `key` and the `name` of a key binding could hold text that breaks the line a client writes it on or that passes for another label. The host now answers `invalid` for one that holds a control character, a line separator or a control that reorders the text around it (U+202A to U+202E and U+2066 to U+2069). The direction marks of Arabic and Hebrew text (U+200E, U+200F, U+061C) are accepted. <!-- fix: 8e93ec85d6 -->
- An extension can bind `+`: `+` and `ctrl++` are key ids, as in Pi. The host refused them. <!-- fix: 8e93ec85d6 -->
- In the terminal, a key your keybindings give to interrupt, clear, exit or suspend no longer raises an extension's binding, also after you change `keybindings.json` and run `/reload`. The extension reads one notice for such a binding. <!-- fix: 8e93ec85d6 -->
- A Go program that mounts a view through `uiview.Registry` with a record it built itself is now held to the same checks as an extension: `Registry.Mount` and `Registry.Update` answer `invalid` for what `DecodeMount` and `DecodeUpdate` refuse. <!-- fix: 8e93ec85d6 -->
- A Go extension that makes a host call in its factory (for example `ext.Events().On`) hung at its first host call after `/reload`, and pig stayed at `Reloading ...`. It hung because the host answered the factory's call with a push of its state ahead of the result, on a connection that had not registered, and the Go SDK's factory pump dropped that frame without counting it, while a host call returns only after every notify read before its result is applied. The host's push was never released (it is not in 0.7.0), so no release hangs; the Go SDK defect under it is in every release since 0.5.2. The same hang followed a first load that came after a host state change, such as a model switch. A fused Go extension did not hang: it failed to load with `expected ready message, got notify`. The host now writes no state to a connection before its ready. The ready payload is the first state, and the host pushes a change that lands while it prepares the ready right after it. Every SDK applies a state notify that reaches it before the ready and goes on loading: the Go SDK also counts it; the Python, Rust and Lisp SDKs dropped it when a factory-time call read it and failed the load (`expected ready, got notify`) when the wait for ready or the registration of a listener read it; the Node runtime already applied it. One conformance row runs a factory host call, a load and a reload after a host state change in every SDK, isolated and packed, and in fused Go. <!-- fix: 4a0c240b0159238c7200ffb66f902727a74e81d7 --> <!-- tests: TestAFactoryCallAfterAHostStateChangeIsAnsweredWithoutAStatePush, TestAHostStateChangeAfterAFactoryCallIsInTheReadyPayload, TestAHostStateChangeTheReadySnapshotMissedIsPushedAfterTheReady, TestStateBeforeRegisterIsAppliedAndCountedByTheFactoryPump, TestStateBetweenRegisterAndReadyIsAppliedAndTheLoadGoesOn, TestTheReadySnapshotReplacesTheStateOfAnEarlierFrame, TestConformance_AFactoryHostCallThenAReload, extensions/sdk-py/tests/test_state_before_ready.py -->
- `ctx.ui.viewAbilities()` of a Node extension reported no client after a session log sync until the next state update. <!-- fix: 1eea8f0691 -->
- `view_abilities()` of a Rust extension reported no client from its connect until the first state update, even with a client attached. <!-- fix: a47c8e87c7 -->
- Two clients that a mount's content does not fit, one shown the fallback and one shown no view, were sent the same digest (D614). Each is now sent the digest of its own content, and a client whose limits change so that it is owed the other content is delivered it; before, that delivery was taken for the one already made and the client kept what it drew. <!-- fix: 54bf1a5cfa -->
- A plugin view is sent only to a client that draws every node kind it holds (D614): the registry now reads the client's `nodes` list when it decides what a client is sent. A view with a kind outside the list does not fit that client (code `unsupported` when no attached client draws it) and a client the content does not fit is sent the fallback, as for a limit; an empty or absent `nodes` list draws no kind. <!-- fix: 9e348106ed -->
- An extension handler that called `waitForIdle` outside a command no longer hangs its run. A `tool_call` or `agent_end` handler that waited for the run waited for the run that waited for the handler, in every SDK; as in Pi, only a command context (and a `withSession` callback's context) has `waitForIdle`, so in Node `ctx.waitForIdle` is absent from an event, tool or shortcut context and the call throws `TypeError: ctx.waitForIdle is not a function`, and the Go, Python, Rust and Lisp SDKs get the `not_a_command_context` error back at once (divergence D617). <!-- fix: 2f12a5a0de57ae9f634b2b0e5d4efcd8db00f5c2 --> <!-- cause: D617 left waitForIdle off the command-only list on the assumption that a wait changes no session, overlooking that a handler inside the run waits for itself and that Pi gives the call only to the command context -->
- Starting PiG with a packaged extension is about 40 ms faster, which brings the warm start of a package extension back under Pi's (the Startup latency check had it at 1.157 of Pi against a budget of 1.15). Since v0.7.0 each start encoded the whole model catalog for the extension host (about 2,500 models with the OpenRouter routing variants) by decoding every model's catalog record and encoding it twice just to learn that the model was unchanged; an unchanged built-in model is now recognized by comparing it with its catalog entry, and what the extension receives is unchanged. <!-- fix: 8695b8e54d --> <!-- cause: the OpenRouter routing variants added about a thousand models whose derived records were never in the baseline cache, and the check that a built-in model is unchanged encoded the model and decoded and encoded its record for each model at each start -->
- Chord's plugin watcher watches a directory of the app's base code again when it comes back after its watch had ended: moved away and back (the watch of a renamed directory ends on macOS and BSD, with kqueue), or removed and made again (inotify on Linux, where ext4 also gives the new directory the inode and birth time of the old one). An edit of the app's base code in that directory went unnoticed, so `base` was never marked and the app kept its hosts on the old code, where Pi marks it. When the watcher put a watch back and found the directory missing, it kept the recorded identity of a directory it did not watch, and the directory seen again looked like the same one; the watch now leaves no identity behind, so the directory is watched again. <!-- fix: 336d0dc96f -->
- The plugins watcher's directory identity (record D540, now retired) is inode and ctime where Node gives the ctime as the birth time, as Pi's: on Linux and Android when statx is refused, and always on DragonFly, Solaris, illumos and AIX; it was the inode alone, so a directory made again that got the same inode number was not seen as replaced there, and a chmod was not seen as a change. <!-- fix: b2aac7a52c --> <!-- cause: the divergence record took Go's lack of a birth time for lack of any value, but libuv fills the birth time from the ctime where the kernel gives none. -->
- The reference web client no longer erases what the user is typing when a view is updated: an `input` or `editor` whose `id` is in the next view keeps its text, selection and the focus, unless the extension changed its `value`. <!-- fix: fc028ee6d6c57cc064a2b1cf59babcd0cd55a436 -->
- A program that embeds the alternate-screen renderer without a `CopySelection` function no longer copies a selection holding a lone UTF-16 surrogate as invalid UTF-8 through its OSC 52 fallback. PiG base64-encoded the three internal bytes of the unit, where Pi encodes it as U+FFFD (`Buffer.from(text)`); the `pig` command always installs `CopySelection`, so only embedders saw it. <!-- fix: 390964d30ccfcd21401ce3c415f7fac20af549df -->
- Highlighted code in a markdown block or a tool card, and the label of a legacy bash entry in the session tree, no longer measure a lone UTF-16 surrogate one cell wide. highlight.js works on UTF-16 units and can split a surrogate pair between two scopes, and PiG encoded the leftover unit as U+FFFD before wrapping and truncating the row, so a row could wrap or clip one cell earlier than in Pi. The unit now stays nonprinting while the row is measured and is encoded when it is written to the terminal, as in Pi. <!-- fix: a97bb034e5171c4465cc3ba0f83061e772cecee5 -->
- A tool call whose arguments were cut inside a surrogate pair (the codemode card cuts a call's arguments at 77 UTF-16 units) no longer crashes the main screen with `Rendered line N exceeds terminal width`. PiG encoded the leftover lone surrogate as U+FFFD, one cell wide, before measuring the row, so a card row padded to exactly the terminal width measured one cell too wide. Pi measures the row first, where the lone surrogate is nonprinting, and encodes it when it writes to the terminal; PiG now does the same, and the crash log's rows are encoded the same way. <!-- fix: d6613f895ab8d290786b0bf9d13bc1640be6f1aa -->
- Extension SDKs: `highlightCode` in the Go, Python and Lisp SDKs now returns a lone UTF-16 surrogate that highlight.js leaves in a line (Ruby's `?😀` splits the pair between two scopes) as Pi does, where it came back as U+FFFD. The host sends the unit as a JSON escape, and the Go SDK now reads it with the SDK's codec instead of `encoding/json`. <!-- fix: 713bba5380f005357ca43fb4b9c8a23021b0614f -->
- Rust SDK: `highlight_code` no longer loses every syntax color when the host's reply holds a lone surrogate (the reply was refused and the unstyled code came back); each unit is read as U+FFFD, as a Rust string cannot hold it. <!-- fix: 713bba5380f005357ca43fb4b9c8a23021b0614f -->
- Rust SDK: `Context::tool_input` writes a lone surrogate of the arguments as the `\ud83d` escape `JSON.stringify` gives, as Pi does, and `Context::tool_params` returns the arguments (each unit as U+FFFD) where it returned `None`. <!-- fix: 713bba5380f005357ca43fb4b9c8a23021b0614f, 6658e6998d513751c494f68aa325bee7e0241287 -->
- On Windows, a chord plugin's Node host whose link had closed could be killed by the host after its five-second stop grace instead of exiting by itself (exit status 1, "its link closed and it did not exit within 5s"). The process had ended its channel and run its exit handlers within 50 ms; what kept it alive was Node writing the V8 compile cache of every module it compiled, one file after another, as it exited, which on a loaded Windows machine and a cold cache (a new extraction directory or new plugins) took from one to over five seconds. The host now writes the cache once it is up and after each load and reload, so its exit has none left to write. <!-- fix: 3a6a63bbd4 -->
- A chord plugin that starts a child process which keeps the Node host's output pipes open (a child that inherited stdout or stderr) no longer holds the host's exit: `Close` and the host's `Exited` waited for that child to end, for as long as it lived. The host now waits for its Node process to exit, and for the end of its output only for the stop grace after that, as Pi's server awaits the child's exit and not its output. <!-- fix: 47ec6e80d8 -->
- Windows: a missing Anthropic identity token file reports Pi's message, "Failed to read identity token file at <path>: Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '<path>'", without Windows' own wording ("The system cannot find the file specified.") appended after it. <!-- fix: 0d13d8e6cb778532821d841a6a48a51311315228 -->
- Installing a chord plugin's npm dependencies no longer waits for a process the install command left running: `npm install` ended only when the command had exited and every process holding its output pipes (a daemon npm started and left behind) had let go of them, which could be for as long as that process lived. The install now ends with the command, waiting for what holds the pipes for at most five seconds after the command exited, and a command that exited with code 0 still counts as installed. <!-- fix: 31118b1520 -->
- On Windows, an edit or write waits for an earlier edit or write of the same file reached through a hard link even when the queued file was replaced meanwhile (an atomic write): the queue keeps the identity of the file as it was when the mutation queued, not the one the path names when a later mutation is compared. <!-- fix: 667d4938ce -->
- On Windows, attaching a file in a terminal prompt no longer reads a different file when a parent directory is swapped for a link after the first yes: the identity of the confirmed file is read from an open handle, not looked up again by path when it is compared. <!-- fix: 17d97b46d4 -->
- A plugin install that finds no `package.json` (or another problem) names the directory it was going to install into when the plugins root is reached through a link or a Windows short name, not the staging directory. <!-- fix: 17d97b46d4 -->
- Windows: a connection reset before the response headers, or a response body reset, is reported as Pi reports it ("Connection error.: read ECONNRESET", "terminated: other side closed (UND_ERR_SOCKET)") instead of a bare "Connection error." or "terminated". <!-- fix: e88f858c17ec751b54467fb5db6b02d3f8908aed -->
- `FormatNumber`, `FormatTime` and `PlatformLocale` with no language use the Windows user's default locale (the name `GetLocaleInfoEx` gives, as ICU reads it, so as Node does) and no longer `LC_ALL`, `LC_MESSAGES` and `LANG` there; a Windows user with a non-English locale got English (en-US) numbers and times (D464). <!-- fix: 32c03fdaa1 --> <!-- cause: platformLocale was written for the POSIX branch of ICU's default-locale code only and had no Windows branch, so a Windows user, who has none of the variables, always got en-US. -->
- Windows: the extension host's IPC pipe no longer polls with 1 ms sleeps when a write has to interrupt a pending read or when the pipe is closed; both wait on the operation's own completion. The clipboard open retry ends at once when the command is cancelled. <!-- fix: 285ae70166e1e5275da01c4f82561f08dab3ab91 -->
- Windows: the pipes that carry the output of the bash tool's shell and of `pi.exec` children are overlapped named pipes (as Node's are), and Pig waits for their output on an event instead of polling every millisecond. The child's end of each pipe is still an ordinary synchronous handle, and the order in which stdout and stderr are delivered is unchanged. <!-- fix: aeabf180bee2a3cd31101cd614c2e837389d3d8d -->
- Windows: a Chord worker process now waits for its parent to accept the connection on its IPC pipe instead of giving up after go-winio's default 2 s dial deadline. A parent that started many workers at once, or a loaded machine, could accept later than that; the worker then had no parent, exited, and its start failed. <!-- fix: 4feaeb9e8e794d057fc708cedbd174b8c9af6f08 -->
- chord: a server that closed a connection while the host loop was sending on it could freeze the host for good (seen as a hang of p2's code-mode restart test under stress). The socket's reader ran the close listeners, which take the host loop, inside a once-lock, while the goroutine holding the loop terminated the same socket and waited for that lock. As with Node's `ws`, whose `terminate()` only destroys the connection and whose `close` event follows on a later turn, a second closer no longer waits for the first one's listeners and `Terminate` no longer emits `close` inside the call; `close` is still emitted exactly once, queued sends still fail with `WebSocket is not open` and the close timer is still stopped. <!-- fix: dcf10b28b39c10560b79a06871dbb620350e5c7f -->
- On Linux, the native X11 clipboard reads a `DISPLAY` that starts with `/` or `unix:` as a socket path with an optional screen (`/tmp/.X11-unix/X0.1`, `unix:/tmp/.X11-unix/X0`), as libxcb 1.16 and later do. A socket path now connects where it failed before, and `DISPLAY=unix:0` no longer names display 0 by itself. As libxcb 1.16 does (xcb_util.c `_xcb_parse_display_path_to_socket` and `_xcb_open`), the text after `unix:` is a path that must exist once any `.N` screen suffix is removed (`unix:relative-socket.1` needs `relative-socket`), and only an absolute path is dialed directly: a relative path that exists (`unix:relative-socket`, or `unix:0` with a file named `0` in the working directory) dials display 0's socket, `/tmp/.X11-unix/X0`, and one that does not exist fails. Pi's addon links the host's libxcb, so hosts with libxcb 1.15 or earlier read these displays differently. <!-- fix: 7b6510e67 -->
- A routed `pi.events.emit` no longer lets its emitter run ahead of a listener extension process. As in Pi, every continuation a listener queued runs before any microtask the emitter queues after `emit` returns, and the emitter's settle wait now covers every listener process of the emit: it used to end early when an earlier listener process had already answered (it was inside its own wait for an earlier emit of the same burst), failed or exited before the Host wrote the request of the next one, so that process's continuations could interleave with the emitter's later work. PiG 0.3.0 through 0.7.0 have the defect. <!-- fix: 06582c49c6 --> <!-- tests: coding/extension/host/subprocess/event_bus_settle_test.go::TestDispatchEventEmissionStaysOpenUntilTheLoopHasRegisteredEveryListenerRealm, coding/extension/host/subprocess/event_bus_settle_test.go::TestDispatchEventEmissionSettlesWhenTheLoopEndsWithNoPendingListener, coding/extension/host/subprocess/event_bus_settle_test.go::TestHostEventBusEmitCallSettlesAfterEveryListenerRealm -->
- A routed `pi.events.emit` no longer lets its emitter run ahead of a listener extension process. As in Pi, every continuation a listener queued runs before any microtask the emitter queues after `emit` returns, and the emitter's settle wait now covers every listener process of the emit: it used to end early when an earlier listener process had already answered (it was inside its own wait for an earlier emit of the same burst), failed or exited before the Host wrote the request of the next one, so that process's continuations could interleave with the emitter's later work. <!-- fix: 8a4cf80a3e4 --> <!-- tests: coding/extension/host/subprocess/event_bus_settle_test.go::TestDispatchEventEmissionStaysOpenUntilTheLoopHasRegisteredEveryListenerRealm, coding/extension/host/subprocess/event_bus_settle_test.go::TestDispatchEventEmissionSettlesWhenTheLoopEndsWithNoPendingListener, coding/extension/host/subprocess/event_bus_settle_test.go::TestHostEventBusEmitCallSettlesAfterEveryListenerRealm -->
- An extension that emits an event to listeners in another extension process no longer pays a host round trip, and its allocations, for a varying share of its emits (a cost only: what the emits return is unchanged). The listener process now reports that it has run its listeners before it sends its answer, so the host settles the emit when the answer arrives and does not depend on whether a second read has already delivered the report; the same 200 emits cost the same frames and allocations on every run. <!-- fix: 301270f76a -->

### Security

- Updated `github.com/klauspost/compress` from v1.19.2 to v1.20.3, which fixes GO-2026-6865 (a panic on two-block zstd frames). PiG reached it through `zstd.Encoder.EncodeAll`, which compresses the request body for the Codex provider.
- A model id that no catalog, `models.json` definition or extension registration lists no longer becomes a model object with no API, endpoint or limits. Such an object was reachable through the library's `coding.BuildModel`, an extension's `set-model` by `provider/id`, and an extension's model stream and complete by `provider/id`. On v0.7.0 the object of an API-key provider was sent as OpenAI chat completions to `api.openai.com` with that provider's key, so the key went to a host the user never configured for it. On the release line a provider that fills in its own API (GitHub Copilot) still posted the object to its own host with the user's OAuth token. `BuildModel` now answers `Model not found: provider/id`, and nothing is sent. <!-- fix: a1af4d7dd --> <!-- cause: BuildModel treated a provider that exists as a model that exists and filled the gaps with an empty object, so an id the registry did not list reached the provider's stream function with the provider's credential -->
- The Node extension runtime's bundled `undici` is updated from 8.12.3 to 8.12.4, which Pi's `efbcd5adb4bc` does for six advisories that `nodejs/undici` published on 2026-11-05. GHSA-mqg3-3v4r-cm32 (high): with `compose(redirect(), cache())` on an originless `Agent` and a shared cache, the cache decided from the final redirect hop only, so a redirect chain through another origin could poison the cached entry of the original URL or serve one user's response to another; affected `>= 8.12.2, < 8.12.4`. The other five are medium and affected `>= 8.0.0, < 8.12.4`: GHSA-7xg3-fphp-28hg (a shared cache behind `compose(redirect(), cache())` could store a credential-dependent response of a same-origin redirect), GHSA-5rm8-gv32-r954 (a cross-origin redirect during cache revalidation could let a `304` validate another origin's cached response), GHSA-9v6h-8rgp-m69f (the redirect interceptor did not strip credentials on a cross-origin redirect when the request headers were given as `[name, value]` pairs), GHSA-3g9m-rv3r-w5w2 (a handler exception during cache replay could end the process) and GHSA-r4pc-4jcp-7pqc (`fetch()` could skip Subresource Integrity verification when the integrity metadata was separated or surrounded by a tab or another ASCII whitespace other than a space). The severities, ranges and patched versions are those of GitHub's repository advisory API for `nodejs/undici` (`GET /repos/nodejs/undici/security-advisories/<id>`, read 2026-11-16). The only undici that PiG ships is the copy in the Node extension runtime (`runtime-node/shims/undici`); the Go `pig` binary's own HTTP transport is Go's `net/http`. The undici 6.29.1 pins that replace npm's own copy (`automation/images/npm-runtime`, `automation/ci/npm-toolchain`) stay: no affected range includes the 6.x line, the earliest starts at 7.0.0. The parity oracle's installed Pi, the `automation/images/ci-parity` lock, `extensions/sdk-ts` and the benchmark extension sets under `bench/bolt-aot` resolve 8.12.4 too. Follows Pi efbcd5adb4bc.
- Updated the pinned Go toolchain from 1.27.3 to 1.27.4, which fixes GO-2026-6859 (an HTTP/1 server crash from a data race on the response header map when `net/http.MaxBytesReader` or `MaxBytesHandler` limits a request body) and GO-2026-6848 through GO-2026-6858 (cgo compiler and linker flag injection). `govulncheck -show traces` at Go 1.27.3 reported only GO-2026-6859 as reached, through 64 example traces to `net/http` symbols. The trace nearest the flaw is `net/http.maxBytesReader.Read`, reached from `googleSSEReader.Read` in `ai/google.go` through `io.LimitedReader.Read`. PiG code does not call `MaxBytesReader` or `MaxBytesHandler` directly. `govulncheck` did not report GO-2026-6848 through GO-2026-6858. It failed on every build with the previous toolchain because of GO-2026-6859.
- Updated the pinned Go toolchain from 1.27.3 to 1.27.4, which fixes GO-2026-6859 (an HTTP/1 server crash from a data race on the response header map when `net/http.MaxBytesReader` or `MaxBytesHandler` limits a request body) and GO-2026-6848 through GO-2026-6858 (cgo compiler and linker flag injection). `govulncheck -show traces` at Go 1.27.3 reported only GO-2026-6859 as reached, through 64 example traces to `net/http` symbols. The trace nearest the flaw is `net/http.maxBytesReader.Read`, reached from `googleSSEReader.Read` in `ai/google.go` through `io.LimitedReader.Read`. PiG code does not call `MaxBytesReader` or `MaxBytesHandler` directly. `govulncheck` did not report GO-2026-6848 through GO-2026-6858. It failed on every build with the previous toolchain because of GO-2026-6859.
- A user or extension that registers a provider again with `insecure: false` now gets certificate verification back for that provider. Before, the earlier `insecure: true` stayed in force until the provider was unregistered.
- A registration's explicit `insecure: false` now verifies certificates on every route; before, a provider built from a model entry kept the file's `insecure: true` and skipped verification. An opt-in written in `models.json` for one endpoint no longer carries over to a different endpoint an extension names.
- A `models.json` provider or model whose `api` is not the name of a registered API (a typo such as `openai-completion`, or any other unknown name) is now refused when its first request starts, with Pi's message `No API provider registered for api: <name>`, and nothing is sent: print mode exits 1 with that line on stderr, and RPC, JSON and interactive mode end the turn with it as the error. Before, PiG built an OpenAI chat-completions request for any unknown name and sent the conversation, system prompt included, to the provider's `baseUrl`. Affects 0.3.0 through 0.7.0. A model object with no api, which PiG built for a model id its registry does not list (for example through an extension's set-model call or the Go library's `BuildModel`), was sent as OpenAI chat completions to `api.openai.com` with the selected provider's credential and the conversation. Affects 0.2.0 through 0.7.0. It is now refused with `No API provider registered for api: undefined`, which is what Pi reports for a model object without an api, and nothing is sent. A GitHub Copilot model whose `api` is empty or is not one the Copilot catalog lists is refused the same way and is no longer sent as chat completions to the Copilot endpoint with the Copilot token, the conversation and the system prompt. What to check: any `models.json` provider or model whose `api` is not one of the known names sent its conversation to that base URL as OpenAI chat-completions. The same holds for a provider an extension registers with an unknown `api` and no stream handler of its own, and for the Go `ai.StreamSimple`, which now reports the same message even when the request has no key.
- A `models.json` provider or model whose `api` is not the name of a registered API (a typo such as `openai-completion`, or any other unknown name) is now refused when its first request starts, with Pi's message `No API provider registered for api: <name>`, and nothing is sent: print mode exits 1 with that line on stderr, and RPC, JSON and interactive mode end the turn with it as the error. Before, PiG built an OpenAI chat-completions request for any unknown name and sent the conversation, system prompt included, to the provider's `baseUrl`. Affects 0.3.0 through 0.7.0. A model object with no api, which PiG built for a model id its registry does not list (for example through an extension's set-model call or the Go library's `BuildModel`), was sent as OpenAI chat completions to `api.openai.com` with the selected provider's credential and the conversation. Affects 0.2.0 through 0.7.0. It is now refused with `No API provider registered for api: undefined`, which is what Pi reports for a model object without an api, and nothing is sent. A GitHub Copilot model whose `api` is empty or is not one the Copilot catalog lists is refused the same way and is no longer sent as chat completions to the Copilot endpoint with the Copilot token, the conversation and the system prompt. What to check: any `models.json` provider or model whose `api` is not one of the known names sent its conversation to that base URL as OpenAI chat-completions. The same holds for a provider an extension registers with an unknown `api` and no stream handler of its own, and for the Go `ai.StreamSimple`, which now reports the same message even when the request has no key.
- PiG's Codex WebSocket transport sent frames masked from a predictable generator (GO-2026-6278, medium); the WebSocket library is moved to the upstream commit that fixes it. Affects 0.7.0 and earlier since 0.2.0.

### Known issues

- extensions: when the process of a cell is killed or crashes just before a `/reload` begins, the reload starts the cell again and nothing says that the process had exited. Before the fix above, each extension of a Node cell was reported in that case as disabled (`packed member connection closed; /reload restarts it`), which asked for the `/reload` that was already running.
- tui (Windows): in fullscreen mode PiG scrolls the rows that only moved inside a scroll region (D205) on every terminal whose environment sets `TERM`, which on Windows includes Git Bash (mintty) and a Windows Terminal tab that runs one; a terminal that sets no `TERM` gets Pi's bytes. Windows Terminal itself was not run with scroll regions. `PIG_TUI_SCROLL_ROWS=0` restores Pi's bytes.

## [0.7.0] - 2026-11-05

### Upgrading

- **Breaking (Go API):** `ai`: the Amazon Bedrock provider moves to the new package `ai/providers/bedrock`, so a program that imports `ai` alone no longer links the AWS SDK. `ai.BedrockProvider`, `ai.NewBedrockProvider`, `ai.NewBedrockProviderWithName`, `ai.NewBedrockProviderWithModel` and `ai.NewBedrockAPIProvider` are now `bedrock.BedrockProvider`, `bedrock.NewBedrockProvider`, `bedrock.NewBedrockProviderWithName`, `bedrock.NewBedrockProviderWithModel` and `ai.NewOptionalAPIProvider(ai.APIBedrockConverseStream, model)`. Before: `ai.NewBedrockProvider(id, baseURL)`. After: `bedrock.NewBedrockProvider(id, baseURL)` with `import "github.com/MichaelKinsy/PiG/ai/providers/bedrock"`. A program that only builds models through `ai`, `agent` or `coding` and wants Bedrock imports the package for its side effect: `import _ "github.com/MichaelKinsy/PiG/ai/providers/bedrock"`, or `import _ "github.com/MichaelKinsy/PiG/ai/all"` for every provider package. Without the import, building a provider for an `amazon-bedrock` model fails with `Provider amazon-bedrock: API bedrock-converse-stream is not linked into this program; import github.com/MichaelKinsy/PiG/ai/providers/bedrock`. The `pig` command imports `ai/all`: its providers, models and errors are unchanged.
- Go API `coding/extension/host/subprocess`: a program that embeds the extension host and serves an extension's `TuiAltScreen` calls `subprocess.EnableTuiAltScreens()` once before the first extension loads. The `pig` command does, where it creates the extension host. A program that links the host without the call, such as `examples/headless`, does not link the alternate-screen renderer or the word-segmentation dictionaries (6.3 MB) behind its text inputs, and an extension's `tui.alt` call fails with an error that names the call. `TuiAltScreen` is unreleased, so no released program changes.
- **Breaking (Go API):** `chord`, `durable/session`: the watch handle implementation moves from Durable to Chord, as in Pi. `session.CommittedWatch`, `session.NewCommittedWatch`, `session.NewCommittedWatchOn`, `session.DeliveryScheduler` and `session.NewDeliveryScheduler` are removed. Use `chord.Watch` with `chord.NewWatch(scheduler, value, detach, report, replace)`, and `chord.DeliveryScheduler` with `chord.NewDeliveryScheduler()`. Code inside Durable builds a Session watch with `session.NewSessionWatch(session, value, detach, replace)`.
- The stored format of `pi.live` changes: its version is now 2, and a compaction's trigger is stored as `trigger` (was `reason`) in `compactions` and `compactionFailure`. A conversation stored by an earlier version reads through a migration that renames the key, so existing stores open unchanged; a store written by this version cannot be read by a build that still expects `pi.live` version 1 (the previous Pi and PiG releases). The Cloudflare host facade and the Durable core's wire follow: report info is tagged `kind`, and a document commit change is `{type:"document", kind:"change"|"retire"}`.
- Go API `durable/harness`: `ConversationView.Entries` is a window over the transcript instead of the active transcript: the fork-aware history `Conversation.Entries` scans, in entry ID order, with head markers (compaction summaries, resets, handoffs) appended in place instead of cutting the entries before them. A watch starts with the newest 50 entries; new entries are appends, and past 100 the oldest leave in one splice down to 50, which also sets the new `ConversationView.Before`, the ID of the entry just before the window (nil when the window starts the transcript). Read the active transcript the model sees from `Conversation.Context`; render a transcript with `ConversationTranscript`. Ports Pi's windowed conversation view.
- Go API `durable/harness`: `Conversation.Watch(ctx, window)` and `Harness.ObserveConversation(ctx, id, observer, window)` take a `*ConversationWindow` (`From`, `Min` default 50, `Max` default `2 * Min`); nil takes the defaults. Each watch and observer has its own window. Before: `conversation.Watch(ctx)`. After: `conversation.Watch(ctx, nil)`. Bounds that are below 1 or put `Max` below `Min` fail the call.
- Go API `durable/harness`: `WatchEvents`, `AgentEventStream` and the agent event types (`AgentEvent`, `SnapshotEvent`, `MessageChange`, `ToolEventCall` and the rest) are removed, as in Pi. Render state instead: a `ConversationTranscript` over `Conversation.Watch` gives the entries, and `pi.live` the run, the streamed answer, the tool slots, the compactions and why a run failed; a nested call's result is in its caller's `NestedCallDoc`.
- `pi.live` is no longer empty after a run that ended without an answer: it keeps `runFailure` until a later run starts. Code that compares an idle `pi.live` with `{}` checks `Run == nil` instead.
- The Durable core's watch of a conversation view takes the window (`window: {from?, min?, max?}` in the `watch.open` target) and no longer serves `changes`, `completing` or `view.attach`; the Cloudflare facade drops `watchEvents` and `Harness.retryTask` and exports `ConversationTranscript`.
- Go API `durable/harness`: `Harness.RetryTask` and the `retryTask` request of the Durable core and the Cloudflare facade are removed, with the `task_parked` report (`ReportTaskParked`) and the `restart_limit` blocked reason of a task's inspection. A task cut off `settings.restartLimit` times in a row no longer waits to be retried: it ends visibly (below), so nothing is left to retry. Code that called `RetryTask` or matched `task_parked` or the `restart_limit` blocked reason drops them: read `pi.live.runFailure`, `pi.live.compactionFailure` or the task's outcome, and handle `ReportTaskInterrupted` and `ReportTaskFaulted` with reason `restart_limit`.
- `RunFailureReason` gains `RunInterrupted` (`interrupted`: the host stopped while the model was answering and no retry was left) and `RunRestartLimit` (`restart_limit`: the run's task was cut off `settings.restartLimit` times in a row), so a switch over the reasons handles both. `onReport` gets `ReportTaskInterrupted` (`task_interrupted`, with `ReasonRestartLimit` or `ReasonInterrupted` and `ReportInfo.Restarts`); the telemetry report attributes gain the type `task_interrupted` and the reason `interrupted`.
- The stored format of two built-in tasks changes. `pi.tool` is version 3: an input may carry `unoffered: true`; a stored version 1 or 2 task migrates when the Harness loads it (version 1 gets `kind: "model"`, version 2 is kept as it is). `pi.generation` is version 2: a sequential round keeps calls to tools not offered in its `pending` list, flagged in their slots. A build that still expects `pi.tool` version 2 or `pi.generation` version 1 (the previous Pi and PiG releases) leaves a task a newer build stored blocked (`task_too_old`).
- Stored submission records may now have `type: "continue"`; a store written with continue submissions cannot be read by a build that does not know the type.
- The stored format of `pi.live` changes again: its version is now 3 and `run` stores `turns`. A `run` stored without `turns` (versions 1 and 2) reads with `turns` 0, so a run in flight across the upgrade counts its rounds from 0 (Pi `018fdcf4`); a store written by this version cannot be read by a build that still expects `pi.live` version 2.
- The stored checkpoint of `pi.generation` gains two phases: `finish` (`{phase, run: {reason, answer, last, first}}`) and `drain` (`{phase, answer, tasks}`), and `pi.live.run` holds `afterRun: {tasks?}` while a run that answered waits for its tasks. A build without them cannot continue a generation stored in these phases. `harness.HookApi` and `durable.TaskRuntime` gain methods: implementations (the Durable core's driver) must add `Entry`/`Entries`.
- Stored formats written by the core change as in the Harness: `pi.live` is version 3 (a run carries `turns`, `first` and `afterRun`; a stored run without `turns` reads as 0), `pi.generation` is version 2 and `pi.tool` is version 3 (input `unoffered`). A store written by this version cannot be read by a build that expects the earlier versions.
- **Breaking (Go API):** `coding/extension/host/subprocess`: editor nodes of an extension's view need `subprocess.EnableEditorViews()`, which the `pig` command calls where it creates the extension host. A program that serves extension views to its own terminal calls it once before the first view is built; until then a view that holds an editor fails with an error that names the call. PiG 0.5.3 served editor views without it, so code that hosts them must add the call. A program that draws no extension editor needs no change and no longer links the terminal editor.
- **Breaking (Go API, test-only):** `coding`: building the test-only `test-faux` provider under `PIG_TEST_FAUX=1` needs `coding.EnableTestFauxProvider()`, which the `pig` command calls where it starts. A program that serves `test-faux` through `coding.BuildModel` calls it once first; until then the build fails with an error that names the call. The registry lists `test-faux` only once that call ran; `coding.TestFauxProviderEnabled()` reports whether it did and `PIG_TEST_FAUX=1` is set. A program that never serves it needs no change.
- The `retry` message of the Chord v2 link protocol (`chord/next/link`) has `hops` in place of `operation` and `through`; both ends of a link must be built from the same revision (the protocol is experimental and has no version negotiation).
- Go API `coding/extension/host/subprocess` and `coding/extension/source`: a program that loads Lisp extensions imports the new package `coding/extension/host/lispcell` for its side effect (`import _ "github.com/MichaelKinsy/PiG/coding/extension/host/lispcell"`). The `pig` command does. A program that links the extension host without it, such as `examples/headless`, does not resolve Lisp extension sources and fails a Lisp cell with "this program was built without Lisp extension support". `subprocess.EnableLisp` and `source.EnableLisp` are the hooks the package calls. No released PiG had Lisp extension support, so this is a note for embedders and not a break.
- Go extension SDK: `HostHelpers.HighlightCode` loses its `markdown` parameter, `func(code, lang string, palette []byte) ([]string, error)`, because `getMarkdownTheme().highlightCode` is `highlightCode`. Before: `func(code, lang string, markdown bool, palette []byte) ([]string, error)`. Only a fused host that installs its own helpers with `SetHostHelpers` sets this field; delete the `markdown` parameter and answer with the same lines for both. `pig extension upgrade` names the change.
- **Breaking (Go API):** `coding/extension/host/runtimecell`: a failed Go build is classified as SDK drift (the "written for an older SDK" message and `BuildFailure.Drift`) through `runtimecell.SetDriftClassifier`, which the `pig` command installs. `BuildFailure.Drift` is a list of `runtimecell.Drift`, with the fields and JSON of `upgrade.Drift`; it was a list of `upgrade.Drift`, so code that names the element type must change it. A program that embeds the extension host without the `pig` command and starts Go extensions reports a failed build with the compiler's own message, as it does for an error that is not an SDK change; one that wants the drift calls `SetDriftClassifier` from an init function.

### Added

- After a package update, PiG shows the package's changelog entries newer than the last seen version under "Extension Updates" at startup, one line per package with `collapseChangelog`. The first launch of a package only records its version.
- A package manifest may name its changelog with `pi.changelogPath` (default: `CHANGELOG.md` in the package root; a path outside the package root is ignored). Every resource of the package carries the file as the `changelogPath` of its source info, and the new `extensionChangelogVersions` setting records the last changelog version seen per extension package (Pi #8790).
- `ai.RegisterOptionalAPI` and `ai.NewOptionalAPIProvider` register and build the provider of an API that lives in a package under `ai/providers`. `ai` also exports the shared stream machinery such a package builds on (`AssistantStreamBuilder`, `NewObservedProviderBuilder`, the continuation executor and Node readable emulation, `GetProviderEnvValue` and the like); it is for provider packages and not a stable surface for other callers.
- Extensions can format the user's configured keybindings with `keyText()` and `keyHint()` on the tool render context and on the message and entry renderer options, in the Go (`KeyText`, `KeyHint`), Rust (`key_text`, `key_hint`), Python (`key_text`, `key_hint`), Lisp (`tool-render-context-key-text`, `message-render-options-key-hint` and the matching forms for entries) and Node SDKs. `keyText` returns an empty string for a keybinding with no keys. TypeScript extensions get Pi's own `KeybindingHints` declaration.
- `pi.exec()` accepts a `maxBuffer` option that limits stdout and stderr combined, and its result has a `truncated` field that is true when output exceeded the limit, in the Go (`ExecOptions.MaxBuffer`, `ExecResult.Truncated`), Rust (`max_buffer`, `truncated`), Python (`exec(max_buffer=)`, `ExecResult.truncated`), Lisp (`:max-buffer`, `exec-result-truncated`) and Node SDKs. `extensions/sdk-ts` declares both for TypeScript extensions. A `maxBuffer` that is not an integer from 0 to the runtime string limit rejects the call before the command runs.
- Go API `chord/next/host` (core, jobs and remote): the Chord v2 host of Pi `e7a0df27` (`createHost`, `Host.Load/Get/Hold/Accept/Connect/Route/Revoke/Registry/Root/Close`), attempts and objects (`Self`, factories, documents, natives, routines, jobs), references and `Held`, the remote side (holds, remote objects, host links, paths, provider and consumer sides, relays, replicas) and jobs (`DefineJob`, persisted runs). Link handshakes no longer lose a message sent while the channel opens, `Source.Changed` honors an embedder's `Watched`, and a memory link pair can run on a caller's microtask queue (`MemoryLinkPairOn`). <!-- feat: chord-next-host-core -->
- Go API `chord/next/store`: the store of Chord v2 (`@earendil-works/chord/next`, experimental) as Pi `e7a0df27` has it, on `chord/sqlite`. Tables with flat and `json(...)` columns, queries and bulk writes, eager table migrations, the documents engine, one commit queue serializing the commit step, the outbox, export and import of archives with their JSONL encoding, claims, and batch replay. The SQL it runs and the bytes it stores (catalog, outbox, archives) are Pi's. <!-- feat: chord-next-store -->
- Go API `chord/next/documents`: the documents of Chord v2 (`@earendil-works/chord/next`, experimental) as Pi `e7a0df27` has them: `DefineState` definitions (singleton or keyed, in memory or persisted in the host's store with `CheckpointWhen`), the handles an object's attempts get, keyed watches and `At(key)`, retirement, idle eviction of persisted keyed documents, and transactions over documents, tables and job runs on the object's line. <!-- feat: chord-next-documents -->
- Go API `chord/next/host` (helpers): the host-side helpers of Chord v2 (`@earendil-works/chord/next`, experimental) as Pi `e7a0df27` has them. Retry backoff and the activation deadline, `Sleep` and `UntilAborted`, the handler `Ctx` and root scopes, routines (`on`, `onLive`) with their backoff, facets, natives, followed sources, member sources and keyed members across attempts, the member check, presence lists, the unbound-request index, dependency checks and parked calls, `ref.state`, retry wake signals, revocation keys, routes and destinations, and the host's event `Loop`. One package carries Pi's `host`, `jobs` and `remote` directories (see `chord/next/DESIGN-go-layout.md`). <!-- feat: chord-next-host-helpers -->
- Go API `chord/next/link`: the links of Chord v2 (`@earendil-works/chord/next`, experimental) as Pi `e7a0df27` has them. A host's end of a link with its handshake, heartbeat, checks and in-order handling (`Channel`), the protocol messages with the binary and text codecs (the same bytes as Pi's own codecs write for every case of a golden set, Pi `5ec24188` and `339847eb` included), parts with their limits and compression at the origin, errors on the wire, and the in-memory, IPC and WebSocket links. <!-- feat: chord-next-link -->
- Go API `chord/next/contracts`, `chord/next/data`, `chord/next/state`, `chord/next/registries` and `chord/nextnode`: the foundation of Chord v2 (`@earendil-works/chord/next`, experimental) as Pi `e7a0df27` has it. Contracts declare and evolve object types with fingerprints and accepts tables, remote contracts carry a `HostAddress` (Pi `5ec24188`), `ChordError` and the failure causes of the dependency model (Pi `339847eb`), the checked params and arguments, the batch, derives and writables behind watchables, registries and their composed values, and `nextnode.NodeCompression` (raw deflate at level 1, inflate bounded by a limit). <!-- feat: chord-next-foundation -->
- `chord.NativeWatchable[T]`, the in-process counterpart of `Watchable`: `Value` and `Watch(ctx)`, which returns a `NativeWatchHandle`. Ports Pi's `NativeWatchable`. <!-- feat: 7f02969bd4 -->
- Go API `chord`: `Watch`, `NativeWatch` and `NativeWatchHandle`, the one watch handle implementation (Pi 42cb822f1). `NativeWatch` delivers in-process values with a listener `(ctx, value)` and no ops; an overflow collapses to the newest value.
- Go API `chord/nextnode/workers` (Pi `next-node/workers` at `6d4b7443`): Chord v2's workers component. `CreateWorkers` routes a host kind to one worker process per address (started on demand, stopped when idle, never restarted by itself: a crash, a `fatal`, a lost link or a failed start leaves the address failed until `Retry` or a rollout), `WorkerMain` is the worker's side (start message, process lock, the worker's Node host over the shipped scripts, routed from the worker's Go host, `ready` and idle flips read from the Node host's keep-alive counts, reloads, shutdown), and `ProcessLock` is the kernel lock of one live worker per address. A worker is a child process in its own process group (killed with everything it spawned) with an IPC channel beside its stdout and stderr. <!-- feat: chord-nextnode-workers -->
- A Piglet can set `contextFiles: trusted-only`. A run of that Piglet loads no `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.override.md` or `CLAUDE.md` of a project that is not trusted, and a project that has such a file needs a trust decision. The file in the agent directory and the file in your home directory still load. Print, JSON and RPC runs write one line to stderr that names the skipped files, and the interactive trust warning names them. Stock pig is unchanged (D211, awaiting owner sign-off).
- The Durable core defers storing throttled progress as Pi 1.4.0 (6c2fd73b) does. A commit marked `{persistence: {kind: "deferred", withinMs?}}` (`Session.commit`, `Conversation.commit`, `TaskRuntime.commit`, a tool's `api.commit`) that only changes existing latest, initial-fork conversation documents is adopted in memory and shown to watches and views at once, and stored with the next commit that reads or writes the document, before the document leaves memory, at close, or after `withinMs` (default `settings.progress.persistWithinMs`, 1000 ms, the new `persistWithin()` export of `session/session.ts`). Generation partials and running tool output are deferred this way: a streamed answer costs one storage transaction per window, not per partial, and a crash loses up to about one window of it (a stream that crashed before its first store leaves no aborted entry). `Session` options `setTimer` and `persistWithinMs` and `documentCacheSizes.held` follow Pi.
- The Durable core streams a partial answer at the cost of the new text, as Pi's partial commits (da412b03): the host sends each partial as what grew since the last one (`partial.ts`, `core/turn/partial_patch.go`), and a commit notice carries a document change's operations, not its whole value, once the host holds it (`valuechain.ts`). A streamed answer of any length no longer costs host memory that grows with it per partial.
- `harness.ConversationTranscript` (`NewConversationTranscript`) keeps what a client has of one conversation over any `ConversationView`: `Merge` returns the view with `Items`, the client's whole transcript (entries, a gap where a later window did not continue it, and an earlier marker until the start is loaded), `LoadEarlier` and `FillGap` page entries through a loader such as `Conversation.Entries`, and `Resume` is the window that continues it after a drop. Ports Pi's `ConversationTranscript`.
- `pi.live.runFailure` (`harness.RunFailure`, `RunFailureReason`) records why the newest run ended without an answer: `model_error`, `no_model`, `aborted`, `reset`, `faulted` or `orphaned`, with the run's task and inputs and a detail where one exists. The Durable core writes it too.
- `harness.TranscriptItem` has `Kind()` (`entry`, `gap` or `earlier`, Pi's `kind` discriminator), and the three variants write it as their JSON `kind` (`{kind: "gap", after, upTo}`), so a `TranscriptView` marshals to Pi's wire form.
- The Durable core records Pi's telemetry for `HarnessOptions.telemetry` of the TypeScript host: a `pi.durable.submit` span around each submission (inputs start their own trace linked to their caller), a `pi.durable.phase` span for every task phase with its checkpoint, entry, settlement, replay and report events, tool names, and the phase-duration, active-task and report metrics. Submissions and tasks store the span carriers, so a task's phases and a run's linked inputs stay in their admission trace across a restart, and `TaskOptions.trace` and `links` are honored. <!-- fix: 8cf5ded1543ae98061fab5a4d4a01c06eaa7b17e -->
- The durable core and its hosts run the `beforeProviderRequest` generation hook (Pi `d280e1ff`): a generation request sets the provider's `onPayload` as its last stream option, the host sends each request body to the core, and the core runs the replacement chain over it (a throw is reported and the chain continues) and answers with the body to send. Compaction requests do not use it. Both hosts (the JS facade and the Go driver) implement it; the ABI tables and `abi_id` are regenerated.
- `HarnessOptions.onReport` of the TypeScript host takes the `ReportInfo` as its second argument (the task that reported or faulted, the extension whose definition, hook, section or wrapper failed, the host callback, a listener or a failed Session), and `HarnessOptions.models` and `settings` may be functions read at each use, as in Pi.
- `pi.exec` takes `maxBuffer` (Go `ExecOptions.MaxBuffer`, Rust `max_buffer`, Python `max_buffer`, Lisp `:max-buffer`) and its result carries `truncated`, in every extension SDK. Output past the cap (default 256 MiB) ends the command with `truncated` and `killed` set and a nonzero code, and a command that ignores SIGTERM after a timeout, abort or overflow is killed five seconds later (Pi c466a359).
- An extension's `SourceInfo` and package resource metadata carry `changelogPath` through the SDKs and the session graph (Pi b4b72a35), and a component's optional `capturesViewportInput` and the `getSelectPageIndex` helper are available in every SDK (Pi 3bae8527).
- A `continue` submission starts a run on the context as it is, without a user message (Pi `fb524dd2`, #11043): `durable.SubmissionDraft{Type: durable.SubmissionTypeContinue}`. It is only for an idle conversation (a busy one rejects it with `ConversationBusy`; it never queues), places the inputs an earlier failed run left queued first and joins them in its run, and records a `continue` submission (`SubmissionTypeContinue`; never queued, `placed` then `done` with the run's answer or `unanswered`). Its `pi.durable.submit` span is a root trace linked to its caller, like an input's, and `submission.type` may now be `continue`.
- `SubmissionDraft.WhenIdle = durable.WhenIdleReject` rejects an input that reaches an idle conversation with the new `durable.ConversationIdle` error (`NewConversationIdle`, carries `ConversationId`) and writes nothing; a busy conversation admits it as before (Pi `6a282511`).
- `Conversation.SubmitIn(tx, draft)` and `ConversationHandle.SubmitIn(tx, draft)` admit a submission inside the caller's commit with the rules of `Submit`, and return its ID (Pi `cc9c5231`, #11149). The admission is stored or lost with that commit; it must come before the commit's first table write (else `ReadAfterWrite`), rejections throw before any write, and a transaction of another Session (or a wrapper of one) fails with "The transaction belongs to another Session". Entries admitted from a task's or tool's commit carry its `byTaskId`; the handle form also fails once the invocation is aborted. `ConversationHandle.Submit` now takes any `SubmissionDraft`.
- A conversation can limit how many tool rounds one run takes (Pi `f6a9db1d`, #11043). `AgentState.MaxTurns` (set with `AgentChange{MaxTurns: SetTo(n)}`, cleared with `Cleared[float64]()`, resolved as `Agent.MaxTurns`; task-owned children and forks inherit it) is an integer 1 or more, else `Configure` fails with `maxTurns must be an integer 1 or more, got X`. The tool round that reaches it runs its tools, then the run ends `unanswered` with the new `turn_limit` failure (`RunTurnLimit`, detail `"1 turn"` or `"N turns"`), and `HarnessSettings.AfterFailedRun` decides the inputs queued behind it; a `continue` submission resumes on the round's results with a fresh budget. An `onYield` continuation also starts the count over. A run that cannot answer (a context ending in neither a user message nor tool results) ends `unanswered` with the new `nothing_to_answer` failure (`RunNothingToAnswer`) before any request.
- `LiveRun` records `Turns` (tool rounds so far) and `First` (the run's first entry), `RunFailure.First` keeps the failed run's, and `LiveRun.AfterRun` marks a run that answered and waits for its after-run tasks, which records no failure however it ends. `BoundaryResult` and `StartRun` (`RunStart{Inputs, First}`) carry the first entry.
- `GenerationHooks.AfterRun` (Pi `7e15f960`): a hook that runs after a run answered (a final answer, or a tool round whose every call asked to terminate), with a `RunSummary` (`Reason`, `First`, `Answer`, `Last`). The tasks it asks for with `RunEndTaskOf` are created together as children of the generation, which keeps the run and the conversation busy until they are terminal; the run's inputs settle `done` at the answer, and queued items are placed only after the tasks end, then the run ends. A crash before the tasks exist asks again, once created never. A request for an unknown or built-in task, a non-JSON input, or an `Initial` that fails is rejected and reported against the hook's extension. A run whose finish or drain phase was cut off `restartLimit` times ends completed, without a failure, and is reported `task_interrupted`.
- `HookApi.Entry`, `HookApi.Entries` and `TaskRuntime.Entries` (Pi `65fba65b`): committed raw history of the task's conversation, bounded by entry IDs, so a hook or task reads the entries of a run even after a compaction.
