- The Durable core's TypeScript facade (`durable/core/host/cf`) has Pi's continue submissions, `whenIdle: "reject"` (`ConversationIdle`), `Conversation.submit(tx, draft)` (a transaction `submit` operation; a transaction of another Session, or a wrapped one, throws `The transaction belongs to another Session`), `maxTurns` on the agent, `afterRun` hooks with `runEndTask`, and entry reads (`entry`, `entries`) for hooks and tasks (Pi `fb524dd2`, `6a282511`, `cc9c5231`, `f6a9db1d`, `7e15f960`, `65fba65b`). `ReadAfterWrite` names its operation, an afterRun hook's rejected task requests report as an `AggregateError`, and `pi.live` is version 3, `pi.generation` version 2, `pi.tool` version 3.
- `examples/headless` is a complete small embed: the session API, MCP servers from `mcp.json` and one provider (Anthropic), no terminal. Its test runs a prompt against a fake provider and a stdio MCP server and checks that the server's tool reaches the provider and is called.
- The Go SDK page has a section on headless embedding: the `pig_strip_*` build tags an embedder can pass to leave out features it does not use (the Node runtime, the AWS SDK, highlighting grammars and others), with the size each one saves, and how to use `mcpext` without a terminal.
- `TestHeadlessEmbedBinarySizeGate` holds the size of `examples/headless`, plain and with every strip tag except `pig_strip_mcp`, on each release platform to a ceiling in `automation/perf/ratchet.toml` (`binary.headless.*`), the way `binary.pig.*` holds the `pig` command.
- Go API `durable`: `ToolCreateTask` and `harness.HookEntry` are the typed forms of Pi's `ToolExecutionApi.createTask` and `HookApi.entry(token, id)`, which Go methods cannot take as generics. `harness.NewRegistryReader` is Pi's `registryReader`: it reads a Chord registry value, composed as a registry snapshot, as a `RegistryReader` that wakes the Harness scheduler on each composition.
- A session that runs a Piglet now sets `PIG_ACTIVE_PIGLET_SOURCE` in the environment of its tools: the path of the Piglet file, or the name of a Piglet Binary. `pig status`, `pig diagnose` and `pig piglet show` (with no argument) read it, so they work from the agent's shell. The variable is informational and selects no Piglet. A run with no Piglet removes it (D209).
- `pig status --json` has a `trust` object, an `activePiglet` object when a Piglet is active, an `ignored` count in `resources`, and an `ignored` field on each resource item. `pig diagnose` prints the project trust decision, the active Piglet, the effective default model and the settings file each default-model setting came from.
- `pig install <path> --validate-only` adds `autoDiscovered` to the report of a valid extension and a warning when auto-discovery would not load it from an extensions directory.
- Go API `chord/next/host`: `Host.Reload(facets, ctx, ReloadOptions)`, the reload in the kernel (Pi `4b535d57`, per plugin since `a14cdf90`): the complete new plugin set is staged per plugin against a recording `self`, committed once (types, registries, contributions), and each object takes its fate (a pure swap in place, a native restart after its drain, a retry on the new code, or its end by its type's removal) with a `ReloadReport`. A plugin whose new code fails keeps its old code (an added one is left out), and a plugin whose recorded requests would not bind because of such a plugin keeps its old code too (the closure rule). `Host.Load` now returns a `LoadReport` listing the plugins left out (`PluginFailure`), and never closes the host for a failing plugin. `Host.Route` returns a `RouteHandle` with `Retry` and `Suspend`.
- Go API `chord/nextnode/plugins`: Pi's plugins component (slice 7c): plugin discovery, dependency installs, the watcher's marks (`dirty`, `install`, `set`, `base`), the build (`BuildFacet`, a 1:1 port of `build.ts` on esbuild's Go API at Pi's pin 0.28.2), the plugin runtime (`NewPluginRuntime`, `NodeHost`: Pi's own `evaluate.ts`, `stack.ts` and `runtime.ts` evaluate and load the built scripts in a Node subprocess whose chord host is the child of a Go host over the chord link wire, as a forked worker is of its server: the app attaches `NodeHost.Link()` with `Host.Route` or `Host.Accept`; the host's background errors arrive as `NodeHostError` with every field of their kind, errors as `*NodeError` with their `cause` chain, and `RuntimeLoad` forwards `CloseTimeout`, `ReadyTimeout`, `Heartbeat` and `Compression`; Node 22.19 or newer), and the component (`CreatePlugins`: per kind current sets, `Build`, `Load`, `Reload`, `Step`, `Rollout`). Pi's chord sources and their two packages are vendored under `chord/nextnode/plugins/node` (`make vendor-chord-plugins-node`, run by `make pin-bump`).
- Go API `chord/next/store`: `ChordStore.CommitSeries`, several commits in one backend transaction (Pi `e5c6182b`), and the table version fence of `TableHandle`.
- The Lisp SDK exports `TuiAltScreen`, pi-tui's alternate-screen TUI host, with all 45 members: `pig:make-tui-alt-screen` (a `pig:tui-terminal` and `pig:tui-component`s the extension supplies), `pig:tui-alt-screen-<member>` and `pig:tui-alt-overlay-*`. The 46 `pi-tui: TuiAltScreen` rows of the SDK exports ledger are `native:` cells with conformance reach in every isolated and packed Lisp cell, and divergence D204, which recorded the missing export, is removed. A call a Lisp extension makes while it serves a host callback is a child of that callback's request, so a component's `render` can read and change its screen. <!-- feat: 9659f93a1c -->
- Durable's `StoreStorage` (`durable/storage/store`) keeps Durable's records in Chord's store tables and commits a batch list as one series, through Chord's store `CommitSeries` (Pi e5c6182b).
- `harness.GenerationHooks.BeforeProviderRequest(ctx, ProviderRequest{Model, Payload}, api)` replaces the provider request body of a generation request, for that request only, for example to set a provider-specific field. The body is in the provider API's format; the hook returns `&ProviderPayload{Payload}` or nil. Hooks chain in extension order and run each time the provider builds a body; a returned error is reported and the chain continues. Compaction requests do not use it (Pi `d280e1ff`).
- `pig mcp add --oauth-client-registration <mode>` sets `oauth.clientRegistration` (`auto`, `cimd` or `dcr`) for a remote MCP server.
- `pig update` can update PiG through a wrapper or another package manager. Set `PI_SELF_UPDATE_COMMAND` (or `PIG_SELF_UPDATE_COMMAND`, read first), for example `mise use -g npm:{packageName}@{version}`, or the global `selfUpdateCommand` setting. `pig update` runs it when the signed release manifest names a newer release (or with `--force`), fills `{packageName}`, `{version}` and `{installSpec}` from that release, and reports `Updated pig from X to Y` only when `pig --version` confirms Y. The command replaces PiG's own update tiers and never falls through to one; a project's settings cannot set it. See "Custom update command" in the CLI docs.
- Go API `chord/nextnode/http`: Chord v2's HTTP component of Pi `6d4b7443` (`CreateHttp`, the registries `Http` and `Authenticators`, the router and its security baseline, admission with relays, signed cookies, `FileResponse`, requests and responses as descriptions, Chord's own listener, `NodeRequestOf` for apps that mount `Fetch`, the links endpoint and plugin sockets over `gorilla/websocket`). `chord/next/host` gains `RootOptions.Anonymous`, the form of Pi's explicit `principal: undefined` for a root scope with no principal. <!-- feat: chord-nextnode-http -->
- A Nix flake builds PiG from source in the Nix sandbox with pinned inputs: `nix run github:MichaelKinsy/PiG`, `nix profile add github:MichaelKinsy/PiG`, or the flake's overlay. As in Pi's flake, the package puts `fd`, `ripgrep` and the clipboard commands first on `PATH` and Node.js last. Extensions build and run as in any other installation.
- A `Nix vendor hash` CI check fails when the flake's `vendorHash` no longer matches the Go modules PiG links, and prints the hash to set. `nix/vendor-hash.sh update` rewrites it where Nix is installed.
- The `schema` package validates JSON values against JSON Schema drafts 2020-12 and 7 and builds schemas, as Pi's new `pi-schema` package does. `schema.Compile` returns a validator with `Check` and `Errors` (JSON Pointer paths); `schema/formats` supplies the standard format checks. Nothing in PiG uses it yet.
- When a Piglet hides tools, PiG tells you at the first prompt which MCP servers and extension tools it hid and why, `pig piglet show` prints why the Piglet hides MCP tools and which built-in tools a run activates by default (the `tools` list limits tools and does not activate them), and the agent gets one line that names the active Piglet and its tool scope. The Piglet documentation and the MCP documentation have a table of the tool scope rules that the code computes, and a test keeps the table equal to the code.
- A Piglet Binary accepts overlay Piglets like stock PiG, so a custom base such as `pig-tern` is a base harness that behaves like stock PiG started with a different Piglet, and no longer needs a fused Piglet for every combination. Its Binary takes `--piglet`, `PIG_PIGLET_PATH` and `PIG_PIGLET_NAME` as stock PiG does, with the same project trust, Piglet directories and Package install flow. The overlay merges onto the Binary's Piglet exactly as an `extends` child merges onto its base: `systemPrompt` replaces, `extends.remove` removes extensions, skills, Packages, strip entries and the frontend slot (the Binary then starts without its compiled-in frontend), and `extends.allowWiden: true` widens `tools`, `discovery`, `agentEnv` and an extension's `tools`. An `extends` block may omit `source` in an overlay; it then extends the Binary. Only what is compiled into the Binary is refused, with the field, the Binary and the reason named: setting a new `slots.frontend`, re-enabling a strip entry a build tag compiled out (`stripped(binary)`, such as `strip.extensions: [mcp]`; runtime strips of tools, commands, themes, skills and prompt templates can be re-enabled), and naming a fused or embedded extension again with origins. A Binary also accepts `--system-prompt` with stock precedence and discovers ambient extensions and skills from its effective Piglet's `discovery`, as stock PiG does. `/piglet` prints `Overlay of: <Binary>` on an overlay run.
- `build.closed: true` in the Piglet you build makes its Binary closed: it refuses `--piglet`, `PIG_PIGLET_PATH`, `PIG_PIGLET_NAME` and `--system-prompt` with a message that names `build.closed`, and it discovers no ambient extensions or skills. The default is `false`. Like all of `build`, it is not inherited through `extends`. The setting is part of the baked Piglet, so its digest covers it and `pig piglet verify --source` fails when a source flips it. `pig piglet show` in a Binary session says whether the Binary is open or closed. A closed Binary also refuses `-e`/`--extension`, `pig install`, `pig remove`, `pig update --extensions` (and `--all`, `--extension` and a package source), `pig mcp add`, `settings.extensions` entries and the servers of the user and project `mcp.json`, each with a message that names the flag, the Binary and `build.closed`; a closed Binary exits 1 for the flag and the commands, and reports a notice for the two configuration files and ignores them. Stock PiG and an open Binary accept all of them as before.
- `ctx.ui.custom()` takes a `blocked: { kind, message }` option for an inline component, so terminals that support OSC 7501 program status show PiG as blocked while the component is visible. `kind` is `"question"`, `"permission"` or `"auth"`; overlays ignore the option. Go SDK: `RemoteOverlayOptions.Blocked`; Rust and Python pass `blocked` in their options object; in-process Go: `extension.CustomOptions.Blocked`. <!-- feat: 1d7922152f -->
- `delta.PendingOps` holds the op batches a slow consumer has not taken yet and folds them while they wait (appends and primitive sets per path, `r` drops what came before, past 10,000 ops only "replace with the current value" stays). Ports Pi's `PendingOps`.
- `delta.AppendText(draft, key, text)` appends to a string in a draft and records the change as one append op without comparing the old and new strings (a plain `Set` of the longer string makes `Prepare` read the whole string). Ports Pi's `appendText`.
- Deferred commits: `Session.Commit`, `Conversation.Commit`, `TaskRuntime.Commit` and a tool's `Commit` take an optional `durable.CommitOptions{Persistence: &durable.CommitPersistence{Kind: durable.CommitDeferred, WithinMs: ...}}`. A commit that changes only existing latest, initial-fork conversation documents is adopted in memory and shown to watches at once, and stored with the next commit that reads or writes the document, before the document leaves memory, at close, or within `WithinMs` (default `Settings.Progress.PersistWithinMs`, or `session.CreateSessionOptions.PersistWithinMs`); any other write makes it immediate. A crash loses what is held. `SubscribeCommits` sees a deferred commit once it is stored, with exactly what was stored. Ports Pi's deferred commits (spec section 4.1).
- `ProgressPolicy.PersistWithinMs` (`settings.progress.persistWithinMs`, default 1,000 ms) is how long deferred progress commits may stay in memory.
- `ai.StreamingJSONParser` and `ai.ToolCallArgumentsStream` read streamed JSON text once per piece: tolerant of incomplete and malformed text, with immutable snapshots, change reports and cost linear in the text. `ToolCall.AppendStreamedArguments` shows a call's partial arguments from a stream. Ports Pi's `StreamingJsonParser` and `ToolCallArgumentsStream`.
- `chord.Watchable[T]`, the common interface of values that can be watched: `Value` and `Watch(ctx)`, which returns a `WatchHandle`. Ports Pi's `Watchable`.
- `ResolvedPaths.InstallFailures` (`installFailures` on the extension SDKs' resolve result) lists the configured packages that were skipped because installing them failed.
- `chord/sqlite` `SqliteExecutor` gains `RunCounted(sql, params...)`, which runs one statement like `Run` and returns the rows it inserted, updated or deleted as SQLite's `changes()` counts them (index writes and trigger changes do not count). The Node driver takes the count from the statement result and the Durable Object driver reads `SELECT changes()` after the statement, because the cursor's rows written also counts index writes. Ports Pi's `SqliteExecutor.runCounted`.
- `chord/nextnode/plugins`: the app's Go functions and JSON values reach its plugins as host packages (`GoPackage`), and the Node host calls the app's `telemetry` adapter, `principalKey` and `revokedBy` (`RuntimeLoad`/`PluginsLoad`), with `NodeHost.Revoke` and `NodeHost.ExtractTelemetry`.
- `chord/nextnode/plugins`: the Node subprocess that evaluates plugins is found beyond `PATH`: `PIG_NODE` (an executable; when set it is the only candidate), then `node` on `PATH`, then the usual locations of nvm, fnm, Volta, asdf, mise, `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin` and `/usr/bin` (on Windows `%NVM_SYMLINK%`, the versions of nvm and fnm, Volta, `%ProgramFiles%\nodejs` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\nodejs`). The first candidate that is Node 22.19.0 or newer wins; when none is, the error names the newest version found or where it looked (D221).
- `chord/nextnode/plugins`: the plugins' Node subprocess takes a store (`StoreOptions`), a spare process (`Warm`, `KeepWarm`) and a stop grace (`StopGrace`, 5 s), reports how it ended (`NodeExit` `Code`, `Signal`, `Reason`), and `host.DeliveryAwaiter` and `link.Channel.Idle` let a link to another process wait for the host that took it (D223).
- The `schema` package follows Pi's pi-schema changes for tool-argument validation: `UnresolvedRefs: schema.UnresolvedRefsReject` compiles a `$ref` that names nothing as `false` (the error is `unresolved reference <ref>`), the `url` and `json-pointer-uri-fragment` formats are checked, a string's length counts an unpaired high surrogate as one code point, and error messages cap an enum listing at 20 values, word `contains` bounds in plain language and blame a failed union on the branch that declares most of the object's properties.
- The `schema` package can coerce loosely typed input towards a schema, as Pi's `compile(schema, { coerce: true })` does. `schema.CompileCoercing` returns a validator that also has `Coerce` and `Parse`: optional `null`s are dropped, TypeBox 1.3.27's `Value.Convert` rules apply by JSON Schema keyword (numeric strings, `"true"`, a single value to a one-item array, `const`/`enum` members, the first union branch the value converts to), then Ajv-style primitive coercion by `type`. `Coerce` copies only the paths it changes, returns its input itself when nothing changes, never modifies it, and allocates nothing for a value that needs no change; `Parse` coerces, then checks. Nothing in PiG uses it yet.
- Common Lisp extensions. `pig extension init --lang lisp` scaffolds an ASDF system whose `new-extension` factory registers tools, commands, shortcuts, flags and event handlers through the `pig` package of the new Lisp SDK, and Pig builds it into a cached, uncompressed SBCL 2.6.9 image (about 9 ms to start) that it runs isolated or packed beside other Lisp extensions. Lisp extensions may depend on Quicklisp libraries: a system listed in `:depends-on` is resolved from the pinned Quicklisp dist 2026-01-01 with its dependencies, the dist's index files checked against recorded SHA-256 digests and every archive against its listed size and MD5 and a recorded SHA-256; anything else fails the build, and `PIG_OFFLINE` builds from the cache only. The SDK covers the exports listed as native in `docs/extension-sdk-exports.md`; the rest are named gaps. SBCL runs on Linux, macOS and Windows (Winsock AF_UNIX), and the Windows CI job runs the Lisp conformance rows.
- The Lisp SDK serves the whole extension API the Go, Rust and Python SDKs serve. Model streams and `complete`/`classify`/`generateImages`, session replacement (`ctx-new-session`, `ctx-fork`, `ctx-navigate-tree`, `ctx-switch-session` with `withSession`) and the session log watcher, child agent sessions, `create-agent-session-runtime` and services, providers (config, native `Provider` objects, remote proxies), OAuth, login and sprites, message, entry and tool renderers, virtual models and MCP servers, the component kit, `ctx-custom` overlays with mouse, widgets, footer and header, editor components, autocomplete providers and terminal input, the SessionManager, SettingsManager, resource loader, package manager, project trust, ModelRuntime, ExtensionRunner, extension factories, event bus and builtin tool delegation, tool exposure, loadout, prepare/refine arguments and constrained sampling, nested tool calls and `ctx-exec` with a signal, and the Type engine, pi-ai, pi-tui and pi-coding-agent helpers, each with a conformance row that runs the Lisp SDK through the real host (the scenario table, the SDK harness and per-family fixtures) and Pi-generated vector tests. The surface matrix and the export ledger gain a Lisp column: every Lisp cell is native, a kit view, a host call, a numbered divergence or the same gap lane as the other SDKs.
- The Lisp SDK reaches the host calls the other SDKs already have for the session, models, themes and the editor text: `ctx-set-active-tools`, `ctx-get-commands`, `ctx-get-context-usage`, `ctx-get-system-prompt-options`, `ctx-get-model-info`, `ctx-get-model-auth`, `ctx-get-scoped-models`, `ctx-set-model`, `ctx-set-thinking-level`, `ctx-set-label`, `ctx-wait-for-idle`, `ctx-project-trusted-p`, `ctx-get-session-id`, `ctx-get-leaf-id`, the theme and editor-text getters, `registry-find`, `registry-get-provider-auth`, `registry-refresh` and `registry-get-available-of-type`, and `ctx-on-width-change` for terminal resizes. The wire-capability gate now covers Lisp and names every host call it does not serve yet.
- The extension authoring guide now shows how to price what compaction would drop with `findCutPoint`, `sessionEntryToContextMessages` and `estimateTokens`, which the Go (`sdk.FindCutPoint`, `sdk.SessionEntryToContextMessages`, `sdk.EstimateTokens` in the separate `extensions/sdk` module), Rust and Python SDKs export over the entries `getBranch()` returns (`findCutPoint` and `estimateTokens` since 0.5.0, `sessionEntryToContextMessages` since 0.5.2). The Go SDK ships a runnable example whose expected output Pi's own functions produce, and benchmarks that run the helpers over branches of 1k, 10k and 100k entries.
- The Go, Rust and Python SDKs export the first part of pi-ai's `Type` (TypeBox 1.3.27): `Object`, `String`, `Number`, `Integer`, `Boolean`, `Null`, `Array`, `Union`, `Intersect`, `Literal`, `Enum`, `Record`, `Optional`, `Readonly`, `Immutable`, `Unsafe`, `With`, `Ref`, `Any`, `Unknown`, `Never`, `Undefined`, `Void`, `Symbol`, `BigInt` and the matching `Is...` guards. A schema built with them is exactly the JSON Schema Pi's `Type` returns, including member order and the optional markers `Type.Object` reads, and is checked against Pi's own answers for 292 cases. The other members come in later releases; the Codec family (`Codec`, `Decode`, `Encode`, `DecodeBuilder`, `EncodeBuilder`, `IsCodec`) is not served (D198).
- The Go, Rust and Python SDKs export `Type.Refine` and `Type.IsRefine` of pi-ai's `Type`. A tool whose parameters carry refinements has its arguments checked in the host in TypeBox's own order, with each predicate and error message run in the extension that defined it, so an extension tool rejects, words and orders its failures as it does under Pi (checked against Pi's own `validateToolArguments` for the same cases in every SDK). A tool without refinements validates exactly as before.
- The Go, Rust and Python SDKs serve the function options of Pi's `createMcpExtension` (`loadConfig`, `createTransport`, `credentials`, `openUrl`, `updateConfig`): the functions stay in the extension's process and the host calls them over the connection, so a loader's MCP extension can read its configuration, speak through a transport and keep its OAuth state in the caller's own code.
- The Go, Rust and Python SDKs serve Pi's `new ModelRegistry(runtime)`: a registry facade over a `ModelRuntime` the extension built, whose members all forward to that runtime, and the runtime's `registerNativeProvider`, `getRegisteredNativeProvider`, `getProvider` and `getProviders`. A Provider object an extension registers on its own runtime stays in the extension and the runtime calls it over the connection; a builtin provider's object still fails with the D78 error, while its display name is answered.
- The Go, Rust and Python SDKs export pi-ai's `createProvider`: a provider built from parts (an `api` for every chat model or one per `model.api`, `fetchModels`, `filterModels`, image and classifier implementations) that behaves as Pi's, including the stream error a model whose api has no implementation gets and the transactional model refresh. Register it with `RegisterNativeProvider`.
- The Go, Rust and Python SDKs export Pi's `createExtensionRuntime` and `ExtensionRunner`. The runner is built over the extensions a `DefaultResourceLoader` loaded (they stay in their own processes), dispatches every `emit*` through them in extension order with Pi's chaining and error isolation, answers the registries, and binds the actions, contexts and UI context of the caller. The members of the UI context that take TUI components are served by the TUI handle, not here. The SDK loader takes an additive `runtime` option (D201).
- The same SDKs export Pi's `createAgentSessionRuntime` and `AgentSessionRuntime`: the runtime owns the current session and its services, calls the caller's factory on every `newSession`, `switchSession`, `fork` and `importFromJsonl`, and emits `session_before_switch`, `session_before_fork` and `session_shutdown` to the replaced session's extensions as Pi does. `AgentSession` gains `refreshContext` and `sessionManager`. The `withSession` option is not served yet.
- The Go, Rust and Python SDKs export Pi's `createAgentSessionServices` and `createAgentSessionFromServices`: the services of one session cwd (model runtime, settings manager, resource loader, diagnostics) and a session built over them, with the new `sessionStartEvent` option on child sessions. The registrations and extension flag values of the extensions the services' loader loaded apply as in Pi, and an extension a session loads from such a loader now reads those flag values with `getFlag`.
- The Go, Rust and Python SDKs export Pi's `buildSessionContext(entries, leafId?, byId?)`: the model context of a session (the path to the leaf with compaction, branch summaries and context edits applied, the thinking level and the model). It is tested against Pi's own answers for 41 cases in all three SDKs.
- The Go, Rust and Python SDKs export Pi's `createCodemodeExtension` and `createToolSearchExtension`, and the data options (`logPath`, `startupWaitMs`) of `createMcpExtension`, as references to the compiled-in extensions: pass them in a `DefaultResourceLoader`'s `extensionFactories` and a session built over that loader has the `codemode`, `tool_search` and `/mcp` extensions (the tools inactive until a `tools` option or setting names them).
- The Go, Rust and Python SDKs export every remaining member of pi-ai's `Type` (TypeBox 1.3.27): `Pick`, `Omit`, `Partial`, `Required`, `KeyOf`, `Index`, `Mapped`, `Conditional`, `Extends`, `ExtendsResult`, `Evaluate`, `Instantiate`, `Exclude`, `Extract`, `NonNullable`, `Capitalize`, `Lowercase`, `Uncapitalize`, `Uppercase`, `Parameters`, `ReturnType`, `ConstructorParameters`, `InstanceType`, `Function`, `Constructor`, `Tuple`, `TemplateLiteral`, `Cyclic`, `Module`, `Interface`, `Call`, `Generic`, `Script` and the rest, with their `Is...` guards. Pig ports TypeBox's type engine once, in the host, and every SDK asks it through a blocking request while a schema is built, so each member returns exactly what Pi's `Type` returns, member order and hidden markers included, and is checked against Pi's own answers for hundreds of cases. A `Record` whose key is an enum, an intersection or a template literal now works too. A schema can hold a bigint (`Type.Script("1n")`) as Pi's value does and fails only when it is written as JSON, with Pi's "Do not know how to serialize a BigInt"; the Python SDK raises "Invalid Arguments" for `Infer`, `Parameter`, `Script` and `Refine` called with another argument count, as Pi does.
- An extension can own thinking runs with `pi.ownThinkingRuns(enabled = true)` (Go `OwnThinkingRuns`, Rust and Python `own_thinking_runs`, Lisp `own-thinking-runs`, in-process Go `extension.API.OwnThinkingRuns`), at load or later, and turn it off again. While any extension owns them, a thinking run that is hidden, or that a Markdown transformer rewrote to empty text, leaves no stub row and no blank rows before or after it; the thinking stays in the message, click-to-hide and Ctrl+T work as before, and without such an extension the message draws as Pi does (D214, issue #384). <!-- feat: 2b316c5f08 -->
- The /model and /scoped-models rows show the model name in parentheses after the id when it has words the id lacks, so renamed overrides from models.json are visible. <!-- feat: c55a48a7a6 -->
- `make test-term-engines` replays the alternate screen's scroll-region frames (D205) and Pi's exact bytes (`PIG_TUI_SCROLL_ROWS=0`) of a deterministic corpus through xterm.js, `alacritty_terminal`, `wezterm-term`, libvterm and pyte, and requires each engine to show the same screen after every frame. CI runs it in the `toolchains` shard (`docs/testing/term-engines.md`).
- The Go, Rust and Python SDKs export `TuiAltScreen`, pi-tui's alternate-screen TUI host, with all 45 members (Go `sdk.NewTuiAltScreen`, Rust `TuiAltScreen::new`, Python `TuiAltScreen`). The extension supplies the `Terminal` and the components; the host runs Pi's scrolling viewport, selection, overlays, focus and rendering and calls back for terminal output, component render and input, input listeners and the option callbacks. The SDKs reported the export as divergence D204; it is closed. <!-- feat: c9b90e2bb2 -->
- PiG lists OpenRouter's `:nitro` (providers sorted by throughput) and `:floor` (providers sorted by price) routing variants beside every OpenRouter model, for example `openrouter/openai/gpt-5.2:nitro`, in `--list-models`, the model selector and the SDKs, and resolves them by name. OpenRouter accepts them on every model id but does not list them, so Pi's catalog has none (D199). A variant carries its base model's limits and listed prices and is derived when it is listed or named, so startup and the binary do not grow. A partial model text such as `--model 4o` still resolves as it does in Pi; naming a variant selects it.

### Changed

- Package filters, manifest `!`/`+`/`-` overrides, settings resource patterns, model scopes and built-in extension overrides follow minimatch 11.0.3, as in Pi: a path portion is matched by a state machine (`@isaacs/nonrecursive-glob-match`) instead of a regular expression. An empty path portion matches only an empty pattern portion (so `""` no longer matches `*(a)`), `*\.5` matches `gpt-5.5`, case folds one code point at a time with Unicode simple case folding, and a pattern that minimatch 10.2.6 could not compile (a POSIX class beside an escaped `,`, as in `[[:alpha:]]*,md`) now compiles; only a pattern over 65,536 UTF-16 units still fails.
- Skill load warnings in the startup resource listing are headed `[Skill warnings]` instead of `[Skill conflicts]`, as in Pi.
- In fullscreen mode the `Model scope: ...` notice appears in the header instead of being printed to the terminal before the alternate screen opens, so it no longer stays in the shell after exit.
- The session selector no longer keeps its selection valid when a page key arrives before any session has loaded; like Pi, it stays unselected until a key moves it.
- PageUp and PageDown no longer move the selection in the extension selector, trust selector and first-time setup dialog, and no longer keep the fullscreen transcript from scrolling while those or the config selector are open, as in Pi. The config selector still pages its own list.
- A program that embeds PiG and links no Bedrock package is smaller (39.9 MB to 36.7 MB for `examples/headless` on linux/amd64, and 18.3 MB to 15.0 MB for a program that only imports `ai`): `import _ "github.com/MichaelKinsy/PiG/ai"` no longer links the AWS SDK and smithy (89 packages). The `pig_strip_bedrock_converse_stream` build tag still works: with it, `ai/providers/bedrock` compiles to the strip registration alone.
- The bug report form now requires only "What happened"; the versions, platform, steps and Pi comparison are optional, so a `/bug` report can be filed without knowing the cause (#394).
- Chord v1 (`chord/host`) validates with the `schema` package instead of the TypeBox-era engine, as Pi does since the switch to pi-schema. A `Schema` is a `*schema.Object` that keeps the order its members were declared in; a failed check's `Details` are `{path, keyword, message}` per error (the first three), with pi-schema's messages (`state thing: / expected string, got integer`). `format` is an annotation: no format is checked. Schemas a peer sends in a contract token are stripped of unknown fields like any other (before, a decoded token's schemas stripped nothing). A frame is checked against the frame schema compiled once, at 110 to 840 ns and no allocation per frame (before: 5 to 34 µs and 48 to 335 allocations).
- A host a route resolves is admitted before the route authorizes again and the request's currency is checked, so a worker spawned for a relayed hold that was released, refused or revoked meanwhile still has its link read; its own references to its parent no longer wait until they fail with `unavailable/ready_timeout`.
- The `chord/delta` tracker keeps its most recent open change in a plain field and registers a weak pointer only for a second change open at the same time, as Pi's tracker does without a `WeakRef`. A draft dropped without `Prepare()` or `Abort()` now stays referenced by its tracker until the tracker's next `BeginChange()` or `Adopt()`, not reclaimed at the next collection.
- Chord v2 (`chord/next`) checks arguments, params, documents, json columns and archive parts with the `schema` package instead of the TypeBox-era validator, as Pi does since the switch to pi-schema. A failed check explains itself with pi-schema's messages (`args/title: expected string, got integer`, `params: expected object, got string`, `args/blob: expected at most 2 bytes`), a missing field and an unknown field are reported at their own path, and `~` and `/` in keys are escaped in `details.path` (`/tags/a~1b`). `format` is an annotation: it is part of a schema's normal form and fingerprint, but no format is checked. A `bytes()` leaf is checked natively, also inside a `Map`. Fingerprints and normal forms of contracts, documents, tables and jobs, and the data stored before the switch, are unchanged (proved against Pi's recorded fingerprints, SQLite store and archive).
- `contracts.Obj` writes `properties` before `required`, as pi-schema's `obj` does, and `contracts.Opt(...)` outside an object is refused by schema snapshots (`<path>: expected a schema`). Params refuse an optional field before reading its schema.
- Document, conversation view, task graph and event watches use Chord's `Watch`; behaviour is unchanged.
- CI: `automation/gen/pending-test-batches.py` and `automation/gen/test-ported-baseline.py` no longer default to the policy and mapping ledgers of a removed Pi version. Both read the committed Pi pin through `automation/pin/pinlib.py`.
- CI: the live-providers workflow no longer names Rust 1.97.1 and npm 12.1.0 itself. It reads both from `ci.yml`, as the nightly workflow does.
- `make compliance` checks the npm pin (`NPM_VERSION` in `ci.yml`) against `automation/ci/npm-toolchain/package.json`, `automation/images/npm-runtime/package.json`, the CI parity image and the documented requirement, and checks the Go pin against `AGENTS.md`.
- Tests fail on a version literal in `automation/`, the top-level `Makefile` or a workflow that is neither derived from its source nor recorded with a reason, and on an `UpstreamReviewedVersion` that is after the pin or has no ledgers.
- CI: the light pull-request run's `Linux / test-fast` shard now runs `make ci-test-changed`: the fast packages that `automation/ci/changed-packages.py` selects against the pull request's base branch (the edited packages, every package whose tests import them, and the pigfault tests of the durable driver), without `-race`. A change to `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `go.work` or `go.work.sum`, or to a file no package test reads, runs the whole shard, and the run summary lists the selection and says when and why it fell back. `changelog.d` fragments map to the packages whose Go source names the directory. The full run is unchanged and stays the merge gate.
- `make test-changed` runs a package CI shards (`ai`, `coding`, `internal/codingagent`, the extension host and conformance packages and others) in CI's shards, each in its own `go test` process and timeout, and runs a package the change edits under `-race` in `TEST_CHANGED_RACE_SHARDS` (default 3) times as many shards. A whole-package run outlived `go test`'s 10-minute timeout on a loaded host, and a timeout kill skips `TestMain` cleanup, which then read as scratch-directory leaks.
- Durable: opening a store that pi-durable 1.3.0 wrote now upgrades it in place, as Pi does, and no longer leaves a `<path>.schema-1.bak` copy beside it. PiG 0.5.2 and 0.5.3 made that copy because no Pi release read schema version 2 yet; pi-durable 1.4.0 writes version 2, so the upgraded store opens in the released Pi. Copies earlier versions already wrote stay where they are and can be deleted. `driver.OpenHarness` and `node.OpenNodeSqliteStorage` write no extra file. Divergence D188 is retired.
- Updated Go module dependencies: `github.com/Microsoft/go-winio` 0.6.4, `go.yaml.in/yaml/v3` 3.0.5 and `golang.org/x/sys` 0.49.0.
- The security page states what a Piglet Binary guarantees (fused extensions, no overlay or ambient Resource selection, tool ceilings enforced in the tool registry, strips an overlay cannot undo, signed Binaries, the declared agent container), what it does not guarantee (a Binary still loads `-e` extensions, runs the package commands and MCP configuration, and does not pin `PATH`; revocation is local; builds are not locked), what needs the planned Piglet Image, and how each enterprise control maps to a Piglet setting. It no longer says a Piglet is not a security boundary, and it states that session files and `trust.json` are created with mode 0644. `.github/SECURITY.md` links to it and no longer says that no version is supported.
- The site and the agent docs bundle now share one source for their common pages. `automation/gen/gen-docs-bundle.py` copies 15 site pages (`json`, `llama-cpp`, `rpc`, `rpc-commands`, `rpc-extension-ui`, `session-format`, `usage`, `cli-integration`, `message-types`, `virtual-models`, `publishing`, `codemode`, `mcp`, `security`, `compaction`) and `how-pig-works` into the bundle, with bundle-local links, and `make generate` and `make docs-drift` keep them current. `internal/pigdocs/bundle-manifest.json` lists every bundle page and who owns it. A test fails when a generated page is edited by hand.
- New site and bundle pages: a glossary generated from `docs/project/CONTEXT.md`, a project trust page with a comparison to Pi, and a Piglet lifecycle page (author to update, with the Overlay Piglet and the tool scope). The site quickstart has a "Choose how to customize PiG" table that the bundle's `extend-pig.md` shares. Links to Pi's repository files now point at `blob/main`, as Pi's own docs do; a test rejects a tag link.
- The docs bundle README now has a "Start by task" row for each of the 12 pages that had none (compaction, config, divergences, extension-api, message-types, models, rpc-commands, rpc-extension-ui, runtime-cells, skills, terminal-setup, trust), and the docs-drift reachability test requires such a row for every page. `models.md` now opens with how to choose a connection, as Pi's models page does, and its "Adding a model" section is now "Add a custom provider" with the contributor steps under it. `tui.md` now has a "Choose an integration point" table that links the extension UI calls.
- The docs bundle has a new page, `piglet-strip.md`, that explains how `tools` limits a Piglet, what the `strip` lists remove, and how to inspect the active Piglet. The README starts with four PiG-specific task rows and a hint to search `divergences.md` with `grep -n -i`. The README now puts the install and bundle details after the task table.
- The bundle pages `tui.md`, `sdk.md`, `themes.md`, and `custom-provider.md` link to bundle pages as `<page>.md`, and a drift test rejects root-absolute links in the bundle.
- The Additive features table in `divergences.md` is generated from `docs/additive-features.md` (`make additive-list`, part of `make generate`) and lists all additive records, each with a one-sentence `Summary:` line from the ledger. `knowledge-graph.md` has rows for the slot, strip list, and overlay Piglet, and it no longer names paths that exist only in a source checkout.
- The docs bundle has a new page, `extend-pig.md`, that ranks the ways to change PiG (settings, skills, extensions, Packages, Piglets, Binaries, source) with where files go and how to verify each one. The README leads with it. `additive-features.md` is a new generated page that lists the additive records written for authors, chosen by an `Audience:` line in `docs/additive-features.md`.
- The `skills.md` page names the real skill paths (`~/.pig/agent/skills/` and `~/.agents/skills/`), `themes.md` has the theme file format and the 51 required color roles, and `extensions.md` states which files load and that `--lang lisp` exists. `README.md`, `settings.md`, `extensions.md`, `skills.md`, and `piglet-strip.md` start with a short "Differs from Pi" box.
- The `piglets.md` overlay section now says that a name in `extends.remove` must exist in the Binary, how to test an overlay (`./pig-base --piglet <overlay>`), and that `docs` is a `strip.features` ID. `skills.md` says a skill needs a `description`, and `themes.md` says an unknown color name makes a theme invalid.
- The Piglets topic in the system prompt, shown only while a Piglet is active, now also names `docs/piglet-strip.md`. The prompt without a Piglet is unchanged.
- Durable's and Chord's watches, observers and reports share one vocabulary, as in Pi (`5f312dac`). A watch listener gets a tagged `WatchCall`: `WatchCallValue` (the value, its ops, `Retired`) or `WatchCallFailed` (the error of a failure the source recovers from; the watch stays open and the next value arrives as `[["r", value]]`). `WatchEnd`, `SessionEnd` and `ReportFrom` carry their tag in `Kind`, an aborted context ends a watch `aborted` (was `cancelled`), and `Observer.End` takes a `WatchEnd`. `HarnessOptions.OnReport` gets one `Report` (`Kind`, `Error`, and the fields of its `ReportInfo`); the report about a failed Session is `storage_failed` (was `session_failed`), and a `task_outdated` report uses the scheduler's reasons (`missing_task`, `task_too_old`, `migration_failed`; `incompatible_task` is gone). `Session.SubscribeCommits` is `ObserveCommits` and takes a `CommitObserver` that is told when the Session ends; `FileChange` has a `FileChangeFailed` variant (was `FileChangeError`) and a `FileWatcher` is stopped with `Stop` (was `Close`). A committed document retirement is a `DocumentRetireChange`, and `TaskInspection` calls a task the next scheduling pass reserves `pending` (was `ready`). Go callers of these names must change; the old names are removed.
- The Durable core's microtask schedule follows Pi 1.4.0 (6c384aa3): `Conversation.submit` returns two hops later (the span of `pi.durable.submit`), a task phase's decision commit continues three hops later (the span of `pi.durable.phase`), `runtime.commit` returns one hop later, `Harness.waitForIdle`, `Conversation.waitForIdle` and `Harness.waitForTask` return as Pi's async methods do, and a host-driven commit is published when Storage adopts it. <!-- fix: 228dbea36a -->
- The Durable core holds about a quarter less memory for a large task graph: U-harness-scheduler-retention's 20,000-task chain now fits a TinyGo heap of 80 MiB (it needed about 102 MiB, and ran out of memory at the 96 MiB the core is built with). A queued scheduler step or reconcile pass, an invocation and a run are each one smaller allocation, tasks a host creates keep the objects its operation parsed and share equal checkpoints and outcomes, and the encoder lets go of each statement's parameters as it writes it.
- The Durable core follows pi-durable 1.4's `Storage.commit(writes, adopt, context)`: a Storage adopts a durable batch by calling `adopt(seq)` once, synchronously, before it resolves, and the core applies and publishes the commit inside that call. `subscribeCommits()` listeners run one microtask after the adoption, and a task run is signalled to abort after them. A commit the Storage rejects after adopting it stays published and counted, and then fails the Session; a call that rejects before adopting discards what was staged, and one that resolves without adopting fails the Session. Observers of the Session that throw fail it once the Storage returned. The core's own storage adapters (memory, SQLite, JSONL-over-SQLite) and the storage conformance provider adopt the same way.
- `durable/core/driver` opens a Harness with `HarnessOptions.ReadOnly` instead of refusing it with `driver.ErrUnsupported` (removed): over the core, open loads live tasks as committed (a `running` one stays running), a commit with writes fails with `*durable.ReadOnlySession` before it reaches the store and the Session stays healthy, `Resume()` panics with it, and every call that enables scheduling returns it, as on the Go Harness. The TypeScript host takes `readOnly` in its open options and exports `ReadOnlySession`.
- The Durable core group-commits like Pi `e5c6182b`: a Session no longer holds its line while Storage stores a commit. Commits that arrive while one call is in flight go out together in the next call, one seq per part, and outcomes and publications are delivered in line order, one commit per macrotask. `Storage.commit` in the core's hosts takes batches and a receive callback; a Storage that has no `publishing` scope is called as before. Direct Storage commits keep one core session.
- A task cut off `settings.restartLimit` times in a row ends instead of parking: a tool call ends with an error result (diagnostic code `restart_limit`) and its task fails with detail `{reason: "restart_limit"}`, a compaction fails into `pi.live.compactionFailure`, a generation ends its run with `pi.live.runFailure` reason `restart_limit` (its inputs settle `unanswered` with that reason), and a task of an extension's kind ends `faulted` with detail `{reason: "restart_limit"}`, reported as `task_faulted` with reason `restart_limit`. The built-in tasks are reported as `task_interrupted`. The Durable core's scheduler faults extension tasks at the limit; it does not emit `task_interrupted` from a generic commit hook, the built-in tasks' terminal commits report it.
- A generation whose model request was in flight when the host died no longer resends it on open: the attempt counts as failed under `settings.retry`. Its partial becomes an aborted entry, as before; the next attempt waits for the backoff, shown in `pi.live.generation.retry`, and with no retry left the run ends with `pi.live.runFailure` reason `interrupted` and the inputs settle `unanswered` with that reason. A deferred poll whose fetch was in flight is charged the same way, and its next attempt polls the same deferred response again instead of submitting a new request; a run that ends instead cancels it. A close still resends.
- `afterTool` runs on every result a tool task writes, not only on an executed call's, as in Pi (`87eff524`): also on the error results the Harness writes itself, for a tool that does not resolve (`tool_unavailable`), invalid arguments (`invalid_arguments`, with `call.Arguments` as the model sent them), a block (`blocked`), an interruption (`interrupted`), the restart limit (`restart_limit`), and an abort (`aborted`, `abandoned`); the diagnostic code tells them apart. Such a result is bounded with the tool's output limits after the hooks, never keeps a `StructuredOutput`, and applies `Control` only when the call completes; a nested call a hook turns into a success gets its bounded output as value unless the tool declares a schema. Once a tool task was cut off more than `settings.restartLimit` times the hooks no longer run, nor in the last attempt the scheduler gives an abort handler. On an abort the hooks run inside the abort handler, so a slow hook delays `Abort()`. A slot's truncation diagnostic of an interrupted, cut-off, or aborted call is now listed after the call's own diagnostic, and stays only while the hooks keep the output.
- A call to a tool its request did not offer gets a `pi.tool` task like any call (Pi `1c6928b3`), flagged `Unoffered: true` in its input and its `pi.live.tools` slot, instead of a result the generation wrote without one: the task resolves nothing (a deferred tool the agent has still never runs), settles `tool_unavailable`, and runs `afterTool`, whose `Control` then counts toward the round (one such call no longer prevents `terminate`). Its slot starts `pending` with a `TaskId` instead of `done`, and its result entry lands in a later commit than the tool-calling answer. A round applies controls in call order, and an aborted sequential round answers its unstarted unoffered calls `tool_unavailable` instead of `aborted`.
- `durable.ReadAfterWrite` names the whole operation: `NewReadAfterWrite(operation)` takes `"Tx.task()"` (or `"submit(tx, draft)"`), the field `Method` is now `Operation`, and the message is `<operation> cannot read tables after the first table write` (unchanged for table reads). `Tx.SettleSubmission` on a record that is not placed fails with `Submission N is not a placed input or continue`.
- The Durable core and its host protocol follow the Pi features of `87eff524..e7a0df27`: continue submissions and `whenIdle: "reject"` (`ConversationIdle`), a submission admitted inside a host transaction (the transaction operation `submit`, refused after the transaction's first table write with `ReadAfterWrite`), the per-conversation turn limit (`maxTurns` in the resolved agent, run failure `turn_limit`), a run whose context has nothing to answer (`nothing_to_answer`, decided from the new `owes` field of the context summary), the `afterRun` hook and the run-end tasks it asks for (the host checks the requested tasks and answers `{tasks, rejected}`; several rejections report an `AggregateError` with its `errors`), `afterTool` on every tool task result including calls to tools not offered (their own flagged tool task), and entry reads for hooks and tasks. `host/PROTOCOL.md` section "Pi 7e15f960..e7a0df27 additions" is the contract.
- The conformance corpus runs rows E32 to E34 and the upstream Durable harness test rows against the candidates; their golden traces are recorded (`durable/contract/traces`). A commit listener receives its caller's own `Context`.
- A program that embeds PiG is smaller again (`examples/headless` on linux/amd64: 37.13 MB to 36.89 MB with a plain build, 30.59 MB to 30.44 MB with the strip tags). The model catalog's maps (headers, thinking levels, prompt cache) are built from pairs the linker lays out instead of a store for each model, `internal/minimatch` has the one memory-bounded brace expansion that matches Pi's brace-expansion 5.0.12, and it serves every caller of `minimatch.Match` (`coding/packagecontent` keeps only its separate port of Node's bundled copy, which Node's glob uses), the key, theme and keybinding tables that were built by code are data, and the Codex zstd encoder and the Mermaid Markdown parser are built on first use without being referenced by package initialization. Lower- and upper-casing in `tui`, `internal/codingagent` and `internal/nodespawn` use `internal/jsstring` (JavaScript's `toLowerCase` and `toUpperCase`) instead of `golang.org/x/text/cases`, which is no longer linked; the two agree on every code point and on the Final_Sigma contexts of ordinary text, and `jsstring` is the one that matches JavaScript where they differ: `cases` stops looking for a following letter after 30 case-ignorable characters, so `"ΑΣ"` plus 31 combining marks plus `"Β"` lowers to a final `ς` there and to `σ` in `jsstring` and Node; an ill-formed UTF-8 byte becomes U+FFFD in `jsstring` and passes through `cases`; a lone surrogate is kept by `jsstring` (see Fixed), as in JavaScript.
- A program that embeds PiG without a terminal is 7.1 MB smaller (47.2 MB to 40.1 MB for `examples/headless` on linux/amd64): the terminal editor, the word-segmentation dictionaries behind it (6.3 MB) and the interactive mode's announcement image (0.5 MB) are no longer linked into a program that never draws an editor. The `pig` command links them as before; its size is unchanged within one page (69,812,384 to 69,816,480 bytes on linux/amd64).
- A program that embeds PiG without the `pig` command no longer links the test-only `test-faux` provider and its scenario classifier. `examples/headless` on linux/arm64, stripped as released, is 131,072 bytes smaller (28,180,640 to 28,049,568).
- `docs/terminal-setup.md` now names the source of Pigpen's herdr extension as `pig`, as it reports it, not `custom:pig` (#136).
- `ParseDate` and `Context.ParseDate` in the Go SDK, `parse_date` and `Context::parse_date` in Rust, and `parse_date` and `ctx.parse_date` in Python answer text in the form `Date.prototype.toISOString` writes for a four-digit year (`2026-10-24T18:30:15.042Z`, how Pi writes the timestamp of every session entry) in the SDK instead of asking the host, so `SessionEntryToContextMessages` and the branch-summary helpers make no host call for an entry from a session file. Every other text still goes to the host's parser, and the answers are the same.
- References are the only indirection (Pi `4b535d57`): a reference's members and keys attach straight to the object instance's own document or derive and move to a new instance with one frame, keeping their last values while the object is unbound; consumers of an older contract version read through the instance's shared mapping (`accepts`, `Provider.Accepts`). The member sources and keyed members of the host are removed.
- A route has no backoff timer (Pi slice 10 R2): a rejected `resolve`, or a link closed before its handshake, fails the address's holders `failed { waiting }` until a new hold, `RouteHandle.Retry` or a link that completed its handshake dropping.
- A `retry` over a link carries a hop budget (`hops`, 16 from the first host, one less per host) instead of an operation id and the objects it passed through (Pi audit A5); `parked_long` is reported for any long park, naming the first blocker and its state; registry cycles are caught when a registry composes, not when a contribution is made.
- `chord/output`: `SanitizeOutput` removes whole ANSI escape sequences, not only their control characters (Pi `50d9f823`, `output.ts`).
- `examples/headless` no longer links the Lisp image build, the Quicklisp resolver or the Lisp source resolver (about 78 KB on linux/amd64), so its default binary is back under its size ceilings on all four release platforms. The Go, Rust and Python cell staging of the extension host shares one code path with the same error messages.
- Durable scheduler decisions are decision regions: they read the scheduler's memory while recording the keys they read, and a decision that read what an earlier, still unpublished commit wrote waits for that commit's publication and runs again, so several commits overlap in storage while decisions stay serialized. Each commit writes the ownership memberships its task changes alter (`TaskScheduler.MembershipKeys`), chain loads stay pinned until their job's commit is published, and a tool slot's running status and arguments and a generation's attempt are stored like progress (a run with one tool call stores 12 commits instead of 14). Idle checks after a task change cover only the conversations above it, kept context ranges are advanced by the entries of published commits (no Storage read for the bounds), and idle ranges expire in the order they went idle (Pi `e5c6182b`, `35dfa757`).
- The interface ledger reads `StoreStorage`: its `publishing` capability and `entry` overloads are renamed as the other storages' are, `StoredEntry` is a reviewed type exception, and four modules of `durable/storage/store` that Pi's entry point does not export carry a `// pi:` marker with a mutant that makes their tests fail. <!-- fix: 015bed2a37 -->
- A watch listener that blocks on something the host cannot see (a channel, a lock, network I/O, a child process) calls `chord.DeliveryEntered()` first, or blocks on its own goroutine; until then it holds back the Harness waits and the Session's publications that follow its delivery (divergence D224).
- A Session now group commits: commits admitted while a storage call is in flight are stored as one `Storage.Commit` call, each with its own seq, and published in line order, one part per hop. A commit's callback can run while an earlier commit is being stored; at its first read of what an unpublished commit wrote it waits for that commit's publication. A commit returns once it is stored and published, and outcomes are delivered in line order. `Session.ReadOnLine` and `ReadWithTicket` take the job as `func(storage durable.Storage)`, which reads through a view that waits for what the line admitted before. Commit observers run at the commit's publication, not inside Storage's adopt.
- `Storage.Commit` stores a call's batches in order, each with its own seq, and stops at the first batch Durable's own checks refuse, keeping the batches before it. Memory, JSONL and SQLite storage implement it; a JSONL commit appends its batches' markers in one write, and JSONL reads wait while a commit is being appended.
- `oauth.clientRegistration` accepts `auto`, the new default. `auto` identifies with Pi's Client ID Metadata Document only when the application is named `pi`; PiG is not, so it keeps registering a client dynamically, as Pi does for rebranded builds. `cimd` still always uses the document, and now fails sign-in only when it was asked for explicitly. A client registered before stays in use under `auto`; `cimd` replaces it.
- The default system prompt is tighter: a shorter preamble, "Additional tools may be available.", a shorter skills hint, a docs section that says "the harness itself" and ends with one instruction to read the relevant docs in full before implementing harness changes, and two shorter `edit` guidelines. The same skills hint is used by the Go, Rust, Python and Lisp extension SDKs.
- Switching the model registry, registering a provider whose models an extension wrote, and listing models for `/model` allocate far less when extensions registered models. An extension model's catalog record (Pi's spread of the definition) was encoded again for every model each time the registry rebuilt its entries; it is now encoded once per registration. Matching a model pattern no longer lowercases every model id and name per query, and the compaction and branch-summary cost rows no longer take big-number arithmetic for an exact tie such as 0.125.
- A Chord link that holds many state subscriptions behind a full flow-control window sends them in O(n) when the peer acknowledges, as Pi does: releasing 10000 waiting subscriptions took 482 ms and 797 MiB of allocation, now 3.7 ms and 1.3 MiB. Ending a hold while subscriptions wait no longer allocates.
- `EstimateTokens` and `FindCutPoint` in the Go, Rust and Python SDKs count the UTF-16 length of ASCII text without visiting each character: a 1 KiB ASCII string takes about a third of the time in Go, a twentieth in Rust and a seventh in Python, and `EstimateTokens` over the messages of a 10k-entry branch of ASCII text takes about half as long. The counts are unchanged, and text with other characters takes the time it did.
- While a Piglet is active, the "When asked about" list in the system prompt names the Piglet documentation (`docs/piglets.md`). Without a Piglet the docs section is unchanged.
- A Binary built with 0.7.0 accepts `--piglet`, `PIG_PIGLET_PATH`, `PIG_PIGLET_NAME`, `--system-prompt` and ambient discovery by default, where a 0.5.3 Binary refused them. Set `build.closed: true` in the Piglet you build to keep the 0.5.3 behavior; a closed Binary also refuses `-e`, the package commands, `pig mcp add`, `settings.extensions` and `mcp.json` servers.
- `chord.Watch` queues frames while its listener is busy or not started and delivers one call with the newest value, the folded ops (or a root replacement after an overflow) and the newest frame's context, instead of one call per frame with a 100-frame collapse. `chord.NewWatch` no longer takes a `replace` function; `chord.NativeWatch` still delivers every value in order and takes the optional `replace`. Durable's event stream keeps every event batch in order; document, view and task-graph watches fold.
- Partial answers and running tool output are stored later than they are shown: their throttled commits are deferred, so watches, views and agent events see each at once, while Storage gets them together with the next commit that reads `pi.live` (the end of the answer, a tool settling, a run ending) and at the latest after `PersistWithinMs`. A crash now loses up to about a second of streamed content instead of 100 ms; a stream that crashes before its first store leaves no aborted entry, and that attempt's usage is not recorded. <!-- fix: 60a2b8b4fe -->
- The Session's own observers (`ObserveCommits`, used by document watches, the conversation view, agent events, the task graph and the scheduler) take a `session.ObservedCommit`, which also reports a commit held in memory; a document watch follows memory, so it holds an observer, not a `SubscribeCommits` subscription.
- The core host stores every commit before it returns: it accepts `CommitOptions` and treats a deferred commit as immediate.
- Partial messages no longer carry the provider's stream state: a tool call holds no `partialJson`, `partialArgs`, `customInput` or `streamIndex`, and an open Anthropic or Bedrock block holds no `index`; the providers, the proxy stream and the faux provider keep that state beside the block. The grammar tool input functions take a delta (`appendGrammarToolInputJSONDelta`) and a complete input (`closeGrammarToolInputJSON`).
- A pi-messages `done` or `error` event that carries `responseModel` sets it on the assistant message, so a virtual model reports the physical model behind it.
- A custom `SqliteExecutor` or `SqliteDatabase` implementation must add `RunCounted`.
- The default model of the `openai` provider is `gpt-6.1-sol` (it was `gpt-5.5`), as for `openai-codex` and `github-copilot`: it is the model selected after `/login` when no model is set, the startup fallback, and the default for `--provider openai`.
- `chord/nextnode/plugins`: a plugin input the build cannot read is reported at the import that names it (`worker.ts:1:19: EACCES: permission denied, open '<path>'`), where Pi prints the line of esbuild's own library; the difference is numbered D222.
- Track parity interface snapshots only for the active Pi pin and reviewed delta baseline. Pin synchronization updates their ignore rules, and `make pin-check` rejects obsolete tracked snapshots.
- Node extensions import `@earendil-works/pi-ai` through the extension view, as in Pi: pi-ai's compat entry plus TypeBox's `Type` and a TypeBox-built `StringEnum`. pi-ai's own entry no longer re-exports `Type`, so the shim adds it explicitly; extensions that import `Type`, `Static` or `TSchema` from `@earendil-works/pi-ai` keep working.
- The built-in durable tools `read`, `write`, `edit`, `bash` and `powershell` declare their parameters in the member order of pi-schema's builders (`type`, `properties`, `required`, objects open) instead of TypeBox's (`type`, `required`, `properties`), as Pi does since 6536f801; the read tool's structured output schema names the image block's `type` as a bare `{"const":"image"}`.
- A tool's `structuredOutput` is checked against its `structuredOutputSchema` with the schema package (the standard formats; a `$ref` that names nothing rejects the value) instead of the TypeBox checker, so an `invalid_structured_output` report words the failure as the schema package does, for example `count: expected number, got string`, and a property name is a name, not a pattern.
- The `schema` builders take options typed by builder: `schema.Str(schema.MinItems(1))` or `schema.Num(schema.Open())` no longer compile, and `schema.Obj` writes `properties` and `required` in JavaScript's own-key order (array-index names first), as Pi's `obj()` does.
- Tool arguments are validated as JSON Schema by pi-schema, as Pi does: every tool schema, whether built in, from an extension or from an MCP server, gets the same coercion (`"42"` for a number, `null` for a required string is `"null"`, `"3.5"` for an integer is 3, one value for an array is wrapped) and the same error text (`- limit: expected number, got string`, `- path: missing`, then the arguments received). Features of TypeBox outside JSON Schema no longer apply: `Type.Refine()` refinements are not run, a `BigInt` or `Undefined` schema rejects every JSON argument, a property name is a name rather than a regular expression, and `additionalProperties` converts only undeclared properties. A `$ref` that names nothing (a dangling definition in an MCP server's schema) rejects only the arguments at its place instead of failing every call of the tool.
- 0.7.0 no longer runs `Type.Refine()` callbacks on a tool's arguments (changed from 0.6.x, matching Pi 1.5.0, which validates tool arguments as plain JSON Schema): arguments a refinement would reject are accepted, so check such constraints in the tool's `execute()` (its handler). Go, Rust, Python and Lisp keep `Refine` as a schema constructor whose callback no API runs (D226). The Go, Rust, Python, Lisp and Node extension runtimes no longer declare a tool's refinements or answer the host's `tool_refine_arguments` request, which no longer exists. `Type.Refine` and `Type.IsRefine` stay as schema constructors in the Go, Rust and Python SDKs (Lisp `type-refine`), and the schema's JSON is unchanged.
- The generated `schemas/models.schema.json` lists the `required` properties of every object of the pi-ai compat and model schemas (`ModelCost` and its tiers, `ProviderCompat`, the routing and fallback-model objects) after its `properties`, as Pi's pi-schema-built schemas do. Editors and validators read the same schema; only the key order of the file changes.
- A program that embeds the coding library without loading an extension SDK no longer links the TypeBox type engine, the codemode sandbox (its QuickJS wasm module and wazero) or the tool-search index. `examples/headless` is 0.8 MB smaller than it would be with the SDK export batch. The host answers the `type.engine` call of the Go, Rust and Python SDKs with an engine that the program registers (`coding/extension/pigsdk`, which the `pig` command links, registers it), and the compiled-in extensions that `createCodemodeExtension` and `createToolSearchExtension` name are registered by `coding/extension/builtin`; a program that links neither answers such a reference as a build that strips the extension does: `the compiled-in extension "codemode" is not in this build`.
- The `pig` binary is 1.4 MB smaller. The Go, Rust and Python SDK sources that it embeds to stage for extension builds are stored gzipped when a file is 32 KiB or more (23 files, as the Rust and Python unicode tables already were); staging writes the same files back. `BundledFiles()` of the three bundles names such a file `.gz/<name>.gz`; `embed-bundle -gzip-over` writes the compressed copy under the bundle's `.gz` directory, which a walk of the SDK source tree skips as hidden.
- A program that embeds PiG and starts extensions no longer links `go/types` and the SDK upgrade rules: the host reached them through `extensions/sdk/upgrade` only to classify a failed extension build, and the `pig` command now installs that classification (`examples/headless` on linux/amd64: 40,190,112 to 39,809,184 bytes). The `pig` command links them as before.
- The Python and Rust SDK bundles in the `pig` binary carry their unicode property tables gzipped (`_tables.py.gz`, `tables.rs.gz`, an eighth of the 375 KB of text) and staging writes the files back: the stock binary is 323,584 bytes smaller (69,705,888 on linux/amd64) and the staged SDKs hold the same files as before.
- The embedded Node runtime archive no longer carries any README.md outside `shims/pi-dist` (the package READMEs of undici, quickjs-wasi, semver, minimatch, lru-cache, chalk and others, and nested ones such as undici's `types/README.md`), which no code opens: `runtime-node.pack` shrinks from 4,719,013 to 4,649,723 bytes, under the 4,700,000-byte budget, which is unchanged. Pi's own READMEs under `shims/pi-dist` stay.
- Fullscreen mode writes far less to the terminal while an answer streams. When the transcript grows or scrolls, PiG now moves the rows that only moved with a terminal scroll region and draws only the rows that changed, where Pi draws every changed row (D205). A 20,000-character answer in a 160x48 tmux pane takes 544 KB instead of 3,578 KB, and tmux's CPU for it falls by about three quarters. The screen is the same. Set `PIG_TUI_SCROLL_ROWS=0` to draw every changed row, as Pi does. A terminal with no scroll regions (`TERM` unset, `dumb`, `unknown`, `vt52`) or Zellij gets Pi's bytes.
- A component's `render` in the Go, Rust and Python `TuiAltScreen` may call its screen and change it: the host runs each such call at once on the goroutine that draws the frame, while it holds the frame lock, so a change applies immediately and a later read in the same render sees it, as in Pi. A child a render adds is rendered by the frame in progress. `render`, `renderNow`, `start`, `stop`, `copyActiveSelectionToClipboard` and `queryTerminalColors` called from inside a render return the error `tui.alt: <op> cannot run while a component renders` where Pi recurses (D208). `children` is a copy of Pi's live array: read it again after `addChild`, `removeChild` or `clear` (D207). The Go SDK takes pointer components only and rejects any other value with an error at the call that receives it, because Pi compares components by reference. <!-- feat: 1d917fc889 -->
- Development: the fullscreen renderer's unit-test harness reads the screen a frame leaves by replaying the frame's bytes through a terminal model that scrolls regions, not by reading the row addresses it wrote. In a terminal where PiG scrolls moved rows (`TERM` set, as on a developer's Mac), `TestAltScreenKeyboardNavigationHasFourRowsOfPageOverlap` read the rows a scroll had moved as unchanged and failed on every run, though a Kitty key release never scrolled the viewport; the tests now run in both modes and a Kitty press and release stream split at every byte reaches the viewport as one page scroll.
- Development: the fullscreen renderer's unit-test harness reads the screen a frame leaves by replaying the frame's bytes through a terminal model that scrolls regions, not by reading the row addresses it wrote. In a terminal where PiG scrolls moved rows (`TERM` set, as on a developer's Mac), `TestAltScreenKeyboardNavigationHasFourRowsOfPageOverlap` read the rows a scroll had moved as unchanged and failed on every run, though a Kitty key release never scrolled the viewport; the tests now run in both modes and a Kitty press and release stream split at every byte reaches the viewport as one page scroll.

### Removed

- `Description`'s unexported order lists and `Contract.decoded`: a decoded schema keeps its order itself.
- `contracts.CheckBytes` and the `data.Validator.Type` accessor: a bytes leaf is plain data checked by the validator.
- The Go, Rust and Python SDKs no longer fail a tool's registration for a `Type.Refine` refinement under a schema keyword the host did not traverse, and a child session's custom tools may carry refinements. The `validation_parameters` member of a tool declaration, which carried TypeBox's `~kind` form of the schema for the old validator, is gone with the validator that read it; the Python `refinement_sites` and Rust `RefinementSite` and `TSchema::refinement_sites`, `refinement_count` and `to_validation_value` are removed.

### Added

- Anthropic requests with a session id (and cache retention not `none`) use message threads (`message-threads-2026-08-12` beta), as in Pi: the server continues from the previous reply and PiG sends only the new messages. When anything earlier in the request changed, or the server can't continue the thread, the full request is sent. On by default only for the `anthropic` provider on `api.anthropic.com`; set `compat.supportsMessageThreads` in `models.json` to change that, for example for gateways that forward the `thread` field. `ai.CleanupSessionResources` frees a session's thread state. Cache warming does not touch the session's thread.
- Go API `ai`: `StreamOptions.DisableContinuation` keeps a request from using or replacing server-side continuation state such as Anthropic message threads. Set it on requests that repeat an earlier one, such as cache warming.

### Fixed

- PageUp and PageDown (`tui.select.pageUp` and `tui.select.pageDown`) move the selection by one page in the select list, settings list, editor autocomplete, and the model, OAuth, scoped-models, user-message and settings-submenu selectors. A focused component that handles these keys now receives them in fullscreen mode instead of the transcript scrolling, as in Pi. <!-- fix: 69cd9d29e6 -->
- The regular-mode renderer no longer writes OSC 133 prompt markers to the terminal. Terminals that show program status read them as a new shell prompt and dropped the working indicator during runs. Fullscreen mode still uses them for prompt navigation. <!-- fix: c60a7b14aa -->
- Bare URLs in Markdown now stop at CJK punctuation such as `，` and `。`, so Chinese, Japanese and Korean text after a URL is no longer part of the link. Explicit `[text](url)` links and `<url>` autolinks keep these characters. <!-- fix: c60a7b14aa -->
- The session selector, the `/llama` search and the `/mcp` menus move their selection on `tui.select.pageUp` and `tui.select.pageDown`, and a page key bound to Ctrl+V pages an open autocomplete menu instead of pasting an image. In fullscreen mode a focused list that handles those keys receives them instead of the transcript. <!-- fix: f2431b9153 -->
- Tool output and streamed shell output no longer keep the parameters of private-parameter CSI sequences such as the SGR mouse report `ESC[<35;59;1M`, which left `35;59;1M` in the text. A private prefix (`<`, `=`, `>`) counts only directly after `ESC [` or the 8-bit CSI, so the keypad-mode sequences `ESC =` and `ESC >` still keep the digits that follow them (Pi #11377). <!-- fix: 4706781900 -->
- A package whose `pi` object holds only metadata such as `changelogPath` is loaded by directory auto-discovery instead of loading no resources. <!-- fix: 4706781900 -->
- With `codemode.mode: "on"`, the description of a tool whose output schema is a union of objects lists each variant's field names (a `const` field shows its value, for example `{ action: "start", process } | { action: "list", processes }`), and any other multi-line output type says `a value; `await describeTool("name")` shows its type` instead of inlining the whole type into every request (Pi #11501). <!-- fix: 4706781900 -->
- Starting `pig` from a directory that has been deleted, including `pig --version` and `pig --help`, prints `Error: The current working directory no longer exists. Change to an existing directory and try again.` and exits 1 (Pi #11509). <!-- fix: 4706781900 -->
- Resizing an image that does not fit its limits now sends the smaller of the PNG and the JPEG at the configured quality, and tries lower JPEG qualities only when neither fits. Photos used to go out as multi-megabyte PNGs whenever the PNG fitted, which made requests large enough to fail or time out (Pi #11551). <!-- fix: 4706781900 -->
- `pig update` warns when an npm package update leaves the installed version unchanged, for example `npm:demo-pkg is still 1.0.0 (registry reports 1.0.1); npm registry metadata may be stale, try again in a few minutes`, instead of reporting success for an update that installed nothing. The package commands print these warnings in yellow (Pi #11536). <!-- fix: 4706781900 -->
- Compaction and branch summaries in a session created by `CreateAgentSession` now let the session's own stream resolve auth, as prompts do, instead of passing a pre-resolved OAuth access token on as an explicit API key. A provider whose API-key path differs from its OAuth path no longer fails every summary while normal prompts work (Pi #11520). <!-- fix: 4706781900 -->
- Setting the same active tools again in a different order, as `pi.setActiveTools([...pi.getActiveTools()].reverse())` does, keeps the order of the tools that stay active and appends new ones, so the system prompt no longer records a `System Prompt Update: tools, rules` message and no longer loses the prompt cache (Pi #11495). <!-- fix: 4706781900 -->
- When a shared extension cell fails to build or start, each member that then runs in its own process shows `packed cell failed:` and the error that ended the shared cell in `/reload --explain`. A retry that succeeded used to hide why the members were not shared. <!-- fix: bb70e6b139 -->
- An extension build that began after its deadline or cancellation no longer fails with `wait for cell build lock: context deadline exceeded` while no lock was held. The error now says the context had ended before the build began. <!-- fix: bb70e6b139 -->
- The faux provider (`ai.NewFauxProvider`) no longer ends a streamed chunk inside a multibyte character. It cut a response at byte offsets where Pi slices a JavaScript string, so a text delta of non-ASCII text could end halfway through a character, and the partial arguments of a tool call that such a chunk extended were not valid text: every one of those chunks copied and checked all the arguments again. A tool call of 180 KB of mixed-width text allocated 3.2 GB and took 12.7 s (74 s under `-race`) before it ran; it now allocates 25 MB and takes 48 ms. A chunk is `tokenSize * 4` UTF-16 units, as in Pi's `splitStringByTokenSize`, and ends at the first character boundary at or after that size. <!-- fix: 38e6506b0e, b119c53026, 6b64bc1bee -->
- A streamed OpenRouter-style `reasoning_details` no longer costs more with every delta. Each delta merged into the entry list and then wrote the whole thinking signature again, so a reasoning stream of 10000 deltas took seconds and gigabytes (10000 discrete `reasoning.encrypted` entries: 94 s and 51 GB; 10000 merged text deltas: 5.5 s and 6.4 GB). The details now accumulate in memory and the signature is written once, when the thinking block ends or the stream fails, as in Pi; 10000 merged text deltas take 87 ms and 25 MB, and the signature is unchanged. <!-- fix: 7aab6c26e5 -->
- A tool call whose arguments hold a number out of float64 range (`1e999`, `-1e999`) no longer ends the session with a panic (`clone validated JSON value: json: unsupported value: +Inf`). Pi reads such a number as an infinity, keeps it in the call's arguments, and writes `null` wherever it serializes them (events, the session file, requests); PiG now does the same, for a streamed argument text, a tool call a Go caller or the faux provider supplies, and an Anthropic `content_block_start` input, which used to end the turn with a decode error. <!-- fix: 958e80d99f -->
- Anthropic non-strict tool schemas keep the root `$defs` and `definitions`, so property `$ref`s resolve. They were dropped, which left the `$ref`s pointing at nothing, made Claude produce wrong arguments for such tools (common in MCP servers), for example a JSON string instead of an object, and made some Anthropic-compatible gateways reject the request. Root `anyOf`, `oneOf` and `allOf` stay out, because Anthropic rejects them with a 400. Ports Pi's fix 4a6a58eb5 ([#9557](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9557)). <!-- fix: d3f6c2b6ff -->
- A context-overflow error from a LiteLLM proxy's pre-call check (`litellm.ContextWindowExceededError ... Context Window exceeded for given call`) is now recognised as context overflow, so compaction recovery runs instead of the turn failing (Pi #11492). <!-- fix: df5964b4e79776c08d758641a1f2f926f31acbdf -->
- A Zhipu/Z.ai usage-limit error (error code 1308, sent as HTTP 429) is no longer retried: the plan's limit resets after hours, not seconds (Pi #11537). <!-- fix: df5964b4e79776c08d758641a1f2f926f31acbdf -->
- The faux provider no longer counts newly cached prompt tokens as input as well as cache writes: with a session every prompt token is a cache read or a cache write. <!-- fix: 006a4963df -->
- `pig login <provider>` now prints what Pi's `packages/ai/src/cli.ts` prints and keeps `auth.json` private.
