It left a blank line after every authorization URL, listed a provider's select options as `1) label` and took the first option for an empty answer, and printed an unknown provider without the `Error:` prefix that every other login failure has. Pi asks `Enter number (1-N): ` for a select option, lists `1. label`, and fails an answer that is not a listed number with `Invalid selection`. An existing `auth.json` keeps the permissions an older version gave it while the new OAuth tokens are written into it; login now sets it to owner-only (`0600`) before it saves, as `cli.ts` does. <!-- fix: 85c4c8f1e4 -->
- The Anthropic workload-identity token exchange now reads `expires_in` with JavaScript's `Number()`, as the Anthropic SDK does. A response that sent the lifetime as a string such as `"0x10"`, `"0b11"` or `[5]` was rejected as missing required fields although `Number()` accepts it, and one such as `"1_0"` or `"0x1p3"` was accepted as a finite lifetime although `Number()` yields NaN and Pi rejects the response. <!-- fix: 1f2f94065d -->
- Text typed over an extension's autocomplete provider and followed at once by Enter no longer skips the menu Pi opens. With an extension that wraps the provider through `ctx.ui.addAutocompleteProvider` and answers without I/O, `/model provider/id` typed and entered in one go switched the model in PiG, where Pi accepts the suggestion into the editor on the first Enter and switches on the second (the same holds for `/thinking level`, any command with argument completions, and a command name). Pi awaits the whole wrapper chain in the Promise jobs after the terminal read, so a chain that needs no I/O has opened its menu before the next read, and a chain that awaits a timer, a socket or a process has not. PiG's chain is a round trip through the extension runtime that the next read overtook. The editor now starts the extension chain's request at the end of each read and the host holds the next read until the menu is published or the chain says it awaits real I/O; a provider that awaits a timer or a socket still lets the Enter submit at once, as in Pi, and a synchronous provider that blocks holds the read until it returns, as it holds Pi's loop. The Node runtime says so at the end of its macrotask (microtasks, `queueMicrotask` and `process.nextTick` stay inside Pi's checkpoint, a timer or `setImmediate` leaves it), including for a chain another extension of the same runtime calls (D213). Extension authors change nothing. <!-- fix: 8e3613da73c16a90a2952f1a20e7d0f1f59be346 -->
- On Linux and macOS, the bash tool, a `!` command and an extension's `exec` no longer report no output for a command that printed, when the machine is too busy to run PiG's pipe reader within 100 ms of the command's exit. PiG ended the wait for the output pipe after Pi's 100 ms post-exit grace even though the command had written its output before it exited and the reader had not yet taken it, so the output was lost; on a loaded machine `echo answer` came back as `(no output)`. PiG now asks the pipe itself when the grace elapses: a pipe that no process holds is read to its end, a pipe that holds output nobody has read yet keeps the wait going, and only a pipe that a background process still holds and that is quiet is released after the grace, as in Pi. <!-- fix: 224dbd923fb6b1c29713ca79314dd07505f5e777 -->
- `/tree` with summarization no longer sends an attempt that was hidden from the model back to the summarizer. When a partial assistant reply failed and automatic retry succeeded, the branch summary still contained the failed attempt, and a context edit that replaced an entry's content was ignored. The summary input now applies each entry's latest context edit through the projection the live context and compaction use: an omission drops the entry and a replacement swaps its content (Pi d0fe21308). <!-- fix: 4b9f5f800d -->
- The built-in `read` tool no longer resolves to `""` for an image in Code Mode scripts, so `image(await tools.read(...))` works: `read` declares a structured output, a text file's text or an image's block. Carried forward from Pi 04414839 (earendil-works/pi#11015), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: 04414839 -->
- `pig update` now warns when an npm package update leaves the installed version unchanged: shortly after a publish `npm view` can report the new version while `npm install` still resolves the old one, and `Updated packages` was printed with nothing updated. The warning names the package, the installed and the registry version, and is printed in yellow. Carried forward from Pi 0d23d534 (earendil-works/pi#11536), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: 0d23d534 -->
- The `env` daemon reports a watch `change` whose path list would not fit in a frame (16 MiB less 64 KiB) as an overflow event, which clients read as "rescan". An oversized list used to make the frame writer fail and end the daemon's only output writer, leaving every request hanging until the client's 30 s silence limit. Carried forward from Pi 102d1287 (earendil-works/pi#10516), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: 102d1287 -->
- The working status (OSC 7501) no longer disappears in Rex and iTerm2 during runs in regular TUI mode. Rendered messages wrote OSC 133 prompt markers to the terminal, which those terminals read as a new shell prompt; the regular-mode renderer now drops them as fullscreen mode already did. Carried forward from Pi 19ce8059 (earendil-works/pi#11519), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: 19ce8059 -->
- Windows paths are compared case-insensitively. `c:\Users\me` and `C:\Users\me` name one directory, but exact string comparison treated them as two: with a working directory and a home directory that differ only in casing, global skills loaded as project skills and every one was reported as a name collision, `~/.agents/skills` counted as a project resource that needs trust, saved trust decisions in `trust.json` were not found, `--continue` and resume by id hid sessions recorded under another casing of the working directory, and `pig remove` did not match a package configured under another casing. Resource, extension and skill path keys, source matching, local package identity, the session-import self-check and the worktree `AGENTS.md` shadowing now use one comparison key. Carried forward from Pi 1be312b4 (earendil-works/pi#10488), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: 1be312b4 -->
- The `--help` text and the `/resume` and `/import` descriptions now say which working directory a resumed session runs in (`--continue` the current directory, `--resume` and `--session` the session's own, `--fork` the current directory), and `/import` says it preserves the session ID and working directory. Carried forward from Pi 2a46c420 (earendil-works/pi#11532), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: 2a46c420 -->
- Wrapped text no longer starts the next line with a space when a styled word ends exactly at the wrap width, and strikethrough no longer runs into the right padding of a wrapped line: the wrap closes `\x1b[29m` at line end like underline and opens it again on the next line. The text-wrapping helpers in the Go, Rust, Python and Lisp extension SDKs wrap the same way. Carried forward from Pi 2ce9d527 (earendil-works/pi#10925), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: 2ce9d527 -->
- The model catalog no longer offers models.dev's realtime and image models as chat models: `gpt-realtime-2.1` (Azure and OpenAI), `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` and `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image` (Google and Google Vertex). Carried forward, as the row removal only, from Pi 2e0f175b (earendil-works/pi#11368), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: 2e0f175b -->
- A saved "Do not trust" decision is no longer ignored for a project without trust-requiring resources, for example a folder with only `AGENTS.md`. `pig` auto-trusted such a project whatever `trust.json` held, so `ctx.isProjectTrusted()` returned true and the package commands treated it as trusted. A saved decision now takes precedence, and auto-trust applies only when none is saved; `pig status` and `pig diagnose` report the saved decision too. Carried forward from Pi 31ade0e0 (earendil-works/pi#10947), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: 31ade0e0 -->
- The durable scheduler's per-commit work no longer grows with the number of conversations: after a commit it re-checks idleness only for the conversations above the tasks that became live or ended (a task whose chain is not loaded yet is settled when the chain loads), expires idle context ranges from an index ordered by `idleSince`, and `wake()` takes the earliest sleep from the sleeping tasks and scans the live tasks only while nothing runs. Before, every commit re-walked every conversation read in the last `contextRetentionMs`. A task run with 4,000 conversations keeping a context range took 3.2 ms and 8,800 allocations in the Harness, and about 4.2 ms in the core; it now costs what it does with 100. Carried forward from Pi 35dfa757, past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: 35dfa757 -->
- In fullscreen mode a focused selection list takes every viewport key, not only the page keys, so `Ctrl+Home` in a model, session or tree selector no longer scrolls the transcript behind it. The `/mcp` manager takes them while a menu list is shown, a searchable settings submenu pages with `PageUp` and `PageDown` instead of sending them to its search box, and the session selector in rename mode and the tree selector while a label is edited give the keys back to their input. The public `tui` names now follow Pi: `GetSelectPageIndex` replaces `PageSelectionIndex`, and `ViewportInputCapturer`, `CapturesViewportInput` replace `SelectPageInputCapturer`, `CapturesSelectPageInput`. Carried forward from Pi 3bae8527 (earendil-works/pi#7629), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: 3bae8527 -->
- OpenRouter's `~anthropic/claude-*-latest` aliases (`~anthropic/claude-fable-latest`, `-haiku-`, `-opus-` and `-sonnet-latest`) no longer lose Claude's earlier thinking after each tool call. They used the Chat Completions API, where the thinking signature was dropped and OpenRouter then ignored the unsigned thinking; they now use the Anthropic Messages API with adaptive thinking, like the versioned Claude models. Carried forward from Pi 44f6851b (earendil-works/pi#9534), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: 44f6851b -->
- Tool output bounded by `chord/output`, the durable core and the Cloudflare host now loses whole ANSI escape sequences (strings up to BEL or ST, CSI, short `ESC x` forms), not only their ESC bytes, which left `[31m` in transcripts; a sequence split across chunks goes too. Carried forward from Pi 50d9f823 (earendil-works/pi#11604), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: 50d9f823 -->
- Clipboard image paste, copy through `powershell.exe` and opening the browser for sign-in no longer fail silently on WSL when the working directory is deep: the helpers now start from `/`, because WSL cannot start Windows programs from a working directory whose `\\wsl.localhost\...` path exceeds MAX_PATH. The external editor keeps the working directory on purpose. An external editor that fails now says so (`Failed to launch external editor: <command>`, `External editor exited with code N; prompt unchanged`, or the signal name) in the status line, and inline in the extension editor dialog, instead of being redrawn over silently. Carried forward from Pi 6454d07e (earendil-works/pi#11592), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: 6454d07e -->
- Fullscreen mode no longer leaves the `Model scope: …` startup notice in the shell after exit; it shows in the header instead. Carried forward from Pi 7391dbb0 (earendil-works/pi#11508), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: 7391dbb0 -->
- `tool_search` and codemode `searchTools()` (the coding agent's and durable's) find tools by words in any script, not only ASCII letters and digits. The text is NFC-normalized and split into words with Unicode word segmentation (the ICU dictionaries split Chinese, Japanese, Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar text without spaces, such as `搜索记录`, into words), so `café` and `cafe\u0301` match and `Поиск документов`, `البحث عن الملفات` and `फ़ाइल खोजें` are searchable. This replaces PiG's earlier one-term-per-character matching of Chinese, Japanese and Korean (D173), and a Piglet Binary built without the word dictionaries (D92) keeps such a run as one term. Carried forward from Pi 79006f06 (earendil-works/pi#10816, #11037), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: 79006f06 -->
- `Shift+Enter` inserts a newline instead of queueing a follow-up in Apple Terminal setups that send `ESC` + Return. Where native Shift detection is available (Apple Terminal, native Windows), `ESC` + Return with Shift held is `Shift+Enter`; without Shift it stays `Alt+Enter`. Carried forward from Pi 86dc686c (earendil-works/pi#11559), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: 86dc686c -->
- Starting `pig` from a working directory that has been deleted now prints "Error: The current working directory no longer exists. Change to an existing directory and try again." and exits 1, where it printed `get cwd:` with the operating system error. Carried forward from Pi 88ffcdc7 (earendil-works/pi#11509), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: 88ffcdc7 -->
- A renderer that imported `keyText` or `keyHint` from its own copy of the extension package rendered hints without the key, because that copy did not see the host's keybindings. The hints on the render context and options read the host's keybindings. From Pi 9376c8d1 (earendil-works/pi#4748). <!-- fix: 9376c8d1 -->
- Tool output and `!` command output no longer show the parameters of control sequences with a `<`, `=` or `>` prefix as text, for example `35;59;1M` from a mouse report `ESC[<35;59;1M` or `0;276;0c` from a terminal reply `ESC[>0;276;0c`. Text after the keypad-mode sequences `ESC=` and `ESC>` is still kept. Carried forward from Pi b5fc6dc8 (earendil-works/pi#11377), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: b5fc6dc8 -->
- The `env` daemon kills the commands it started when it receives `SIGTERM`, `SIGINT` or `SIGHUP`, then exits with status 128 plus the signal. `Connection.Close()` sends `SIGTERM`, which used to end the daemon before its kill-all ran and left running commands, and the processes they started, behind as orphans. On Windows nothing changes: the daemon cannot catch `TerminateProcess`. Carried forward from Pi b6d5c2ec, past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: b6d5c2ec -->
- A redundant system prompt update (tools, rules) no longer follows an extension setting the same active tools in a different order, for example a reversed `pi.setActiveTools()` list. Tools that stay active keep their order and newly activated tools are appended. Carried forward from Pi b9e3eef6 (earendil-works/pi#11495), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: b9e3eef6 -->
- `pig mcp login -l` and `pig mcp logout -l` no longer fail with `Unknown option --local.`, as `pig mcp add` and `pig mcp remove` already accept `-l`; with `-l` they require the server to be a project server. Unknown options are reported as typed, and a mistyped server name gets a suggestion, for example `Did you mean "fixture"?`. Carried forward from Pi be15fe3c (a Pi commit without an issue number), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: be15fe3c -->
- `pig -e git:<repo>@<branch>` no longer stays on its first checkout. A temporary Git source with a ref is now fetched and reset to the ref on each start and `/reload`, as an unpinned source is; a commit-hash ref that is already checked out is not fetched. Offline mode and a failed refresh keep the cached checkout. Carried forward from Pi bec60c54 (earendil-works/pi#11375), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: bec60c54 -->
- `pi.exec()` no longer buffers a command's output without limit, which exhausted memory when a command printed too much. The default cap is 256 MiB, counted over stdout and stderr together; past the cap the command is terminated, a character the cap cuts is dropped whole, and the result has `truncated: true`, `killed: true` and a nonzero code. Carried forward from Pi c466a359 (earendil-works/pi#11360), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: c466a359 -->
- `pi.exec()` no longer waits forever for a command that ignores SIGTERM after a timeout, an abort or the output cap: the host sends SIGKILL 5 seconds later if the command has not exited, as Pi intended. Carried forward from Pi c466a359 (earendil-works/pi#11360), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: c466a359 -->
- A Zhipu/Z.ai usage limit (HTTP 429 with error code `1308`, which resets after hours) is no longer retried, in `ai.IsRetryableAssistantError`, the durable turn classifier and the Go, Rust, Python and Lisp extension SDKs. Carried forward from Pi c719d5b0 (earendil-works/pi#11537), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: c719d5b0 -->
- Durable's `tool_search` and Code Mode `searchTools()` rank like the coding agent's tool search: a query that is exactly a tool's name ranks it first, a tool matching more of the query's distinct terms ranks above one matching fewer, a query term in the name outweighs any number of mentions in the description, and a tool whose whole name is in the query gets a large bonus. `thread_read` with a limit of 1 no longer loads `queue_read`, and `peekaboo app` finds `mcp__peekaboo__app`. `searchTools()` also searches the namespace instructions, as a low-weight field that does not lower the scores of the namespace's tools. Carried forward from Pi c7372af4 (earendil-works/pi#11631), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: c7372af4 -->
- `tool_search` and codemode `searchTools()` no longer rank a tool below tools that only mention its name in their descriptions, for example `peekaboo app` ranking `mcp__peekaboo__app` 14th. A query word in a tool's name now scores more than any number of mentions in its description, a tool whose whole name is in the query gets a large bonus, and long server instructions no longer lower the scores of that server's tools. Carried forward from Pi cc44fa21 (earendil-works/pi#11331), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: cc44fa21 -->
- `pig -e npm:<pkg>` no longer stays on the version from the first download. On each start and `/reload`, `pig` now reinstalls an `-e` npm package without an exact version (as `name@latest`, or its configured range) when the registry has a newer matching version; offline mode and a failed refresh keep the cached copy. Carried forward from Pi cd6a8f7f (earendil-works/pi#11375), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: cd6a8f7f -->
- A LiteLLM pre-call context check (`litellm.ContextWindowExceededError: ... Context Window exceeded for given call`) is now recognised as a context overflow, so the turn compacts instead of failing, in `ai.IsContextOverflow`, the durable turn classifier and the Go, Rust, Python and Lisp extension SDKs. Carried forward from Pi d3398f82 (earendil-works/pi#11492), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: d3398f82 -->
- `tool_search` and codemode `searchTools()` rank a tool that matches more of the query's distinct terms, in any field (name, description and schema, namespace), above one that matches fewer, whatever their scores. The name weighting of the previous ranking change put `peekaboo__window` above `peekaboo__image` for `screenshot window` and `peekaboo__app` above `peekaboo__see` for `describe app`. A query that is exactly a tool's name still ranks that tool first. Carried forward from Pi e033f255 (earendil-works/pi#11331), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: e033f255 -->
- `pi update` no longer stops with `git clean -fdx failed with code 1` when a Git package has files that cannot be deleted, for example a native module another pi session still has open on Windows. pi now warns that files may be in use by another pi session, installs the dependencies anyway, and retries the clean on the next update. Carried forward from Pi e3da248e (earendil-works/pi#11648), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: e3da248e -->
- Resizing an image sends the smaller of the PNG and the JPEG at the configured quality instead of the PNG whenever it fit, so a photo that needs resizing no longer goes out as a multi-MB PNG that makes the request fail or time out. Screenshots where the PNG is smaller still go out as PNG, and the lower JPEG qualities are tried only when neither fits. Carried forward from Pi e7a0df27 (earendil-works/pi#11551), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: e7a0df27 -->
- Image components render inline in Orca terminals that advertise Kitty graphics (`TERM_PROGRAM=Orca` with `ORCA_IMAGE_PROTOCOL=kitty`) instead of falling back to text. Orca releases that do not advertise it keep the text fallback. Carried forward from Pi f09d01b8 (earendil-works/pi#9329), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: f09d01b8 -->
- Interactive startup lists skill diagnostics under `[Skill warnings]` instead of `[Skill conflicts]`; most of them are validation warnings for skills that still load, not name collisions. Carried forward from Pi f14813e9 (earendil-works/pi#11521), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: f14813e9 -->
- With `codemode.mode: "on"`, a tool whose output schema is a union of objects or any other multi-line type no longer puts its whole rendered output type, with its comments run together, into every request. The description now lists the field names of each variant of a union of objects (`{ action: "start", process } | { action: "list", processes, truncated? }`), shows the value of `const` fields, and points a longer type to `await describeTool("name")`. Carried forward from Pi f6ee9ce9 (earendil-works/pi#11501), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: f6ee9ce9 -->
- A bare URL in Markdown ends at CJK punctuation, so `https://example.com。后面的中文` links `https://example.com` and keeps the rest as text. The URL took the punctuation and the text after it into the link. Carried forward from Pi fa168515 (earendil-works/pi#10933), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: fa168515 -->
- Paths under a directory whose name merely starts with the home directory's (`/users/bob2/x` with home `/users/bob`) are no longer shown as `~2/x` in tool calls, the loaded-resource listing, the session selector and the tree selector; only a leading home directory, on a path-segment boundary, shortens to `~`. Carried forward from Pi 1be312b4 (earendil-works/pi#10488), past the 1.4.0+b3a29f11 pin. <!-- fix: 1be312b4 -->
- A Session that an extension creates with `createAgentSession`, or that `coding.CreateAgentSession` returns, now reports `entry_appended` to its listeners when an extension that its resource loader loaded calls `pi.appendEntry`, as Pi does. The event arrives before the event the extension was handling, and `ctx.sessionManager.appendCustomEntry` still writes the log without an event. The Session wrote the entry and told no listener. <!-- fix: 1c6b8643abd7fa82af8c817229656696350eb6a9 -->
- `pi.exec` with a `maxBuffer` could keep a child's stderr bytes ahead of its stdout bytes under heavy CPU load, though the child wrote stdout first and Node hands the two pipes to the cap in that order (about one run in two thousand with the host oversubscribed four times over). The reader of stderr decided whether to wait for stdout from two answers taken one after the other, and a stdout reader that took its bytes between them was seen by neither; it now asks the pipe first and the reader second. <!-- fix: 33efd9f93f -->
- Closing a Chord host no longer hangs when a hold arrives over a link that closes at the same time. A frame the link had handed to the host loop before it closed could run after Close took its last look at the host's objects and after the connection had released what it held, so it created an object nothing disposed or released, and Close waited for that object's resource open for good (seen as a 30 minute `chord/host` test timeout on Windows after a `ready_timeout` get). A connection now ignores frames once its link closed, as Pi's link delivers none. <!-- fix: 04ef0acc60ecb7cfc515bfbe2991a455471ab0df -->
- A description decoded from the wire is written back with every schema member in the order it was declared in, as Pi writes it, and `normalize` returns the input's members in their own order followed by the defaults in the schema's declared order; the top-level members of a decoded schema came out sorted and a normalized value's defaults in sorted order. <!-- fix: 4c032a0900 -->
- A Chord object whose factory reads a key of another object (`at(key)`) could fail to go live with `not_ready` ("app.exposer: not live yet") when that object failed and went live again, in memory, while the key's first pin still loaded from the store: the key was handed back before its pin on the new instance had landed, and the factory's derive read it with no value. In Pi a new pin whose load has finished when the old pin settles has landed by then; here the key is now handed back after the new pin has settled when its load has finished. A new pin whose load has not finished when the old pin settles is not waited for, as in Pi, where the consumer's get is then rejected with `not_ready` and `activation_failed`. In the few steps between a load's end and the key being marked loaded the two can differ either way: PiG fails where Pi succeeds, or succeeds where Pi fails. Seen once in a gate run, and 4 times in 5000 runs on 2 CPUs with 8 busy loops. <!-- fix: 4d2f44e5e269bec44a7e33ac14b0fa3c4dd2d091, b478485936430504d20b2c167683b20ff6ab3891, 83216dc40b69c539ec4f8d2bff84db70b06709fd -->
- Schema errors of a `ChordError` of code `invalid` list their members in the order the value arrived in, as Pi's do (the `additionalProperties`, `propertyNames` and `unevaluatedProperties` lists and the order of the errors); they came out in sorted key order. <!-- fix: 78093645cf -->
- A `ChordError` of code `invalid` from a failed args, result, state or input check carries TypeBox's whole error objects as `details` (keyword, schemaPath, instancePath, params and message), as Pi's does; it carried only instancePath and message. <!-- fix: 7f2c05b082 -->
- Schemas decoded from a wire description (a Node child's contracts, a hold token) keep their declared property order, so a failed args, result, state or input check lists its errors in that order as Pi does, and a description is written back in the declared order; they were sorted by name. <!-- fix: f6e46951d1 -->
- Append ops from the Chord delta tracker and `DiffRevisions` own their text, as under Pi, instead of holding a cut of the whole string they were taken from. A delta chain, watch backlog or replica built from appends to a growing text no longer keeps one copy of the text per commit alive (10,000 commits of 8-byte appends retained 430 MB for 80 KB of payload). <!-- fix: f715a15c101ca8a44d759bceeb7ec2a51024c81c -->
- A Chord HTTP connection kept after a host, relay or socket handler it was admitted by was removed and then restored between its upgrade's router check and its keep stayed open, though Pi ends it when the removal arrives. Every router delivered after the check now judges the connection, from the router the check read, so the removal ends it. A router delivered between the check's count and its read no longer ends a connection the router it read admits once that router's delivery is listed. <!-- fix: 59e2efb01257af6ef172706ce726914ec9f58428 -->
- A Chord HTTP socket's once-listener (the close hook an upgrade keeps its connection by) could run before it could remove itself: a close on another goroutine between its registration and the hand-back of its removal called a nil removal (a data race, seen once in 60 starved `-race` runs). It is now built whole before it is attached and fires at most once, as Node's `once` does. An upgrade whose router changed between its last check and its keep was also never ended when its host, relay or socket handler had left in that window (the peer's connection stayed open, seen as a 30 s wait in a soak); a revoke now ends only a connection whose upgrade checked before that revoke's router was delivered, and a connection kept after a later delivery is checked against the newest router, so a lagging revoke against an older router no longer ends a connection the newest one admits. <!-- fix: a967e743523370c29d74c9ff7a16249c059b2280, f75fc15cace1116e0f99db03f6ac9e3b8479c95d, cc090466aae29819a94852c1572e618f081f716b -->
- A Chord HTTP upgrade whose router check read a router that was composed but not yet delivered when the connection was kept could be ended by a delivery that was older than that router, which Pi never does. Routers now carry the order of their composition, and a connection is judged only by the routers composed after the one its check read, whether or not that one is ever delivered; a router composed later than the check still ends it. <!-- fix: 57347b2237078b3b0c0efe80bd92f3d62ca2f6c1 -->
- A Chord HTTP request or upgrade no longer reads the router and the authenticators from its own goroutine while a reload composes them. The read recomposed a changed registry beside the commit that changed it: data races, and a reload that failed with "reload inside a commit or a derive compute" (2 of 5 runs of a reload loop beside readers). Pi reads `registries.router.value` on its one JavaScript thread, between the turns of the host's loop; the reads are now sections of the host's loop, which give the same interleaving. <!-- fix: 12d5c56025d8eb244c68ff331d6bbd91ed418d3b -->
- A Chord derive that returns a value no JSON has (a channel, a function) now fails its delivery, which the host reports as `delivery_failed` while the later frames of the commit are still delivered, as Pi's batch does when diffing throws. The derive's watchers used to receive the non-JSON frame without any report. <!-- fix: 016a19ac68 -->
- `chord/nextnode/workers`: a worker that ended (was stopped or killed) while its Node plugin host was still starting no longer leaves a `chord-plugins-*` socket directory in the temp directory; the server removes what the worker's process left once it has ended. <!-- fix: eeee29b9a8 -->
- The CI image version-literal test no longer reports the Pi part of an image tag (`1.4.0.b3a29f11`, written by `make pin-sync` and checked by `make pin-check`) as a hard-coded version when the pinned commit starts with a letter. <!-- fix: af66ca50b1a62039c2038d15492e809eacfa6e1c -->
- A code mode script in a loop can no longer freeze the whole process. Go cannot stop the world for a garbage collection while compiled guest code runs without calling Go, so a script that never reached the JavaScript engine's interrupt check (a native string or regular-expression loop, or a loop in a custom WebAssembly module) blocked every timer, including the one that stops it, and hung small machines (2 CPUs or fewer) for minutes. Every guest loop, including the QuickJS loops that run JavaScript loops and recursion, now reaches Go at least every 1024 iterations, as Pi's worker `terminate()` reaches a runaway script, so the hard stop runs on time. A custom WebAssembly module that recurses without any loop still never reaches Go, as before. <!-- fix: aff6631677 -->
- The crash message of a deterministic code mode VM that is told a result number it cannot take now reads as Pi's does, `Error: Result 2 has sequence number 5, expected 1 or later, once`, and names `undefined` for a result that carries no number, where it read `Result 2 has sequence number 0, ...`. <!-- fix: d1af7aece304c704c75b1bc32e8690dbeedf0d8f -->
- The errors that name a code mode tool or global (`Tool "x" is already registered`, `Invalid global name "x"`, `Global "x" is already registered`, `Global "x" conflicts with the namespace "x"`) write the name as it was given, as Pi does, instead of Go-escaped (`"we\"ird"`). <!-- fix: d1af7aece304c704c75b1bc32e8690dbeedf0d8f -->
- A code mode `done` message that carries no store writes now fails the execution with Pi's `store writes is not valid JSON` instead of `unknown message from the worker`. <!-- fix: d1af7aece304c704c75b1bc32e8690dbeedf0d8f -->
- With the AWS client log mode for request signing on, the Bedrock signing debug log printed the signed `x-amz-security-token` header, the session token, in clear text. The log now shows `<redacted>` for the `x-amz-security-token` and `authorization` header lines. <!-- fix: 8101d67c40 -->
- An extension provider's model that another provider also catalogs, such as `gpt-6-astra` under `azure`, no longer takes that provider's API when it is built before its own provider registers. Before this fix, such a model took the other provider's API and the turn failed (`LiteLLM model gpt-6-astra declares unsupported protocol "azure-openai-responses"`). `BuildModel` now matches only the requested provider's catalog, as the CLI's startup resolution already did. <!-- fix: 366ae8eb45 -->
- `--session <id>` and `--fork <id>` with an exact session ID now read only the session headers of the project's session directory, as Pi does, and list sessions only to match an ID prefix or to search other projects. Resolving an exact ID no longer decodes every session first: with 20 sessions of 1000 messages it allocated 21.7 MB, growing with the sessions, and it now allocates a size-independent amount. <!-- fix: 9df8c5c8f5 -->
- Running with no home directory now fails the way Pi's package manager does, instead of reading the project's `.agents/skills` as your own. With no `HOME` and no entry for your user in the system's user database (a container run as a user its passwd file does not list), `pig` used to take the home directory to be empty, so the `.agents/skills` directory of the current project was listed as the user's `~/.agents/skills`, with user scope and without the project-trust prompt. Startup in print and RPC mode, a reload and `pig config` now stop with `A system error occurred: uv_os_homedir returned ENOENT (no such file or directory)` and exit status 1, which is what Node's `os.homedir()`, and so Pi, reports there. Pi stops even earlier, at load, whatever the mode; PiG, which can run without a home directory by setting `PIG_HOME`, stops when it loads resources. <!-- fix: beeb36afc78bb184da7bb84d28b803855cef1e2b -->
- Unsubscribing an extension's event-bus subscription is now constant time, as deleting from Pi's `Set` of tracked unsubscribes is. The runtime removed each one from a slice, so unsubscribing 10,000 subscriptions one at a time took 142 ms and the cost grew with the square of their number; it now takes under 1 ms. The factory API also kept every subscription an extension had made, unsubscribed or not, until the extension reloaded; it now keeps only the live ones. <!-- fix: ee96daf3e7 -->
- A program that embeds PiG and never reads session events no longer hangs. A `Session` sent every event to its `Events()` channel from the start, so `Send` stopped once a reply produced more events than the channel's buffer holds (about 128), and the quick start in the `coding` package documentation and `examples/sdk` did exactly that. Events now go to the channel only after `Events()` is first called, as Pi notifies only the listeners it has: before that call nothing is buffered and nothing waits. A program that reads events calls `Events()` before `Send` and passes each event to `coding.AcknowledgeEvent`, and it still receives every event in order; an event sent before the call is not replayed, and a slow reader still slows the turn. A session made by `Clone` starts without a reader, like a forked Pi session, and `DiscardEvents()` stops delivery for a reader that quits. <!-- fix: f4a8f71a23 -->
- A stream header or metadata value changed in place on the settings object a Durable `Harness` returns from its settings callback now reaches the core with the next event, as it does in Pi, which re-reads the settings at every use. The core kept the settings it had encoded last when the new value compared equal to a stored copy that shared the same map. <!-- fix: 776588b309 -->
- A run whose model answer holds a value that is not strict JSON, a function or a non-finite number (`NaN`, `Infinity`), now faults with Pi's text, `Value contains a non-JSON function; expected strict JSON` or `Value contains a non-finite number and is not strict JSON`, in the submission's `detail` and in `pi.live.runFailure.detail`. It used to report Go's `json: ... unsupported type: func()` or `unsupported value: NaN`. <!-- fix: bf89558136, de985c5719 -->
- The agent docs bundle no longer contradicts the site. `/fork` continues from before an earlier user message, the `PIG_HOME` default names `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `defaultThinkingLevel` defaults to `medium`, the site lists all nine Resource kinds, the bundle's Package page documents `pig update --models`, and the Piglet Image is marked as planned. <!-- fix: 0367abc801 -->
- A submission's `Wait` no longer fails with "Harness is closed" when a close begins before the wait wakes: a host `SubscribeCommits` listener that closes the Harness on the commit that settled the submission, or a close that comes between that commit's adoption and its publication. Pi resolves the wait at the commit, so a later close cannot reach it; PiG settled it only after the host listeners, and the close's seal rejected it, turning a settled submission into an error for its waiter. The record is now fixed at the commit and the wait only wakes after the listeners. <!-- fix: 6c26be37c26a26540b42f19d4d1df597b5cf419f -->
- `WaitForIdle` on the Harness or a Conversation no longer fails with "Harness is closed" when a close begins after the commit that made the work idle and before the wait wakes. Pi settles the idle waits at the commit, so a later close cannot reach them; PiG decided and settled them only after the host listeners, and the close's seal rejected them. They are now settled at the commit and only wake after the listeners. <!-- fix: 11866f8f178657151179a0f39e1a7b03864016e2 -->
- The Durable core's conversation view follows Pi f3255de7's mount: a second observer of a conversation only loads its own window and takes the one `docs` object of the mount, so attaching to a mounted view spends Pi's microtask passes and the observers of one conversation share their documents; a window the core rejects (a bound that is not an integer, `max` below `min`) reaches the host as the `RangeError` Pi throws. <!-- fix: 121ba35041cbdd862404532e67e864b4fee5fe3f -->
- The Cloudflare host's report spans record the reason, extension and task of a `task_interrupted` report, as Pi b3a29f11's telemetry does (`task_parked` no longer exists). <!-- fix: ff225d26a557c32175b2a7550bfbba6d1692325e -->
- A call to `Session.DeferUntilPublished` from a goroutine other than the publishing one (a Harness's wait for idleness makes it from its caller's) no longer races the commit that arms the publication it lands on: the commit read the publication's queue without the lock the call appends under, which the race detector reported. <!-- fix: 14886f9f32 -->
- Durable core: a Harness opened through the TypeScript host honours `HarnessOptions.setTimer` and `onWake` (sleeping tasks arm host timers or wake the host once per change, a background timer the host declines is dropped, a foreground one it declines or throws on falls back to `setTimeout` and is reported once, `TaskRuntime.setTimer` timers end with their invocation) and `settings.restartLimit` (including `Infinity`) reaches the core, so a crash-looping task parks. A reservation commit that the host's Storage holds while `close()` seals the Harness now lands and is written back as pending instead of being dropped, and a `sleepUntil` of `NaN` or an infinity is rejected as Pi rejects it. <!-- fix: 432775653a -->
- A durable code mode script's journal now records the calls a script had issued after a batch of results in one commit, as Pi does, and none after the script ended. A batch of results delivered to the script was acknowledged in two or more commits, because the VM reports each result on its own goroutine, and a script that ended on the last result of a batch still had the acknowledgment of the one before it written after its end. <!-- fix: 46b2263428a125d0fc487236f041a679a2b2e672 -->
- A script that ends in its first run while a journaled tool call replays after a restart no longer shows that call as `cancelled` in the error result of a divergence ("it ended after result 0, where it went on before"). The script's end decided the outcome before the replayed call's row had finished, where Pi finishes the row first; the end now waits for the replayed calls the VM issued. <!-- fix: 46b2263428a125d0fc487236f041a679a2b2e672 -->
- A streamed answer's partial commits cost the new text, not the length of the message so far, as in Pi (`harness-view-run.test.ts` "commits a growing text and tool call at a cost that follows the new text"). A commit of `pi.live`'s partial no longer encodes and decodes the whole message: it takes the text and thinking of the partial as they are, and the check that a committed value decodes as its type decodes only the members and content blocks an operation touched, and not at all an append to a text, thinking or argument string. Streaming a 400 KB answer allocates about as much per commit as a 40 KB one. The stored format is unchanged. <!-- fix: 4916f14005 -->
- The Durable core conformance gate runs `U-codemode` and `U-harness-tools` alone, their reference run before their candidate run. Their upstream tests assert inside a real-time window that the run fills itself (`times a script out across a restart` gives a script 300 ms to start the sandbox and reach a tool, 148-207 ms of CPU); next to the other rows, the host starved either run, and in six full runs at `-j 8` the candidate missed the window four times and the reference once. <!-- fix: 78f1007d3e1ade8c0515032e3e9068514a51ffa1 -->
- Closing a Durable Harness while a tool waited on a nested call could leave an abort mark on that nested call in the store, so the next Harness reported it `aborted` instead of `interrupted` (it had started) or `abandoned` (it had not). The native core driver ran the close listeners, which cancel the waits in flight, before it told the core it was closing. The tool that the cancel freed could report its end first, and the core then aborted the nested calls of a caller the close had interrupted. The core is now told first. It failed once in a CI run under load (the nested-call restart test). <!-- fix: 8c829e2c62 -->
- A closed Harness or Session no longer stays reachable from Go's timer heap. `durable.NativeTimer`, the default `SetTimer`, stopped a timer without dropping its callback, and Go keeps a stopped timer and the function it was armed with until the runtime next removes it from the timer heap, which is not at `Stop` and can be as late as the timer's delay (ten minutes for the document sweep); the sweep's callback reaches the Session, so a closed Harness stayed alive that long, where Pi's `clearTimeout` leaves nothing of the callback. A disarmed timer now keeps nothing of its callback. <!-- fix: 9327bc7628 -->
- Closing a Harness over the TypeScript host no longer rejects when the write-back of the tasks the close stopped fails, for example because another process advanced the store. Pi catches that write and the Session reports the failure, so the close resolves. <!-- fix: 98666dfd10d79e195dc65e8002a2e6ea0fede12c -->
- The Go Durable SDK's scheduler no longer resolves the Harness settings for the context a run itself reads: `contextRetentionMs` is read only when the conversation is idle, as Pi's `runtime.context` does, which removes four settings resolutions from every round of one generation with a tool call. <!-- fix: 9eda51265b00744a15a1d37755daa5df9eba7651 -->
- The Durable core's host no longer reads the extensions of the Harness settings before every event it sends: the core never reads them, so they are neither sent nor compared by the change detector (the host made about 187 such reads in a round of one generation with one tool call). The core reads `HarnessOptions.settings` from the snapshot the host sends before each event, where Pi resolves the callback at each use (recorded as D206). <!-- fix: a1efda7e2b68629d6332b3110305315012622ea8 -->
- A tool running under the Durable core's Cloudflare host and `pi-durable` facade now has `api.now()`, the Harness clock (`HarnessOptions.now`, the wall clock when none is given), which throws once the tool call's invocation has ended, as Pi 1.4's `ToolExecutionApi.now` does. Code mode reads its start time, journaled clock and deadline through it, so every code mode call, and every `models.*` call from a script, failed with `api.now is not a function` before. <!-- fix: a9264aabbb9c032cd8d504c22059d73efd84b95d -->
- The Durable core conformance gate no longer writes the reference checkout from a vitest run: its cache lives in the run's output directory. The default, `packages/durable/node_modules/.vite`, added `node_modules` to the listing E17 and E18 print with `ls`, which they capture once for the reference before any U row ran, so `make durable-contract` failed both rows against every build on a fresh clone. <!-- fix: c5b14a57be526a10a0583f82fa702fd2e64663d3 -->
- Large nested-call fan-outs in the Durable core no longer re-send the whole document per call: the core sends the operations since the revision the host holds, and arrays that are only appended to are tracked as a tail. 1000 nested calls take 2.05 s instead of 4.94 s and 4000 calls 8.5 s instead of 49.3 s, with allocations per call flat. <!-- fix: 9883d4b247 -->
- A durable session no longer has a data race between a call to `DeferUntilPublished` from another goroutine (a harness's wait for idleness makes one) and the commit that arms its publication: the commit read the length of the publication's queue after it released the lock that the call appends to it under, so the race detector could report the two in a long durable/harness run. The commit now checks the queue under the lock. <!-- fix: d3aa996f80, 5352452911 -->
- A host that crashes during a model request no longer resends it forever, adding an aborted entry each time: the interrupted request is a failed attempt under the retry policy, and the run ends with `runFailure` reason `interrupted` once no retry is left; other work cut off `settings.restartLimit` times ends instead of keeping its conversation busy. <!-- fix: d40992222bb3b70407b30b15773c2f4e46c578fc, 19aa87d1a67afafed9ed7934393653156fe73efc -->
- A tool's `handoff` control now continues the run in the new context in the Durable core as it does in Pi: the handoff's reset is written first, queued writes and selected steers land after it and join the continuing run, a follow-up queued across the handoff waits for the continuing run's final boundary, and a queued reset ends the handed-off run. The core used to end the run at the handoff and answer it without another model request. <!-- fix: d94328677410f7437d3bc0371fcf84e0b9b323d0 -->
- `HarnessSettings.afterFailedRun` reaches the Durable core from the TypeScript host, so inputs queued behind a failed run start the next run with `continue` and settle `run_failed` with `withdraw`. <!-- fix: d94328677410f7437d3bc0371fcf84e0b9b323d0 -->
- A lone UTF-16 surrogate in a tool result's details, in a nested tool call's result, or in a code mode call's argument or error preview now stays a lone surrogate through the Durable entry and its stored values, written as the `\ud83d` escape that Pi's `JSON.stringify` writes, with `<`, `>` and `&` left as they are. Before, it became three U+FFFD characters (`encoding/json` has no lone-surrogate string), so the preview bytes in a stored result differed from Pi's. The session file, JSON mode and RPC mode already wrote the escape and are unchanged. <!-- fix: db1ee65be2 -->
- `WaitForTask` on a task whose terminal commit was adopted no longer fails with "Harness is closed" when a close begins before the wait wakes: a host `SubscribeCommits` listener that closes the Harness on that commit, or a close that comes between the commit's adoption and its publication. Pi settles the wait at the commit, so a later close cannot reach it; PiG settled it only after the host listeners, and the close's seal rejected it, turning a completed task into an error for its waiter. The receipt is now fixed at the commit and the wait only wakes after the listeners. <!-- fix: 9a9dc9900a4754a7e959b42d9bee188fbcc4500d -->
- `WaitForIdle` on the Harness or a Conversation no longer resumes before the `SubscribeCommits` listeners saw the commit that made the work idle. The idle settle that ends a reconcile pass, and the one the context expiry timer runs, could decide on a commit another goroutine had just adopted and resolve the waits ahead of its host listeners; Pi's continuation there cannot run between an adoption and its publication, and PiG's now leaves the decision to the settle queued behind the listeners. <!-- fix: e65ade9b1b81693d3d880ad62a0ed074423cb395 -->
- The Durable core's Session opens a document watch, a conversation view and the task graph as a job on the Session line, so an attachment made after a commit was queued starts at that commit's value; `watchDoc` and `observeDoc` reject on a closed Session with `Session is closed`; a watch keeps its Session alive while it runs and, once stopped or retired, no earlier incarnation's value; a Session subclass's `report(error, info)` receives the reports of its watches and observers. <!-- fix: 32fe8c41e7 -->
- The Go and Rust SDKs send an empty `prefill` of `Editor`/`editor` and an empty `placeholder` of `Input`/`input` as given, as Pi's `ctx.ui.editor(title, "")` and `ctx.ui.input(title, "")` do (an RPC client sees `prefill: ""`). They used to drop it, so a port of Pi's plan-mode example wrote a different RPC request than Pi. Pi's `editor(title)` and `input(title)`, which write no such member, are now `EditorWithoutPrefill`, `InputWithoutPlaceholder` and `InputWithoutPlaceholderWithOptions` in Go and `editor_without_prefill`, `input_without_placeholder` and `input_without_placeholder_with_options` in Rust, as `ClearStatus` is for `SetStatus`. `TestConformance_UIEmptyMembersAgreeAcrossSDKs` now requires every SDK (isolated, packed, fused) to tell the empty string from the unset member. <!-- fix: cbf4a52c17 -->
- The pi-env daemon runs a command whose `timeoutMs` is above 2^31-1 ms without a deadline, as Pi's daemon does, instead of refusing it; the clients still refuse such a timeout, as Pi's do. <!-- fix: 0387059efb -->
- The `pi-env` daemon now kills every command it started when it receives `SIGTERM`, `SIGINT` or `SIGHUP`, then exits with status 128 plus the signal. A client that closes its connection ends the daemon with `SIGTERM`; the daemon used to die on it before killing its commands, which were left running under init. On Windows a terminated daemon cannot clean up: its job object ends each command's own process, but not processes that one started. <!-- fix: 27f6a7e3bb04ee8bbca7242fe828a2bde1c3ffe3 -->
- The pi-env daemon answers as Pi's daemon does where a differential test found it did not: an error for an empty path carries `path`, `realpath` of a symbolic link loop is `ELOOP`, a directory renamed over a non-empty directory is `ENOTEMPTY` and a file over a directory `EISDIR` (also in the Durable Node environment's `renameFile`), `opendir` of a file is `ENOTDIR` before any permission check, errors the daemon's table does not name are `UNKNOWN` with the system's text, an empty write to a full device succeeds, an exec timeout is `timeout` and `timeoutMs: 0` times out at once, spawn and spill failures read as Rust's `io::Error`, and a command is the leader of a new session as Node's detached spawn makes it. <!-- fix: fa131b5961 -->
- On Windows, an extension's `exec` no longer returns no output for a command that printed, when the machine is too busy to run PiG's pipe reader within 100 ms of the command's exit. The command now starts suspended and joins a job object before it can start another process, as the bash tool's shell already did, so PiG knows when no process holds the output pipes any more and reads them to the end instead of dropping what the command had written before it exited. <!-- fix: 8f88d43fa5e3a208a8294343f2e444811df19055 -->
- Go embedding hosts can bind extension appends through `coding.Session.AppendExtensionEntry`, retaining subprocess IDs and timestamps through the native Session writer and preserving `entry_appended` semantics. Previously, calling `AppendCustomEntry` allocated a new identity instead of retaining the subprocess ID and timestamp because the public Session API lacked a way to pass them through, leaving duplicate entries in the Node session mirror. <!-- fix: bf453203b656bcbb1aa0a0c6f70fa9cc1562ac5e -->
- On Windows, a Go extension's source hash no longer fails, or makes a build beside it fail, with `The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process`. The hash listed every directory of the extension and of the modules its `go.mod` replaces through a handle that did not share delete, so a build that deleted or renamed a directory in those trees while the hash had it open (Cargo and rustc remove temp directories under a replaced repository root) failed with a sharing violation, and the hash failed in turn when it opened a directory that build was deleting. The hash now lists directories with every share mode. A directory that is there and denies the listing (an ACL deny) still fails the hash. <!-- fix: 234316d4356b6173375ddaa6e513264354ca0979 -->
- Node extensions read live `ctx.isIdle()` state, so background callbacks detect when a run finishes or starts. <!-- fix: 2bc49c1 -->
- Starting an extension no longer fails with `fork/exec …: text file busy` when the host builds or starts other extensions at the same moment (seen as a `ci-test-conformance` failure in `TestModelTypesVirtualModelsAcrossSDKs/rust-isolated`). The host copies a compiled extension binary into its cache and starts the copy as soon as it is published: a Rust cell runner when `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` puts the compiler output outside the build directory, a standalone Rust extension, and the embedded cells of a Piglet Binary. A process that another goroutine started while the copy was open still held the copy's write descriptor, and Linux refuses to start a file that any process holds open for writing. The host now starts no process from before the copy is opened until after it is closed, so a start waits for at most one 256 KiB chunk of a copy (about 0.2 ms), not the whole copy. A standalone Rust extension build also no longer reads the whole binary into memory to copy it. <!-- fix: 5ab230421c143524bb409360f4048c3e55334edb -->
- Starting a Go extension no longer fails with `hash <dir> after its build: open …/release/deps/rmeta…: no such file or directory` when a Cargo build runs in a directory its `go.mod` replaces. The source hash that guards a build against an edit made while it ran walked every replaced module in full, including a Cargo target directory not named `target`, and a temp directory rustc deleted between the listing and the read failed the whole hash. The walk now skips a tree marked with a `CACHEDIR.TAG` signature, as Cargo marks every target directory it creates, and a directory that vanishes mid-walk, as the packed-cell hash already did. A source file that cannot be read still fails the hash. <!-- fix: 633152df76c2628bff6aeb5ccefa2cb8b4d2f6a7 -->
- An extension that overrides the `edit` tool with a definition built by the Go, Rust or Python SDK's `createEditToolDefinition` now has the model's legacy edit shapes normalised, as Pi's `{ ...createEditToolDefinition(cwd), execute }` does. The SDK definition dropped the built-in's `prepareArguments`, so `edits` sent as a JSON string, a single edit object or the legacy top-level `{path, oldText, newText}` reached the override unnormalised and the edit was silently not applied, while the model's turn still reported success. The definition's `PrepareArguments` / `prepare_arguments` now runs the built-in's own normaliser on the host (a new `builtinTool.prepareArguments` host call; a fused Go extension calls it directly), and write, read and the other built-ins have none, as in Pi. <!-- fix: 6b97207807802a618e2a2942f0da100fdae84df5 -->
- On Windows, the host reports the load error of a Node extension that exits right after it sends the error. A Node extension whose factory fails connects to its named pipe, writes the error, closes and exits, and the host looks at the pipe only after the exit. Before this fix, the host could report `process_exited` and lose the error. The pipe driver sets the event that the host tested for a client later than the client's open returns, so a client whose event was not yet set was not counted. The host now asks the pipe's own state, which the open changes before it returns. <!-- fix: 82ca8da8221e94edb3991da44b7defcde686475f -->
- The footer's thinking level no longer reads `thinking off` in the first frames of an interactive start. PiG drew the footer and the editor border before the startup bind told them the Session's level, so a frame painted in that window showed `• thinking off` (and the neutral border) where Pi shows the configured level, `• medium` by default; with an extension loaded the bind comes later and the window is longer. The Session's level was right all along (`get_state` and the first request carry it); only the presentation lagged. Pi builds its footer with the Session and reads `session.state.thinkingLevel` on every render (`footer.ts` `render`, `interactive-mode.ts` `init`), so the footer and the editor are now seeded with the Session's level when they are built, for the default level, `--thinking` and settings overrides, and `off`, whichever extension host is loaded. <!-- fix: 87802922044e27059a6ca8aabe6b75856f901c75, b48dfa93ff1b8f923e0b92ef97cb6b42bf571ac6 -->
- A Piglet Binary whose extensions are all fused no longer stages the extension SDK sources into a clean config root before its first prompt. The first start of a Piglet with plan mode fused took 78 ms to the first usable prompt against 30 ms for a bare pig, and now takes 32 ms; later starts were never affected. <!-- fix: 42e2e75c19 -->
- `coding`: while the run of a session-graph client (an ExtensionRunner an extension constructed) was aborted, the Host read the client's `getSignal` function again and again without end, one call to the client each, and sent every runtime a new `run_signal` frame each time. The binding answered an aborted run with a new cancelled context on every read; the Host takes a context it has not seen for a new run and watches it, which fires at once for a cancelled one, so every sync renumbered the run and synced again. A run is now one context from the first read that reports it until a read reports no run, and the abort cancels that context in place, as Pi's `agent.signal` is one `AbortSignal` for a run. The run keeps its number through its abort and an aborted run costs no further read. <!-- fix: 892827ff8c -->
- Code that fails to highlight takes the code-block color, as in Pi: `highlightCode` returns it in the `mdCodeBlock` color in the Go, Rust, Python and Lisp extension SDKs when the host's highlighter fails or cannot be reached, and in the host for a theme that lacks a syntax color, where PiG panicked. `getMarkdownTheme().highlightCode` is `highlightCode`, so the `highlight.code` host call no longer has a `markdown` member. <!-- fix: 84b2fcadd1 -->
- `pig status` no longer lists the resources of an untrusted project as enabled. It resolves project trust as a print run does (saved decision, then `defaultProjectTrust`, else untrusted), shows the decision, and marks each project extension, skill, prompt and theme `ignored: untrusted` and not enabled. The settings and Packages of an untrusted project no longer count. <!-- fix: f21be69251 -->
- `pig diagnose` no longer reports the `defaultModel` of an untrusted project, which the session does not use. It reports the effective default model and the settings file of each part. A provider-qualified `defaultModel` such as `"bench/bench-2"` was printed as `bench/bench/bench-2`. Pi reads `defaultModel` as a model id and does not split it, so startup falls back to the first available model, as before; diagnose now says so and names the fix. <!-- fix: f21be69251 -->
- `pig status` run from the agent's shell no longer lists ambient extensions and skills that the active Piglet's `discovery` excludes. Such resources show `ignored: piglet-discovery`. <!-- fix: f21be69251 -->
- `pig status` now gives a skill without a `description` the health `not loaded: description is required`, and a theme with an unknown color role or another schema error an `invalid:` health, with a warning for each. Pi leaves out the skill and rejects the theme; status listed both as enabled with no health problem. <!-- fix: 6ea3ba8720 -->
- `pig install <path> --validate-only` called a `.mjs` file, or a directory with only `index.mjs`, a valid extension without saying that auto-discovery ignores it. Pi discovers only `.ts` and `.js` files in an extensions directory. The report stays valid, because `-e` and a settings path load the source, and now says what discovery does. <!-- fix: 570c037353 -->
- `pig status --json` now gives a skill without a `description` and a theme that fails the theme schema `enabled: false` as well as the `health` text and the warning, so one field says whether the session has the resource. They were `enabled: true` before. They count as disabled in `resources`. <!-- fix: d9a9c51ff7 -->
- `ctx.isIdle()` read on the statement after a triggering `pi.sendMessage(..., { triggerTurn: true })` is busy as in Pi in every SDK, in print, JSON and RPC mode, isolated and packed: the Host answers busy for every extension from the send until the code that sent it yields, where a run that settled while the read was in flight made the Go, Python, Rust and Lisp SDKs report an idle session. A Go, Python, Rust or Lisp handler yields when it returns or awaits a Promise-returning member (`registerProvider` and `addAutocompleteProvider` return nothing in Pi and no longer end the hold); the Node runtime reports its first microtask checkpoint after the send, so a send from a timer's or an I/O callback that runs after the handler returned holds the Session busy as well, as it does in Pi. The Node runtime's own hold is gone; a message sent from `agent_settled` still reads the Session's idle answer, and a send the Host fails holds nothing. A Go, Python, Rust or Lisp handler that waits for the run it started with `while !isIdle: sleep` uses the SDK's new yield helper (`ctx.Sleep`/`ctx.Yield`, `ctx.sleep`/`ctx.yield_now`, `pig:ctx-sleep`/`pig:ctx-yield`), the stand-in for Pi's `await`; a raw sleep keeps the hold until the handler returns (D225). <!-- fix: 2323d94ce7 -->
- A suspended session that receives SIGCONT while its process group does not own the terminal (`bg`, or `kill -CONT` from elsewhere) no longer re-enters raw mode and draws into the shell's terminal; it stops again and waits for `fg`. A terminal that went away while the session was stopped now ends it with the dead-terminal exit (129) instead of an `interrupted system call` error (#396, #397, D227). <!-- fix: b65e288aca -->
- A write to a terminal that went away (`EIO` after a hang-up, `EPIPE`, `ENOTCONN`, `ENOTTY`) now ends the session with exit 129, as Pi's stdout error listener does, instead of being discarded while the session keeps running (#397). <!-- fix: 1c1b349dbd -->
- After Ctrl+Z, `bg` and `fg`, the session returns to the terminal instead of ending with `Error: interrupted system call`: raw-mode entry and exit retry an ioctl that a stop and continue interrupted, as Node's libuv does (#397). <!-- fix: 6f165a205c -->
- A terminal that went away while an extension's remote editor, an extension title, a clipboard copy (OSC 52), the external-editor notice or the startup model-scope notice wrote to it now ends the session with exit 129 like Pi, instead of the write error being discarded and the session carrying on (#397). <!-- fix: 08edd46dfc, 3cc0c71d33 -->
- A terminal write that fails for a reason other than a lost terminal (not `EIO`, `EPIPE`, `ENOTCONN` or `ENOTTY`) now restores the terminal, records a crash and exits 1 as Pi's uncaught-exception handler does, instead of being dropped (#397). <!-- fix: f2aed24c0d -->
- An extension's `ctx.ui.setTitle` replaces control characters in the title with spaces, as Pi's terminal title does, so a BEL or ESC in it no longer ends the sequence early and sends the rest to the terminal as escapes (#397). <!-- fix: f2aed24c0d -->
- A terminal write that fails for a reason other than a lost terminal while the keyboard protocol is on no longer hangs the exit: the terminal restore does not wait for the output lock the failing write holds, so the terminal is handed back and the process exits 1 as Pi's uncaught-exception handler does (#397). <!-- fix: 3f8277020b -->
- On Windows, `ERROR_PIPE_NOT_CONNECTED`, `ERROR_BAD_PIPE`, `ERROR_GEN_FAILURE`, `ERROR_IO_DEVICE` and `ERROR_NOT_CONNECTED` on the terminal now exit 129 as Pi does, instead of a crash report and exit 1 (#397). <!-- fix: 3f8277020b -->
- Subagents of `pi-open-agents` (and any extension that finds the Pi CLI from the package root of `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`) start under PiG. They died at once with `Cannot find module '.../runtime/dist/cli.js'` (MODULE_NOT_FOUND): `import.meta.resolve` of the package pointed into the runtime's shim directory, so the `dist/cli.js` two directories up did not exist. The package now resolves to `dist/index.js` of the vendored package root, as it does in Pi, and that root's `dist/cli.js` starts PiG with the arguments it is given, as `process.execPath process.argv[1]` does. <!-- fix: d94e83f2ac -->
- `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core`, `pi-tui` and `pi-ai` (and `pi-ai/models`, `pi-ai/oauth`, `pi-ai/providers/all`) now resolve, in an extension, to files of a package root laid out like Pi's: a `package.json` named for the package above the entry, the entry at the path Pi's `main` or `exports` gives (`dist/index.js` and the like), and `pi-ai`'s `dist/cli.js`. An extension that resolves one of these packages and walks up to its `package.json`, reads `../package.json` beside the entry, or computes a `dist/` file from the root found nothing in the runtime's shim directory before. <!-- fix: 27e9bc8860, fa330d4b2d, 5b6dce98de -->
- In macOS Terminal.app, which sends Option+Up as plain Up in its default profile, plain Up with an empty editor and a queued message now restores the queued messages to the editor and clears the queue, as Option+Up does in other terminals; before, Up recalled history while the message stayed queued and was still sent after the tool, even after you deleted the recalled copy. The queued-message hint names Up in that state. Elsewhere (tmux, ssh, other terminals), when Up recalls history while a message is queued, PiG shows one dim line under the editor, once per run, saying the text is a copy and which key edits the queue; tmux, ssh and unknown terminals also get the Terminal.app mapping of Option+Up to `\033[1;3A`. Pi 1.5.0 behaves as PiG did before (D228). <!-- fix: 2359a0a7b8 -->
- `Math.exp` in `internal/jsmath` returns Node's bits on arm64. V8's fdlibm build contracts products into multiply-adds there, and `Exp` rounded them, so the last bit differed from `Math.exp` for about 1 in 2500 arguments on arm64 hosts. GOARCH=amd64 results are unchanged. <!-- fix: 4d32556afa6bcc5937402bcab72fdf9348ad5c5f -->
- `/llama` pointed at llama-swap no longer ends in a bare "llama.cpp returned HTTP 404" when you load or unload a model (#380). llama-swap lists its models like a llama.cpp router but has no load or unload endpoint, because it loads a model when a request names it, and Pi shows the same 404. PiG now recognises llama-swap (its error envelope, or a `GET /running` that answers like it) and says to add it to `models.json` as an `openai-completions` provider and pick models with `/model`; a 404 from a real llama.cpp router keeps Pi's text (D212). The llama.cpp docs page has a new llama-swap section with the `models.json` setup. <!-- fix: 0920a0090e -->
- `pig status` reports the agent and project directories by the same resolved path before and after a run creates them. It resolved symbolic links only once a directory existed, so on macOS, where the temporary directory is `/var/...` and resolves to `/private/var/...`, the paths changed between the first run and the next. <!-- fix: 331ab59c12 -->
- Starting a new Session in a working directory that was removed, where the system still reports its path (macOS), ends with Pi's `Stored session working directory does not exist` message and exit 1 in print, JSON and RPC mode, and offers to continue in the current directory in interactive mode, instead of failing later with a `construct session` error. <!-- fix: eba1115c50 -->
- Closing a session with an MCP server that signs in with OAuth no longer fails at random. The `DELETE` that ends the session could be refused with the `context canceled` of the stream the connection opens to hear from the server, when closing began while that stream's answer was still being handed over, so the server kept the session until it expired; closing now sends the `DELETE` only after the requests it aborted have returned. The stream's first request also reads its token before the connection is reported ready, as in Pi: a stream that started late could refresh a token that was about to expire, and closing then waited up to 15 seconds for the authorization server. <!-- fix: 8a4483647c, 320d389221, 680815deac, d5d34e7742 -->
- Fixed incorrect MCP reconnect behavior after cancellation during transport cleanup. Previously, reconnect still started a replacement connection after the caller had canceled. Reconnect did not check caller cancellation after closing the previous client, so it could still start a replacement connection. Reconnect now completes cleanup and returns the original cancellation cause before starting a replacement. <!-- fix: c3501172abc8672f372b7cb9207e43d685854f9a -->
- An MCP Streamable HTTP `application/json` reply over `maxMessageBytes` (default 16 MiB) is now rejected with `MCP JSON response exceeds N bytes`, like an oversized SSE event, instead of being buffered whole (Pi main #11749, D233). <!-- fix: d4e641bde3 -->
- An MCP Streamable HTTP error body is read only up to its first 8 KiB, and the rest is cancelled; the kept excerpt is 8192 bytes, not 8192 UTF-16 units (Pi main #11749, D233). <!-- fix: d4e641bde3 -->
- Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough and inverse text (markdown headings, quotes, table headers, links and emphasis, tool titles, selector titles, diff highlights) now draw only when Pi's chalk would: its stdout color level is above zero. With `CI` set (outside a known CI service), `TERM=dumb` or stdout redirected, PiG kept drawing them while Pi 1.5.0 drew only the theme colors. <!-- fix: ad0c1678f6, 0a036c9a15 -->
- `/fork` and `/clone` of a very long session no longer decode and rewrite every record of the branch in memory. Forking a 427 MB session peaked at 4.8-5.1 GB and now peaks at about 280 MB (settling at about 190 MB); Pi peaks at about 1.2 GB for the same file. The new file holds the same bytes as before and as Pi writes. <!-- fix: 761f5a208c -->
- Resuming a very long session no longer reads and decodes every entry of the branch to restore the tool loadout. A 365 MB session peaked at 2 GB of memory at startup; it now peaks at about 130 MB, as the 46 MB one does, and Pi's startup peaks at about 640 MB for the same file. <!-- fix: ed01bf62b4, 836d58c4c8 -->
- An entry read from a long session's file no longer keeps the whole shared read (up to 8 MiB) alive: each entry owns its record, so a context built from scattered records retains what it holds and not the gaps between them. <!-- fix: c80895bd4f -->
- Switching to a long session with `/resume`, `/fork` or `/tree` no longer leaves memory the replaced session used: the heap is returned to the OS once the new transcript is painted, as it is at start. A 375 MB session resumed from inside PiG held 2.2 GB until exit; it now holds about 100 MB. <!-- fix: c80895bd4f, 7fae0d4832 -->
- An extension that calls the base autocomplete provider's `shouldTriggerFileCompletion` with a negative cursor column now gets Pi's answer: the column counts back from the end of the line in UTF-16 units as `line.slice(0, col)` does, where it was treated as column 0. <!-- fix: 7689b82bf75082d659d4865272ee4fbe53876724 -->
- An extension dialog (`select`, `input`, `editor`) whose `timeout` carries a fraction of a millisecond past a whole second, such as `1000.5`, now starts its countdown from the next second like Pi's `Math.ceil(timeoutMs / 1000)`; the countdown rounded the milliseconds down to whole milliseconds first and started one second short. <!-- fix: 776d60b196 -->
- A model request from a subprocess extension whose integer field is `2^63` or larger is now rejected instead of converting to the largest `int64` on arm64. <!-- fix: 776d60b196 -->
- The Chord delivery scheduler no longer reads goroutine stacks or depends on how many goroutines the process holds: `AwaitEntered` returns once the synchronous part of every earlier delivery's listener ran (its call returned, or it went on to a wait of the Session, `chord.DeliveryEntered`), as Pi's `#drain` microtask does, so the Durable Session's hop between two publications of one storage call, the Harness waits and the reload report order the listeners' code as in Pi at any goroutine count. A listener blocked on a plain lock the caller holds is the one gap. <!-- fix: 8b1f8a9960 -->
- Nested tool calls reach the Session line in call order, also when the calls waited on the same first memo, and a call's own wait no longer holds the next call's start (a deadlock with the core driver). <!-- fix: 93d0f2f0cb -->
- A wait of a Session continuation stays registered until the continuation has entered, so a publication that looks for the waits it readied after their goroutines ran still waits for it. <!-- fix: 08099eb763 -->
- A Harness wait that ended by cancellation or a close no longer holds the publications after it when its caller brought a `WithContinuation`. <!-- fix: 8b1f8a9960 -->
- Durable's `StoreStorage` serializes a record once: the store takes the record's JSON text with its parsed value (`chordstore.JsonText`) instead of serializing the value again. <!-- fix: 8b1f8a9960 -->
- A tool's invocation-bound conversation handle rejects a `Submit` that queued behind another Session job when the invocation ended before the submit's job started, and stores nothing, as Pi's job-start abort check does; the handle's cancellation no longer detaches before the call queues (Pi session.ts commit). <!-- fix: cf6bb3ac45 -->
- A replay-safe tool's rerun shows its nested call's arguments in the member order of the stored checkpoint, not sorted (Pi tool.ts). <!-- fix: cf6bb3ac45 -->
- Expiring kept contexts stops at the first context still retained instead of copying the whole idle order on every settle, so the cost of a settle no longer grows with the number of idle contexts. <!-- fix: 64e88301d0 -->
- The Session orders the continuations of what a publication resolved before the next part of the same storage call is published at any number of goroutines in the process. The ordering used to read a dump of every goroutine, cost about a millisecond per publication, and was given up above 128 goroutines. The waits of the Session (`SessionImpl.Park`, `SessionImpl.Await`, a commit caller's resumption) now register before they block and acknowledge when they resumed, so a publication costs microseconds and 4 KiB, whatever the process runs. A caller that needs its continuation ordered up to its next wait of the Session passes `session.WithContinuation(ctx)` and calls `Entered`. `SessionImpl.ReadOnLineCtx` and `ReadWithTicketCtx` run a line read with the caller's line admission and continuation. <!-- fix: 4a3ad8b882 -->
- A sleeping task that came due in the millisecond between a reservation pass that found it ahead and the next wake recomputation is run instead of left asleep with no timer armed; a reopened Harness waiting on such a task no longer hangs. <!-- fix: 5528b09988 -->
- A running watch drain registers the call it makes next when its frame is published, so `AwaitEntered` and the Session's hop between two parts of a call see every listener call that is not yet entered; frames published behind a running call no longer fold into one call at more than one processor. <!-- fix: 68a31878e8 -->
- The Session's blocking points a listener can reach (the wait for the previous line job, for room, for the writer's drain and for a part's publication) mark the delivery entered, so a listener that calls `UnloadDocuments` during a multi-part call does not stall the Session's publications. <!-- fix: 674b44978e -->
- A watch listener that calls the Harness (`WaitForTask`, `WaitForIdle`, `Abort`, `Close`) or the Session (`Close`, a line ticket's `Release`) at one of the parts of a multi-part storage call no longer stalls the Session's hop: every wait of the Session a listener can reach marks the delivery entered and ends with its context. <!-- fix: 4b96e48066 -->
- A JSONL commit whose file path fails to resolve after its batch applied in memory now poisons the storage, as every failure after that point does, instead of leaving memory ahead of the files. <!-- fix: 875c5c04b3 -->
- In the Node extension runtime, `ctx.isIdle()` read on the statement after a triggering `pi.sendMessage(..., { triggerTurn: true })` is busy as in Pi, where the started run cannot end before the handler awaits; a run that settled while the read was in flight made print mode report an idle session. The Host now holds that answer for every SDK and extension (`isidle-2323d94ce7`), and the runtime reports only where its handler awaits. <!-- fix: c7237820c1 -->
- On macOS, reading or writing a named pipe (FIFO) through the read, edit, write and grep tools, the node and local execution environments or the JSONL session storage could lose the other end's bytes: a signal that ended the wait for the writer (the Go runtime's SIGURG preemption signal, a child's SIGCHLD) made macOS drop the open from the pipe, so the writer failed with EPIPE and the reader returned an empty file or waited for a writer that had gone (about one open in seven under a steady stream of signals). Pi does not lose them, as Node opens on a libuv worker thread that signals are not delivered to; PiG now opens a FIFO on a thread that blocks every signal. Other platforms and files that are not FIFOs are unchanged. <!-- fix: dbce96c6a2 -->
- The model catalog generator gives OpenCode Zen and Go Claude 5.5 models, Opus 5 and Fable 5.1 per-message effort (`supportsMidConvoEffort`), as Pi's generator does since 9ee7586a9 (#10954). Their `anthropic-messages` requests then carry per-message effort markers and `thinking.block_binding: drop_block` like the Anthropic provider. OpenCode Go rejected replayed thinking with a 400 because the requests carried no `drop_block` binding after the tool list or system prompt changed. The bundled catalog is converted from the published Pi package and carries the flag once the pin moves to a Pi version that includes that commit. Until then the remote catalog overlay can deliver the flag: pi-in-go.dev (D64) serves the overlay that `withRemoteCatalog` reads, as pi.dev does for released Pi. <!-- fix: e8a5d2ef7e -->
