- Opening the model selector no longer composes the whole model catalog, OpenRouter's `:nitro` and `:floor` variants included, to read each scoped model, and the registry no longer derives those variants for a provider it lists no model of. <!-- fix: 67eccd768a -->
- A stream of appends to one text costs the appended bytes instead of the whole text so far. `delta.AppendText` and the preparation of the change that adopts it each copied the text into a new string for every append, and `delta.PendingOps` copied the folded text again for every merged append, as Go strings do where Pi's V8 ropes do not. The new revision's string now shares the bytes of the old one and the queue folds into one buffer. 10000 adopted 8-byte `AppendText` commits take 23 ms and 22 MB (they took 190 ms and 879 MB; the same number of commits that set a number take 23 ms and 18 MB), and 10000 appends to one path fold in `PendingOps` in 1.4 ms and 1 MB (they took 120 ms and 429 MB). The ops and values are unchanged. <!-- fix: 576065f106 -->
- Several `AppendText` calls to one key in one change join their texts as JavaScript string concatenation does: a high surrogate that ends one text and a low surrogate that starts the next make one character in the op, as they already do in the new value. <!-- fix: 576065f106 -->
- Streaming a tool call's arguments allocates less per delta. The incremental parser no longer records changes nobody reads, and a streamed message's published copy keeps the parser's validated snapshot instead of copying it again (an invalid byte in an argument string is still rewritten as before). A 250 KB `write` call streams about 13% faster with about 22% fewer allocations; the print-mode allocation ceilings per delta fall from 20 and 35 to the measured 18.5 and 18.3 (faux provider and OpenAI Completions). <!-- fix: 81e1a45f0b -->
- Reading a JPEG or a WebP image now decodes it with ports of the decoders Photon runs (jpeg-decoder 0.3.1 and the image 0.24.9 WebP decoder: baseline and progressive JPEG in every sampling, restart intervals, CMYK and YCCK; lossy, lossless, alpha and animated WebP), pixel for pixel and error for error, instead of Go's `image/jpeg` and `x/image/webp`. A JPEG or WebP the model is sent after a resize, a rotation or a re-encode is therefore Pi's own bytes, and what depends on its pixels (sizes, the quality ladder, the choice of PNG or JPEG) is Pi's too; with this PiG's image pipeline writes the same bytes as Pi in every measured case. <!-- fix: 9139ed88f2 -->
- Images in the formats Photon decodes beyond PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP and TIFF are now decoded the way Pi decodes them, pixel for pixel and error for error on every file of the oracle corpus: ICO (a bitmap or PNG entry, with its AND mask), PNM (PBM, PGM and PPM in plain and raw form, and PAM), DDS (DXT1, DXT3 and DXT5, also through the DX10 header), Radiance HDR and farbfeld. A clipboard target such as `image/x-icon`, an image the model is sent under any declared type, an attachment, and a file handed to the terminal image conversion or to the durable `read` tool are converted to PNG or resized as Pi does, to the same bytes in every case measured against Pi's own code, where PiG used to say it could not convert them. Files Photon refuses are refused, an image of more than 512 MiB decoded is refused, and an image with no pixels is no longer encoded (Pi's PNG encoder throws on it). TGA, AVIF, OpenEXR and QOI stay unsupported, as in Pi (TGA has no signature, the others are not built into Photon). <!-- fix: bba3679802 -->
- BMP and GIF images are now decoded the way Pi decodes them, pixel for pixel and error for error on every file of the oracle corpus, where PiG used to use Go's decoders. A BMP with non-zero reserved bytes in its file header, an OS/2 core header, any header version, a 16-bit or bitfield layout, RLE4 or RLE8 data, a pixel array offset inside the headers or a top-down height decodes as Photon decodes it (and the ones Photon refuses are refused), and a GIF is read as its first frame placed on the logical screen, with Photon's rules for local and global palettes, transparency, interlacing, frames that do not fit the screen and damaged LZW data. A clipboard bitmap, an attachment, a tool-result image and a file handed to the terminal image conversion or to the durable `read` tool are converted or resized as Pi converts them. <!-- fix: cbc986b4ca -->
- The durable `read` tool prepares an image with a width or a height of zero (a farbfeld file with no pixels, an interlaced GIF with no rows) as Pi does: under a type providers do not take inline, or beyond a limit, the image is resized to at least one pixel and encoded, with the resize recorded from the empty size, instead of being left out. A resize that would need the PNG of the empty image itself fails as it does in Pi. <!-- fix: e77f039733 -->
- An image the model receives is now JPEG-encoded with a port of Photon's encoder (image 0.24.9: the IJG integer DCT, the standard Huffman tables, the libjpeg quality scaling) instead of Go's `image/jpeg`, so for an image that decodes to the pixels Photon decodes (PNG, GIF, BMP) the bytes and sizes are Pi's, and with them every decision that depends on a size: which quality of the ladder fits the byte limit, how far the 3/4 shrink goes, and which of the PNG and the JPEG candidate of a resize is smaller (Pi #11577). The encoder is 1.9 times faster than Go's on a screenshot and 2.4 times faster on a 12 MP photo, with a dozen allocations in place of millions. <!-- fix: 95de1de195 -->
- Resizing an image no longer differs from Photon's by one in a channel of a rare pixel. Photon computes the Lanczos weights with libm's single-precision `sinf`, which is not always the correctly rounded sine Go's `math.Sin` gives; PiG now runs the same `sinf`, so the resized pixels, and the PNG and JPEG written from them, are Photon's for every size measured (251 more pictures against Photon, 19 of which differed before). <!-- fix: 99d6e28a33 -->
- PNG images are now decoded the way Pi decodes them, pixel for pixel and error for error on every file of the oracle corpus, where PiG used to use Go's `image/png`. A PNG is read as Photon's png crate reads it: every colour type and bit depth with its transparency chunk (a grayscale or RGB tRNS chunk longer than its colour, one shorter than the palette), Adam7 interlacing, 16-bit samples converted the way Photon converts them, the first image of an animated PNG, ancillary chunks with a wrong checksum skipped and critical ones refused, a file that stops right after its image data, the memory limit of the crate, and a zlib stream read by its own inflater (which refuses and accepts other streams than zlib's). A clipboard image, an attachment, a tool-result image, an ICO entry and a file handed to the terminal image conversion or to the durable `read` tool are converted or resized as Pi converts or resizes them, and a damaged PNG is accepted or refused as Pi accepts or refuses it. PiG no longer registers Go's PNG decoder for its own use. <!-- fix: 6445df7c9d -->
- A TIFF image is now decoded the way Pi decodes it (Photon links the `tiff` 0.9.1 crate under `image` 0.24.9), pixel for pixel and error for error on every file of the oracle corpus. A TIFF on the X11 or Wayland clipboard (`image/tiff`), an image the model is sent under any declared type, and a TIFF handed to the terminal image conversion or to the durable `read` tool are converted to PNG or resized as Pi does, to the same bytes in every case measured against Pi's own code, where PiG used to answer that it could not convert them. Accepted: 8- and 16-bit gray (BlackIsZero and WhiteIsZero), RGB, RGBA and 8-bit CMYK, strips and tiles, chunky or planar, big- or little-endian, uncompressed, LZW, PackBits, Deflate and JPEG, with or without the horizontal predictor. Refused, as in Pi: palette, bilevel, 1- to 7-bit, 12-bit, 32-bit and floating point images, YCbCr, the floating point predictor, Fax and old-style JPEG, BigTIFF, damaged files, and images of more than 512 MiB decoded. <!-- fix: facd278025 -->
- A Piglet's tool scope now covers the built-in MCP tools. A Piglet with an `extensions:` section that does not list `pig-mcp-adapter` still offered `mcp__<server>__<tool>` from `builtin:mcp`, and `codemode` with them. `ScopeTools` now treats a tool in namespace `mcp__<server>` like the adapter's `mcp:<server>` source: the `pig-mcp-adapter` entry and its `tools` list govern it, and the MCP resource tools follow the same entry by name. Stock PiG without a Piglet is unchanged. <!-- fix: 85d311939a3e56baf0f5ef04d366fac0b3940f3c -->
- A Piglet's tool scope now bounds the Session's tool registry, not only its active tools. A Piglet that allowed some MCP tools, or hid some tools of an extension, still left the others callable from a `codemode` script (the MCP server logged the call) and loadable with `tool_search`, because both read the registry. The Piglet scope now composes with `--tools` and `--exclude-tools` as an intersection wherever Pi applies its allowlist: definitions, the registry, `getAllTools`, activation and the refresh after a late registration. A hidden tool fails in `codemode` as it does under `--tools` (`tools.<name> does not exist`) and `tool_search` cannot find it. `codemode` and `tool_search` are no longer hidden when a Piglet leaves no MCP tool visible; they just reach nothing hidden. The MCP resource tools (`list_mcp_resources`, `list_mcp_resource_templates`, `read_mcp_resource`) are governed by the `pig-mcp-adapter` entry by name. Stock PiG without a Piglet is unchanged. <!-- fix: 227a4c1bff5e42573122263bf2a3ca8caceccf9d -->
- `pig piglet build` produced a dynamically linked Piglet Binary unless `CGO_ENABLED=0` was set, so a Binary needed libc although nothing in it uses cgo. The build now sets `CGO_ENABLED=0` unless you set `CGO_ENABLED` yourself (in the environment or with `go env -w`) or a package of the Binary has cgo sources, so a cgo-free Binary is static and runs in an empty container. <!-- fix: 5689853654 -->
- The `/tree` Summarize option sends the session's thinking level with the branch summary request when the model supports reasoning, as compaction does. Before, the request carried no reasoning, and a reasoning model on OpenAI Responses or Azure Responses that rejects an effort of `none` failed the summary with a 400 error. <!-- fix: 10189c4741 -->
- Device-code logins (GitHub Copilot, Kimi Code, Meta, Radius) use the `verification_uri` a server sends only when it is an `http:` or `https:` URL, and open and show its normalized form, so a malicious login server cannot make `pig` launch a `file:` or custom protocol URL. Ports Pi's `trustedHttpUrl` use in every login that opens a server-supplied URL. <!-- fix: 439c708ebc -->
- A pi-messages event whose `contentIndex` is not an integer naming the next block (for a `_start` event) or an existing block (for any other event) now fails with `Invalid contentIndex <value> in pi-messages <type> event`, as Pi's does, instead of indexing the message's content with a value from the wire. <!-- fix: 439c708ebc -->
- OpenCode and OpenCode Go requests go to the protocol-specific endpoints instead of the shared base: OpenAI-compatible models at `/inference/openai/v1`, Anthropic models at `/inference/anthropic`, Google models at `/inference/google/v1beta` and Jev at `/inference/systemone/v1` (the same paths under `/inference/go` for OpenCode Go). Ports Pi's #11434. <!-- fix: 59b5daed63 -->
- Durable partial commits of a streamed answer no longer compare every growing text, thinking and tool-call argument string in full on each commit and re-assign the arguments snapshot: they append new text with `AppendText` and apply the argument changes of their own parse of the streamed argument text. <!-- fix: 5bf0d4a2ad -->
- An append op whose text starts with the low half of a surrogate pair joins the high half that ends the string it appends to, as JavaScript string concatenation does. <!-- fix: 5bf0d4a2ad -->
- Hidden thinking with an empty label (`ctx.ui.setHiddenThinkingLabel("")`) renders no rows: thinking before a tool call no longer draws blank rows, and thinking before text draws one spacer. <!-- fix: 620abb0ff5 -->
- A session entry whose write to the session file fails (a full disk, a busy or timed-out network drive) is no longer kept in memory: the error is returned, the session keeps its last written entry as the leaf, and the next entry is written as that entry's child. Before, the next entry pointed to the lost one, and resuming the session dropped the history before the gap, including the first system message that declares the tools. <!-- fix: 69899c5212 -->
- A pi-env connection whose daemon exits (or fails) before `hello` now adds the end of the daemon's stderr (the last 20 lines or 2000 characters, terminal escapes and control characters removed) to the start error, for example `pi-env exited with code 3 before it was ready` followed by `remote stderr:` and the profile's message. stderr is decoded as UTF-8 across reads, and a start that fails because the daemon exited waits for its pipes to end so the tail is complete; a ready session still fails as soon as the daemon exits. <!-- fix: 7163ab34f14e7ab9291f4ea80b4cb682d9246281 -->
- A tool call that streams many argument deltas no longer costs time and memory that grow with the square of its text: every provider (Anthropic Messages, Bedrock Converse Stream, Mistral, OpenAI Completions and Responses, Pi messages), the faux provider and the proxy stream read each delta once. A 500 KB `write` call streams in well under a second. <!-- fix: 76f780d05d -->
- A grammar (custom) tool input no longer copies the whole input so far on every delta. <!-- fix: 76f780d05d -->
- `--model <provider>/<id>` now resolves when the provider id itself contains a `/`, such as a URL-derived id like `llama-server=http://host:10800`. Before, the reference was split at its first `/`, so the prefix never named a provider and resolution ended in "not found". The longest matching provider id wins. <!-- fix: 7744a0bd9a -->
- A tool round whose results request `Handoff` no longer ends the run on the tool-calling answer: the handoff's `pi.reset` entry is written and the same run continues with a new generation in the new context, so the submission settles with the eventual answer. Queued writes and selected steers are placed after the handoff text, follow-ups wait for the run's final boundary, and a queued reset still ends the run `unanswered` with reason `reset`. A round whose every result also sets `Terminate` ends the run after the handoff. <!-- fix: 8153bc7a9e -->
- `grep` with `context` numbers a file's lines at line feeds only, as ripgrep does: a lone carriage return no longer adds a line, so the context lines after it keep their line numbers and the match is no longer shown on the wrong line. The carriage return is dropped from the printed line. <!-- fix: 8aff02e0d4 -->
- GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.5 no longer fail with `Missing namespace for function_call` after switching from another model that called tools. On the OpenAI and OpenCode providers they declare their tools in the top-level tool list instead of loading them through `additional_tools` or tool search; GPT-5.6 and later keep `additional_tools`. Ports Pi's #11415. <!-- fix: a30388b92a -->
- The login dialog opens and prints only `http:` and `https:` URLs, in their normalized form (percent-encoded control characters); any other URL is shown with its control characters replaced and is not opened in the browser, and no terminal hyperlink is made for it. Before, a URL from a login server could end a terminal hyperlink early or send its own escape sequences. <!-- fix: ae1ee6d132 -->
- A terminal title that holds a control character (a session name from a session file with an ESC or BEL) no longer ends the title sequence early and sends the rest to the terminal as escape sequences: control characters become spaces, as in Pi's `setTitle`. <!-- fix: ae1ee6d132 -->
- Claude models with per-message effort no longer fail with `Invalid effort level` on accounts whose organization caps effort below `high`: the fixed top-level effort is `low`. <!-- fix: 930c88ec0c -->
- MCP sign-in now rejects authorization endpoints and other OAuth metadata URLs that are not `http:` or `https:`, so a malicious server cannot make pig launch a `file:` or custom protocol URL. <!-- fix: 619443a024 -->
- A configured package or `-e` source that cannot be installed no longer ends startup. It is skipped, as in offline mode, and reported as an extension warning that says how to remove it (`pig remove <source>`, with `--local` for a project package) or to check the source; `--help` and `--list-models` print it too. <!-- fix: 07da4ea3a6 -->
- A line of many `>` characters no longer makes the Markdown renderer's output grow exponentially with the nesting depth. <!-- fix: ae498ebdc6 -->
- `pig install` and `pig remove` no longer add ever deeper nested entries to the npm `package-lock.json` when the agent directory is reached through a symlink, such as `~/.pi` linked into a dotfiles repository. PiG now passes the resolved real path to npm as `--prefix` (or `--cwd` for Bun). <!-- fix: b7d9b2b676 -->
- Bedrock requests no longer fail when `strict: "prefer"` tools exceed Claude's strict tool limits, such as more than 16 optional parameters across all strict tools. The request is sent once more with the preferred tools non-strict while `strict: "require"` tools stay strict, as the Anthropic provider already does, and the reply carries a `bedrock_strict_tools_fallback` diagnostic. Ports Pi's #11416. <!-- fix: d2dafd770b -->
- Replacing the editor component with `ctx.ui.setEditorComponent()` while an extension dialog is open no longer closes a model selector shown over that dialog. <!-- fix: d50faf0882 -->
- Stored assistant messages of a durable conversation now carry `thinkingLevel`: a generation records the thinking level its request asked for on the response, also after polling a deferred one. A poll checkpoint written by an earlier version has no level and records none. <!-- fix: d7fbf0046b -->
- Display math (`$$...$$`, `\[...\]`) wider than the Markdown content width renders as its raw LaTeX source, which wraps like text, instead of wrapping each row of the 2D layout on its own and splitting fractions and sums apart. Layouts that fit render as before. Ports Pi's `latexBlock` width check. <!-- fix: d991498611 -->
- Tool search ranks a tool first when the query is its name, with `-` and other non-identifier characters read as `_` and the `mcp__app__` prefix optional (`thread_read` and `app__thread_read` name `mcp__app__thread_read`). Before, BM25 length normalization could rank a tool with a short description sharing the name's words above it. <!-- fix: e16cbbaf76 -->
- F1-F12 are recognized when the terminal reports them with the Kitty keyboard protocol: `CSI P`/`Q`/`S` and `CSI 1;<mod> P`/`Q`/`S` for F1, F2 and F4, and a modifier on any F-key such as `CSI 15;5~` for Ctrl+F5, so shortcuts bound to `f1` or `ctrl+f5` fire and `parseKey` names them. Releases and repeats of F1, F2 and F4 are no longer taken for presses. F13-F35 and the other Kitty functional keys in the Private Use Area are dropped instead of inserting invisible characters into the prompt. Ports Pi's `matchesKey`, `parseKey`, `isKeyRelease`, `isKeyRepeat` and `decodeKittyPrintable` changes. <!-- fix: eaa4ed7eaa -->
- `pig install`, `pig remove` and `pig update --extensions` run npm with `--no-audit --no-fund`, wherever they already pass `--legacy-peer-deps`, so npm no longer prints audit advice that, followed in the managed package root, would install the host-provided pi packages a second time. bun and pnpm arguments are unchanged. <!-- fix: f6575ff088 -->
- The Node SQLite driver keeps the 256 most recently used prepared statements per connection instead of every statement it ever prepared, closing the evicted ones, so callers that generate SQL of unbounded shapes no longer grow it without bound. <!-- fix: f8d96b7ffdf1f68f073d74128dffd9fedfa3a060 -->
- A Kitty image in a padded or colored box, or with text beside it, is no longer dropped from the fullscreen view once its first row scrolls above the viewport: the visible rows are cropped. <!-- fix: 72e0ca2b6b -->
- Gemini tool schemas send string and number `const` values as single-value `enum`s, which Gemini honors where it ignores `const`; literal data such as `default` and `examples` is left as written. <!-- fix: 9d02a488f0 -->
- `pig install /abs/path` (and `~/path` or a `file://` URL) records the path as you typed it in `packages[]`. It was stored relative to the agent directory as spelled at install, so a later start through another spelling of `PIG_HOME` (a symlinked `~/.local/share/...` directory, a synced config) resolved it to nothing and the Package's tools disappeared with only a stderr line. A relative path is still stored relative to the settings directory. Running `pig install <absolute path>` again rewrites an existing entry for the same Package (D215, #389). <!-- fix: 7e160533d7 -->
- A configured local Package whose directory does not exist is now a startup warning in the session, and an extension warning for programs that embed PiG, with the path it resolved to and the `pig remove` command that drops it, instead of a `[pig] Could not install ... (run pig update when online)` line on stderr (D215, #389). <!-- fix: 7e160533d7, 9a388567fd -->
- `pig install --validate-only [--json]` with no source now checks every local-path entry of `packages[]` (user and trusted project settings): it names each one whose directory does not exist with the path it resolved to and the `pig remove` command that drops it, and exits 1 when any is missing. Before, a Package whose folder was gone passed unnoticed (D216, #389). <!-- fix: b368be57f5 -->
- `chord/nextnode/plugins`: a failed build's empty `errors` list reaches the Node host as `[]` as in Pi, and a proxy script for a Go core facet whose name has `<`, `>` or `&` is written as `JSON.stringify` writes it. <!-- fix: a9d41edbb7 -->
- `chord/nextnode/plugins`: a build error's column is esbuild's own (in bytes), as Pi prints it, where it was counted in UTF-16 units after non-ASCII text. <!-- fix: e5b8ad5546 -->
- `chord/nextnode/plugins`: a `NodeMember.Value` read that is waiting when the Node process dies returns the process's exit alone, not also a cancellation nobody asked for. <!-- fix: e5b8ad5546 -->
- `chord/nextnode/plugins`: the references and watches held for the bridged proxies are released when the Node process ends; a `Close` past its deadline still stops a starting spare; a process running its host's close (Pi ends every object at once, then drains and closes them one by one, each step bounded by `closeTimeout`) is not killed before one `closeTimeout` plus the grace has passed. <!-- fix: 3b9bd165af -->
- `chord/nextnode/plugins`: finding Node stops a version probe that does not answer (10 s) and ends at `ReadyTimeout`; fnm's default directories (including `~/Library/Application Support/fnm` on macOS and `%APPDATA%\fnm` on Windows), and Volta's and mise's installs, are searched, and their shims are never run (D221). <!-- fix: 3b9bd165af -->
- `chord/next/link`: `Channel.Idle` returns when the channel closes. <!-- fix: 3b9bd165af -->
- A cross-harness agent plugin skill whose `description` is long in bytes but at most 1024 characters (for example 600 CJK characters) is no longer dropped from the package's skills. The limit counts UTF-16 units like Pi's skill validation, so 513 astral characters are over it. <!-- fix: f08ffe97f4 -->
- A provider that an extension registers while it loads no longer fails the load when the model registry rejects it. The host asked the registry at once and reported `Failed to load extension: Provider x, model y: no "api" specified.`, with the `pig -ne` hint. Pi queues the registration and applies it after every extension has loaded. PiG now does the same: the extension stays loaded, the other registrations apply, and startup reports `Error: Extension "<path>" error: Provider x, model y: no "api" specified. Set it at model level or provider level.` as Pi does. A registration that an extension makes after it loaded still applies at once and returns its error to the extension. <!-- fix: 0adc7a61525beab8efd166cbca49895faf45ecd6 -->
- A `Provider` object that an extension registers while it loads is now applied after every extension has loaded, like a provider configuration, instead of at once. When the model registry rejects a registration, PiG now leaves nothing of it behind: the login it declared, its entry in the model list that extensions read, and its claim on the provider are given back, so a registration of the same provider by another extension stays as it was. Pi's registry validates a registration before it stores anything of it. <!-- fix: 3a0d0e17113b94d441248a87aa867ca135e7fcf1 -->
- An extension that exits while it loads, sits idle or shuts down no longer leaves the host waiting on its socket: on Windows a socket close can miss a pending read, and the host now ends the read when the extension's process exits, reporting the same transport error as a closed socket. <!-- fix: 108cb7d911 -->
- A Go program that embeds PiG and also links a reflection consumer such as protobuf is no longer about 6 MB larger because of `durable/internal/ordered`: its field metadata embedded `reflect.Type` anonymously, which promoted `MethodByName` onto it and made the linker keep every exported method of every reachable type; the field is now named. <!-- fix: a222037a72 -->
- A native Provider object an extension registers (`registerNativeProvider`, `pi.registerProvider(provider)`) whose models declare no `baseUrl` now reaches the model catalog, as in Pi: the host composes the Provider object untouched, so its models keep the base URL they declare (or none) and its name, models and streams work. Before, such a provider never composed (no models, its name replaced by its id, every stream an error), and a provider-level `baseUrl` was copied onto its models, which Pi does not do (it is only the context of `refreshModels`). <!-- fix: 286d303e8f -->
- A tool card whose call and result are both known when it is first drawn, as after resuming a session or when a tool finishes before the card is drawn, now runs an extension's `renderCall` before its `renderResult`, as Pi does, so a result renderer that reads state its call renderer wrote (`context.state`) sees it. The host sent the two renders to the extension at the same moment and the extension could run them in either order (between 47 and 153 of 300 such cards in a Go SDK test), in every SDK and in Node. It now sends a card's renders one at a time in the order the card asked; a call render that fails, or that the renderer inactivity boundary abandons, holds its result render back for that request only (D56). <!-- fix: 8bf083217b -->
- Tool rows and streamed answers no longer highlight the same code again on every redraw. A running codemode row highlighted its whole script on every progress update and timer tick, and a complete `write` row its whole file on every update and expand toggle. Rows now keep their last highlighting until the code, the theme or the loaded grammars change, a Markdown component keeps the highlighting of the code blocks it rendered until `Invalidate`, and `Text.SetText` with unchanged text keeps its wrapped lines (Pi #10971). <!-- fix: edf18625cb3180d511ef55ce83d4c48925b94d0f -->
- RPC mode now acts on an extension's `ctx.shutdown()` while idle, for example from a timer, instead of waiting for the next command. A request made during startup (for example from `session_start`) is handled once input is attached, and a shutdown requested by an extension command waits until the command's `prompt` response is written. Pi 1.5.0 behaves as before; PiG follows Pi main 1708b4788 (Pi #11599, D231). <!-- fix: 0cced6a687 -->
- `coding/extension/host/subprocess`: in a Host with two or more extension connections (a packed runtime cell or several isolated extensions), a Go, Python, Rust or Lisp handler that held `ctx.signal` and then called `ctx.abort()` could find the signal it held still live while a new read of `ctx.signal` was aborted. The Host numbers each run once for every connection, and a connection's sync that had read the end of the previous run could apply that older state after another connection's sync had numbered the new run, so the live run was numbered again and the runtime replaced the signal the handler held. The Host now reads the run under the lock that numbers it. A Host with one extension connection never raced, and a Node runtime aborts the signal it holds itself. <!-- fix: 4a70ed5306, a3a71c520c -->
- A Node extension that fails to start or crashes no longer dies without saying why. The runtime wrote its error to stderr and exited in the same turn, and because PiG reads that stderr through a pipe, Node could drop a long message (a stack trace past the pipe's 64 KiB buffer) before it was sent. The runtime now exits once the message has been written. <!-- fix: e231cc8441 -->
- Validating arguments against a recursive schema whose object alternatives all reject a deeply nested value no longer takes exponential time: the call is rejected with its errors at once. <!-- fix: 3d980815b1 -->
- A `models.json` number that is not an integer and also below the minimum of an integer field (for example `inputLimits.images.resize.maxBytes: 0.5`) is now reported with both errors, `must be integer` and `must be >= 1`, as Pi's TypeBox validation lists them. Pig listed only `must be integer`. <!-- fix: 2b8731afaf6a9136dd0b24aac9c9c162753fed90 -->
- The eval harness's `submit_documentation_audit` tool declares its `verdict` as Pi's documentation audit does, a union of the three literals (`anyOf` of `{"type":"string","const":...}`), where PiG sent a string enum; the whole schema is exactly what Pi's TypeBox writes. <!-- fix: 23841dce31 -->
- A tool schema built with `ai.StringEnum`, and the schemas of the eval harness's custom tools, reach every provider with their members in the order the author wrote them, as Pi sends them: `{"type":"string","enum":[...]}` and properties in declaration order, where PiG sorted them by name for the Anthropic, OpenAI (completions and responses), Azure, Mistral, Google and Bedrock requests. `ai.StringEnum` returns an ordered schema object and shares the caller's enum slice, as Pi does. <!-- fix: 5d4c43241b -->
- An extension served in-process now refuses to serve a second connection while it serves one, with the error `this extension is already serving a connection; an Extension serves one connection at a time, so build a new one per connection`. A second serve of the same `sdk.Extension` used to overwrite the first one's state and leave the second host waiting for a registration that never came. <!-- fix: bb3d6619673bfea35715c93dd637b2c7bb98dd67 -->
- The Lisp SDK reads a Windows path as one: `with-file-mutation-queue` no longer sends the host the working directory followed by a drive-lettered path, which shared no queue with the host or another SDK, and `agent-session-runtime-import-from-jsonl` finds a session file given by its Windows path instead of looking for `/D:\...\D:\...`. <!-- fix: 7c936f9107 -->
- A Python or Rust extension no longer fails to load when the host releases one of its listeners between registering it and marking it ready (`expected ready, got notify`). A listener that unsubscribes itself while the host dispatches to it during the load is released by an `events.release` notice once that dispatch ends, which can come before `ready`; the Go SDK already served it, and the Python and Rust SDKs now do the same. <!-- fix: 462b96e762 -->
- A Rust extension that registers a flag after load (`Context::register_flag` from a handler) now reads its default through `Context::get_flag` before any value is set, as the Go, Node, Python and Lisp SDKs do and as Pi's `registerFlag` does. The Rust SDK kept flag defaults only from the load-time snapshot, so a flag registered later read `None`. <!-- fix: 8cfd25fa193ba8d5532b07c9900aea1adcae6514 -->
- A shutdown that reaches an extension after it registered and before the host marked it ready now ends its run the same way in every SDK. The Go, Rust and Python SDKs returned an error (`expected ready message, got shutdown`), so an extension process exited non-zero and a packed runner failed because one member's run failed, and the Lisp SDK ignored the frame until the host closed the socket. All five SDKs, and the Node runtime that already did, answer the listener dispatches they read before the shutdown, close their end of the connection and return no error. A shutdown read while the factory's listener subscription or a factory-time host call waits no longer ends that call: the call returns, the extension registers and then ends. <!-- fix: 9841da6f6d -->
- The SDK `DefaultResourceLoader` lists a tool or flag that two extensions register as an error of the extension load result (`Tool "x" conflicts with <path>`), and an extension it loads from `additionalExtensionPaths` has the source `cli`, as Pi's loader reports them. <!-- fix: 8620e9eac5 -->
- The Rust, Python and Lisp extension SDKs now recognize F1-F12 reported with the Kitty keyboard protocol, as the Go SDK and Pi do: `CSI P`/`Q`/`S` and `CSI 1;<mod> P`/`Q`/`S` for F1, F2 and F4, and a modifier on any F-key such as `CSI 15;5~` for Ctrl+F5. Their `matchesKey("f5", ...)`-style checks match `ctrl+f5` and `shift+f4`, `parseKey` names the keys, `isKeyRelease` and `isKeyRepeat` accept `:3` and `:2` on `P`/`Q`/`S`, and `decodeKittyPrintable` returns nothing for the Kitty functional-key Private Use Area instead of an invisible character. The pi-tui bulk vectors (`test/parity/sdk-bulk`), generated from an older pi-tui, are regenerated from the pinned Pi build, so the Go SDK tests no longer assert that `\x1b[P` is no key. Ports Pi's `keys.ts` F-key changes to the Rust, Python and Lisp SDKs. <!-- fix: 51c8f1cb12, 9fbcd3b82e, 2768108d4b -->
- A Lisp extension no longer ignores an `events.dispatch` request that the host sends after registration and before `ready`: the request was read and dropped, so the host waited for an answer that never came. The Lisp SDK now answers it once, under its own request ID, with its own payload, as the Go, Rust, Python and Node SDKs do. <!-- fix: fa0eadbe18 -->
- A Go extension that is sent an `events.dispatch` request while it loads, before the host's `ready`, no longer answers it under another frame's ID with another frame's payload. The listener's goroutine shared the receive loop's envelope variable, which the next received frame (a second dispatch, or `ready`) overwrote while the listener ran; `go test -race` flagged the read and the write. Each listener now keeps the request that started it. <!-- fix: 7475a64e35 -->
- `pig status` and `pig status --json` no longer print the credentials of a configured Package source. A git URL with a user and token, or a secret query parameter, appeared in the Package errors and the resource items; status now names such a URL as Pi's bug report does, without them, and a settings syntax error no longer quotes the text of the file around it. <!-- fix: 316eac6c4b, cf3c76d945 -->
- A Piglet Binary's Node extension archive can no longer write outside the directory it is extracted into. The extraction checked link names as text, but the kernel resolves `z/..` through a link `z`, so a link such as `z/../z/../..` passed the check while resolving above the directory, and a later archive member under it was written there. The extraction now writes through `os.Root`, refuses a member whose path passes through a link the archive wrote, and accepts only a link target that climbs (`..`) before it names anything; the check reads the tree on disk, so a file system that folds case cannot reach a link by another spelling, and a link target holding `:` is refused. `pig piglet build` refuses the same links instead of embedding them. <!-- fix: b22120fdb8, 9155fc460c -->
- A failed install-receipt write during `pig update` or install, such as one rejected because the update CA file is not owner-only, no longer keeps its staged `.install-receipt-*` temp file open. The handle is closed before the temp file is removed, so no stray file is left on Windows. <!-- fix: 80b912a3e28ac5f240428eba73fb72f96c5557e1 -->
- A hung-up terminal now leaves exactly one `exit.log` line, and its exit status stays 129. The kernel's SIGHUP, the input reader's EOF and a failed terminal write each recorded an ending of their own and raced `os.Exit`, so a hangup wrote three lines or two lines without the signal's, never the one line D102 promises. The first path now owns the record and names the first cause observed (`received SIGHUP` when pig leads its session, `terminal gone` when it runs under a shell); the line is flushed before the process exits; a second dead-terminal exit blocks behind the first, as Pi's `emergencyTerminalExit` never returns; and no other exit overtakes a running one. Run's error return and an extension's `ctx.shutdown()` claim the same line (D102). <!-- fix: 3d3f4215ac, c680df851c -->
- An interactive session ended by SIGINT now always exits 130 and leaves its `exit.log` line. The handler was installed only after the first screen was drawn, so a SIGINT in that window killed the session by the default action with no line, and once installed it also asked the session to unwind, which let the process exit 0 before the handler's own exit 130. The handler now goes in first, as Pi registers its signal handlers first in `init()`, and it ends the process without unwinding the session. <!-- fix: f0a9d013e1 -->
- Lower- and upper-casing in `tui`, `internal/codingagent` and `internal/nodespawn` keeps a lone UTF-16 surrogate unchanged, as JavaScript's `toLowerCase` and `toUpperCase` do. `"a\uD800b"` stays `"a\uD800b"` instead of gaining three U+FFFD, so two environment names that differ only in a lone surrogate are no longer merged by the Windows environment-name dedupe, and a Σ beside a lone surrogate is lowered as beside any other non-letter. <!-- fix: d71c4e2361a786ef887fe84b9d68fd1674b6942a -->
- A glob filter, model scope or other `internal/minimatch` pattern with a numeric brace range beyond 2^53 expands as Pi's brace-expansion 5.0.12 does, in JavaScript number arithmetic: `x{99999999999999999999..99999999999999999999}` matches `x100000000000000000000` and no longer `x57`, and `x{9007199254740993..9007199254740995}` matches `x9007199254740992`. <!-- fix: d71c4e2361a786ef887fe84b9d68fd1674b6942a -->
- `pig status` no longer reports a shared extension name as an unhealthy duplicate. Two Packages that both expose `src/index.ts` resolve to the same `"src"` public name, and the loader identifies an extension by its path: it renames the later copies (`"src:2"`) and loads them all, as Pi loads every extension path. The report keeps them enabled and moves the finding to a new `warnings` list, so `pig status` exits 0 and `pig status --json` stays `"healthy": true`. Skills, prompts and themes key their runtime set by name, so their duplicates remain errors. <!-- fix: ad49f9f02e -->
- A tool with JSON-schema constrained sampling `strict: "require"` now fails an OpenAI Chat Completions request with `Tool "<name>" requires JSON-schema constrained sampling, but strict tools are unsupported.` when the model's compat does not enable strict mode, as under Pi. It was sent as an ordinary function tool instead. `prefer` is unchanged. <!-- fix: be2920a2f3 -->
- The Lisp and Python extension SDKs now give each `onThemeChange` handler the theme of its own change, in order, as the Go and Rust SDKs do. They delivered one live theme object to handlers that run on a worker thread, so a handler that ran after the host had switched themes again read the newer palette: two quick changes reached their subscribers as the newer theme twice instead of the second and the third theme, and the Lisp SDK test `theme-and-tools-expanded-changes-reach-their-subscribers-in-order` reported that on a loaded machine in up to a quarter of its runs. Each delivery now carries a snapshot taken with its palette; `ctx.ui.theme` stays live. A new conformance row, `TestOnThemeChangeDeliversEachChangesOwnThemeAcrossSDKs`, holds the first delivery in a gate handler while the host switches themes and requires the handler behind it to log the theme of its own change in every SDK. <!-- fix: 2c3897fdfa, fecee913ad, b3c3d66b4b -->
- Automatic `fd` and `rg` downloads no longer fetch x86-64 binaries on ARM32 and other architectures without a prebuilt release. PiG now warns and recommends installing the tool with the system package manager. <!-- fix: fdbd6ca4f0 -->
- A user message, a branch or compaction summary, a custom message, a skill invocation, the startup changelog, the `/hotkeys` block, the text a slash command appends and an extension's Markdown view no longer keep the memos a streamed Markdown holds for its next delta. They arrive whole and never call `FinishStreaming`, so the wraps, inline renderings and resume point stayed for the life of the message: a 1.2 KB user message retained 17.5 KB, and a transcript of 10,000 of them about 175 MB. Each now finishes its Markdown when it builds it: a user message keeps 9.2 KB (its 6.1 KB of padded, colored rows are the rest) and a boxed message 16 to 18 KB instead of 21 to 23 KB. The rows are unchanged. <!-- fix: 21c27bf578, 6c29071cad -->
- A terminal read that ends inside a UTF-8 character and holds every byte of it no longer restarts the ESC timer, as in Pi, where Node emits no data event for it. ESC, then the two bytes of é arriving 5 ms and 11 ms later, is Escape followed by é, not Alt+é. <!-- fix: 3c2dde41465506033cf266e06e988c6bfa8f7f3f -->
- Text typed and followed at once by Enter no longer skips the autocomplete menu Pi opens: `/model provider/id` typed and entered in one go switched the model in PiG, where Pi accepts the suggestion into the editor on the first Enter and switches on the second (the same holds for `/thinking level`, any command with argument completions, and a partially typed slash command, which Pi accepts and submits). Pi's editor resolves its autocomplete request in the Promise jobs that follow the terminal read that typed the text, so the menu is open when the next read arrives; PiG started the request on a worker and published the menu through two later owner-loop tasks that the Enter overtook, so the Enter found no menu and submitted what was typed. The editor now starts the request of a read when the read has been handled (`Editor.FlushAutocomplete`, called by the interactive loop after each read), and an Enter in the same read as the text still submits it, as in Pi. Typed at human speed both behaved like Pi already. <!-- fix: 58f6697aa5 -->
- On Windows, a custom theme edited in a rapid burst of writes no longer stays on a stale version. A burst that overflowed the native change buffer made the watcher treat the overflow as a failure and close its watch, so writes after the overflow were never seen and the theme kept an older version of the file (seen as `accent="#123456" want="#000064"` in Windows CI, only while the machine was loaded). An overflow now reloads the theme file, as Pi reloads on a change without a filename, and the watcher keeps watching; any other watch failure still closes it, as in Pi. <!-- fix: 8a88c34d51 -->
- The alternate screen's viewport accessors (`ViewportTop`, `IsFollowingOutput`, `ScrollBy`, `ScrollToTop`, `ScrollToBottom`) read the layout of the last frame under the renderer's lock. An extension's `tuiAlt` host call reads them from its own goroutine while a frame stores a new layout, and the race detector reported the Python SDK's conformance row. <!-- fix: 7db4e68fc4 -->
- A session with an extension that registers a markdown transformer no longer crashes while an assistant reply streams. The transformer runs on a background worker, and its completion rebuilt the reply's content from that worker while the interface was streaming the next delta into the same reply, so both could rebuild it at once and the next frame panicked in `Container.renderChildLocked` with a nil child. A finished transform now only marks the reply for redraw, as it already did for a user message, and the interface rebuilds the reply on its own loop. <!-- fix: c5ea0d127b, d0d459e754 -->
- Terminal input bytes decode as Node's StringDecoder does, as Pi's `stdin.setEncoding("utf8")` reads them: a trailing C0, C1, F5-F7, or an E0, ED, F0 or F4 lead followed by an out-of-range byte is held until the next read instead of becoming U+FFFD at once, so a mouse report ending in such a byte is no longer taken as a wheel scroll. <!-- fix: c7b91e7cb9ac4939eeef016dd25ca4b009a2c022 -->
- A session with an extension that registers a markdown transformer no longer crashes while an assistant reply streams. The transformer runs on a background worker, and its completion rebuilt the reply's content from that worker while the interface was streaming the next delta into the same reply, so both could rebuild it at once and the next frame panicked in `Container.renderChildLocked` with a nil child. A finished transform now only marks the reply for redraw, as it already did for a user message, and the interface rebuilds the reply on its own loop. <!-- fix: ecc7b7683c, a654570024 -->
- On Windows, stopping a terminal reader whose input is a pipe no longer hangs. The reader waited on the input handle for input, but a pipe handle reads as ready whether or not input is queued, so a reader over a pipe went into a read that cancellation could not end, and `Stop`, shutdown and an external-editor handoff waited on it for good (seen as a 30 minute `internal/codingagent` test timeout in Windows CI). A pipe is now waited on in a zero-byte read, as Node's libuv does, which takes no input and which cancelling the reader ends, so a cancelled reader returns at once and leaves later input to the next reader. A console, which `pig` itself reads, is waited on as before. <!-- fix: f9648c6fd5, 0869584873 -->
- The renderer's width and height are read through one atomic snapshot. An overlay's visibility callback, an overlay control call and a mouse event on the alt screen read the two numbers from their own goroutines while a frame stored a new terminal size, so during a resize they could see the width of one size and the height of another, and the race detector reported the conformance rows of the alt screen. <!-- fix: c98be55c62 -->
- Fullscreen double-click selection no longer splits paths and tokens at `~`, `.`, `\`, `+` and `_`: the word characters are iTerm2 defaults. <!-- fix: bfae6a0816 -->
- In the alt-screen, a wheel scroll reported in the legacy X10 mouse form (terminals without SGR mouse mode) no longer shows up as typed text when the pointer is at column or row 95 or higher; the report is counted in UTF-16 units as Pi counts it, so it scrolls. <!-- fix: 06cb94f85e -->
- `PI_TUI_ESC_TIMEOUT` now waits as Node's `setTimeout` does for the lone-Escape timer: a fractional value is truncated, and a value under one millisecond or over 2147483647 waits one millisecond instead of that many nanoseconds or about a month. <!-- fix: fe4bd27863 -->
- On Windows, a session replacement whose working directory differs from the previous one only in letter case (`c:\work\proj` after `C:\Work\Proj`) keeps the loaded Node extension factories instead of dropping them and re-running every module, as Pi does (#11588). <!-- fix: 5af3a1803d -->
- After `pig update --models`, OpenRouter's `:nitro` and `:floor` routing variants no longer disappear from `--list-models`, the model selector, `/scoped-models`, RPC `get_available_models` and the SDK lists. The refreshed list replaces the bundled OpenRouter list, and the variants were derived from the bundled models only; they are now derived from whichever list is current (D199). <!-- fix: cb20ec03cd, d58e454dd9 -->

### Security

- In PiG 0.4.0 through 0.5.3, a Piglet's `tools` lists (the root list and the `tools` of an extension entry) removed tools from the model's active set only. A tool that a `codemode` script can call (a tool exposed as `codemode` or `deferred`) stayed callable from `codemode` scripts, and `tool_search` could still find and load it, although the Piglet did not list it. `codemode` and `tool_search` first shipped in 0.4.0, and a Piglet limited tools by name from 0.2.0, so no earlier release is affected. PiG 0.7.0 enforces the scope in the Session tool registry: a tool outside the scope is not registered, so it is not listed, active, callable from `codemode` or findable by `tool_search`, and no later `setActiveTools` call, registration or reload brings it back. A Piglet Binary or a Piglet run with `pig --piglet` gets the fix when you upgrade PiG and rebuild the Binary.

## [0.5.3] - 2026-10-23

### Upgrading

- Go API `durable`: `Storage.Commit` takes an adopt callback, as Pi's `commit(writes, adopt, context)`. Before: `storage.Commit(ctx, writes)`. After: `storage.Commit(ctx, writes, func(seq durable.Seq) {})`. A Storage calls it once, synchronously, when the batch is durable and before its next commit, and never for a commit that fails; a Storage that resolves without calling it fails the Session. Code that wraps or implements Storage must pass it through.
- Go API `durable`, `chord`: `WatchHandle`, `WatchEnd` and the end reasons move to `chord`; `durable.WatchHandle`, `durable.WatchEnd` and the `Watch*` reason constants are aliases of them. The reasons `session_closed` and `session_failed` are now `ended` (`WatchEnded`) and `failed` (`WatchFailed`).
- Go API `durable`: `Session.DocumentStateErased`, `DocumentState`, `DocumentStateOf`, `Conversation.ViewState` and `Harness.TaskGraph` are removed, as in Pi. Use `WatchDoc`, `Conversation.Watch` and `Harness.WatchTaskGraph`; start the watch to keep its value current, and stop it where the state was disposed.
- A document watch ends `retired` only when its document is retired, not on a null value.

### Added

- `durable.HarnessOptions.ReadOnly` opens a Harness as a viewer of a session another process drives: open leaves running tasks as committed instead of recovering them, every commit with writes fails with the new `durable.ReadOnlySession` before it reaches Storage (the Session stays healthy, and a commit that writes nothing succeeds), `Resume()` panics with it and every call that enables scheduling returns it, `Wake()` is always inactive and `OnWake` is never called. Reads, snapshots and watches keep working; reopen without `ReadOnly` to write. Ports Pi's `HarnessOptions.readOnly`.
- `ai.UsageCost.TotalFromProvider` (`usage.cost.totalFromProvider` on the wire) records whether `cost.total` is the billed cost the provider reported or an estimate from the model's catalog rates. Catalog-priced usage writes `false`, an absent value in a recorded session also means `false`, and a combined usage is provider-reported only when both parts are. Ports Pi's `Usage.cost.totalFromProvider`.

### Changed

- The Durable example tests are renumbered as in Pi (`TestExample04Watches` through `TestExample30ReloadAndRestart`); the chord-state example is gone.
- `pig piglet validate` and `pig piglet add` accept `--allow-install-scripts`, which installs a Piglet's Packages with lifecycle scripts for that one command. Migration: a Piglet whose Package needs its install script to produce files must be validated or added with the flag. `pig install`, `pig update` and the other Package commands are unchanged and still run lifecycle scripts, as Pi does.

### Fixed

- A fused Go extension's built-in tool `execute` without an extension context (`createBashTool(cwd).execute(id, params)` and the other `create<Tool>Tool` forms) no longer fails with "extension stopped while waiting for builtinTool.execute response" when another extension in the same process stops while the tool runs. The call has no `Context`, so it was sent over the connection of the first running extension in the process. The host now runs the tool for a fused extension directly, reaching back into the extension in the same process for the functions of its options and its streamed updates. <!-- fix: c47bafd99d -->
- Extensions' `ui_prompt_start` and `ui_prompt_end` notifications are recorded in order when the host is slow to apply the start event's `ctx.ui.notify`: the dialog's answer is no longer let through, and the end event no longer sent, before the handler's own host call has applied. A blocked-on-a-host-call report from an extension runtime admitted the UI prompt drain as soon as it was read, while the call it announced was still queued; the admission now waits for that call. <!-- fix: f0b910f8ca -->
- A fused Go extension's `createLocalBashOperations().exec` (and `createLocalPowerShellOperations`) no longer fails with "extension stopped while waiting for builtinTool.localExec response" when another extension in the same process stops while the command runs; a command past its `timeout` rejects with Pi's `timeout:<seconds>`. The call has no `Context`, so it was sent over the connection of the first running extension in the process, and ended with that extension, whichever made the call. The host now runs the command for a fused extension directly, as it already does for the other helpers that have no `Context`, so the command depends on no extension, as Pi's exec depends on none. <!-- fix: e97346436d -->
- The Piglet JSON Schema that `pig piglet schema` prints rejected `powershell` in `tools`, which `pig piglet validate` accepts as a built-in tool, and stated nothing for most of the other closed vocabulary. It now lists all eight built-in tools, the strip IDs of each strip list, the `agentEnv` runtime modes (`inject`, `image`) and policy presets (`minimal`, `standard`, `elevated`), and carries the parser's name, build target, output name, release version and secret patterns, the required `source` and `target` of a mount, and the rule that `agentEnv` names exactly one of `image`, `devContainer` and `source`. `make piglet-strip-ids` writes the strip ID enums, and tests that read the parser's sets from code fail when the schema and the parser disagree. <!-- fix: 2316fe38fb -->
- OpenRouter turns (the built-in provider and custom providers on OpenRouter's endpoint) now take OpenRouter's reported total as `usage.cost.total` for OpenAI Completions and Anthropic Messages streams, plus the upstream inference cost for a BYOK request, instead of the catalog estimate, and mark it provider-reported. The export HTML header uses the recorded total. Replaces PiG's earlier D124 form of this fix with Pi's. <!-- fix: a9015090a5 -->
- An Anthropic request holds a mid-conversation system update until an assistant message that is actually sent, so an assistant message that converts to no blocks no longer moves the update before a user message. <!-- fix: e5a345eeba -->
- `pig install <source> --validate-only` now validates git and npm sources that are not installed yet. It fetches them into a temporary directory that is removed afterwards, and no longer reports `stat …/git/<host>/<owner>/<repo>: no such file or directory`. Installed packages and settings are not touched. <!-- fix: 871b48d4015ef3e7d99f6581ae3f7fa58698532e -->
- Installing a Package or Piglet from a local `git:file://` source on Windows no longer fails with `fatal: '$GIT_DIR' too big`. A file URL now checks out to `<install root>/localhost/<12 hex of the path's sha256>/<basename>` instead of re-nesting the whole absolute path, which pushed `$GIT_DIR` past Git for Windows' own path limit that `core.longpaths` does not lift. Sources Pi accepts keep Pi's exact layout. A file URL checkout made by an earlier version is not reused and is cloned again. <!-- fix: efded13767cd31c5d180aa24b1eb94a40e5d8696 -->

### Security

- `pig piglet validate` and `pig piglet add` no longer run the lifecycle scripts (`preinstall`, `install`, `postinstall`, `prepare`) of the npm Packages a Piglet names, of their dependencies, of the dependencies of its Git Packages, or of the npm or Git package of a Piglet source. Before, validating or adding a Piglet ran a publisher's `postinstall` before you had looked at it. `pig piglet build` and `pig --piglet` resolve the same way.

## [0.5.2] - 2026-10-22

### Upgrading

- Extensions written in Go, Python or Rust that fell back to a child `pig` process for `createAgentSession({customTools, settingsManager, modelRuntime})` can call the new API. `model` takes a model object, as Pi's option does: resolve a name through `ModelRegistry.Find` first. No existing API changes.
- `HarnessOptions.OnReport` is now `func(err error, info durable.ReportInfo)`, and `durable.TaskRuntime` has `Report(err error, from ...ReportFrom)`: code that sets either must take the new parameter. `harness.Harness` has `RetryTask`.
- A task cut off by a crash 5 times in a row without committing a new state is parked instead of run again; set `HarnessSettings.RestartLimit` to `+Inf` to keep the old behavior. `TaskInspectionState.Reason` can be `restart_limit`.
- If code outside this repository builds `subprocess.CallPayload` with an unkeyed literal, add the two fields (`false` keeps today's behaviour) or switch to keyed fields. `coding.ExtensionHost` gains `SetTimerTurns(*jsloop.Turns)`; an embedder that implements the interface adds a method that does nothing, because `internal/jsloop` is not importable outside the module: it cannot write the parameter type, so such an embedder cannot implement the interface and has no replacement to migrate to. Extensions in every SDK need no change.
- Go API `chord/host`: `Host.Get` and `Ctx.Get` wait until the reference is ready: live, with every state member of its variant. Use `Host.Hold` for the synchronous reference that may still be loading. Before: `ref, _ := host.Get(typ, input, nil)` then `ref.Ready(ctx)`. After: `ref, err := host.Get(typ, input, nil)` for an awaited reference, or `ref, _ := host.Hold(typ, input, nil)` for the old behavior. A failed `Get` releases only its own reference and returns the activation error, `aborted` (`GetOptions.Signal`, or the ctx closing), or `unavailable/ready_timeout` after `HostOptions.ReadyTimeout` (60 s).
- Go API `chord/host`: reading a state member of a reference that is not live yet panics with a `not_ready` ChordError (and `not_in_variant` for a member the variant lacks) where it returned nil. A listener added before the first value gets its snapshot then: the events are `snap`, `ops`, not `snap` with nil, `reset`.
- The Chord link protocol version is 4. A hold implies the state of its variant (`state:false` opts out), state frames are addressed by hold and member (`as: snap | reset | ops | error`, `value`), `sub`, `unsub` and `resync` work per hold, a hold from a client link carries an `origin` the server assigns, and shape frames carry no `codeVersion`. A peer of another version closes the link with `protocol-version`.
- Go API `durable/storage/sqlite`: `Options` is renamed `SqliteStorageOptions`, the name of Pi's type. Before: `sqlite.Open(db, sqlite.Options{WorkingSetBytes: n})`. After: `sqlite.Open(db, sqlite.SqliteStorageOptions{WorkingSetBytes: n})`.
- Go API `durable/storage/sqlite/node`: the connection settings move to `NodeSqliteDatabaseOptions`, and `NodeSqliteStorageOptions` embeds them next to `Prefix` and `WorkingSetBytes`. `OpenNodeSqliteDatabase` takes `NodeSqliteDatabaseOptions`. Before: `OpenNodeSqliteDatabase(path, node.NodeSqliteStorageOptions{BusyTimeoutMs: &ms})`. After: `OpenNodeSqliteDatabase(path, node.NodeSqliteDatabaseOptions{BusyTimeoutMs: &ms})`. A literal of `NodeSqliteStorageOptions` that sets a connection field names the embedded struct (`NodeSqliteStorageOptions{NodeSqliteDatabaseOptions: node.NodeSqliteDatabaseOptions{BusyTimeoutMs: &ms}}`).
- Go API `durable/storage/sqlite/cloudflare`: `DurableObjectSqlCursor` gains `Next() (row, ok, err)`, which returns the next row; a cursor type implements it next to `ToArray`, which then returns the rows not read yet. `OpenDurableObjectSqliteStorage` takes optional `sqlite.SqliteStorageOptions`.
- Go API: `OutputBuffer`, `Progress`, `BoundOutput`, `SanitizeOutput`, `CharacterEnd`, `OutputLimits`, `OutputSlice`, `BoundedOutput` and their helpers move from `durable/harness` to the new package `chord/output`, as Pi 4a5d3729 moves them to `@earendil-works/chord/output`. Before: `harness.NewOutputBuffer(limits)`. After: `output.NewOutputBuffer(limits)`. `PushStringSkipping` and `PushBytesSkipping` take `output.OutputSkip`, which has the fields of `env.ShellOutputSkip`: `output.OutputSkip(skipped)` converts. `Progress`'s clock seam is now exported (`ProgressClock`, `NewProgressWithClock`).
- Go API `ai`: `anthToolResultContent` is internal, but the Anthropic and Bedrock converters now send the images of an error tool result after the tool results of the turn. A caller that read the old note `[image omitted: error tool results cannot contain images]` in an error result sees `(image attached after the tool results)` there and the images in the same user message, after a text block `Images from the error result of tool call <id> (<tool>):`.
- Go API `chord/host`: `CreateHost` needs a principal for the host's own code, as Pi 1.3.0's `createHost({ self })` does, and panics with a `*TypeError` without one. Before: `CreateHost(HostOptions{Name: "server"})`. After: `CreateHost(HostOptions{Name: "server", Self: "host"})`. `HostPrincipal` is gone: PiG no longer makes up principals.
- Go API `chord/host`: `Connect` takes `ConnectOptions` with the principal the parent's own requests act as, and `HostOptions.Upstream` is `&UpstreamOptions{Link: link, ConnectOptions: ConnectOptions{Principal: ...}}`. `Route.Principal` is required. Before: `host.Connect(link, LinkOptions{})`. After: `host.Connect(link, ConnectOptions{Principal: "server"})`.
- Go API `chord/host`: a remote contract says where its objects live and a get no longer names a host. Before: `Remote("t.chat", RemoteDef{...})` and `host.Get(chat, input, &GetOptions{At: &name})`. After: `Remote("t.chat", RemoteDef{..., Host: NewHostFamily("session:", "session")})` and `host.Get(chat, input, nil)`. `GetOptions.At` is gone.
- The Chord link protocol version is 3. A PiG host and a Pi host that speak another version close the link with `protocol-version` and report it through `OnProtocolMismatch`.
- Go SDK: `sdk.AgentToolResult` now marshals as the wire object a tool returns (`content` blocks, `structured_content`, `is_error`) instead of Pi's member names; it was only ever decoded before. Code that marshals it for another purpose should build its own struct.
- Rust SDK: `ExecOptions` has a `signal: Option<ProviderSignal>` field, so a struct literal needs it or `..Default::default()`. Before: `ExecOptions { timeout: Some(250.0), cwd: None }`. After: `ExecOptions { timeout: Some(250.0), ..Default::default() }`. `ProviderSignal` now implements `Debug` and `PartialEq` (two signals are equal when they are the same signal).
- Go SDK `ExecOptions` has a `Signal context.Context` field. Code that builds the struct with named fields is unchanged; an unkeyed literal needs the new field.
- Rust SDK: `pig_sdk::Color` is now `pig_sdk::tui::Color`, so an indexed color is `Color::Indexed(5)` instead of `Color::Indexed { index: 5 }`. `Color::Rgb { r, g, b }`, `Color::Oklch { l, c, h }` and `TextAttributes` are unchanged. The Go SDK's color types are unchanged.
- `ResizedImage` in the Go, Rust and Python SDKs gains `Data`/`data` and `MimeType`/`mime_type`; the Rust struct is no longer `Copy`, and a literal needs `..Default::default()`. `HostInfo` in the host's subprocess package gains `PackageDir` and `Shell`.
- If code outside this repository builds `subprocess.CallPayload` with an unkeyed literal, add a sixth field (`""` keeps today's behaviour) or switch to keyed fields.
- `ai` renames the provider request option `TelemetryContext` to `Telemetry` (Pi `telemetryContext` → `telemetry`, Pi 2ec55d80) on `StreamOptions`, `ClassifierOptions` and `ImagesOptions`, with no alias. Its type is `telemetry.TelemetrySpan`: pass a parent span, not an adapter; nil is the omitted option and uses the no-op span.
- `ai.LazyStream` and `ai.LazyStreamSync` take an optional trailing `LazyStreamObserver` (Pi's `lazyStream(model, setup, observer?)`).
- A Rust extension that calls `ctx.session_name()` receives a `String` instead of a `&str`, and the `session_name` and `model` members of the wire `ReadyMsg` no longer exist (the session name and the model travel in the ready state). A Python or Rust extension that compared `ctx.model` with a model's display name must compare it with the model's id. <!-- fix: 06dc555220 -->
- Rust SDK: a `before_agent_start` handler registers with `Extension::on_before_agent_start` (or `EventSubscriber::on_before_agent_start`) and receives a `BeforeAgentStartEvent` instead of `&mut serde_json::Value`. `Context::current_system_prompt` is removed; the event's `system_prompt()` and `Context::get_system_prompt()` replace it. Before: `ext.on_event_result("before_agent_start", |ctx, data| { data["systemPromptOptions"]["appendSystemPrompt"] = json!("x"); ctx.current_system_prompt(data)?; Ok(None) })`. After: `ext.on_before_agent_start(|ctx, event| { event.edit_system_prompt_options(|options| options["appendSystemPrompt"] = json!("x")); event.system_prompt().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?; Ok(None) })`. `event.payload()` is the host's event without `systemPrompt` and `systemPromptOptions` (`messageType`, `prompt`, `images`, `message`), `event.system_prompt_options()` copies the options, `event.set_system_prompt_options(value)` replaces them, and `event.snapshot()` is the whole event with the prompt and options as they are now. A `before_agent_start` handler still registered through `on_event`, `on_event_result` or `EventSubscriber::on_event` fails each emission with an error that names `on_before_agent_start`. The upgrade rules of `pig extension upgrade` cover Go extensions only, so a Rust extension is rewritten by hand. <!-- fix: 0b6bd6bd45 -->
- Go API `coding/mcpext`: `Host` has a `RegisterTools(definitions []extension.ToolDefinition)` method, which registers a server's tools as one change. A host that has no batch registration can register the definitions one by one. Before: a `Host` implemented `RegisterTool`, `GetAllTools`, `GetActiveTools`, `SetActiveTools` and `GetMcpServers`. After: it also implements `RegisterTools`.
- Go: `ModelRegistry.Find` now returns `(map[string]any, error)`. Receive the error (`model, err := ctx.ModelRegistry().Find(provider, id)`); `nil, nil` still means no model matches, and a failed host call is the error. The SDK upgrade rules name the change (`model-registry-find-returns-error`) but do not rewrite it. <!-- fix: 7abdf5b391 -->
- Rust: `ModelRegistry::find` returns `io::Result<Option<Value>>` instead of `Option<Value>`. Propagate or handle the `Err`; `Ok(None)` means no model matches. <!-- fix: 7abdf5b391 -->
- Python: `ModelRegistry.has_configured_auth` and `is_using_oauth` return `False` for a model with no `provider` instead of raising `KeyError`; drop any `except KeyError` that relied on it. `get_entries()` against a host with no session binding raises instead of returning `None`; do not test its result for `None`. <!-- fix: 7abdf5b391 -->
- If your code declared an `agent.SettleGate` or held an `*agent.SettleSlot` (for example in a tool that settles its own slot through `agent.ToolSettleFromContext`), stop naming the types: keep the value `ToolSettleFromContext` returns in a local variable and call its methods, or drop the call, because a tool that never settles its slot settles it when `Execute` returns. An extension needs no change: extensions in every SDK keep the same order through the wire, not through this type.
- If your code builds an `extension.CallLane` or sets `mcpext.McpToolOptions.Lane`, stop doing so and reserve call order through `ToolDefinition.ReserveCallOrder` with your own `extension.CallOrder` values.
- Extension SDKs (Go, Python, Rust): a dialog returns the JSON value the client answered with, as Pi's does, instead of a string or a bool. Go: `Context.Select`, `Context.SelectWithOptions`, `Context.Input`, `Context.InputWithOptions` and `Context.Editor` return `(any, bool, error)`, and `Context.Confirm` and `Context.ConfirmWithOptions` return `(any, error)`. Before: `choice, ok, err := ctx.Select(t, opts); if choice == "Execute" {...}`. After: `answer, ok, err := ctx.Select(t, opts); choice, _ := answer.(string)`. A cancelled dialog returns `nil` where it returned `""`, and `Confirm` returns `false` when cancelled. Rust: `select`, `input` and `editor` return `(serde_json::Value, bool)` and `confirm` returns `serde_json::Value`; read a string with `value.as_str()`, a boolean with `== json!(true)`; cancelled is `Value::Null`. Python: `select`, `input` and `editor` return `(Any, bool)`, `confirm` returns `Any`; the value is a `str` for a client that follows Pi's protocol, and a cancelled dialog's value is `None` where it was `""`. Node is unchanged. The host and every SDK change together; there is no negotiation.

### Added

- Child agent sessions in the Go, Python and Rust extension SDKs: `ctx.CreateAgentSession(sdk.CreateAgentSessionOptions{...})`, `ctx.create_agent_session(CreateAgentSessionOptions(...))` and `ctx.create_agent_session(CreateAgentSessionOptions { .. })` are Pi's `createAgentSession`. The host builds the child session over the parent's model runtime, so providers the parent registered reach it; `customTools` run in the extension that passed them; in-memory `settings` turn compaction off. The session has `prompt`, `steer`, `follow_up`, `abort`, `bind_extensions`, `state`, `messages`, `subscribe` and `dispose`, and ends with the extension's connection (its run is aborted and it is disposed). Calls block as Pi's Promises resolve: `prompt` returns once the run settled and every listener saw its last event. Node extensions already called Pi's own implementation. <!-- fix: cc584f5b -->
- The conformance rows for child sessions assert Pi's own observation, not PiG's: Node rows run Pi's `createAgentSession` through the sentinel, model-error and abort-mid-tool scenarios, and the Go (isolated, packed, fused), Python and Rust rows assert the same event lists, transcript roles, leading system message and error messages (`test/extension-conformance/testdata/child-session-want.json`). <!-- fix: 304bd443 -->
- `output.OutputBuffer.Push(chunk, skipped)` takes a string or bytes chunk and an optional skipped-output record in one call, as Pi's `OutputBuffer.push` does.
- Durable crash-loop guard (Pi `a30c2a81`): open counts each task that a crash, eviction, or reset cut off (`TaskRecord.Restarts`); a close writes the tasks it stopped back as `pending` without a count, and a new state the task commits starts the count over. At `HarnessSettings.RestartLimit` (default 5; `+Inf` never parks) the task is parked: blocked with reason `restart_limit` in `Inspect` and the task graph, not active in `Wake`, and reported once. `Harness.RetryTask` runs it again. An abort handler cut off that many times ends its task `faulted` with detail `{reason: "restart_limit"}`. Both Durable engines (the reference Harness and the core) implement it.
- `OnReport` receives a second argument, `durable.ReportInfo`, that says what the report is about: `session_failed`, `task_faulted`, `task_parked`, `migration_failed`, `task_outdated`, `task_error`, `extension_error`, `host_error` or `listener_error`, with the task, the extension that installed its definition, the failing host callback, or the conversation. `TaskRuntime.Report` takes an optional `durable.ReportFrom` to report extension or host code a task called.
- `HarnessSettings.AfterFailedRun`: a run that fails with `model_error` or `no_model` keeps the inputs queued behind it (`keep`, the default), starts the next run with them (`continue`), or settles them `unanswered` with reason `run_failed` (`withdraw`).
- The task graph shows why a task cannot run (`TaskGraphNode.Blocked`: `missing_task`, `task_too_old`, `migration_failed`, `restart_limit`) and follows registry changes and failed migrations. A registry change that unblocks a task makes `OnWake` report the Session active.
- Headless MCP (#214): package `coding/mcpext` no longer imports the terminal UI. The `/mcp` manager view and the tool renderers moved to `coding/mcpext/mcptui`, and the `pig` binary wires them through `mcpext.Options.Terminal` (`mcptui.Terminal()`), so its output is unchanged. `mcpext.NewHeadless` is the headless entry point. Package `mcp` links no terminal UI; `coding/mcpext` still links it through `coding/extension` (see `docs/design/extension-api-tui-split.md`). `mcpext.McpManagerView`, `NewMcpManagerView` and `CreateMcpToolRenderers` moved to `mcptui`; `McpMenu.Items` is now `[]McpMenuItem`.
- `ai.ClientIdentity`, as pi-ai's `ClientIdentity`, chooses a request's `User-Agent` (detailed with a version, short, or custom) and provider attribution headers for OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM and OpenCode. `StreamOptions.Identity`, `ClassifierOptions.Identity`, `ImagesOptions.Identity` and `CreateModelsOptions.Identity` carry it, `ai.MergeClientIdentity` merges identities field by field, and `ai.WithClientIdentity` gives a models object a default identity. Attribution is off by default in `ai` and on by default in the agent loop (`agent.DefaultAgentIdentity`, `AgentOptions.Identity`) and the durable Harness (`HarnessOptions.Identity`).
- Models and the coding Model Runtime add `x-opencode-session` for custom providers pointing at OpenCode, not only for the built-in OpenCode providers.
- `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` is in the catalog for the `minimax` and `minimax-cn` providers. Thinking levels low through max go out as `output_config.effort` with adaptive thinking, and thinking cannot be turned off for this model. New MiniMax models from models.dev now appear without a manual allowlist entry; only the older M2, M2.1, M2.5 and M2.5-highspeed models stay hidden (Pi d2e7d8b7, #11121).
- `HarnessOptions.Telemetry` emits the content-free `harness.DurableTelemetrySchema` (Pi 2ec55d80): public submission admission spans (`pi.durable.submit`), task phase spans (`pi.durable.phase`, including extension tasks), committed entry and submission events, running phase-change checkpoint events, nested-tool replay events, report events and counters, and the `pi.durable.phase.duration` and `pi.durable.tasks.active` metrics. Failed phases record the fixed categories `task_faulted`, `task_failed` and `task_orphaned` with a diagnostic capped at 500 characters; an aborted outcome keeps status ok.
- `durable.TaskOptions.Trace` (a carrier, or `durable.TaskTrace{Root: true}`) and `TaskOptions.Links` choose a task's stored trace carrier and creation-time links; absence inherits the creator's carrier.
- PiG detects the Rex terminal (`TERM_PROGRAM=rex`) and uses OSC 8 hyperlinks and true color there (and, since Pi 396ecd7b, Kitty images; see the later entry). The check runs before the Kitty variables, so a leaked `KITTY_WINDOW_ID` does not turn images on (Pi 0ed1b043, #11131).
- `chord/telemetrysqlite` ports Pi's `@earendil-works/chord/telemetry-sqlite`: `CreateSqliteTelemetry(db, options)` records settled spans with inline events and links and metrics aggregated per series per ten seconds into any `chord/sqlite` database, flushes once a second with retention cleanup, bounds its queue (counting `DroppedSpans` and `DroppedMeasurements`), and serves `telemetry.TelemetryStore` queries over the committed rows.
- `chord/host`: one shared binding per host and key for remote references. References to one object share one hold, one snapshot per member and one frame per change. `HostOptions.Linger` keeps a released binding for a time (cap 4), `GetOptions.State` false gives a method-only reference, and a re-hold after a link loss keeps the last values readable.
- `chord/host`: a local object goes live only with its state, also where it forwards or derives from a remote reference's member; activation and a reload's prepare wait at most `HostOptions.ReadyTimeout` and name what they wait for.
- `chord/host`: `LinkOptions.PendingCap` bounds the state ops that wait for a slow peer on one link (default 4 windows). Beyond it the oldest streams are replaced by their current value, and a relay asks the provider for a reset.
- `durable/storage/sqlite`: `SqliteStorageOptions.Prefix` namespaces every table and index of the SQLite storage, for a database shared with host tables (Pi f7e3cb54). `node.OpenNodeSqliteStorage` and `cloudflare.OpenDurableObjectSqliteStorage` forward it; an invalid prefix (not an identifier, or starting with `sqlite_`) fails before the database is created. The default names are unchanged, and changing the prefix does not migrate existing data.
- `chord/output`: the Go counterpart of `@earendil-works/chord/output`, with `OutputSkip` and `Utf8ByteLength`. `durable.Utf8ByteLength` calls it.
- `ai.SplitErrorToolResultImages` and `ai.SplitErrorToolResult`: split an error tool result into a text-only result and the images to send after the tool results, for APIs that reject images in error results (Pi 5ab7fe74).
- `chord/host`: `Self.State` takes a `StateInit` as the initial value, so a cell's first value comes from its source. `Init` runs after the object's resources are open and before the object goes live, and a reload runs it for a cell it adds. Until then the cell's `Value` fails `not_ready`.
- `chord/host`: contract placement. `NewHostNamed` and `NewHostFamily` give a remote contract its host. `Serve` refuses a type the host is not the place of, a host refuses a hold whose input its own contract places elsewhere (`invalid/placement`), and a relay refuses a hold whose target disagrees with its contract token. The placement is part of the description and the fingerprint, and an `Accepts` adapter never bridges two placements.
- Go, Python and Rust extensions can override a built-in tool and delegate to the original, as Pi's `create<Tool>ToolDefinition` factories let Node extensions do. `sdk.CreateReadToolDefinition(cwd, opts)` (and the write, edit, bash, grep, find, ls and powershell siblings; Python `create_read_tool_definition`, Rust `create_read_tool_definition`) return the tool's definition, which registers as is, and whose `Execute` runs the host's own tool with Pi's options: `operations` and `spawnHook` functions stay in the extension and are called back while the call runs. The `create<Tool>Tool` forms, `createCodingTools`, `createReadOnlyTools`, `createLocalBashOperations` and `createLocalPowerShellOperations` come with them. New host calls `builtinTool.definition`, `builtinTool.execute` and `builtinTool.localExec`. A built-in's result is a value an `Execute` can return or pass to `OnUpdate` as it is. `TestConformance_BuiltinToolDelegationAcrossSDKs` compares every SDK with Pi's own code. <!-- fix: 1b5b705930 -->
